path: P3.2.3 - Knowledge and use of double
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = 5 cos x - 12 sin x, where x is in degrees. Given that 5 cos x - 12 sin x = 13 cos(x + 67.4 degrees), solve, for 0 <= x < 360 degrees, the equation 5 cos x - 12 sin x = 6.5. Give your answers to one decimal place.
steps: For 0 <= x < 360, the angle x + 67.4 lies between 67.4 and 427.4 degrees.
x + 67.4 = 300 or 420 (the value 60 is out of range), so x = 232.6 or 352.6 degrees.

items.name: Trig identities and equations
path: P3.2.3 - Knowledge and use of double
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = 5 cos x - 12 sin x, where x is in degrees. Using the result 5 cos x - 12 sin x = 13 cos(x + 67.4 degrees), find the minimum value of 20 + 5 cos x - 12 sin x, and the smallest positive value of x, in degrees to one decimal place, at which this minimum occurs.
steps: The smallest value of cos is -1, so the minimum is 20 - 13 = 7.
This needs x + 67.4 = 180, so x = 180 - 67.4 = 112.6 degrees.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
items.question: A sector of a circle has radius 8 cm and angle 0.75 radians. What is the area of the sector? A 24 cm², B 48 cm², C 6 cm², D 32 cm²
steps: Area of a sector = (1/2) r² theta = 0.5 x 8² x 0.75 = 24 cm^2.
B leaves out the factor 1/2; C is the arc length r theta = 6 cm; D leaves out theta.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: In triangle ABC, BC = 7 cm, AC = 5 cm and angle ACB = 60 degrees. What is the length of AB? A sqrt(39) cm, B sqrt(109) cm, C sqrt(74) cm, D 39 cm
steps: Cosine rule: AB² = 7² + 5² - 2(7)(5)cos 60 = 74 - 35 = 39.
So AB = sqrt(39) cm (about 6.24 cm).
B adds the cosine term; C leaves it out; D forgets to take the square root.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: In triangle PQR, PQ = 9.2 cm, QR = 12.5 cm and angle PQR = 48 degrees. Calculate the area of triangle PQR, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
steps: Area = (1/2) x PQ x QR x sin(PQR).
Area = 0.5 x 9.2 x 12.5 x sin 48 degrees = 42.7 cm^2.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
items.question: The sector OAB of a circle has centre O and radius 10 cm, and angle AOB = 1.2 radians. Find the area of the segment bounded by the chord AB and the arc AB, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
steps: Area of sector OAB = (1/2) x 10² x 1.2 = 60 cm^2.
Area of triangle OAB = (1/2) x 10² x sin 1.2 = 46.60 cm² (calculator in radian mode).
Area of segment = 60 - 46.60 = 13.4 cm^2.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 10 cm, BC = 6 cm and angle BAC = 30 degrees. Find the two possible sizes of angle ACB, giving your answers to one decimal place.
steps: Sine rule: sin(ACB)/10 = sin 30/6, so sin(ACB) = 10 x 0.5/6 = 0.8333.
The acute solution is ACB = 56.4 degrees.
The obtuse solution is ACB = 180 - 56.4 = 123.6 degrees.
Both are possible because 30 + 123.6 < 180, so two different triangles fit the data.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: A ship leaves port P and sails 12 km on a bearing of 065 degrees to a lighthouse A. It then sails 9 km on a bearing of 140 degrees to a buoy B. Show that angle PAB = 105 degrees.
steps: The bearing of P from A is 065 + 180 = 245 degrees (the back bearing).
The bearing of B from A is 140 degrees, so angle PAB = 245 - 140 = 105 degrees.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: A ship leaves port P and sails 12 km on a bearing of 065 degrees to a lighthouse A. It then sails 9 km on a bearing of 140 degrees to a buoy B. Given that angle PAB = 105 degrees, calculate the distance PB, giving your answer in km to 3 significant figures.
steps: Cosine rule in triangle PAB: PB² = 12² + 9² - 2(12)(9)cos 105.
PB = 16.8 km.

items.name: Sine and cosine rules
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: A ship leaves port P and sails 12 km on a bearing of 065 degrees to a lighthouse A. It then sails 9 km on a bearing of 140 degrees to a buoy B. Given that PB = 16.76 km and angle PAB = 105 degrees, find the bearing of B from P, giving your answer to the nearest degree.
steps: Sine rule: sin(APB)/9 = sin 105/16.76, so sin(APB) = 0.5187.
Angle APB = 31.2 degrees (acute, since the angle at A is obtuse).
B lies clockwise of A as seen from P, so the bearing is 065 + 31.2 = 096.2 degrees.
To the nearest degree the bearing of B from P is 096 degrees.

items.name: Trig graphs
path: P1.1.12 - Knowledge of the effect of s
items.question: The graph of y = cos x is stretched by scale factor 1/3 parallel to the x-axis. What is the equation of the new graph? A y = cos(x/3), B y = cos 3x, C y = 3 cos x, D y = (1/3) cos x
steps: A stretch with scale factor k parallel to the x-axis replaces x by x/k.
With k = 1/3, x is replaced by 3x, giving y = cos 3x.
A uses scale factor 3 instead; C and D are stretches parallel to the y-axis.

items.name: Trig graphs
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun
items.question: The curve y = 2 sin(x + 30 degrees) - 1 is drawn for 0 <= x <= 360 degrees. What is its maximum value, and at what value of x does it occur? A maximum 1 at x = 60 degrees, B maximum 1 at x = 120 degrees, C maximum 2 at x = 60 degrees, D maximum 3 at x = 60 degrees
steps: The maximum value of sin is 1, so the maximum of y is 2(1) - 1 = 1.
This occurs when x + 30 = 90, so x = 60 degrees.
B uses x - 30 = 90; C forgets the -1; D adds 1 instead of subtracting it.

items.name: Trig graphs
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun
items.question: The curve C has equation y = 5 tan 3x, where x is in radians. State the period of C, and the equation of the asymptote of C with the smallest positive value of x.
steps: tan x has period pi, so tan 3x has period pi/3.
The first asymptote of tan x is at x = pi/2, so for tan 3x it is where 3x = pi/2, giving x = pi/6.

items.name: Trig graphs
items.question: Describe fully a sequence of three transformations that maps the graph of y = sin x onto the graph of y = 2 sin 3x + 1.
items.answer: Stretch parallel to the x-axis, scale factor 1/3; stretch parallel to the y-axis, scale factor 2; translation by the vector (0, 1)
steps: Stretch parallel to the x-axis with scale factor 1/3 (gives y = sin 3x).
Stretch parallel to the y-axis with scale factor 2 (gives y = 2 sin 3x).
Translation by the vector (0, 1), i.e. 1 unit in the positive y direction (gives y = 2 sin 3x + 1), applied after the stretches.
accept: The two stretches may be done in either order.
Any other valid sequence, e.g. translation by (0, 1/2) first and then a stretch parallel to the y-axis with scale factor 2.
Equivalent wording: "horizontal compression by factor 3" for the x stretch, "vertical stretch by factor 2" for the y stretch.

items.name: Trig graphs
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun
items.question: The curve C has equation y = 3 sin(2x - pi/3) for 0 <= x <= pi, where x is in radians. Find the exact coordinates of the maximum point and of the minimum point of C.
steps: For 0 <= x <= pi the angle 2x - pi/3 runs from -pi/3 to 5pi/3.
Maximum: sin(2x - pi/3) = 1 when 2x - pi/3 = pi/2, so x = 5pi/12 and y = 3.
Minimum: sin(2x - pi/3) = -1 when 2x - pi/3 = 3pi/2, so x = 11pi/12 and y = -3.
The next maximum, at 2x - pi/3 = 5pi/2, lies outside the interval.

items.name: Trig graphs
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun
items.question: The depth of water, D metres, in a harbour t hours after midnight is modelled by D = 6 + 2.5 sin(30t), where 30t is measured in degrees and 0 <= t <= 12. Write down the maximum depth of water predicted by the model and the first time after midnight at which it occurs.
steps: The maximum value of sin(30t) is 1, so D = 6 + 2.5 = 8.5 m.
sin(30t) = 1 when 30t = 90, so t = 3.

items.name: Trig graphs
items.question: The depth of water, D metres, in a harbour t hours after midnight is modelled by D = 6 + 2.5 sin(30t), where 30t is measured in degrees and 0 <= t <= 12. Find the times, to the nearest minute, at which D = 5 during the first 12 hours after midnight.
steps: t = 6.786 hours or 11.214 hours.
6.786 hours = 6 h 47 min and 11.214 hours = 11 h 13 min, so the times are 06:47 and 11:13.

items.name: Trig graphs
items.question: The depth of water, D metres, in a harbour t hours after midnight is modelled by D = 6 + 2.5 sin(30t), where 30t is measured in degrees and 0 <= t <= 12. Determine the total time during the first 12 hours for which the depth of water is at least 7.5 m. Give your answer in hours to 3 significant figures.
steps: sin(30t) = 0.6 gives 30t = 36.87 or 143.13 degrees within 0 to 360.

items.name: Trig graphs
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun
items.question: The depth of water, D metres, in a harbour t hours after midnight is modelled by D = 6 + 2.5 sin(30t), where 30t is measured in degrees and 0 <= t <= 12. The model has a period of exactly 12 hours. Suggest one reason why it might not give accurate predictions of the depth of water over several weeks.
items.answer: Real tides have a period of about 12.4 hours, not exactly 12, so the predicted times would drift away from the real ones
steps: Real tides do not repeat exactly every 12 hours (the period is about 12.4 hours), so the predicted times drift from the real times.
accept: The height of high and low tide changes over the month (spring and neap tides), but the model has a constant amplitude of 2.5 m.
Weather, such as air pressure and wind, changes the actual depth of water.
The model has the same maximum depth every cycle, which is not true of real tides.

items.name: Modulus and transformations
items.question: Which of the following gives all the solutions of |2x - 3| = 7? A x = 5 or x = -2, B x = 5 or x = 2, C x = 5 only, D x = -5 or x = 2
steps: The modulus equation gives two cases: 2x - 3 = 7 or 2x - 3 = -7.
2x - 3 = 7 gives x = 5 and 2x - 3 = -7 gives x = -2.
C ignores the negative case; B and D make sign slips when solving the second case.

items.name: Modulus and transformations
items.question: The curve y = f(x) has a minimum point at (2, -3). What are the coordinates of the minimum point on the curve y = 2f(x - 1) + 4? A (3, -2); B (1, -2); C (3, 2); D (3, 1)
steps: f(x - 1) is a translation of 1 unit to the right, so the x-coordinate becomes 2 + 1 = 3.
The y-coordinate is stretched by factor 2 then raised by 4: 2(-3) + 4 = -2.
B translates the wrong way; C applies the stretch after adding 4; D leaves out the stretch.

items.name: Modulus and transformations
items.question: Solve the inequality |2x + 1| > |x - 4|.
steps: Both sides are non-negative, so square them: (2x + 1)² > (x - 4)^2.
Divide by 3: x² + 4x - 5 > 0, which factorises as (x + 5)(x - 1) > 0.
The quadratic is positive outside its roots, so x < -5 or x > 1.

items.name: Modulus and transformations
items.question: Solve the equation |3x - 1| = 2x + 5.
steps: Case 1: 3x - 1 = 2x + 5, so x = 6.
Check: for x = 6, 2x + 5 = 17 and |17| = 17; for x = -0.8, 2x + 5 = 3.4 and |-3.4| = 3.4. Both are valid since 2x + 5 > 0.

items.name: Modulus and transformations
path: P1.1.12 - Knowledge of the effect of s
items.question: The curve C has equation y = x² - 4x. The curve C is reflected in the x-axis, and the resulting curve is then translated by 3 units in the positive x direction. Show that the equation of the final curve is y = -x² + 10x - 21.
steps: Reflection in the x-axis replaces y by -y, giving y = -(x² - 4x) = -x² + 4x.
Translation by 3 in the positive x direction replaces x by (x - 3): y = -(x - 3)² + 4(x - 3).

items.name: Modulus and transformations
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = |2x - 5| - 3, for x in R. Write down the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of y = f(x) and the range of f.
steps: |2x - 5| has its smallest value, 0, when x = 2.5, so f(2.5) = -3 and the vertex is (2.5, -3).
Since |2x - 5| >= 0 for all x, f(x) >= -3.

items.name: Modulus and transformations
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = |2x - 5| - 3, for x in R. Solve the equation f(x) = 4.
steps: 2x - 5 = 7 gives x = 6.
2x - 5 = -7 gives x = -1.

items.name: Modulus and transformations
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = |2x - 5| - 3, for x in R. Find the set of values of x for which f(x) < 1.

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: Which of the following gives the equations of the asymptotes of the curve y = (3x + 1)/(x - 2)? A x = 2 and y = 3, B x = 2 and y = 1/3, C x = -2 and y = 3, D x = 3 and y = 2
steps: The denominator is zero when x = 2, so there is a vertical asymptote x = 2.
Dividing top and bottom by x, y = (3 + 1/x)/(1 - 2/x) tends to 3 as x becomes large, so y = 3 is the horizontal asymptote.
B inverts the ratio of the leading coefficients; C has the wrong sign; D swaps the two lines.

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: Which of the following is equal to (4x + 5)/((x + 1)(x + 2))? A 1/(x + 1) + 3/(x + 2), B 3/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 2), C 4/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 2), D 1/(x + 1) - 3/(x + 2)
steps: Put x = -1: 1 = P. Put x = -2: -3 = -Q, so Q = 3.
B swaps P and Q; D has a sign error in Q; C does not satisfy 4x + 5 = P(x + 2) + Q(x + 1).

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: Show that (3x² - x - 10)/(x² - 4) simplifies to (3x + 5)/(x + 2), where x is not equal to 2 or -2.
steps: Factorise the numerator: 3x² - x - 10 = (3x + 5)(x - 2).
Factorise the denominator (difference of two squares): x² - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2).
Cancel the common factor (x - 2), which is non-zero since x is not 2, to get (3x + 5)/(x + 2).

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: Express (3x + 1)/((x - 1)(x + 1)²) in partial fractions.
steps: Put x = 1: 4 = 4A, so A = 1.
Compare coefficients of x²: 0 = A + B, so B = -1.

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: The curve C has equation y = (2x + 3)/(x - 1), where x is not equal to 1. Determine the coordinates of the points where C crosses the coordinate axes, and write down the equations of the asymptotes of C.
items.answer: Crosses x-axis at (-3/2, 0), y-axis at (0, -3); asymptotes x = 1 and y = 2
steps: y = 0 when 2x + 3 = 0, so the curve crosses the x-axis at (-3/2, 0).
x = 0 gives y = 3/(-1) = -3, so it crosses the y-axis at (0, -3).
The denominator is zero at x = 1, so x = 1 is a vertical asymptote.
As x becomes large y tends to 2/1 = 2, so y = 2 is a horizontal asymptote.

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = (2x² + 5x + 1)/((x + 1)(x + 2)), for x in R, x not equal to -1 or -2. Express f(x) in the form A + B/(x + 1) + C/(x + 2), where A, B and C are constants to be found.
steps: The denominator is x² + 3x + 2 and the numerator has the same degree, so divide: 2x² + 5x + 1 = 2(x² + 3x + 2) - x - 3.
x = -1 gives P = 2; x = -2 gives 1 = -Q, so Q = -1.

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = (2x² + 5x + 1)/((x + 1)(x + 2)), for x in R, x not equal to -1 or -2. Using f(x) = 2 - 2/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 2), write down the equations of the asymptotes of the curve y = f(x).
steps: The term 2/(x + 1) is unbounded as x tends to -1, giving the asymptote x = -1.
The term 1/(x + 2) is unbounded as x tends to -2, giving the asymptote x = -2.
As x becomes large both fractions tend to 0, so y tends to 2 and y = 2 is an asymptote.

items.name: Rational functions
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = (2x² + 5x + 1)/((x + 1)(x + 2)), for x in R, x not equal to -1 or -2. Find the exact x-coordinates of the points where the curve y = f(x) crosses the x-axis.
steps: y = 0 when the numerator is zero: 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0.
The quadratic formula gives x = (-5 +/- sqrt(25 - 8))/4.
So x = (-5 + sqrt(17))/4 or x = (-5 - sqrt(17))/4 (about -0.219 and -2.28; neither makes the denominator zero).

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.3.1 - The function ex and its grap
items.question: The curve C has equation y = 4e^(-0.5x) + 2. Which statement about C is correct? A C meets the y-axis at (0, 6) and has asymptote y = 2; B C meets the y-axis at (0, 4) and has asymptote y = 2; C C meets the y-axis at (0, 6) and has asymptote y = 0; D C meets the y-axis at (0, 2) and has asymptote y = 4
items.answer: A: C meets the y-axis at (0, 6) and has asymptote y = 2
steps: When x = 0, y = 4e⁰ + 2 = 6, so C meets the y-axis at (0, 6).
As x becomes large e^(-0.5x) tends to 0, so y tends to 2 and the asymptote is y = 2.
B forgets to add the 2 to the intercept; C ignores the translation of 2 upwards; D swaps the intercept and the asymptote.

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.3.2 - The function ln x and its gr
items.question: The curve y = ln(x - 3) meets the x-axis at the point P. Which of the following gives the coordinates of P and the equation of the vertical asymptote? A P(4, 0), x = 3; B P(4, 0), x = -3; C P(1, 0), x = 3; D P(3, 0), x = 4
steps: ln(x - 3) = 0 gives x - 3 = 1, so x = 4 and P is (4, 0).
The graph of y = ln x is translated 3 units to the right, so the asymptote x = 0 moves to x = 3.
B has the wrong sign for the translation; C is the intercept of y = ln x untranslated; D swaps the intercept and the asymptote.

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.3.2 - The function ln x and its gr
items.question: Solve the equation e^(2x) - 7e^x + 10 = 0, giving your answers as exact values.
steps: Let y = e^x, so e^(2x) = y² and the equation becomes y² - 7y + 10 = 0.
Factorise: (y - 2)(y - 5) = 0, so y = 2 or y = 5.
e^x = 2 gives x = ln 2 and e^x = 5 gives x = ln 5.

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.3.1 - The function ex and its grap
items.question: The curve y = e^x is reflected in the y-axis and then translated by 3 units in the negative y direction. Write down the equation of the resulting curve, the coordinates of the point where it crosses the y-axis, and the equation of its asymptote.
items.answer: y = e^(-x) - 3; crosses y-axis at (0, -2); asymptote y = -3
steps: Reflection in the y-axis replaces x by -x, giving y = e^(-x).
Translating down by 3 gives y = e^(-x) - 3.
At x = 0, y = 1 - 3 = -2, so the curve crosses the y-axis at (0, -2).
As x becomes large e^(-x) tends to 0, so the asymptote is y = -3.

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.3.3 - Use logarithmic graphs to es
items.question: Experimental data are modelled by y = a b^x, where a and b are constants. A graph of log10 y against x is a straight line with gradient 0.30 and a vertical intercept of 1.2. Find the values of a and b, giving each to 3 significant figures.
steps: Take logs of y = a b^x: log10 y = log10 a + x log10 b.
The intercept gives log10 a = 1.2, so a = 10^1.2 = 15.8.
The gradient gives log10 b = 0.30, so b = 10^0.30 = 2.00.

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.4.4 - and use exponential growth a
items.question: The value, V pounds, of a car t years after it was bought is modelled by V = 18000e^(-0.15t), for t >= 0. Write down the value of the car when it was bought, and describe what the model predicts for V as t becomes large.
items.answer: 18000 pounds; V decreases towards 0 but never reaches it
steps: At t = 0, V = 18000e⁰ = 18000, so the car cost 18000 pounds.
As t becomes large e^(-0.15t) tends to 0, so V tends to 0 (decreasing but always positive).

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.4.4 - and use exponential growth a
items.question: The value, V pounds, of a car t years after it was bought is modelled by V = 18000e^(-0.15t), for t >= 0. According to the model, find the value of the car after 4 years. Give your answer to the nearest pound.
steps: V = 9878.6, which is 9879 pounds to the nearest pound.

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.3.2 - The function ln x and its gr
items.question: The value, V pounds, of a car t years after it was bought is modelled by V = 18000e^(-0.15t), for t >= 0. According to the model, find the value of t at which the car is worth 5000 pounds. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
steps: Take natural logs: -0.15t = ln(5/18) = -ln 3.6.

items.name: Exponential and log graphs
path: P3.4.4 - and use exponential growth a
items.question: The value, V pounds, of a car t years after it was bought is modelled by V = 18000e^(-0.15t), for t >= 0. Suggest one reason why the model may not give a realistic value for the car after 40 years.
items.answer: The model gives only about 45 pounds after 40 years, but an old car keeps a scrap or collector value, so the prediction is too low
steps: The model predicts V = 18000e⁻⁶, about 45 pounds, but a 40-year-old car would still be worth more than this (for example scrap value or classic/collector value).
accept: The value of a car depends on factors other than age, such as mileage, condition and model.
An exponential model assumes the car loses the same percentage of its value every year, which is unlikely to hold for 40 years.
Cars lose value fastest in the first few years, so a constant rate of decay (0.15) is not realistic.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 3x - 1 and g(x) = x² + 2, for x in R. What is gf(x)? A 9x² - 6x + 3, B 3x² + 5, C 9x² + 3, D 3x² - 1
steps: Expand: 9x² - 6x + 1 + 2 = 9x² - 6x + 3.
B is fg(x), the wrong order; C leaves out the middle term when squaring; D applies f to x² only.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = (2x - 1)/(x + 3), for x in R, x not equal to -3. What is f⁻¹(x)? A (3x + 1)/(2 - x), B (x + 3)/(2x - 1), C (3x - 1)/(2 + x), D (3x + 1)/(x - 2)
steps: Let y = (2x - 1)/(x + 3), so y(x + 3) = 2x - 1 and xy + 3y = 2x - 1.
Collect x terms: x(y - 2) = -1 - 3y, so x = (3y + 1)/(2 - y).
Hence f⁻¹(x) = (3x + 1)/(2 - x). B is 1/f(x); C and D have sign errors.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The function g is defined by g(x) = ln(2x - 1), for x > 1/2. Find g⁻¹(x), and state its domain.
items.answer: g⁻¹(x) = (e^x + 1)/2; domain x in R (all real numbers)
steps: Let y = ln(2x - 1), so e^y = 2x - 1.
Hence x = (e^y + 1)/2 and g⁻¹(x) = (e^x + 1)/2.
The domain of g⁻¹ is the range of g. As x > 1/2, 2x - 1 takes every positive value, so g takes every real value.
So the domain of g⁻¹ is all real numbers.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 3x + 2, for x in R, and g(x) = 1/(x - 1), for x in R, x not equal to 1. Solve the equation fg(x) = x, giving your answers as exact values.
steps: Set 3/(x - 1) + 2 = x and multiply by (x - 1): 3 + 2(x - 1) = x(x - 1).
So 2x + 1 = x² - x, giving x² - 3x - 1 = 0.
x = (3 +/- sqrt(9 + 4))/2 = (3 +/- sqrt(13))/2; neither equals 1, so both are valid.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² - 4x + 1, for x in R. Explain why f does not have an inverse function, and find the smallest value of the constant k for which f, with domain x >= k, does have an inverse.
items.answer: f is many-to-one (for example f(1) = f(3) = -2), so it has no inverse; k = 2
steps: f is many-to-one (not one-to-one): two different inputs give the same output, for example f(1) = f(3) = -2, so f has no inverse.
Complete the square: f(x) = (x - 2)² - 3, so the graph is symmetrical about its minimum point at x = 2.
f is one-to-one for x >= 2, so the smallest value of k is 2.
accept: Any other correct pair of inputs with the same output, for example f(0) = f(4) = 1.
A horizontal line cuts the graph of y = f(x) at two points (fails the horizontal line test).
Differentiate: f'(x) = 2x - 4 = 0 at x = 2, to find the turning point instead of completing the square.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = (x - 3)² + 2, for x >= 3, and g(x) = 4x - 7, for x in R. Write down the range of f.
steps: (x - 3)² >= 0, with equality at x = 3, so the smallest value of f is f(3) = 2.
f increases for x >= 3 with no upper limit, so the range is f(x) >= 2.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = (x - 3)² + 2, for x >= 3, and g(x) = 4x - 7, for x in R. Find f⁻¹(x) and state the domain of f^-1.
steps: Let y = (x - 3)² + 2, so (x - 3)² = y - 2.
Since x >= 3, take the positive root: x = 3 + sqrt(y - 2), so f⁻¹(x) = 3 + sqrt(x - 2).
The domain of f⁻¹ is the range of f, so x >= 2.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = (x - 3)² + 2, for x >= 3, and g(x) = 4x - 7, for x in R. Solve the equation gf(x) = 17.
steps: x = 5 or x = 1, but the domain of f is x >= 3, so x = 5 only.

items.name: Composite and inverse functions
path: P3.1.2 - Definition of a function. Do
items.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = (x - 3)² + 2, for x >= 3, and g(x) = 4x - 7, for x in R. The graphs of y = f(x) and y = f⁻¹(x) meet at a single point, which lies on the line y = x. Find the exact x-coordinate of this point.
steps: The point lies on y = x, so f(x) = x: (x - 3)² + 2 = x.
Expand: x² - 6x + 9 + 2 = x, so x² - 7x + 11 = 0.
The domain of f is x >= 3 and (7 - sqrt(5))/2 is about 2.38, so reject it. x = (7 + sqrt(5))/2.

items.name: Straight lines
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: A straight line has equation 3x - 4y + 8 = 0. What is the gradient of the line? A 3/4, B -3/4, C 3, D 4/3
steps: Rearrange to make y the subject: 4y = 3x + 8, so y = (3/4)x + 2.
The gradient is 3/4. B is a sign error; C reads off the coefficient of x without dividing by 4; D inverts the gradient.

items.name: Straight lines
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: The points A and B have coordinates (1, 2) and (5, -4). Which of the following is an equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB? A 2x - 3y - 9 = 0, B 3x + 2y - 7 = 0, C 3x - 2y - 11 = 0, D 2x + 3y - 3 = 0
steps: The gradient of AB is (-4 - 2)/(5 - 1) = -3/2, so the perpendicular gradient is 2/3.
The midpoint of AB is (3, -1), so y + 1 = (2/3)(x - 3), which gives 3y + 3 = 2x - 6, i.e. 2x - 3y - 9 = 0.
B is the line AB itself (gradient -3/2); C has gradient 3/2 (sign slip); D has gradient -2/3 (not negated after inverting).

items.name: Straight lines
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The line l passes through the points P(-2, 5) and Q(4, 1). Find an equation of l in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are integers.
steps: Using point P: y - 5 = -(2/3)(x + 2), so 3y - 15 = -2x - 4.
Rearrange: 2x + 3y - 11 = 0 (check Q: 8 + 3 - 11 = 0).

items.name: Straight lines
items.question: The line l1 has equation 4x + 3y = 5 and the line l2 has equation 5x - 2y = 12. Find the coordinates of the point where l1 and l2 intersect.
steps: Multiply l1 by 2 and l2 by 3: 8x + 6y = 10 and 15x - 6y = 36.
Add the equations: 23x = 46, so x = 2.
Substitute into l1: 8 + 3y = 5, so y = -1. The point is (2, -1).

items.name: Straight lines
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: Show that the points A(-1, 2), B(2, 8) and C(5, 14) are collinear.
items.answer: Gradient AB = gradient BC = 2, with B common, so A, B and C lie on one straight line
steps: Gradient of BC = (14 - 8)/(5 - 2) = 6/3 = 2. The gradients are equal and B is common to both segments, so the points are collinear.

items.name: Straight lines
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The points A and B have coordinates (2, 7) and (8, -1) respectively. Find an equation of the line l1 through A and B, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are integers.
steps: Rearrange: 4x + 3y - 29 = 0 (check B: 32 - 3 - 29 = 0).

items.name: Straight lines
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: The points A and B have coordinates (2, 7) and (8, -1) respectively. The line l1 through A(2, 7) and B(8, -1) has equation 4x + 3y - 29 = 0. The line l2 is perpendicular to l1 and passes through the midpoint of AB. Find an equation of l2 in the form px + qy + r = 0, where p, q and r are integers.
steps: The midpoint of AB is ((2 + 8)/2, (7 - 1)/2) = (5, 3).
The gradient of l1 is -4/3, so the gradient of l2 is 3/4.
Rearrange: 3x - 4y - 3 = 0.

items.name: Straight lines
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The points A and B have coordinates (2, 7) and (8, -1) respectively. The line l2 with equation 3x - 4y - 3 = 0 is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining A(2, 7) and B(8, -1). The line l2 meets the x-axis at the point C. Find the area of triangle ABC.
steps: At the x-axis y = 0, so 3x - 3 = 0 and C is (1, 0).
The midpoint of AB is M(5, 3) and C lies on l2, so CM is perpendicular to AB: CM = sqrt(4² + 3²) = 5.
AB = sqrt(6² + 8²) = 10.

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: A circle has equation x² + y² - 6x + 10y + 18 = 0. What are its centre and radius? A centre (3, -5) and radius 4; B centre (-3, 5) and radius 4; C centre (3, -5) and radius 16; D centre (3, -5) and radius sqrt(34)
steps: Complete the square: (x - 3)² - 9 + (y + 5)² - 25 + 18 = 0.
So (x - 3)² + (y + 5)² = 16, giving centre (3, -5) and radius sqrt(16) = 4.
B has the signs of the centre wrong; C gives r² as the radius; D leaves out the constant 18.

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: A circle has centre (2, -1) and passes through the point (5, 3). What is an equation of the circle? A (x - 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25, B (x + 2)² + (y - 1)² = 25, C (x - 2)² + (y + 1)² = 5, D (x - 2)² + (y + 1)² = 7
steps: The radius is the distance from (2, -1) to (5, 3): r² = (5 - 2)² + (3 + 1)² = 9 + 16 = 25.
So the equation is (x - 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25.
B has the signs of the centre wrong; C uses r instead of r²; D uses 3 + 4.

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The circle C has equation (x - 1)² + (y + 2)² = 20. Show that the line with equation y = 2x + 6 is a tangent to C, and find the coordinates of the point of contact.
items.answer: The line is a tangent (repeated root); the point of contact is (-3, 0)
steps: Substitute y = 2x + 6: (x - 1)² + (2x + 8)² = 20.
(x + 3)² = 0 has a repeated root, so the line meets the circle at exactly one point: it is a tangent.
x = -3 and y = 2(-3) + 6 = 0, so the point of contact is (-3, 0).

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The points A(-3, 4) and B(5, -2) are the ends of a diameter of a circle. Find an equation of the circle.
steps: The centre is the midpoint of AB: ((-3 + 5)/2, (4 - 2)/2) = (1, 1).
AB = sqrt(8² + 6²) = 10, so the radius is 5.
The equation is (x - 1)² + (y - 1)² = 25.

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The circle C has equation x² + y² - 4x + 6y - 12 = 0 and the point P has coordinates (5, 1). Show that P lies on C, and find an equation of the tangent to C at P in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are integers.
steps: Substitute (5, 1): 25 + 1 - 20 + 6 - 12 = 0, so P lies on C.
Complete the square: (x - 2)² + (y + 3)² = 25, so the centre is (2, -3).
The gradient of the radius from (2, -3) to P is (1 + 3)/(5 - 2) = 4/3, so the tangent has gradient -3/4.

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The circle C has equation x² + y² - 8x + 2y - 8 = 0 and centre N. Find the coordinates of N and the radius of C.
steps: Complete the square: (x - 4)² - 16 + (y + 1)² - 1 - 8 = 0.
The centre N is (4, -1) and the radius is 5.

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The circle C has equation x² + y² - 8x + 2y - 8 = 0 and centre N. The line with equation y = x - 4 meets C at the points A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B.
steps: Substitute y = x - 4: x² + (x - 4)² - 8x + 2(x - 4) - 8 = 0.
2x(x - 7) = 0 gives x = 0 or x = 7.
y = x - 4 gives the points (0, -4) and (7, 3).

items.name: Circles
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The circle C has centre N(4, -1) and the points A(0, -4) and B(7, 3) lie on C. Find the area of triangle ABN.
steps: AB = sqrt(7² + 7²) = 7 sqrt(2).
The midpoint of the chord AB is M(3.5, -0.5), and NM is perpendicular to AB.
NM = sqrt(0.5² + 0.5²) = 1/sqrt(2).
Area = (1/2) x 7 sqrt(2) x 1/sqrt(2) = 3.5.

items.name: Parametric equations
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: A curve has parametric equations x = 2t + 1, y = t² - 3, for t in R. Which of the following is a Cartesian equation of the curve? A y = (x - 1)²/4 - 3, B y = (x - 1)²/2 - 3, C y = (x + 1)²/4 - 3, D y = 4(x - 1)² - 3
steps: Rearrange x = 2t + 1 to give t = (x - 1)/2.
Substitute into y = t² - 3: y = ((x - 1)/2)² - 3 = (x - 1)²/4 - 3.
B forgets to square the 2; C has a sign error in t; D multiplies by 4 instead of dividing.

items.name: Parametric equations
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: A curve has parametric equations x = 3 + 2cos t, y = -1 + 2sin t, for 0 <= t < 2pi. Which of the following is a Cartesian equation of the curve? A (x - 3)² + (y + 1)² = 4, B (x + 3)² + (y - 1)² = 4, C (x - 3)² + (y + 1)² = 2, D (x - 3)² + (y + 1)² = 16
steps: cos t = (x - 3)/2 and sin t = (y + 1)/2.
Use cos² t + sin² t = 1: (x - 3)²/4 + (y + 1)²/4 = 1, so (x - 3)² + (y + 1)² = 4.
B has the signs of the centre wrong; C and D use the wrong value of r² (2 or 2⁴ instead of 2²).

items.name: Parametric equations
items.question: A curve C has parametric equations x = t² + 1, y = 2t³ - 3t, for t in R. Find the gradient of C at the point where t = 2.
steps: dx/dt = 2t and dy/dt = 6t² - 3.
dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = (6t² - 3)/(2t).

items.name: Parametric equations
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: A curve has parametric equations x = 3t - 2, y = t² - 4t, for t in R. Find the coordinates of the points where the curve meets the x-axis.
steps: The curve meets the x-axis when y = 0: t² - 4t = 0, so t(t - 4) = 0 and t = 0 or t = 4.
When t = 0, x = -2; when t = 4, x = 10.
The points are (-2, 0) and (10, 0).

items.name: Parametric equations
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: A curve C has parametric equations x = 2 sin t, y = 1 - cos 2t, for 0 <= t <= 2pi. Find a Cartesian equation of C in the form y = f(x), and state the set of possible values of x.
steps: Use cos 2t = 1 - 2sin² t, so y = 1 - (1 - 2sin² t) = 2sin² t.
From x = 2 sin t, sin t = x/2, so y = 2(x/2)² = x²/2.
Since -1 <= sin t <= 1, the values of x satisfy -2 <= x <= 2.

items.name: Parametric equations
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: The curve C has parametric equations x = t², y = t³ - 3t, for t in R. Show that a Cartesian equation of C is y² = x(x - 3)^2.
steps: y = t³ - 3t = t(t² - 3), so y² = t²(t² - 3)^2.
Substitute t² = x: y² = x(x - 3)^2.

items.name: Parametric equations
items.question: The curve C has parametric equations x = t², y = t³ - 3t, for t in R. Find dy/dx in terms of t.
steps: dx/dt = 2t and dy/dt = 3t² - 3.
dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = (3t² - 3)/(2t), for t not equal to 0.

items.name: Parametric equations
items.question: The curve C has parametric equations x = t², y = t³ - 3t, for t in R. Given that dy/dx = (3t² - 3)/(2t), find an equation of the tangent to C at the point where t = 2, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are integers.
steps: When t = 2: x = 4 and y = 8 - 6 = 2, so the point is (4, 2).
The gradient is (12 - 3)/4 = 9/4.
Rearrange: 9x - 4y - 28 = 0.

items.name: Parametric equations
items.question: The curve C has parametric equations x = t², y = t³ - 3t, for t in R. Given that dy/dx = (3t² - 3)/(2t), find the coordinates of the points on C where the tangent is horizontal.
steps: The tangent is horizontal when dy/dx = 0, so 3t² - 3 = 0 and t = 1 or t = -1.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The points A and B have coordinates (-2, 3) and (4, 7). What is the distance AB? A 2sqrt(13), B sqrt(104), C 10, D sqrt(20)
steps: AB = sqrt(52) = 2sqrt(13).
B adds the coordinates instead of subtracting; C adds the differences without squaring; D subtracts the squares.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The vertices of a triangle are A(1, 1), B(5, 2) and C(2, 6). What is the area of the triangle? A 9.5, B 19, C 11.5, D 15.5
steps: Enclose the triangle in a rectangle with corners (1, 1) and (5, 6), of area 4 x 5 = 20.
Subtract the three right-angled triangles outside ABC: (1/2)(4)(1) = 2, (1/2)(4)(3) = 6 and (1/2)(1)(5) = 2.5.
B forgets the factor 1/2 in the shoelace method; C and D come from sign slips in it.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: The vertices of triangle ABC are A(1, 2), B(5, 0) and C(7, 4). Show that triangle ABC is isosceles and right-angled, and find its area.
items.answer: AB = BC = sqrt(20) and AB² + BC² = AC², so the triangle is isosceles and right-angled at B; area 10
steps: AB² = 4² + 2² = 20 and BC² = 2² + 4² = 20, so AB = BC and the triangle is isosceles.
AC² = 6² + 2² = 40 = AB² + BC², so by the converse of Pythagoras the angle at B is 90 degrees.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: ABCD is a parallelogram with vertices A(1, 1), B(5, 3), C(8, 7) and D, in that order. Find the coordinates of D, and the area of the parallelogram.
steps: In a parallelogram DC is equal to AB. AB = (4, 2), so D = C - (4, 2) = (4, 5).
The diagonal AC splits the parallelogram into two equal triangles, so the area is 2 x 5 = 10.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: The quadrilateral OABC has vertices O(0, 0), A(8, 0), B(6, 5) and C(1, 5). Show that OABC is a trapezium, and find its area.
items.answer: OA is parallel to CB (both horizontal) while OC and AB are not parallel; area 32.5
steps: OA and CB both have gradient 0, so they are parallel. The gradients of OC (5) and AB (-5/2) are different, so exactly one pair of sides is parallel and OABC is a trapezium.
The parallel sides have lengths OA = 8 and CB = 6 - 1 = 5, and the distance between them is 5.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The vertices of triangle PQR are P(-2, 1), Q(6, 5) and R(2, -3). Show that triangle PQR is isosceles.
steps: PQ = QR = sqrt(80) = 4sqrt(5), so the triangle is isosceles.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: The vertices of triangle PQR are P(-2, 1), Q(6, 5) and R(2, -3). The midpoint of PR is M. Show that QM is perpendicular to PR.
items.answer: Gradient QM = 1 and gradient PR = -1, so QM is perpendicular to PR (shown)
steps: Gradient of QM = (5 + 1)/(6 - 0) = 1.
Gradient of PR = (-3 - 1)/(2 + 2) = -1. The product of the gradients is -1, so QM is perpendicular to PR.

items.name: Coordinates and areas
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The vertices of triangle PQR are P(-2, 1), Q(6, 5) and R(2, -3). Given that M(0, -1) is the midpoint of PR and that QM is perpendicular to PR, find the area of triangle PQR.
steps: PR = sqrt(4² + 4²) = 4sqrt(2), taken as the base.
The height is QM = sqrt(6² + 6²) = 6sqrt(2).
Area = (1/2) x 4sqrt(2) x 6sqrt(2) = 24.

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
path: P1.1.1 - Laws of indices for all rati
items.question: Simplify (27x⁶)^(2/3). A 9x⁴, B 18x⁴, C 9x⁹, D 18x⁹
steps: B multiplies 27 by 2/3 instead of taking the cube root and squaring.
C inverts the power on x (6 times 3/2 = 9); D makes both errors.

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
items.question: Given that log_a 5 = p and log_a 3 = q, log_a 75 is equal to: A 2p + q, B p² + q, C 2pq, D 25p + q
steps: 75 = 5² x 3, so log_a 75 = log_a 5² + log_a 3.
Power law: log_a 5² = 2 log_a 5 = 2p, so log_a 75 = 2p + q.
B squares p instead of doubling it; C multiplies the logarithms instead of adding.
D treats log_a 25 as 25p.

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
path: P1.1.2 - Use and manipulation of surd
items.question: Express (3 + sqrt(5))/(2 - sqrt(5)) in the form a + b sqrt(5), where a and b are integers.
steps: Multiply numerator and denominator by (2 + sqrt(5)).
Denominator: (2 - sqrt(5))(2 + sqrt(5)) = 4 - 5 = -1.
Numerator: (3 + sqrt(5))(2 + sqrt(5)) = 6 + 3 sqrt(5) + 2 sqrt(5) + 5 = 11 + 5 sqrt(5).
So the expression is (11 + 5 sqrt(5))/(-1) = -11 - 5 sqrt(5), with a = -11 and b = -5.

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
path: P2.5.3 - The solution of equations of
items.question: Solve the equation 2^(2x) - 9(2^x) + 8 = 0.
steps: Let y = 2^x. Since 2^(2x) = (2^x)² = y², the equation becomes y² - 9y + 8 = 0.
Factorise: (y - 1)(y - 8) = 0, so y = 1 or y = 8.
2^x = 1 gives x = 0; 2^x = 8 gives x = 3.

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
items.question: Solve the equation log_3(2x + 1) = 2 + log_3(x - 1).
steps: Rearrange: log_3(2x + 1) - log_3(x - 1) = 2, so log_3[(2x + 1)/(x - 1)] = 2.
Remove the logarithm: (2x + 1)/(x - 1) = 3² = 9.
Check: x > 1, so both log_3(2x + 1) and log_3(x - 1) are defined.

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
path: P2.5.1 - y  ax and its graph
items.question: The value, V pounds, of a car t years after it was bought is modelled by V = 18000 x 0.85^t. Find the value of the car after 4 years, giving your answer to the nearest pound.
steps: To the nearest pound, V = 9396.

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
path: P2.5.3 - The solution of equations of
items.question: The value, V pounds, of a car t years after it was bought is modelled by V = 18000 x 0.85^t. Using logarithms, find the time for the value of the car to fall to 5000 pounds, giving your answer in years to 3 significant figures.
steps: Take logarithms: t ln 0.85 = ln(5/18).

items.name: Indices, surds and logs
path: P3.3.3 - Use logarithmic graphs to es
items.question: The value, V pounds, of a car t years after it was bought is modelled by V = 18000 x 0.85^t. A graph of log10 V against t is a straight line. Show that this is so, and find the gradient and the vertical intercept of the line, giving each to 3 significant figures.
steps: Take log10 of both sides: log10 V = log10 18000 + t log10 0.85.
This has the form y = c + mt, so the graph of log10 V against t is a straight line.
Vertical intercept = log10 18000 = 4.26 (3 s.f.).

items.name: Polynomials and factors
items.question: When f(x) = 2x³ - 5x + 1 is divided by (x + 2), the remainder is: A -5, B 7, C 1, D -25
steps: By the remainder theorem the remainder is f(-2).
B is f(2), using the wrong sign for the root of the divisor; C is the constant term.
D comes from -5(-2) evaluated as -10.

items.name: Polynomials and factors
path: P1.1.4 - The discriminant of a quadra
items.question: The equation x² + kx + (k + 3) = 0 has equal roots. The possible values of k are: A -2 or 6, B 2 or -6, C 1 or 3, D 6 or -6
steps: Equal roots need b² - 4ac = 0: k² - 4(k + 3) = 0.
k² - 4k - 12 = 0, so (k - 6)(k + 2) = 0, giving k = 6 or k = -2.
B reads the roots from the factors with the wrong signs; C comes from forgetting the bracket, k² - 4k + 3 = 0.
D takes the roots to be plus and minus the larger value, k = 6 or k = -6.

items.name: Polynomials and factors
items.question: f(x) = 2x³ - 3x² - 11x + 7. Find the quotient and the remainder when f(x) is divided by (x - 3).
steps: 2x³ - 3x² divided by x gives 2x²; subtract 2x²(x - 3) = 2x³ - 6x² to leave 3x² - 11x + 7.
3x² divided by x gives 3x; subtract 3x(x - 3) = 3x² - 9x to leave -2x + 7.
-2x divided by x gives -2; subtract -2(x - 3) = -2x + 6 to leave 1.
Quotient 2x² + 3x - 2, remainder 1 (check: f(3) = 54 - 27 - 33 + 7 = 1).

items.name: Polynomials and factors
items.question: Express 3x² + 12x - 7 in the form a(x + b)² + c, where a, b and c are constants. Hence write down the minimum value of 3x² + 12x - 7 and the value of x at which it occurs.
steps: Factor out 3 from the x terms: 3(x² + 4x) - 7.
Complete the square: 3[(x + 2)² - 4] - 7 = 3(x + 2)² - 12 - 7 = 3(x + 2)² - 19.
(x + 2)² >= 0 with equality when x = -2, so the minimum value is -19 when x = -2.

items.name: Polynomials and factors

steps: Equate: x² - 3x + 7 = 2x + k, so x² - 5x + (7 - k) = 0.
Two distinct points need two distinct real roots, so b² - 4ac > 0.

items.name: Polynomials and factors
items.question: f(x) = 3x³ - 4x² - 9x + 10. Show that (x - 2) is a factor of f(x).
steps: By the factor theorem, (x - 2) is a factor if f(2) = 0.
So (x - 2) is a factor of f(x).

items.name: Polynomials and factors
items.question: f(x) = 3x³ - 4x² - 9x + 10 and (x - 2) is a factor of f(x). Hence factorise f(x) completely.
steps: Divide by (x - 2): f(x) = (x - 2)(3x² + 2x - 5).
Check the quotient: (x - 2)(3x² + 2x - 5) = 3x³ + 2x² - 5x - 6x² - 4x + 10 = 3x³ - 4x² - 9x + 10.
Factorise the quadratic: 3x² + 2x - 5 = (3x + 5)(x - 1).

items.name: Polynomials and factors

items.question: f(x) = (x - 2)(x - 1)(3x + 5). Hence find the set of values of x for which f(x) > 0.
steps: The roots of f(x) = 0 are x = -5/3, x = 1 and x = 2.
The coefficient of x³ is positive, so f(x) is negative for x < -5/3, positive between -5/3 and 1, negative between 1 and 2, and positive for x > 2.
So f(x) > 0 for -5/3 < x < 1 or x > 2.

steps: Factorise: (2x - 3)(x + 2) >= 0, with critical values x = 3/2 and x = -2.
The graph of y = 2x² + x - 6 is a positive (u-shaped) parabola, so y >= 0 outside the roots: x <= -2 or x >= 3/2.
B is the solution of the opposite inequality (<= 0); C uses the wrong signs for the roots.
D gives only one of the two regions.

items.question: A student claims that n² + n + 11 is a prime number for every positive integer n. Which value of n is a counter-example to the claim? A 5, B 7, C 9, D 10
steps: Test each value: n = 5 gives 41, n = 7 gives 67 and n = 9 gives 101, and all three are prime.
n = 10 gives 100 + 10 + 11 = 121 = 11 x 11, which is not prime.
One counter-example is enough to show the claim is false, so the answer is D.

items.question: Prove that the sum of the squares of any two consecutive odd integers is 2 more than a multiple of 8.
steps: Let the odd integers be 2n + 1 and 2n + 3, where n is an integer.
Sum of squares = (4n² + 4n + 1) + (4n² + 12n + 9) = 8n² + 16n + 10.
8(n + 1)² is a multiple of 8, so the sum is 2 more than a multiple of 8.

items.name: Inequalities and proof
items.question: Prove by contradiction that sqrt(3) is irrational.
items.answer: Assume sqrt(3) = p/q in lowest terms; p and q are then both multiples of 3, a contradiction, so sqrt(3) is irrational
steps: Assumes the opposite: sqrt(3) is rational, so sqrt(3) = p/q where p and q are integers with no common factor
Squares to get p² = 3q², so p² is a multiple of 3, and therefore p is a multiple of 3 (3 is prime); writes p = 3k
Substitutes to get 9k² = 3q², so q² = 3k², so q² and hence q is also a multiple of 3
p and q then have a common factor of 3, which contradicts the assumption, so sqrt(3) is irrational
accept: Uses 'p/q in its lowest terms' or 'p and q are coprime' as the opening assumption
Shows that p² divisible by 3 forces p divisible by 3 by checking p = 3k + 1 and p = 3k + 2 (squares leave remainder 1 on division by 3)
Uses a and b (or m and n) for the integers in place of p and q
Final statement 'this is a contradiction, so the assumption is false and sqrt(3) is irrational', provided the earlier steps are correct

items.question: Prove that, for all real numbers a and b, a² + b² >= 2ab.
items.answer: a² + b² - 2ab = (a - b)² >= 0, so a² + b² >= 2ab
steps: Considers a² + b² - 2ab and writes it as (a - b)² (or starts from (a - b)² and expands it)
States that (a - b)² >= 0 because a and b are real, so a² + b² - 2ab >= 0 and hence a² + b² >= 2ab
accept: Starts with (a - b)² >= 0 for all real a and b, expands to a² - 2ab + b² >= 0 and rearranges
Starts from (a - b)² >= 0 and reasons that the square of a real number cannot be negative
Completes the square on a² - 2ab + b² and states that a square is never negative

items.question: Given that a² + b² >= 2ab for all real a and b, prove that x/y + y/x >= 2 for all positive real numbers x and y.
items.answer: Apply a² + b² >= 2ab with a = x, b = y, then divide by xy > 0
steps: Uses the given result with a = x and b = y to obtain x² + y² >= 2xy
Divides both sides by xy, stating that xy > 0 (x and y are positive) so the inequality is not reversed
Simplifies x²/(xy) + y²/(xy) to x/y + y/x, reaching x/y + y/x >= 2
accept: Applies the given result with a = sqrt(x/y) and b = sqrt(y/x), noting ab = 1, to get x/y + y/x >= 2
Writes x/y + y/x - 2 = (x - y)²/(xy) and states (x - y)² >= 0 and xy > 0, so the expression is non-negative
Multiplies the required inequality by xy (positive) to reach x² + y² >= 2xy, with every step shown to be reversible

items.name: Inequalities and proof
items.question: A student claims that x/y + y/x >= 2 for all non-zero real numbers x and y. Show that the claim is false by giving a counter-example, and state which step of the proof of the result for positive x and y fails for your counter-example.
items.answer: x = 1, y = -1 gives -2, which is less than 2; dividing by xy < 0 reverses the inequality.
steps: Chooses x and y of opposite signs, e.g. x = 1 and y = -1, and finds x/y + y/x = -1 + (-1) = -2
States that -2 < 2 (not >= 2), so the claim is false
Identifies that dividing x² + y² >= 2xy by xy needs xy > 0; here xy < 0, so the inequality sign would reverse
accept: Any other valid pair with xy < 0, e.g. x = 2 and y = -3 gives -13/6, which is less than 2
Identifies the failing step as the division by xy, stating that dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality
States that the proof assumed xy > 0, which is not true when x and y have opposite signs
Notes that when xy < 0 the result becomes x/y + y/x <= -2

items.answer: A: There is strong negative linear correlation between x and y
steps: r is close to -1, so the linear correlation is strong, and the sign is negative: as x increases, y tends to decrease.

items.question: The age, x years, and the selling price, y thousand pounds, of used cars of one model aged between 2 and 9 years are recorded. The regression line of y on x is y = 15.4 - 1.2x. Interpret the value -1.2 in this context, and show by calculation why the equation should not be used to predict the price of a car aged 14 years.
items.answer: The price falls by about 1200 pounds for each extra year of age; the equation gives y = -1.4 at 14 years, a negative price, and 14 is outside the range of the data
steps: On average the price falls by 1.2 thousand pounds (1200 pounds) for each extra year of age.
At x = 14: y = 15.4 - 1.2(14) = -1.4, a negative price, which is impossible.
x = 14 is outside the range of the data (2 to 9 years), so this is extrapolation and the prediction is unreliable.
accept: The gradient is the average rate of depreciation: about 1200 pounds per year.
The equation gives a price of zero at x = 15.4/1.2, about 12.8 years, so any older car gets a negative price.
The relationship may not stay linear outside the range of the data.

items.name: Hypothesis and data
items.question: A manager records x, the number of weeks of training completed, and y, the number of faulty items produced in a day, for 6 employees. The values of x lie between 2 and 10. The data are summarised by n = 6, sum of x = 36, sum of y = 136, sum of x² = 258 and sum of xy = 724. The regression line of y on x is y = 35.8 - 2.19x, based on values of x between 2 and 10. Use the equation to estimate the number of faulty items for an employee with 9 weeks of training, and explain why the equation should not be used for an employee with 20 weeks of training.
items.answer: About 16 faulty items; x = 20 is outside the range of the data and the line gives y = -8, which is impossible
steps: x = 9: y = 35.8 - 2.19(9) = 16.09, so about 16 faulty items.
x = 20 lies outside the range of the data (2 to 10), so this is extrapolation and the estimate is unreliable.
The equation gives y = 35.8 - 2.19(20) = -8, a negative number of faulty items, which is impossible.
accept: 16.1 (not rounded to a whole number) earns the first mark.
The linear relationship may not continue beyond the observed values.
The number of faulty items cannot fall below 0, so the line must level off before long: it reaches 0 at about 16 weeks (35.8/2.19).

items.name: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising…
items.question: Given that $$\mathrm{f(x) = \frac{4x^2-9{2x^2+x-6 - \frac{3{x^2+x-2, \qquad x > \dfrac{3{2,$$ show that $\mathrm{f(x) = \dfrac{2x-3{x-1$. Hence solve the equation $\mathrm{f(x) = 3 - x$.
items.ms: Correct factorisation of at least two of $4x^2-9=(2x-3)(2x+3)$, $2x^2+x-6=(2x-3)(x+2)$ and $x^2+x-2=(x+2)(x-1)$ Combines the two fractions over a common denominator, e.g. $\dfrac{(2x+3)(x-1)-3{(x+2)(x-1)$ $\dfrac{2x^2+x-6{(x+2)(x-1)=\dfrac{(2x-3)(x+2){(x+2)(x-1)=\dfrac{2x-3{x-1$ * Sets $2x-3=(3-x)(x-1)$ and multiplies out to a three-term quadratic $x^2-2x=0$ $x=2$ only, with $x=0$ rejected because $x>\dfrac{3{2$
items.why: P3.1.1 has come up in 14 of 21 sessions; combining two fractions to a given simplified form was asked in Jan 2024 Q4(a) and Oct 2021 Q1, and the domain is the usual place to lose the last mark.

items.name: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising…
items.question: The function $\mathrm{f$ is defined by $$\mathrm{f(x) = \frac{x^2+7x+19{x+2, \qquad x > -2.$$ Express $\mathrm{f(x)$ in the form $Ax+B+\dfrac{C{x+2$, where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are integers to be found. Hence, using calculus, find the coordinates of the minimum point on the curve with equation $y=\mathrm{f(x)$. State the range of $\mathrm{f$.
items.ms: Long division, or compares coefficients in $x^2+7x+19\equiv(Ax+B)(x+2)+C$ Two of $A=1$, $B=5$, $C=9$ $\mathrm{f(x)=x+5+\dfrac{9{x+2$ Differentiates their $Ax+B+C(x+2)-1$ to $A\pm C(x+2)-2$ Sets $1-\dfrac{9{(x+2)^2=0$ and solves to $(x+2)^2=9$, $x+2=3$ $(1,\ 9)$ $\mathrm{f(x)\geqslant 9$
items.why: Division into the form $Ax+B+\dfrac{C}{x+2}$ came up in Oct 2024 Q9(c) and Jan 2026 Q3; using the divided form to find a stationary point and then the range has not been asked yet.

items.name: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising…
items.question: The function $\mathrm{h$ is defined by $$\mathrm{h(x) = \frac{x^3-8{x^2+x-6, \qquad x > 2.$$ Show that $\mathrm{h(x) = \dfrac{x^2+2x+4{x+3$. Hence, or otherwise, express $\mathrm{h(x)$ in the form $Ax+B+\dfrac{C{x+3$, where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are integers. Hence find the exact value of $$\int_3^6 \mathrm{h(x)\,\mathrm{dx,$$ giving your answer in the form $p+q\ln r$, where $p$, $q$ and $r$ are rational numbers.
items.ms: Factorises $x^3-8=(x-2)(x^2+2x+4)$ and $x^2+x-6=(x+3)(x-2)$ Cancels $(x-2)$ to reach $\dfrac{x^2+2x+4{x+3$ * Divides $x^2+2x+4$ by $x+3$, or compares coefficients in $x^2+2x+4\equiv(Ax+B)(x+3)+C$ Two of $A=1$, $B=-1$, $C=7$ $\mathrm{h(x)=x-1+\dfrac{7{x+3$ Integrates $\dfrac{C{x+3$ to $C\ln(x+3)$ $\dfrac{x^2{2-x+7\ln(x+3)$ Substitutes the limits 6 and 3 and subtracts $\dfrac{21{2+7\ln\dfrac{3{2$
items.why: Division followed by an exact ln integral is the commonest P3.1.1 pattern (Oct 2022 Q1, Jan 2026 Q3); factorising a difference of two cubes, as in the spec's $\dfrac{x^3+1}{x^2-1}$ example, has not been asked.

items.name: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising…
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$y = \ln\left(\frac{2x^2+5x-3{x^2+2x-3\right), \qquad x > 1.$$ Show that the equation of $C$ can be written as $y=\ln\left(\dfrac{2x-1{x-1\right)$. Show that $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{-1{(2x-1)(x-1)$. The point $P$ on $C$ has $x$ coordinate 2. Find an equation of the normal to $C$ at $P$, giving your answer in the form $y=mx+c$, where $m$ is an integer and $c$ is an exact constant. By writing $\dfrac{2x-1{x-1$ in the form $A+\dfrac{B{x-1$, where $A$ and $B$ are integers, find the set of possible values of $y$ on $C$.
items.ms: Factorises $2x^2+5x-3=(2x-1)(x+3)$ and $x^2+2x-3=(x+3)(x-1)$ Cancels $(x+3)$ to reach $y=\ln\left(\dfrac{2x-1{x-1\right)$ * Differentiates $\ln(2x-1)-\ln(x-1)$ to $\dfrac{p{2x-1-\dfrac{q{x-1$, or uses the chain rule with the quotient rule on $\ln\left(\dfrac{2x-1{x-1\right)$ $\dfrac{2{2x-1-\dfrac{1{x-1$ or $\dfrac{x-1{2x-1\times\dfrac{2(x-1)-(2x-1){(x-1)^2$ $\dfrac{2(x-1)-(2x-1){(2x-1)(x-1)=\dfrac{-1{(2x-1)(x-1)$ * $y$ coordinate of $P$ is $\ln 3$ Gradient of tangent $-\dfrac{1{3$, so uses gradient of normal $=3$ with $(2,\ \ln 3)$ in a line equation $y=3x-6+\ln 3$ $\dfrac{2x-1{x-1=2+\dfrac{1{x-1$ Since $\dfrac{1{x-1>0$ for $x>1$ (and takes all positive values), $y>\ln 2$
items.why: Simplifying a rational expression is often the first step of a longer P3 question (Jan 2024 Q4, Oct 2021 Q1); simplifying inside a logarithm before differentiating is a likely new setting.

items.question: The functions $\mathrm{f$ and $\mathrm{g$ are defined by $$\mathrm{f(x)=\mathrm{e2x+3, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R$$ $$\mathrm{g(x)=\ln(x-1), \qquad x>1$$ Find $\mathrm{f-1(x)$, stating its domain. Show that $\mathrm{fg(x)=x^2-2x+4$. Hence solve the equation $\mathrm{fg(x)=3x$.
items.ms: Rearranges $y=\mathrm{e2x+3$ to $\mathrm{e2x=y-3$ and takes ln of both sides $\mathrm{f-1(x)=\dfrac{1{2\ln(x-3)$ Domain $x>3$ $\mathrm{fg(x)=\mathrm{e2\ln(x-1)+3$ and uses $\mathrm{e2\ln(x-1)=(x-1)^2$ $(x-1)^2+3=x^2-2x+4$ * Solves $x^2-5x+4=0$, e.g. $(x-1)(x-4)=0$ $x=4$ only, with $x=1$ rejected as it is not in the domain of $\mathrm{g$
items.why: P3.1.2 is hot (19 of 21 sessions); the inverse of an exponential function with its domain and a log-exponential composite were both asked in Jun 2026 (Q2 and Q5), so this is the core type in a new pairing.

items.question: The functions $\mathrm{f$ and $\mathrm{g$ are defined by $$\mathrm{f(x)=2+3\sin x, \qquad -\frac{\pi{2\leqslant x\leqslant\frac{\pi{2$$ $$\mathrm{g(x)=\ln(x+2), \qquad x>-2$$ State the range of $\mathrm{f$. Find $\mathrm{f-1(x)$, stating its domain. Explain why the composite function $\mathrm{fg$ cannot be formed. Find, to 3 significant figures, the value of $x$ for which $\mathrm{gf(x)=1$.
items.ms: $-1\leqslant\mathrm{f(x)\leqslant 5$ Rearranges to $\sin x=\dfrac{y-2{3$ and uses arcsin $\mathrm{f-1(x)=\arcsin\left(\dfrac{x-2{3\right)$ Domain $-1\leqslant x\leqslant 5$ The range of $\mathrm{g$ is all real numbers, which is not contained in the domain of $\mathrm{f$, $-\dfrac{\pi{2\leqslant x\leqslant\dfrac{\pi{2$ (e.g. $\mathrm{g(3)=\ln 5>\dfrac{\pi{2$) $\ln(4+3\sin x)=1\Rightarrow 4+3\sin x=\mathrm{e$ $\sin x=\dfrac{\mathrm{e-4{3$ and uses arcsin (radians) $x=-0.441$
items.why: A function with a restricted trig domain, its arcsin inverse and the existence of a composite are in the P3.1.2 and P3.2.1 spec wording but are not among the recent P3.1.2 questions; gf with ln was asked in Jun 2026 Q2.

items.question: The function $\mathrm{f$ is defined by $$\mathrm{f(x)=\frac{2x+5{x-2, \qquad x>2.$$ State the range of $\mathrm{f$. Show that $\mathrm{ff(x)=x$. Hence write down $\mathrm{f-1(x)$, stating its domain. The function $\mathrm{g$ is defined by $$\mathrm{g(x)=\mathrm{ex+2, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R.$$ Find the exact solution of the equation $\mathrm{fg(x)=5$.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f(x)>2$ $\mathrm{ff(x)=\dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{2x+5{x-2\right)+5{\dfrac{2x+5{x-2-2$ Multiplies numerator and denominator by $(x-2)$: $\dfrac{2(2x+5)+5(x-2){(2x+5)-2(x-2)$ $=\dfrac{9x{9=x$ * $\mathrm{f-1(x)=\dfrac{2x+5{x-2$ Domain $x>2$ $\mathrm{fg(x)=\dfrac{2(\mathrm{e^x+2)+5{\mathrm{e^x+2-2=\dfrac{2\mathrm{e^x+9{\mathrm{e^x$ $2\mathrm{e^x+9=5\mathrm{e^x\Rightarrow\mathrm{e^x=3$ $x=\ln 3$
items.why: Range, inverse and composite of a rational function were asked in Jan 2026 Q2 and Jun 2026 Q5; a self-inverse function (ff(x) = x) is not among the recent questions and is a likely twist.

items.question: The function $\mathrm{f$ is defined by $$\mathrm{f(x)=a+b\mathrm{e-2x, \qquad x\geqslant 0,$$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants and $b>0$. The range of $\mathrm{f$ is $-3<\mathrm{f(x)\leqslant 5$. Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$. Find $\mathrm{f-1(x)$, stating its domain. The function $\mathrm{g$ is defined by $$\mathrm{g(x)=\ln(x+4), \qquad x\geqslant -3.$$ Show that $\mathrm{fg(x)=\dfrac{8{(x+4)^2-3$. Hence solve the equation $\mathrm{fg(x)=-1$.
items.ms: $a=-3$ (since $\mathrm{e-2x\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$) $b=8$ (from $\mathrm{f(0)=a+b=5$) Rearranges to $\mathrm{e-2x=\dfrac{y+3{8$ and takes ln of both sides $\mathrm{f-1(x)=-\dfrac{1{2\ln\left(\dfrac{x+3{8\right)$ Domain $-3<x\leqslant 5$ $\mathrm{fg(x)=-3+8\mathrm{e-2\ln(x+4)$ Uses $\mathrm{e-2\ln(x+4)=(x+4)-2$ to reach $\dfrac{8{(x+4)^2-3$ * $\dfrac{8{(x+4)^2=2\Rightarrow(x+4)^2=4$ $x=-2$ only, with $x=-6$ rejected as $x\geqslant -3$
items.why: Inverses of exponential functions recur (Jun 2026 Q5(b)); working back from a stated range to the constants of the function has not been asked recently and tests the link between the range and the asymptote.

items.question: The function $\mathrm{f$ is defined by $$\mathrm{f(x)=x^2-6x+13, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R.$$ Explain why $\mathrm{f-1$ does not exist. The function $\mathrm{g$ is defined by $$\mathrm{g(x)=x^2-6x+13, \qquad x\geqslant 3.$$ Find the range of $\mathrm{g$. Find $\mathrm{g-1(x)$, stating its domain. On the same axes, sketch the graphs of $y=\mathrm{g(x)$ and $y=\mathrm{g-1(x)$, showing the coordinates of the end point of each graph. Using algebra, prove that the graphs of $y=\mathrm{g(x)$ and $y=\mathrm{g-1(x)$ do not meet.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f$ is many-to-one (not one-to-one), e.g. $\mathrm{f(1)=\mathrm{f(5)=8$ Completes the square: $(x-3)^2+4$, or finds the minimum value $\mathrm{g(3)=4$ $\mathrm{g(x)\geqslant 4$ Rearranges $y=(x-3)^2+4$ to $x=3\pm\sqrt{y-4$ $\mathrm{g-1(x)=3+\sqrt{x-4$ (positive root only) Domain $x\geqslant 4$ $y=\mathrm{g(x)$: increasing curve, getting steeper, starting at $(3,\ 4)$ $y=\mathrm{g-1(x)$: increasing curve, getting less steep, starting at $(4,\ 3)$ The two graphs are reflections of each other in the line $y=x$ (drawn or implied) As $\mathrm{g$ is increasing, any intersection lies on $y=x$: sets $x^2-6x+13=x$ to obtain $x^2-7x+13=0$ Discriminant $49-52=-3<0$, so there are no real roots and the graphs do not meet
items.why: The graphs of a function and its inverse (spec wording 'inverse functions and their graphs') and restricting a domain so that an inverse exists are not among the recent P3.1.2 questions; the 'no real solutions' proof matches Jan 2026 Q2(d).

items.question: The functions $\mathrm{f$ and $\mathrm{g$ are defined by $$\mathrm{f(x)=\mathrm{ex-2, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R$$ $$\mathrm{g(x)=\frac{3{x+1, \qquad x>-1$$ State the range of $\mathrm{f$. Find $\mathrm{f-1(x)$, stating its domain. Find the exact value of $x$ for which $\mathrm{fg(x)=1$. Find $\mathrm{gf(x)$, and explain why $\mathrm{gf(x)$ is defined only for $x>0$. The equation $\mathrm{gf(x)=x$, $x>0$, has a single root $\alpha$. Show that $\alpha$ is a root of the equation $$x=\ln\left(1+\frac{3{x\right).$$ Using the iteration formula $$xn+1=\ln\left(1+\frac{3{x_n\right)$$ with $x_1=1.5$, find the values of $x_2$, $x_3$ and $x_4$, giving your answers to 4 decimal places.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f(x)>-2$ Rearranges to $\mathrm{ex=y+2$ and takes ln $\mathrm{f-1(x)=\ln(x+2)$ Domain $x>-2$ $\mathrm{fg(x)=\mathrm{e\frac{3{x+1-2$, set equal to 1 $\dfrac{3{x+1=\ln 3$ $x=\dfrac{3{\ln 3-1$ $\mathrm{gf(x)=\dfrac{3{\mathrm{ex-1$ The input to $\mathrm{g$ must be greater than $-1$, so $\mathrm{e^x-2>-1$, i.e. $\mathrm{e^x>1$, so $x>0$ $\dfrac{3{\mathrm{e^x-1=x\Rightarrow\mathrm{e^x-1=\dfrac{3{x$ $\mathrm{e^x=1+\dfrac{3{x\Rightarrow x=\ln\left(1+\dfrac{3{x\right)$ * Attempts the iteration: $x_2=\ln 3$ $x_2=1.0986$ $x_3=1.3166$ and $x_4=1.1874$
items.why: The long functions question (Oct 2024 Q9, 14 marks) mixes inverse, composite and another topic; the largest domain on which a composite exists, and an iteration built from a composite, are not among the recent P3.1.2 questions.

items.question: Sketch the graph with equation $y=|3x-4|$, stating the coordinates of the points where the graph meets the coordinate axes. Solve the equation $|3x-4|=x+2$. Hence, or otherwise, find the set of values of $x$ for which $|3x-4|>x+2$.
items.ms: V shape with its vertex on the positive $x$-axis $\left(\dfrac{4{3,\ 0\right)$ and $(0,\ 4)$ Solves $3x-4=x+2$ or $-(3x-4)=x+2$ $x=3$ and $x=\dfrac{1{2$ Chooses the outside region for their two critical values $x<\dfrac{1{2$ or $x>3$
items.why: P3.1.3 has come up in 19 of 21 sessions; the spec's own example is to sketch y = |2x - 1| and use it to solve the matching equation and inequality, and the inequality is not among the recent modulus questions.

items.question: The diagram shows a sketch of the curve with equation $y=\mathrm{f(x)$, $x\in\mathbb{R$. The curve crosses the $x$-axis at $(-5,\ 0)$, at the origin $O$ and at $(6,\ 0)$. It has a maximum point at $A(-2,\ 4)$ and a minimum point at $B(3,\ -5)$. As $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, $y\to-\infty$. Sketch the curve with equation $y=|\mathrm{f(x)|$, showing the coordinates of the turning points and of any points where the curve meets the coordinate axes. Sketch the curve with equation $y=\mathrm{f(|x|)$, showing the coordinates of the turning points and of any points where the curve meets the coordinate axes. Find the set of values of $k$ for which the equation $|\mathrm{f(x)|=k$ has exactly four solutions.
items.ms: Shape: the parts of the curve below the $x$-axis reflected in the $x$-axis, with cusps on the $x$-axis and both ends going upwards $(-5,\ 0)$, $(0,\ 0)$ and $(6,\ 0)$ Maximum points $(-2,\ 4)$ and $(3,\ 5)$ Shape: the part of $y=\mathrm{f(x)$ for $x\geqslant 0$ together with its reflection in the $y$-axis (a W shape with a cusp at $O$) $(-6,\ 0)$, $(0,\ 0)$, $(6,\ 0)$ and minimum points $(-3,\ -5)$, $(3,\ -5)$ Uses 4 and 5, the heights of the two maximum points of $y=|\mathrm{f(x)|$, as critical values $4<k<5$
items.why: The spec names y = |f(x)| and y = f(|x|) for a given graph of y = f(x); the recent P3 modulus questions have all used linear moduli, so these sketches are due.

Solve the equation $|4-\mathrm{e2x|=2$, giving your answers as exact values. Find the set of values of $k$ for which the equation $|4-\mathrm{e2x|=k$ has exactly two solutions.

items.name: The modulus function
items.question: Sketch the graph with equation $y=|x^2-6x+5|$, showing the coordinates of the turning point and of any points where the graph meets the coordinate axes. Solve the equation $|x^2-6x+5|=3$, giving your answers in exact form. Hence find the set of values of $x$ for which $|x^2-6x+5|<3$.
items.ms: Shape: U-shaped parabola with the part between $x=1$ and $x=5$ reflected above the $x$-axis (cusps at $x=1$ and $x=5$) $(1,\ 0)$, $(5,\ 0)$ and $(0,\ 5)$ Maximum point $(3,\ 4)$ Solves $x^2-6x+5=3$, i.e. $x^2-6x+2=0$, by formula or completing the square $x=3\pm\sqrt{7$ Solves $x^2-6x+5=-3$, i.e. $x^2-6x+8=0$ $x=2$ and $x=4$ Uses their four critical values to choose two separate inside regions $3-\sqrt{7<x<2$ or $4<x<3+\sqrt{7$
items.why: The spec asks for y = |f(x)| for a given f and for modulus equations and inequalities; the modulus of a quadratic with four exact roots extends the linear cases of Jan 2026 Q7 and Q8.

items.question: The function $\mathrm{g$ is defined by $$\mathrm{g(x)=|2x-5|+1, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R.$$ The diagram shows a sketch of the graph of $y=\mathrm{g(x)$. The graph has a vertex at $V$. State the coordinates of $V$. Solve the equation $\mathrm{g(x)=2x$. Given that the equation $\mathrm{g(x)=mx$, where $m$ is a constant, has exactly two solutions, find the set of possible values of $m$. State the coordinates of the vertex of the graph with equation $y=4\mathrm{g(x-2)-7$.
items.ms: $\left(\dfrac{5{2,\ 1\right)$ Attempts $-(2x-5)+1=2x$, i.e. $6-2x=2x$ $x=\dfrac{3{2$ Shows $2x-5+1=2x$ has no solution (or the line $y=2x$ is parallel to the branch $y=2x-4$), so $x=\dfrac{3{2$ only Gradient of the line from $O$ to $V$: $\dfrac{1{5/2=\dfrac{2{5$ Upper limit 2: the line must be less steep than the right-hand branch, gradient 2 $\dfrac{2{5<m<2$ $x=\dfrac{9{2$ $y=-3$
items.why: The vertex, a modulus equation and a line through the origin meeting the graph is the core recurring set-up (Jan 2026 Q7, Jun 2026 Q9); asking for exactly two meeting points, with the transformed vertex of Jan 2026 Q7(d), is the variation.

items.question: In this question $a$ is a positive constant. On the same axes, sketch the graphs with equations $y=|2x-3a|$ and $y=|x|+a$, showing, in terms of $a$, the coordinates of the points where each graph meets the coordinate axes. Find, in terms of $a$, the values of $x$ for which $|2x-3a|=|x|+a$. Hence find, in terms of $a$, the set of values of $x$ for which $|2x-3a|<|x|+a$. The two graphs enclose a region $R$. Given that the area of $R$ is 150, find the value of $a$.
items.ms: $y=|2x-3a|$: V shape with vertex $\left(\dfrac{3a{2,\ 0\right)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,\ 3a)$ $y=|x|+a$: V shape symmetrical about the $y$-axis with vertex $(0,\ a)$, below $(0,\ 3a)$ Attempts to solve $3a-2x=x+a$ or $2x-3a=x+a$ $x=\dfrac{2a{3$ $x=4a$ Chooses the region between their two critical values $\dfrac{2a{3<x<4a$ Uses the vertices $\left(\dfrac{2a{3,\ \dfrac{5a{3\right)$, $\left(\dfrac{3a{2,\ 0\right)$ and $(4a,\ 5a)$ in a correct method for the area of the triangle Area $=\dfrac{25a^2{6$ $\dfrac{25a^2{6=150\Rightarrow a=6$
items.why: Two modulus graphs in terms of a constant came up in Jan 2026 Q8 and Jun 2026 Q9 (with a triangle area); the matching inequality has not been asked in recent papers.

items.question: The function $\mathrm{f$ is defined by $$\mathrm{f(x) = \mathrm{e2x - 8\mathrm{ex + 6x, \quad x \in \mathbb{R$$ In this question you must show all stages of your working. items.question: The diagram shows a sketch of part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = \frac{3\ln x{x + 2, \quad x > 0$$ The point $P$ is the maximum turning point of $C$. Show that the $x$ coordinate of $P$ is a solution of the equation $$x = \mathrm{e1 + \frac{2{x$$ Using the iteration formula $$xn+1 = \mathrm{e1 + \frac{2{x_n$$ with $x_1 = 4$, find, to 4 decimal places, the value of $x_2$ and the value of $x_3$. items.question: Oil leaking from a damaged ship forms a circular slick on the surface of the sea. Show that $$\frac{\mathrm{dA{\mathrm{dt = 800\pi\left(\mathrm{e-0.25t - \mathrm{e-0.5t\right)$$ Hence find, according to the model, the exact time at which the area of the slick is increasing most rapidly.

items.ms: Uses the chain rule: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dy = \dfrac{\sec^2 y{\tan y$ Writes in terms of $\sin y$ and $\cos y$: $\dfrac{1{\cos^2 y \times \dfrac{\cos y{\sin y = \dfrac{1{\sin y\cos y$ $= \dfrac{2{2\sin y\cos y = \dfrac{2{\sin 2y = 2\operatorname{cosec 2y$ * $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{1{2\operatorname{cosec 2y = \dfrac{1{2\sin 2y$ $\tan y = \mathrm{ex$ Expresses $\sin 2y$ in terms of $\tan y$, e.g. $\sin 2y = 2\tan y\cos^2 y = \dfrac{2\tan y{\sec^2 y = \dfrac{2\tan y{1 + \tan^2 y$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{\tan y{1 + \tan^2 y = \dfrac{\mathrm{ex{1 + \mathrm{e2x$ * $x = \ln\left(\tan\frac{\pi{6\right) = \ln\frac{1{\sqrt{3 = -\frac{1{2\ln 3$ Gradient of $C$ at $P$: $\frac{1{2\sin\frac{\pi{3 = \frac{\sqrt{3{4$ (or from $\mathrm{ex = \frac{1{\sqrt{3$ in (b)) Normal: $y - \frac{\pi{6 = -\frac{4{\sqrt{3\left(x + \frac{1{2\ln 3\right)$, using $-1 \div$ their gradient $y = -\dfrac{4\sqrt{3{3x + \dfrac{\pi{6 - \dfrac{2\sqrt{3{3\ln 3$ $\frac{1{2\sin 2y$ is greatest when $2y = \frac{\pi{2$ (or $1 + \mathrm{e2x - 2\mathrm{ex = (\mathrm{ex - 1)^2 \geqslant 0$, or differentiates), giving $y = \frac{\pi{4$ and $x = 0$ $\left(0,\ \frac{\pi{4\right)$ with greatest gradient $\frac{1{2$
items.why: Long P3 questions build $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ from $x = \mathrm{f}(y)$ with trig identities (Jun 2026 Q6, Jan 2026 Q8, Jan 2025 Q10); $x = \ln(\tan y)$ links the chain rule, the double angle formula and a normal in one question.

items.name: Understand and use exponential growth and decay
path: P3.4.4 - and use exponential growth a
items.question: The number of active users of a new mobile phone app, $N$ thousand, $t$ months after the app is launched, is modelled by the equation $$N = 12 \times 1.25t, \quad t \geqslant 0$$ State the number of active users at the launch of the app, according to the model. Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dN{\mathrm{dt$. Find, according to the model, the rate at which the number of active users is increasing 6 months after the launch. Give your answer in users per month to 3 significant figures. Give one reason why this model may not be suitable for predicting the number of active users for large values of $t$.
items.ms: 12 000 users Uses $\dfrac{\mathrm{d{\mathrm{dt\left(1.25t\right) = 1.25t\ln 1.25$, or writes $1.25t = \mathrm{et\ln 1.25$ and differentiates $\dfrac{\mathrm{dN{\mathrm{dt = 12 \times 1.25t\ln 1.25$ Substitutes $t = 6$ into their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dN{\mathrm{dt$ 10200 users per month The model predicts that $N$ increases without limit, but the number of possible users is limited (e.g. by the population or by competition from other apps)
items.why: Exponential growth models are in 15 of 21 sessions; the spec expects $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(a^{x}) = a^{x}\ln a$, which past papers have rarely tested directly.

items.name: Understand and use exponential growth and decay
path: P3.4.4 - and use exponential growth a
items.question: A metal casting is taken out of a furnace and left to cool in a workshop. The temperature of the casting, $\theta$ °C, $t$ minutes after it is taken out of the furnace, is modelled by the equation $$\theta = 22 + A\mathrm{e-kt$$ where $A$ and $k$ are positive constants. The temperature of the casting is $380$ °C when it is taken out of the furnace and $150$ °C fifteen minutes later. Find the value of $A$. Show that $k = 0.0686$ to 3 significant figures. Find the rate at which the temperature of the casting is decreasing at the instant when its temperature is $100$ °C.
items.ms: $A = 358$ $150 = 22 + 358\mathrm{e-15k \Rightarrow \mathrm{e-15k = \dfrac{128{358$ Takes logs correctly: $-15k = \ln\dfrac{128{358$ $k = \dfrac{1{15\ln\dfrac{179{64 = 0.068567\ldots = 0.0686$ * $\dfrac{\mathrm{d\theta{\mathrm{dt = -358k\mathrm{e-kt$ Uses $358\mathrm{e-kt = 100 - 22 = 78$ (or finds $t = 22.2$ and substitutes) Decreasing at 5.35 °C per minute
items.why: Cooling models recur (Jun 2026 Q9, Jun 2025 Q6, Jan 2024 Q5); finding the rate from a given temperature rather than a given time is a likely variation.

items.question: A herd of deer is introduced into a nature reserve. The number of deer, $P$, $t$ years after the herd is introduced is modelled by the equation $$P = \frac{1500{1 + 14\mathrm{e-0.3t, \quad t \geqslant 0$$ Find the number of deer in the herd when it was introduced. State the upper limit to the number of deer predicted by this model. Show that $$\frac{\mathrm{dP{\mathrm{dt = 0.3P\left(1 - \frac{P{1500\right)$$ Find the two values of $t$ at which, according to the model, the number of deer is increasing at a rate of 72 deer per year. Give your answers to 1 decimal place. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.
items.ms: $P = \dfrac{1500{1 + 14 = 100$ 1500 (as $t \to \infty$, $\mathrm{e-0.3t \to 0$) Uses the chain rule (or quotient rule) to obtain $\dfrac{\mathrm{dP{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{k\mathrm{e-0.3t{\left(1 + 14\mathrm{e-0.3t\right)^2$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{dP{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{6300\mathrm{e-0.3t{\left(1 + 14\mathrm{e-0.3t\right)^2$ Eliminates $t$ using $1 + 14\mathrm{e-0.3t = \dfrac{1500{P$ and $14\mathrm{e-0.3t = \dfrac{1500{P - 1$ (or expands the right-hand side in terms of $t$) $\dfrac{\mathrm{dP{\mathrm{dt = 450\left(\dfrac{1500{P - 1\right)\dfrac{P^2{1500^2 = 0.3P\left(1 - \dfrac{P{1500\right)$ * Sets $0.3P\left(1 - \dfrac{P{1500\right) = 72$ and solves $P^2 - 1500P + 360\,000 = 0$ to give $P = 300$ and $P = 1200$ Solves $\dfrac{1500{1 + 14\mathrm{e-0.3t = 300$ or $1200$ for $t$ using logs, e.g. $\mathrm{e-0.3t = \frac{2{7$ or $\mathrm{e-0.3t = \frac{1{56$ $t = 4.2$ and $t = 13.4$
items.why: Models with a long-term limit and a rate condition recur (Oct 2025 Q7 bees, Jun 2026 Q8 algae); a logistic model whose rate is written in terms of $P$ has not yet been asked.
