items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = \dfrac{x^3{4 - \dfrac{16{x + 10, \quad x > 0$$ The point $P(2, 4)$ lies on $C$. The line $l$ is the normal to $C$ at $P$. Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$. Find an equation of $l$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
items.ms: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{3{4x^2 + 16x-2$ Substitutes $x = 2$ into their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$: $3 + 4 = 7$ Normal gradient $= -\dfrac{1{7$, the negative reciprocal of their tangent gradient Uses $y - 4 = -\dfrac{1{7(x - 2)$ with their normal gradient $x + 7y - 30 = 0$
items.why: A normal at a given point was asked in Jun 2026 Q6, Jan 2026 Q7 (as ax + by + c = 0) and Oct 2025 Q9, so one is near-certain.

items.name: Tangents, normals and gradients
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 4$$ The line $l$ has equation $8x - 2y + 7 = 0$. The points $A$ and $B$ lie on $C$, and the tangents to $C$ at $A$ and at $B$ are both parallel to $l$. The point $A$ has a positive $x$ coordinate. The diagram shows part of $C$ and the tangents at $A$ and $B$. Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$. Find the $x$ coordinate of $A$ and the $x$ coordinate of $B$. The tangent to $C$ at $A$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$, and the tangent to $C$ at $B$ meets the $y$-axis at $Q$. Find the length $PQ$.
items.ms: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 3x^2 - 6x - 5$ Gradient of $l$ is 4 (from $y = 4x + \dfrac{7{2$); sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 4$ and solves the 3TQ $3x^2 - 6x - 9 = 0$ $x = 3$ at $A$ and $x = -1$ at $B$ Finds the $y$ coordinate of $A$ or $B$: $A(3, -11)$, $B(-1, 5)$ Uses $y - y_1 = 4(x - x_1)$ to find at least one $y$-intercept: $y = 4x - 23$ or $y = 4x + 9$ $PQ = 9 - (-23) = 32$
items.why: P1.4.3 is hot (21 of 23 sessions, 11.5% of marks); reading the gradient from a line given as ax + by + c = 0 links it to P1.2.1, and the distance between the intercepts of two parallel tangents is a fresh finish.

items.name: Tangents, normals and gradients
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$, $x > 0$, where $$\mathrm{f'(x) = \dfrac{5x^2 - k{2\sqrt{x$$ and $k$ is a constant. The point $P$ on $C$ has $x$ coordinate 4. The tangent to $C$ at $P$ has equation $y = 18x - 52$. The diagram shows part of $C$ and the tangent at $P$. Show that $k = 8$. Find $\mathrm{f(x)$, giving each term in its simplest form. Find an equation of the normal to $C$ at $P$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
items.ms: Sets $\mathrm{f'(4) = 18$: $\dfrac{5(16) - k{2 \times 2 = 18$ $80 - k = 72 \Rightarrow k = 8$ Writes $\mathrm{f'(x) = \dfrac{5{2x\frac{3{2 - 4x-\frac{1{2$ $x^n \to xn+1$ for at least one term $x\frac{5{2 - 8x\frac{1{2$ ($+\,c$) Finds $y = 18(4) - 52 = 20$ at $P$ and substitutes $x = 4$, $y = 20$ into their $\mathrm{f(x)$ to find $c$ $\mathrm{f(x) = x\frac{5{2 - 8\sqrt{x + 4$ Uses gradient $-\dfrac{1{18$ with the point $(4, 20)$: $y - 20 = -\dfrac{1{18(x - 4)$ $x + 18y - 364 = 0$
items.why: Given f'(x) with an unknown k, using a tangent or normal to find k and then working with the curve is the pattern of Jun 2026 Q7, Jun 2026 Q8 and Oct 2025 Q8–Q9; integrating to find f(x) adds the P1.5.2 link.

items.name: Tangents, normals and gradients
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$y = x\frac{3{2 - x + 4, \quad x \geq 0$$ The point $P$ on $C$ has $x$ coordinate $p$, where $p > 0$. Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$. Show that an equation of the tangent to $C$ at $P$ is $$y = \left(\dfrac{3{2p\frac{1{2 - 1\right)x - \dfrac{1{2p\frac{3{2 + 4$$ Given that the tangent to $C$ at $P$ passes through the origin $O$, find the value of $p$ and an equation of this tangent. The diagram shows part of $C$ and the tangent found in part (c). Using the substitution $u = \sqrt{x$, or otherwise, show that this tangent meets $C$ only at $P$. You may use without proof that $u^3 - 3u^2 + 4 = (u - 2)^2(u + 1)$.
items.ms: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{3{2x\frac{1{2 - 1$ Gradient at $P$ is $\dfrac{3{2p\frac{1{2 - 1$ and the $y$ coordinate of $P$ is $p\frac{3{2 - p + 4$ Uses $y - (p\frac{3{2 - p + 4) = \left(\dfrac{3{2p\frac{1{2 - 1\right)(x - p)$ Expands and simplifies to the given equation with no errors Sets $-\dfrac{1{2p\frac{3{2 + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow p\frac{3{2 = 8$ $p = 4$ and $y = 2x$ Sets $x\frac{3{2 - x + 4 = 2x$ and writes it as $u^3 - 3u^2 + 4 = 0$ where $u = \sqrt{x$ $(u - 2)^2(u + 1) = 0$; $u = \sqrt{x \geq 0$ so $u \neq -1$; only $u = 2$, so $x = 4$, which is $P$
items.why: A tangent through a given external point (here the origin) is not among recent P1.4.3 questions but needs only the tangent at a general point; showing that the line touches C only once links to P1.1.11.

items.name: Tangents, normals and gradients
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = \dfrac{x^2{2 + \dfrac{32{x - 6, \quad x > 0$$ The point $P(4, 10)$ lies on $C$. The tangent to $C$ at $P$ meets the $y$-axis at $A$, and the normal to $C$ at $P$ meets the $y$-axis at $B$. Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$. Show that an equation of the tangent to $C$ at $P$ is $y = 2x + 2$. Find an equation of the normal to $C$ at $P$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers. Find the area of triangle $APB$, shown shaded in the diagram.
items.ms: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = x - 32x-2$ Substitutes $x = 4$ into their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$: $4 - \dfrac{32{16 = 2$ Uses $y - 10 = 2(x - 4)$ $y = 2x + 2$ with no errors Normal gradient $= -\dfrac{1{2$ Uses $y - 10 = -\dfrac{1{2(x - 4)$ $x + 2y - 24 = 0$ Finds $A(0, 2)$ and $B(0, 12)$ and uses $\dfrac{1{2 \times AB \times 4$ (the $x$ coordinate of $P$) Area $= 20$
items.why: A tangent and a normal at the same point is the most common P1.4.3 pairing (Jan 2026 Q8, Oct 2025 Q8); a triangle with an axis adds the usual coordinate-geometry finish (P1.2.1).

items.name: Tangents, normals and gradients
items.question: The diagram shows a sketch of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = 6\sqrt{x - x, \quad x \geq 0$$ The curve meets the $x$-axis at the origin $O$ and at the point $A$. The tangent to $C$ at the point $B$ is perpendicular to the tangent to $C$ at $A$. The tangents at $A$ and $B$ meet at the point $R$. Find the coordinates of $A$. Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$. Find an equation of the tangent to $C$ at $A$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers. Find the coordinates of $B$. Find the coordinates of $R$.
items.ms: Sets $6\sqrt{x - x = 0$ and factorises or rearranges, e.g. $\sqrt{x(6 - \sqrt{x) = 0$ or $\sqrt{x = 6$ $A(36, 0)$ $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 3x-\frac{1{2 - 1$ Substitutes $x = 36$ into their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$: $\dfrac{3{6 - 1 = -\dfrac{1{2$ Uses $y - 0 = -\dfrac{1{2(x - 36)$ with their gradient and their $A$ $x + 2y - 36 = 0$ Gradient of the tangent at $B$ is 2, the negative reciprocal of their $-\dfrac{1{2$ Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 2$ and solves: $\dfrac{3{\sqrt{x = 3 \Rightarrow x = 1$ $B(1, 5)$ Tangent at $B$: $y - 5 = 2(x - 1)$, i.e. $y = 2x + 3$ Solves simultaneously with their tangent at $A$: $x + 2(2x + 3) - 36 = 0$ $R(6, 15)$
items.why: Long P1 questions (Oct 2022 had two 14-mark ones) chain tangents with coordinate geometry; perpendicular tangents, found by solving dy/dx = −1/m, are not among recent P1.4.3 questions and are the fresh angle.

items.name: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: The diagram shows triangle $ABC$ with $AB = 3k$ cm, $BC = 7k$ cm and $AC = 8k$ cm, where $k$ is a positive constant. Show that angle $BAC = \dfrac{\pi{3$ radians. Given that the area of triangle $ABC$ is $24\sqrt{3$ cm², find the value of $k$.
items.ms: $\cos BAC = \dfrac{(3k)^2 + (8k)^2 - (7k)^2{2\times 3k\times 8k$ $\cos BAC = \dfrac{24k^2{48k^2 = \dfrac{1{2$, so angle $BAC = \dfrac{\pi{3$ cso $\dfrac{1{2\times 3k\times 8k\times\sin\dfrac{\pi{3 = 24\sqrt{3$, i.e. $6\sqrt{3\,k^2 = 24\sqrt{3$ $k = 2$ only
items.why: Oct 2025 asked for an angle of a triangle with sides in a given ratio; working back from a given area to the scale factor is the reverse step not yet asked.

items.name: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: The diagram shows triangle $PQR$ with $PQ = 4$ cm, $PR = 6$ cm and angle $QPR = heta$ radians, where $ heta$ is obtuse. The area of triangle $PQR$ is 10 cm². Find the value of $\theta$, giving your answer to 3 decimal places. Find the length of $QR$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: $\dfrac{1{2\times 4\times 6\sin\theta = 10 \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{5{6$ $\theta = \pi - 0.9851\ldots = 2.156$ (awrt), as $\theta$ is obtuse $QR^2 = 4^2 + 6^2 - 2\times 4\times 6\cos\theta$ with their obtuse $\theta$ $QR^2 = 78.5\ldots$ (awrt 78.5; exactly $52 + 8\sqrt{11$) $QR = 8.86$ cm (awrt)
items.why: Jun 2026 asked for sin θ from a given area and then a side for the obtuse angle; this is the same core type with a new triangle, in radians, answered with a calculator.

items.name: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: The diagram shows triangle $ABC$ with $AB = (x + 2)$ cm, $AC = (x + 3)$ cm, $BC = (2x + 3)$ cm and angle $BAC = \dfrac{2\pi{3$ radians. Show that $x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0$ Hence find the value of $x$, giving a reason for rejecting any other value. Find the exact area of triangle $ABC$.
items.ms: Uses the cosine rule: $(2x + 3)^2 = (x + 2)^2 + (x + 3)^2 - 2(x + 2)(x + 3)\cos\dfrac{2\pi{3$ Uses $\cos\dfrac{2\pi{3 = -\dfrac{1{2$ and expands all brackets, e.g. $4x^2 + 12x + 9 = 3x^2 + 15x + 19$ $x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0$ cso Solves $x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0$, e.g. $(x - 5)(x + 2) = 0$ $x = 5$ only, since $x = -2$ gives $AB = 0$ (a side must have positive length) $\dfrac{1{2\times 7\times 8\times\sin\dfrac{2\pi{3$ (with their $x$) $14\sqrt{3$ cm²
items.why: Cosine-rule questions recur in almost every session; algebraic side lengths turn it into a quadratic, the kind of link with P1.1.5 that long P1 questions use.

items.name: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: In triangle $ABC$, $AC = 10$ cm, $AB = 5\sqrt{2$ cm and angle $ACB = 30^\circ$. The diagram shows the two possible positions, $B_1$ and $B_2$, of the point $B$. Use the sine rule to find the two possible sizes of angle $ABC$. Given that $BC = x$ cm, use the cosine rule to show that $$x^2 - 10\sqrt{3\,x + 50 = 0$$ Hence find the exact length of $BC$ when angle $ABC$ is obtuse. Give your answer in the form $p\sqrt{3 + q$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers.
items.ms: $\dfrac{\sin ABC{10 = \dfrac{\sin 30^\circ{5\sqrt{2$ $\sin ABC = \dfrac{1{\sqrt{2$ or $\dfrac{\sqrt{2{2$ Angle $ABC = 45^\circ$ and $135^\circ$ $(5\sqrt{2)^2 = 10^2 + x^2 - 2\times 10\times x\cos 30^\circ$ Uses $\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2$ and $(5\sqrt{2)^2 = 50$ to reach $x^2 - 10\sqrt{3\,x + 50 = 0$ cso Solves the quadratic, e.g. $x = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3 \pm \sqrt{300 - 200{2$ or $(x - 5\sqrt{3)^2 = 25$ $x = 5\sqrt{3 \pm 5$ $BC = 5\sqrt{3 - 5$ cm with a reason, e.g. when angle $ABC = 135^\circ$, angle $BAC = 15^\circ$ is the smallest angle so $BC$ is the shortest side, or $B_1$ is the position nearer to $C$
items.why: The ambiguous case was asked in Jun 2026 (both angles, then a side); finding the side from a quadratic given by the cosine rule, with surds, is the likely fresh twist.

items.name: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a
items.question: A yacht race is sailed around a triangular course. The yachts sail from buoy $P$ to buoy $Q$, a distance of 8 km on a bearing of 060°. They then sail from $Q$ to buoy $R$, a distance of 5 km on a bearing of 180°, and finally return directly from $R$ to $P$. The diagram shows the course. The buoys are modelled as points on a horizontal plane. Show that angle $PQR = 60^\circ$ Find the distance $PR$. Find the exact area of the region enclosed by the course. A safety boat waits at the point $B$ on $PR$ that is closest to $Q$. Using your answers to parts (b) and (c), find the distance $QB$, giving your answer in km to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: Uses the parallel north lines at $P$ and $Q$: the angle between $QP$ and due south at $Q$ is $60^\circ$ (alternate angles), or the bearing of $P$ from $Q$ is $060^\circ + 180^\circ = 240^\circ$ Angle $PQR = 60^\circ$ (e.g. $240^\circ - 180^\circ$) cso Uses the cosine rule: $PR^2 = 8^2 + 5^2 - 2\times 8\times 5\cos 60^\circ$ $PR^2 = 89 - 40 = 49$ $PR = 7$ km cao Uses $\dfrac{1{2\times 8\times 5\sin 60^\circ$ $10\sqrt{3$ km² Uses area of triangle $PQR = \dfrac{1{2\times PR\times QB$ with their $PR$ and their area $QB = \dfrac{2\times 10\sqrt{3{7$ $QB = \dfrac{20\sqrt{3{7 = 4.95$ km (awrt)
items.why: P1.3.1 has come up in 21 of 23 sessions with the cosine rule then the area as its core; a bearings course and a perpendicular distance found from the area are not among the recent questions.

items.name: Radians, arc length, sector area
items.question: The minute hand of a clock is 6 cm long. The diagram shows the clock face, centre $O$, with the minute hand in two positions 20 minutes apart. Show that the minute hand turns through an angle of $\dfrac{2\pi{3$ radians in 20 minutes. Find the exact area swept out by the minute hand in 20 minutes. Find the time taken for the tip of the minute hand to travel a distance of $5\pi$ cm.
items.ms: $\dfrac{20{60\times 2\pi = \dfrac{2\pi{3$ $\dfrac{1{2\times 6^2\times\dfrac{2\pi{3$ $12\pi$ cm² $6\theta = 5\pi \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{5\pi{6$ $\dfrac{5\pi{6\div 2\pi\times 60 = 25$ minutes
items.why: Radian measure with s = rθ and A = ½r²θ underlies every P1.3.2 question; turning a time into an angle, and an arc length back into a time, is a simple unfamiliar context.

items.name: Radians, arc length, sector area
items.question: The diagram shows a windscreen wiper. The arm $OA$ turns about the fixed point $O$. The blade is fixed to the arm between the points $B$ and $A$, where $OB = 10$ cm and $OA = 40$ cm. The arm turns through an angle of $\theta$ radians. The end $A$ moves along an arc of length 96 cm and the blade wipes the shaded region. Show that $\theta = 2.4$ Find the area of the region wiped by the blade. Find the perimeter of the region wiped by the blade.
items.ms: $\theta = \dfrac{96{40 = 2.4$ cso Uses $\dfrac{1{2r^2\theta$ with $r = 40$ or $r = 10$ $\dfrac{1{2\times 40^2\times 2.4 - \dfrac{1{2\times 10^2\times 2.4$ $(= 1920 - 120)$ 1800 cm² Inner arc $= 10\times 2.4 = 24$ Perimeter $= 96 + 24 + 30 + 30 = 180$ cm
items.why: Arc length and sector area are asked in almost every session; the region between two arcs with a non-standard radian angle is the routine opening question in a fresh context.

items.name: Radians, arc length, sector area
items.question: The diagram shows the cross-section of a tunnel. The cross-section is the major segment of a circle with centre $O$ and radius 4 m, cut off by the horizontal floor $AB$. Angle $AOB = \dfrac{2\pi{3$ radians. Show that the width of the floor, $AB$, is $4\sqrt{3$ m. Find the height of the tunnel, measured from the floor to the highest point of the cross-section. Find the area of the cross-section, giving your answer in m² to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: $AB^2 = 4^2 + 4^2 - 2\times 4\times 4\cos\dfrac{2\pi{3$ $AB^2 = 32 + 16 = 48$, so $AB = \sqrt{48 = 4\sqrt{3$ cso Perpendicular distance from $O$ to $AB$ $= 4\cos\dfrac{\pi{3 = 2$ Height $= 4 + 2 = 6$ m Major sector $= \dfrac{1{2\times 4^2\times\left(2\pi - \dfrac{2\pi{3\right) = \dfrac{32\pi{3$ Triangle $AOB = \dfrac{1{2\times 4^2\times\sin\dfrac{2\pi{3 = 4\sqrt{3$ $\dfrac{32\pi{3 + 4\sqrt{3 = 40.4$ m² (awrt)
items.why: Areas made from a major sector and a triangle recur (Jan 2026 Q5); a segment-shaped cross-section and its height are a fresh context for the same skills.

items.name: Radians, arc length, sector area
items.question: The diagram shows a circle with centre $O$ and radius 6 cm. The point $P$ is such that $OP = 12$ cm. The lines $PA$ and $PB$ are tangents to the circle at the points $A$ and $B$. The region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by the tangents $PA$ and $PB$ and the minor arc $AB$. Show that angle $AOB = \dfrac{2\pi{3$ radians. Find the exact perimeter of $R$. Find the exact area of $R$, giving your answer in the form $a\sqrt{3 - b\pi$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
items.ms: Angle $OAP = \dfrac{\pi{2$ (a tangent is perpendicular to the radius) $\cos AOP = \dfrac{6{12 = \dfrac{1{2$, so angle $AOP = \dfrac{\pi{3$ Angle $AOB = 2\times\dfrac{\pi{3 = \dfrac{2\pi{3$ by symmetry cso $PA = \sqrt{12^2 - 6^2 = \sqrt{108 = 6\sqrt{3$ (or $6\tan\dfrac{\pi{3$) Arc $AB = 6\times\dfrac{2\pi{3 = 4\pi$ $12\sqrt{3 + 4\pi$ cm Area of kite $OAPB = 2\times\dfrac{1{2\times 6\times 6\sqrt{3 = 36\sqrt{3$ Sector $OAB = \dfrac{1{2\times 6^2\times\dfrac{2\pi{3 = 12\pi$ $36\sqrt{3 - 12\pi$ cm²
items.why: P1.3.2 has come up in 21 of 23 sessions; a region between two tangents and an arc, which needs the right angle at the point of contact, is a likely unfamiliar setting for the usual arc and sector work.

items.name: Radians, arc length, sector area
items.question: The diagram shows the design for a logo. The logo consists of the sector $OBC$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius 4 cm, joined along $OB$ to the triangle $OAB$. Angle $BOC = \dfrac{5\pi{6$ radians, $OA = 4\sqrt{3$ cm and $COA$ is a straight line. Write down the size of angle $AOB$, in radians. Show that $AB = 4$ cm. Find the exact perimeter of the logo, giving your answer in the form $a + b\sqrt{3 + c\pi$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are rational numbers. Find the exact area of the logo.
items.ms: $\dfrac{\pi{6$ $AB^2 = 4^2 + (4\sqrt{3)^2 - 2\times 4\times 4\sqrt{3\cos\dfrac{\pi{6$ Uses $\cos\dfrac{\pi{6 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2$: $AB^2 = 16 + 48 - 48 = 16$ $AB = 4$ cm cso Arc $BC = 4\times\dfrac{5\pi{6 = \dfrac{10\pi{3$ Adds $AB$, arc $BC$, $CO$ and $OA$: $4 + \dfrac{10\pi{3 + 4 + 4\sqrt{3$ $8 + 4\sqrt{3 + \dfrac{10\pi{3$ cm Sector $OBC = \dfrac{1{2\times 4^2\times\dfrac{5\pi{6 = \dfrac{20\pi{3$ Triangle $OAB = \dfrac{1{2\times 4\times 4\sqrt{3\times\sin\dfrac{\pi{6 = 4\sqrt{3$ $\dfrac{20\pi{3 + 4\sqrt{3$ cm²
items.why: Composite logos made of a sector and a triangle came up in Jun 2026, Jan 2026 and Oct 2025 (area and perimeter with the cosine rule); this is that core type in exact form.

items.name: Radians, arc length, sector area
items.question: A gardener uses 20 m of edging to make the whole boundary of a flower bed. The flower bed is in the shape of a sector $OAB$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $r$ metres, where angle $AOB = \theta$ radians, as shown in the diagram. The area of the flower bed is $A$ m². Show that $A = 10r - r^2$ Given that the area of the flower bed is 21 m², find the two possible values of $r$ and the corresponding values of $\theta$. Write $10r - r^2$ in the form $p - (r - q)^2$, where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Hence state the maximum possible area of the flower bed and find the value of $\theta$ when the area is a maximum. Find the set of values of $r$ for which the area of the flower bed is greater than 21 m².
items.ms: Perimeter: $2r + r\theta = 20$ Substitutes $r\theta = 20 - 2r$ or $\theta = \dfrac{20 - 2r{r$ into $A = \dfrac{1{2r^2\theta$ $A = \dfrac{1{2r(20 - 2r) = 10r - r^2$ cso Solves $r^2 - 10r + 21 = 0$, e.g. $(r - 3)(r - 7) = 0$ $r = 3$ and $r = 7$ $\theta = \dfrac{14{3$ when $r = 3$ and $\theta = \dfrac{6{7$ when $r = 7$ $-(r - 5)^2 + \ldots$ or $q = 5$ $25 - (r - 5)^2$ Maximum area $= 25$ m² (their $p$) $r = 5$, so $\theta = \dfrac{20 - 2\times 5{5 = 2$ $10r - r^2 > 21 \Rightarrow r^2 - 10r + 21 < 0$ with critical values 3 and 7, and chooses the inside region $3 < r < 7$
items.why: Jun 2026 Q7 set up equations from a sector's area and perimeter; fixing the perimeter turns the area into a quadratic whose maximum (by completing the square) and inequality are a likely new angle within P1.

items.name: Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun
items.question: The diagram shows the graph of $y = \sin x$, $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. The angle $\alpha$ is such that $0 < \alpha < \dfrac{\pi{2$ and $\sin\alpha = p$, as shown. Using the symmetries of the graph of $y = \sin x$, write down, in terms of $p$, $\sin(\pi - \alpha)$ $\sin(\pi + \alpha)$ $\sin(-\alpha)$ Find, in terms of $\alpha$, the solutions of the equation $\sin x = -p$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
items.ms: $p$ $-p$ $-p$ $x = \pi + \alpha$ $x = 2\pi - \alpha$
items.why: The spec lists symmetries and periodicity, but recent P1.3.3 questions read values off a graph; using the symmetry of y = sin x with a general angle is not among the recent questions and is a likely surprise.

items.name: Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun
items.question: Two rods, $OA$ of length 6 cm and $OB$ of length 10 cm, are hinged at $O$. The ends $A$ and $B$ are joined by an elastic string to form the triangle $OAB$, as shown in the diagram. Angle $AOB = \theta$ radians, where $0 < \theta < \pi$. Show that the area, $S$ cm², of triangle $OAB$ is given by $S = 30\sin\theta$ State the maximum value of $S$ and the value of $\theta$ at which it occurs. Using the graph of $y = \sin\theta$, find the set of values of $\theta$ for which the area of the triangle is at least 15 cm².
items.ms: $S = \dfrac{1{2\times 6\times 10\sin\theta = 30\sin\theta$ cso Maximum $S = 30$ $\theta = \dfrac{\pi{2$ $30\sin\theta \ge 15 \Rightarrow \sin\theta \ge \dfrac{1{2$ Critical values $\dfrac{\pi{6$ and $\pi - \dfrac{\pi{6 = \dfrac{5\pi{6$ from the symmetry of the sine graph $\dfrac{\pi{6 \le \theta \le \dfrac{5\pi{6$
items.why: Jan 2026 Q8 gave a triangle's area as a sine function and asked for its maximum; reading an inequality off the sine graph is the next step and has not been asked.

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \cos 3x$, where $x$ is in radians. Describe fully the single transformation that maps the graph of $y = \cos x$ onto $C$. Write down the period of $C$. On the axes provided, sketch $C$ for $0 \le x \le \pi$. Show the coordinates of the points where $C$ meets the coordinate axes. State the number of solutions of the equation $\cos 3x = 0.4$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$
items.ms: Stretch parallel to the $x$-axis Scale factor $\dfrac{1{3$ $\dfrac{2\pi{3$ Cosine shape with one and a half cycles, starting at a maximum on the $y$-axis and ending at a minimum at $x = \pi$ $(0, 1)$ $\left(\dfrac{\pi{6, 0\right)$, $\left(\dfrac{\pi{2, 0\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{5\pi{6, 0\right)$ 6
items.why: The spec names y = sin 2x-type stretches; describing the stretch and sketching with exact intercepts is a core P1.3.3 task, and counting solutions over several periods recurred in Jan 2026 and Jun 2026.

items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $y = \tan(x + k)$, $0 \le x \le 360^\circ$, where $k$ is a constant and $0 < k < 90^\circ$. The line with equation $x = 60^\circ$ is an asymptote to $C$. The curve $C$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$ and meets the $x$-axis at the points $Q$ and $R$. State the value of $k$. Write down the equation of the other asymptote to $C$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 360^\circ$ Find the exact $y$ coordinate of $P$. Write down the coordinates of $Q$ and $R$. Given that the point $(15^\circ, 1)$ lies on $C$, use the periodicity of $C$ to write down another value of $x$, with $0 \le x \le 360^\circ$, for which $y = 1$ Find the number of solutions of the equation $\tan(x + k) = 5$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 3600^\circ$
items.ms: $k = 30^\circ$ $x = 240^\circ$ $y = \tan(0 + 30^\circ) = \tan 30^\circ$ (their $k$) $\dfrac{\sqrt{3{3$ or $\dfrac{1{\sqrt{3$ $Q(150^\circ, 0)$ $R(330^\circ, 0)$ $x = 195^\circ$ Uses one solution in each interval of length $180^\circ$ (the period of $C$), e.g. $3600 \div 180 = 20$, or one solution on each branch 20
items.why: Jun 2026 asked for k from where y = cos(x + k) meets the x-axis and then for solutions over a long interval; tan graphs appear far less often (only Jan 2026 Q9(b) among the newest parts), so asymptotes are a likely surprise.

items.question: A Ferris wheel turns at a constant speed. A passenger gets on at the lowest point of the wheel at time $t = 0$. The height, $h$ metres, of the passenger above the ground $t$ minutes later is modelled by the equation $$h = 20 - 18\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t{15\right)$$ where $\dfrac{\pi t{15$ is measured in radians. State the maximum height of the passenger above the ground. Find the time taken for the wheel to make one complete revolution. Find the height of the passenger above the ground when $t = 4$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures. Using the symmetry of the graph of $h$ against $t$, write down the other value of $t$, with $0 < t < 30$, at which the passenger is at the same height as when $t = 4$ Describe fully the single transformation that maps the graph of $y = \cos x$ onto the graph of $y = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x{15\right)$. Show that the passenger is 29 m above the ground when $t = 10$ Hence, using the symmetry of the graph of $h$ against $t$, find the length of time, during each revolution, for which the passenger is more than 29 m above the ground.
items.ms: 38 m Period $= 2\pi\div\dfrac{\pi{15 = 30$ minutes $h = 20 - 18\cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi{15\right)$ 7.96 m (awrt) $t = 26$ Stretch parallel to the $x$-axis (horizontal stretch) Scale factor $\dfrac{15{\pi$ $h = 20 - 18\cos\dfrac{2\pi{3 = 20 - 18\left(-\dfrac{1{2\right) = 29$ Uses the symmetry about $t = 15$, where $h$ is a maximum, to find the other time at which $h = 29$: $t = 30 - 10 = 20$ $20 - 10 = 10$ minutes
items.why: Jun 2026 used a sine model for temperature; a cosine model of a Ferris wheel tests maximum, period, symmetry and a stretch in one context, and the time spent above a height is a new step.

items.question: Given that $$y = x2\sqrt{x - \dfrac{8{x, \quad x > 0$$ find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$, giving each term in its simplest form. Hence, or otherwise, find $$\int\left(5x\sqrt{x + \dfrac{16{x2\right)\mathrm{dx$$
items.ms: Writes $y$ in index form: $x\frac{5{2 - 8x-1$ Reduces the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{5{2x\frac{3{2 + 8x-2$ Recognises the integrand as $2\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$ and writes $2y$, or integrates directly, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $2x2\sqrt{x - \dfrac{16{x + c$
items.why: Only one past part (Oct 2024 Q8) has P1.5.1 as its main point; a 'differentiate, then hence integrate a multiple of the derivative' chain tests integration as the reverse of differentiation directly and has not been set.

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$, $x > 0$, where $$\mathrm{f'(x) = \dfrac{k{\sqrt{x - x$$ and $k$ is a constant. The point $P(4, 30)$ lies on $C$. The line $l$ is the normal to $C$ at $P$, as shown in the sketch. The line $l$ is parallel to the line with equation $x + 2y = 9$. Show that $k = 12$. Hence find $\mathrm{f(x)$, giving each term in its simplest form.
items.ms: Gradient of $x + 2y = 9$ is $-\dfrac{1{2$, so the gradient of the tangent to $C$ at $P$ is 2 Substitutes $x = 4$ into $\mathrm{f'(x)$ and sets it equal to their tangent gradient: $\dfrac{k{2 - 4 = 2$ $k = 12$ * Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term of $12x-\frac{1{2 - x$ $24x\frac{1{2 - \dfrac{1{2x2$ (may be unsimplified) Substitutes $x = 4$, $y = 30$ into their $\mathrm{f(x)$ including a constant $c$ and solves: $48 - 8 + c = 30$ $\mathrm{f(x) = 24\sqrt{x - \dfrac{1{2x2 - 10$
items.why: The only past part with P1.5.1 as its main point (Oct 2024 Q8, 7 marks) found an unknown from the normal and then integrated to find the constant; this is that type in a new setting.

items.name: Indefinite integration as the reverse Students should know that…
items.question: A family of curves all have the same gradient function $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 3x2 - 6x$$ The sketch shows two curves of this family, $C1$ and $C2$. The curve $C1$ passes through the origin $O$ and the curve $C2$ passes through the point $A(1, 2)$. Find an equation of $C1$. Find an equation of $C2$. Describe fully the single transformation that maps $C1$ onto $C2$. The line with equation $x = t$, where $t$ is a constant, meets $C1$ at the point $Q$ and meets $C2$ at the point $R$. Explain why the tangent to $C1$ at $Q$ is parallel to the tangent to $C2$ at $R$.
items.ms: Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $y = x3 - 3x2 + c$ Uses $(0, 0)$ to show $c = 0$: $y = x3 - 3x2$ Substitutes $x = 1$, $y = 2$ into their $y = x3 - 3x2 + c$: $1 - 3 + c = 2$ $y = x3 - 3x2 + 4$ Translation by 4 units in the positive $y$ direction, i.e. by the vector $\begin{pmatrix0\\4\end{pmatrix$ Both curves have the same gradient function, so at the same value of $x$ (here $x = t$) they have the same gradient, so the tangents are parallel
items.why: P1.5.1 requires students to know why a constant of integration is needed; two members of one family and the translation between them (P1.1.12) test that idea directly and have not been asked.

items.question: Find $$\int\left(8\sqrt[3]{x - \dfrac{3{2x4 + 5\right)\mathrm{dx$$ giving each term in its simplest form.
items.ms: Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term, e.g. $x\frac{1{3 \to x\frac{4{3$ or $x-4 \to x-3$ Any two of $6x\frac{4{3$, $+\dfrac{1{2x-3$, $+5x$ correct (may be unsimplified) All three terms correct (may be unsimplified), e.g. $\dfrac{8x\frac{4{3{\frac{4{3 - \dfrac{3{2 \times \dfrac{x-3{-3 + 5x$ Fully correct and simplified, with $+c$: $6x\frac{4{3 + \dfrac{1{2x-3 + 5x + c$
items.why: P1.5.2 has come up in 21 of 23 sessions and a direct 'integrate a sum of powers' question opens most papers (Jan 2026 Q1(b), Oct 2025 Q5); every recent one uses square roots, so a cube root (coefficient 3/4) is the likeliest new twist.

items.question: Given that $$y = \dfrac{(4 - 3\sqrt{x)2{2\sqrt{x, \quad x > 0$$ write $y$ in the form $Ax-\frac{1{2 + B + Cx\frac{1{2$, where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are constants to be found. Hence find $\displaystyle\int y\,\mathrm{dx$, giving each term in its simplest form.
items.ms: Expands the numerator to three terms, one of them in $\sqrt{x$: $16 - 24\sqrt{x + 9x$ Divides each term by $2x\frac{1{2$, using the index laws correctly on at least two terms $8x-\frac{1{2 - 12 + \dfrac{9{2x\frac{1{2$, so $A = 8$, $B = -12$, $C = \dfrac{9{2$ Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term of their expression from (a) Two terms correct, ft their $A$, $B$ and $C$ (may be unsimplified) $16x\frac{1{2 - 12x + 3x\frac{3{2 + c$
items.why: Writing an algebraic fraction as a sum of powers before integrating is set almost every session (Oct 2025 Q5, Jun 2026 Q1); here a squared bracket sits over a root, so the index work is the test.

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$, $x > 0$, where $$\mathrm{f'(x) = \dfrac{x3 - 8\sqrt{x{x2$$ The point $P$ lies on $C$ and has $x$ coordinate 4. The tangent to $C$ at $P$ passes through the origin $O$, as shown in the sketch. Show that the $y$ coordinate of $P$ is 12. Find $\mathrm{f(x)$, giving each term in its simplest form.
items.ms: Substitutes $x = 4$ into $\mathrm{f'(x)$: $\mathrm{f'(4) = \dfrac{64 - 8 \times 2{16 = 3$ The tangent through $O$ with gradient 3 is $y = 3x$, so at $x = 4$, $y = 12$ * Writes $\mathrm{f'(x)$ as separate terms in index form: $x - 8x-\frac{3{2$ Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $\dfrac{1{2x2 + 16x-\frac{1{2$ (may be unsimplified) Substitutes $x = 4$, $y = 12$ into their $\mathrm{f(x)$ including a constant $c$ and solves: $8 + 8 + c = 12$ $\mathrm{f(x) = \dfrac{1{2x2 + \dfrac{16{\sqrt{x - 4$
items.why: Finding f(x) from f'(x) and a point is the commonest P1 integration question (Jun 2026 Q7(b), Jan 2026 Q7(a), Oct 2025 Q9(b), Jun 2025 Q10(c)); fixing the point through a tangent that passes through the origin is a fresh twist.

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$, $x > 0$, where $$\mathrm{f''(x) = 6x + \dfrac{16{x3$$ The point $P(1, 2)$ lies on $C$ and the tangent to $C$ at $P$ is parallel to the $x$-axis. Find $\mathrm{f'(x)$. Find $\mathrm{f(x)$. Find an equation of the tangent to $C$ at the point where $x = 2$, giving your answer in the form $y = mx + c$.
items.ms: Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term of $\mathrm{f''(x)$ $3x2 - 8x-2$ (+ constant) Includes a constant and sets their $\mathrm{f'(1) = 0$ to find it $\mathrm{f'(x) = 3x2 - \dfrac{8{x2 + 5$ Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least two terms of their $\mathrm{f'(x)$ Includes a new constant and substitutes $x = 1$, $y = 2$ into their $\mathrm{f(x)$: $1 + 8 + 5 + d = 2$ $\mathrm{f(x) = x3 + \dfrac{8{x + 5x - 12$ Finds $\mathrm{f'(2) = 15$ and $\mathrm{f(2) = 10$ from their expressions and uses $y - \mathrm{f(2) = \mathrm{f'(2)(x - 2)$ $y = 15x - 20$
items.why: Every recent P1.5.2 question starts from f'(x); starting from the second derivative f''(x) (P1.4.1 notation), so that two constants must be found, has not yet been asked and is the likeliest surprise.

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$, where $$\mathrm{f'(x) = 3x2 + 2kx + 12$$ and $k$ is a positive constant. There is exactly one point on $C$ at which the tangent to $C$ is parallel to the $x$-axis. Show that $k = 6$. Given also that $C$ passes through the point $(-1, 1)$, find $\mathrm{f(x)$. Write $\mathrm{f(x)$ in the form $(x + p)3$, where $p$ is a constant to be found, and hence describe fully the single transformation that maps the curve with equation $y = x3$ onto $C$.
items.ms: Sets $3x2 + 2kx + 12 = 0$ and uses $b2 - 4ac$ with $a = 3$, $b = 2k$, $c = 12$ $(2k)2 - 4 \times 3 \times 12 = 0$, i.e. $4k2 = 144$ $k2 = 36$ and $k > 0$, so $k = 6$ * Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least two terms $x3 + 6x2 + 12x$ (+ $c$) Substitutes $x = -1$, $y = 1$ into their $\mathrm{f(x)$ including a constant $c$: $-1 + 6 - 12 + c = 1$ $\mathrm{f(x) = x3 + 6x2 + 12x + 8$ $\mathrm{f(x) = (x + 2)3$ Translation by 2 units in the negative $x$ direction, i.e. by the vector $\begin{pmatrix-2\\0\end{pmatrix$
items.why: P1.5.2 is hot (21 of 23 sessions) but a gradient function whose unknown comes from the discriminant (P1.1.4) has not been seen; the 'exactly one horizontal tangent' condition leads to a perfect cube and a transformation (P1.1.12).

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$, $x > 0$, where $$\mathrm{f'(x) = \dfrac{3{2\sqrt{x - \dfrac{16{x2$$ The point $P(4, 6)$ lies on $C$. The tangent to $C$ at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at the point $A$ and the normal to $C$ at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at the point $B$, as shown in the sketch. Find $\mathrm{f(x)$, giving each term in its simplest form. Show that $A$ has coordinates $(1, 0)$. Find the area of triangle $APB$.
items.ms: Raises the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $x\frac{3{2 + 16x-1$ (may be unsimplified) Substitutes $x = 4$, $y = 6$ into their $\mathrm{f(x)$ including a constant $c$ and solves: $8 + 4 + c = 6$ $\mathrm{f(x) = x\frac{3{2 + \dfrac{16{x - 6$ Substitutes $x = 4$ into $\mathrm{f'(x)$: $\mathrm{f'(4) = \dfrac{3{2 \times 2 - \dfrac{16{16 = 2$ Uses $y - 6 = 2(x - 4)$ with their gradient and sets $y = 0$ $x = 1$, so $A$ is $(1, 0)$ * Gradient of the normal is $-\dfrac{1{2$ (negative reciprocal of their 2) and an equation of the normal through $(4, 6)$: $y - 6 = -\dfrac{1{2(x - 4)$ Sets $y = 0$: $x = 16$, so $B$ is $(16, 0)$ Area $= \dfrac{1{2 \times (16 - 1) \times 6$, using $AB$ as the base and the height 6 Area $= 45$
items.why: Long P1 questions join 'find f(x)' to tangents and normals (Oct 2024 Q8; Jun 2025 Q10 found k before f(x)); ending with the area of a triangle on the x-axis brings in coordinate geometry, as the last questions on real papers often do.

items.question: The line $l$ passes through the points $A(-4,\ 5)$ and $B(8,\ -4)$. Find an equation for $l$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers. The line $l$ crosses the $x$-axis at the point $P$ and the $y$-axis at the point $Q$. Find the area of triangle $OPQ$, where $O$ is the origin.
items.ms: Attempts the gradient $\dfrac{-4-5{8-(-4) \left(= -\dfrac{3{4\right)$ Uses $y - 5 = -\dfrac{3{4(x + 4)$ or $y + 4 = -\dfrac{3{4(x - 8)$, or $y = mx + c$ with their gradient and either point $3x + 4y - 8 = 0$ Finds $P\left(\dfrac{8{3,\ 0\right)$ and $Q(0,\ 2)$ and uses $\dfrac{1{2 \times \dfrac{8{3 \times 2$ Area $= \dfrac{8{3$
items.why: P1.2.1 has come up in 22 of 23 sessions: a line through two points in the form ax + by + c = 0 opened the coordinate question in Oct 2025 and Jan 2026, and areas from axis intercepts followed in Jan 2026 and Jun 2026.

path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The line $l$ passes through the points $A(-1,\ 7)$ and $B(3,\ -5)$. Find an equation for $l$ in the form $y = mx + c$, where $m$ and $c$ are constants. The curve $C$ has equation $y = x^2 - 5x + 5$. Show that $l$ is a tangent to $C$. Hence write down the set of values of $k$ for which the line with equation $y = k - 3x$ meets $C$ at two distinct points.
items.ms: Attempts the gradient $\dfrac{-5-7{3-(-1) \left(= -3\right)$ Uses $y - 7 = -3(x + 1)$ or $7 = -3(-1) + c$ with their gradient $y = -3x + 4$ Sets $x^2 - 5x + 5 = -3x + 4$ (their line) and collects terms to a 3-term quadratic $x^2 - 2x + 1 = 0$ Shows $b^2 - 4ac = (-2)^2 - 4(1)(1) = 0$, or $(x - 1)^2 = 0$, so there is a repeated root: $l$ meets $C$ at exactly one point and is a tangent $k > 4$
items.why: A line through two points recurs (Jun 2025 Q8, Jan 2024 Q5); none of the 12 most recent P1.2.1 parts asks whether a line touches a curve, so a tangency check by the discriminant (P1.1.4) is a likely synoptic twist.
keywords: Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.question: The line $l_1$ has equation $2y = x + 6$. The line $l_2$ has gradient $-3$ and passes through the point $(4,\ -2)$. The lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ meet at the point $P$. The diagram shows $l_1$, $l_2$ and the shaded region $R$, which is bounded by $l_1$, $l_2$ and the $x$-axis. Find an equation for $l_2$ in the form $y = mx + c$. Find the coordinates of $P$. Find the area of $R$. Use inequalities to define the region $R$.
items.ms: Uses $y + 2 = -3(x - 4)$, or $-2 = -3(4) + c$ $y = -3x + 10$ Solves $l_1$ and their $l_2$ simultaneously, e.g. $2(-3x + 10) = x + 6$, to find $x$ $P(2,\ 4)$ Finds where both lines cross the $x$-axis, $x = -6$ and $x = \dfrac{10{3$, and uses $\dfrac{1{2 \times \left(\dfrac{10{3 + 6\right) \times 4$ with their $y$-coordinate of $P$ Area $= \dfrac{56{3$ Two of $y \geqslant 0$, $2y \leqslant x + 6$, $y \leqslant -3x + 10$ All three correct, and no others
items.why: Intersections of lines recur (Jun 2025 Q5, Oct 2025 Q8) and so do areas; describing the bounded region with inequalities (P1.1.8) has not been joined to the line work in recent papers, so it is a likely surprise.
keywords: Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,
items.question: The points $A(-2,\ 1)$, $B(4,\ 4)$ and $C(6,\ -2)$ are shown in the diagram. The line $l_1$ passes through $A$ and $B$. Find an equation for $l_1$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers. The line $l_2$ passes through $C$ and is parallel to $l_1$. The line $l_2$ crosses the $y$-axis at the point $D$, as shown in the diagram. Find the coordinates of $D$. Show that the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is 42. Hence, or otherwise, find the shortest distance between $l_1$ and $l_2$, giving your answer as a fully simplified surd.
items.ms: Attempts the gradient $\dfrac{4-1{4-(-2) \left(= \dfrac{1{2\right)$ Uses $y - 1 = \dfrac{1{2(x + 2)$ or $y - 4 = \dfrac{1{2(x - 4)$ with their gradient $x - 2y + 4 = 0$ Uses gradient $\dfrac{1{2$ (their gradient from (a)) with $C$: $y + 2 = \dfrac{1{2(x - 6)$, and sets $x = 0$ $D(0,\ -5)$ A complete method for the area, e.g. enclosing rectangle $8 \times 9 = 72$ minus the four corner triangles $9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30$; or the sum of the areas of triangles $ABC$ and $ACD$; or the shoelace method Area $= 72 - 30 = 42$ with no errors Finds $AB = \sqrt{6^2 + 3^2 = \sqrt{45 = 3\sqrt{5$ (or $DC = 3\sqrt{5$) Uses area $=$ base $\times$ height (or $\dfrac{1{2(AB + DC) \times h = 42$): $h = \dfrac{42{3\sqrt{5$ $h = \dfrac{14\sqrt{5{5$
items.why: Areas of shapes cut off by lines are asked almost every year (rectangle May 2024, quadrilateral Jan 2026, triangle Jun 2026) and exact surd distances in May 2024 and Jun 2025; the distance between two parallel lines is not among the recent questions.
keywords: Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.question: The line $l_1$ has equation $kx + 3y - 6 = 0$ and the line $l_2$ has equation $y = (k - 2)x + 4$, where $k$ is a constant. Given that $l_1$ and $l_2$ are parallel, find the value of $k$. Given instead that $l_1$ and $l_2$ are perpendicular, find the possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Attempts the gradient of $l_1$, $\pm\dfrac{k{3$, and sets it equal to $k - 2$ $k = \dfrac{3{2$ Uses $m_1 m_2 = -1$: $-\dfrac{k{3(k - 2) = -1$ $k^2 - 2k - 3 = 0$ (or any equivalent 3-term quadratic) Solves their 3-term quadratic, e.g. $(k - 3)(k + 1) = 0$ $k = 3$ and $k = -1$
items.why: P1.2.2 has come up in 21 of 23 sessions and Oct 2025 asked for an unknown from a right angle; an unknown in both gradients, giving a quadratic (P1.1.5), is the natural next step and is not among the recent questions.

path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
items.question: The points $A(1,\ -2)$ and $C(7,\ 2)$ are opposite vertices of the rhombus $ABCD$, shown in the diagram. The line $l$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AC$. Find an equation for $l$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers. Explain why the vertices $B$ and $D$ lie on $l$. Given that $B$ lies on the $y$-axis, find the coordinates of $B$ and the coordinates of $D$. Find the area of the rhombus $ABCD$.
items.ms: Midpoint of $AC$ is $(4,\ 0)$ Attempts the gradient of $AC$: $\dfrac{2-(-2){7-1 \left(= \dfrac{2{3\right)$ Uses the gradient $-\dfrac{3{2$ (negative reciprocal of their gradient) with their midpoint: $y - 0 = -\dfrac{3{2(x - 4)$ $3x + 2y - 12 = 0$ The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so the diagonal $BD$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AC$; or $BA = BC$ and $DA = DC$, so $B$ and $D$ are equidistant from $A$ and $C$ $B(0,\ 6)$ $D(8,\ -6)$, using $(4,\ 0)$ as the midpoint of $BD$ A complete method, e.g. $\dfrac{1{2 \times AC \times BD$ with $AC = \sqrt{52 = 2\sqrt{13$ and $BD = \sqrt{208 = 4\sqrt{13$, or $4 \times$ area of triangle $ABM$ where $M(4,\ 0)$ Area $= 52$
items.why: Perpendicular bisectors were asked in Oct 2024 and Jan 2025 and exact areas in Jan 2024 and Jan 2026; a rhombus, whose diagonals bisect at right angles, combines both in a shape not used in the recent papers.
keywords: Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.question: The diagram shows the first three patterns in a sequence of patterns made from dots. Pattern $n$ contains $u_n$ dots, where $$u_n = an2 + bn$$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants. Use the diagram to find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$. Find which pattern contains exactly 1081 dots.
items.ms: Uses two of $u_1 = 3$, $u_2 = 10$, $u_3 = 21$ to form two equations, e.g. $a + b = 3$ and $4a + 2b = 10$ Solves their simultaneous equations to find a value of $a$ or of $b$ $a = 2$ and $b = 1$ Sets $2n2 + n = 1081$ and solves the 3TQ $2n2 + n - 1081 = 0$, e.g. $(2n + 47)(n - 23) = 0$ Pattern 23 only (rejects $n = -\dfrac{47{2$)
items.why: P2.4.1 has come up in 16 of 22 sessions, but always as a recurrence relation; a sequence given by a formula for the nth term (the other half of the spec statement) has not been asked recently, so it is the likeliest surprise.

items.name: Sequences, including those given by a formula for the nth term…
items.question: A sequence is defined by $$u_1 = 3, \qquad un+1 = u_n2 - ku_n, \quad n \geq 1$$ where $k$ is a constant. Find, in terms of $k$, an expression for $u_2$ and an expression for $u_3$, giving each answer in its simplest form. Given that $$\sumr=13 u_r = 9$$ find the possible values of $k$.
items.ms: $u_2 = 9 - 3k$ Attempts $u_3 = (\text{their u_2)2 - k(\text{their u_2)$ $u_3 = 12k2 - 63k + 81$ Sets $3 + (\text{their u_2) + (\text{their u_3) = 9$ $12k2 - 66k + 84 = 0$ or $2k2 - 11k + 14 = 0$ Solves their 3TQ, e.g. $(2k - 7)(k - 2) = 0$ $k = 2$ and $k = \dfrac{7{2$
items.why: Recurrences with an unknown constant followed by a sum condition giving a quadratic came up in Oct2025, Jun2023, Oct2021 and Jan2021; a recurrence that is quadratic in u_n is the fresh form.

items.name: Sequences, including those given by a formula for the nth term…
items.question: A wildlife reserve keeps a herd of deer. The number of deer in the herd at the start of year $n$ is modelled by $d_n$, where $$d_1 = 400, \qquad dn+1 = 1.15d_n - k$$ and $k$ is the number of deer moved to other reserves during each year. Find, in terms of $k$, an expression for $d_2$ and an expression for $d_3$. Given that $d_3 = 443$, find the value of $k$. Using the model with this value of $k$, find the first year in which the number of deer at the start of the year is more than 600. The managers decide instead that the number of deer at the start of every year should stay at 400. Find the number of deer that should be moved to other reserves each year.
items.ms: $d_2 = 460 - k$ Attempts $d_3 = 1.15(\text{their d_2) - k$ $d_3 = 529 - 2.15k$ Sets their $d_3 = 443$ and solves the linear equation, e.g. $2.15k = 86$ $k = 40$ Continues the sequence with $k = 40$: $d_4 = 469.45$, $d_5 = 499.87\ldots$, $d_6 = 534.85\ldots$, $d_7 = 575.08\ldots$, $d_8 = 621.34\ldots$ (at least as far as $d_7$ and $d_8$) Year 8 $400 = 1.15 \times 400 - k \Rightarrow k = 60$
items.why: Linear recurrences u(n+1) = ku(n) + c came up in Oct2021 and Oct2024; a real-world recurrence model that needs an iteration to a threshold and a constant (steady) sequence has not yet been asked.

items.name: Understand and work with arithmetic sequences and series,…
path: P2.4.2 - and work with arithmetic seq
items.question: An arithmetic series has first term $a$ and common difference $d$. Prove that the sum of the first $n$ terms of the series is $$\dfrac{n{2\left[2a + (n - 1)d\right]$$ Hence, or otherwise, find the sum of all the integers from 1 to 500 inclusive that are not multiples of 4.
items.ms: $S_n = a + (a + d) + (a + 2d) + \ldots + [a + (n - 1)d]$, showing at least the first two terms and the last term Writes the series in reverse, $S_n = [a + (n - 1)d] + [a + (n - 2)d] + \ldots + a$, and adds the two lines term by term $2S_n = n[2a + (n - 1)d] \Rightarrow S_n = \dfrac{n{2[2a + (n - 1)d]$ Sum of the integers 1 to 500: $\dfrac{500{2(1 + 500) = 125\,250$ Sum of the multiples of 4 from 4 to 500: $\dfrac{125{2(4 + 500) = 31\,500$ $93\,750$
items.why: Arithmetic series came up in 20 of 22 sessions; the spec says the proof of the sum formula should be known but it has not been asked in recent papers, and the 'not a multiple of 4' sum uses the sum of the first n natural numbers named in the spec.

items.name: Understand and work with arithmetic sequences and series,…
path: P2.4.2 - and work with arithmetic seq
items.question: Identical cylindrical pipes are stored in stacks. Each layer of a stack has one pipe fewer than the layer directly below it. The diagram shows a complete stack with 6 pipes in the bottom layer and 1 pipe in the top layer. A complete stack has 40 pipes in its bottom layer and 1 pipe in its top layer. Find the total number of pipes in this stack. A different stack has 8 pipes in its top layer and 297 pipes in total. Find the number of pipes in the bottom layer of this stack. A builder has 1000 pipes. She uses them to build the largest complete stack that she can, with 1 pipe in the top layer. Find the number of pipes that are left over.
items.ms: Uses $\dfrac{n(n + 1){2$ or $\dfrac{n{2(a + l)$ with $n = 40$ 820 Uses an arithmetic series with $a = 8$, $d = 1$ and $n$ layers: $\dfrac{n{2[16 + (n - 1)] = 297$ (or $\dfrac{N(N + 1){2 - 28 = 297$ with $N$ pipes in the bottom layer) $n2 + 15n - 594 = 0$ (or $N2 + N - 650 = 0$) Solves their 3TQ, e.g. $(n + 33)(n - 18) = 0 \Rightarrow n = 18$ layers 25 pipes in the bottom layer Sets $\dfrac{n(n + 1){2 \leq 1000$ (or $= 1000$) and attempts to solve, e.g. $n = 44.2\ldots$ 44 layers, using 990 pipes 10 pipes left over
items.why: Sums of arithmetic series in context came up in Jan2026, Oct2025 and Jan2025; the sum of the first n natural numbers (named in the spec) and choosing the valid root of a quadratic for n are the likeliest new twists.

path: P2.4.2 - and work with arithmetic seq
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. The first three terms of an arithmetic sequence are $$\log_3 x, \qquad \log_3 (x + 4), \qquad \log_3 (3x + 4)$$ where $x$ is a constant. Show that $x2 - 2x - 8 = 0$ Hence find the value of $x$, giving a reason for rejecting any other value. Show that the common difference of the sequence is $\log_3 2$ Find the least value of $n$ for which the sum of the first $n$ terms of the sequence is greater than 100.
items.ms: Uses a property of an arithmetic sequence, e.g. $2\log_3 (x + 4) = \log_3 x + \log_3 (3x + 4)$ or $\log_3 (x + 4) - \log_3 x = \log_3 (3x + 4) - \log_3 (x + 4)$ Correct use of the laws of logarithms to reach an equation without logs, e.g. $(x + 4)2 = x(3x + 4)$ $x2 + 8x + 16 = 3x2 + 4x \Rightarrow x2 - 2x - 8 = 0$ Solves: $(x - 4)(x + 2) = 0$ $x = 4$ only, rejecting $x = -2$ because $\log_3 (-2)$ is not defined (the log of a negative number) $\log_3 8 - \log_3 4 = \log_3 \dfrac{8{4 = \log_3 2$ Uses $S_n = \dfrac{n{2[2\log_3 4 + (n - 1)\log_3 2]$ $S_n = \dfrac{n(n + 3){2\log_3 2$ or equivalent, e.g. $0.3155n2 + 0.9464n$ Sets $S_n > 100$ (or $= 100$) and solves the 3TQ, e.g. $n2 + 3n - 316.99\ldots = 0 \Rightarrow n = 16.37\ldots$ $n = 17$
items.why: Arithmetic sequences came up in 20 of 22 sessions and Jan2026 set a geometric sequence whose terms involve sin θ; an arithmetic sequence of logarithms, joining sequences to the laws of logs, has not yet been asked.
