path: P2.4.2 - and work with arithmetic seq
items.question: Leila is offered two jobs. Offer A: an annual salary of £30,000 in year 1, increasing by £1200 each year until it reaches £42,000. After that the annual salary stays at £42,000. The graph shows the annual salary for Offer A. Offer B: an annual salary of £27,000 in year 1, increasing by 4% each year. Show that, under Offer A, the annual salary first reaches £42,000 in year 11. Find the total amount that Leila would be paid in the first 20 years under Offer A. Using algebra, find the first year in which the annual salary under Offer B is greater than the annual salary under Offer A. Determine which offer would pay Leila more in total over the first 20 years. You must show your working.
items.why: Long context questions comparing an arithmetic model with a geometric model came up in Jan2026 (mining) and Oct2024 (savings schemes); an arithmetic model with a cap, which needs the sum split in two, has not yet been asked.

items.name: Increasing sequences, decreasing sequences and periodic…
items.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon with $(n + 2)$ sides is $u_n$ degrees, where $$u_n = \dfrac{180n{n + 2, \quad n \geq 1$$ Prove that $u_1, u_2, u_3, \ldots$ is an increasing sequence.
items.ms: Attempts $un+1 - u_n = \dfrac{180(n + 1){n + 3 - \dfrac{180n{n + 2$ over a common denominator $un+1 - u_n = \dfrac{180[(n + 1)(n + 2) - n(n + 3)]{(n + 2)(n + 3) = \dfrac{360{(n + 2)(n + 3)$ States that this is positive for all $n \geq 1$ (since $n + 2 > 0$ and $n + 3 > 0$), so $un+1 > u_n$ and the sequence is increasing
items.why: P2.4.3 came up in 9 of 22 sessions, always as a periodic sequence; proving that a sequence is increasing (the other half of the spec statement) has never been asked, so it is the likeliest surprise.

items.name: Increasing sequences, decreasing sequences and periodic…
items.question: A sequence is defined by $$u_1 = 2, \qquad u_2 = 7, \qquad un+2 = un+1 - u_n, \quad n \geq 1$$ The sequence is periodic. Find the values of $u_3$, $u_4$, $u_5$, $u_6$, $u_7$ and $u_8$, and hence state the order of the sequence. Find the value of $u100$ Find the value of $$\sumr=1100 u_r$$
items.ms: Applies the recurrence correctly at least three times, e.g. $u_3 = 5$, $u_4 = -2$, $u_5 = -7$ $u_6 = -5$, $u_7 = 2$, $u_8 = 7$ and order 6 $u100 = u_4 = -2$ (as $100 = 6 \times 16 + 4$) Sum of one period: $2 + 7 + 5 - 2 - 7 - 5 = 0$ Uses 16 complete periods (96 terms) plus $u97 + u98 + u99 + u100 = u_1 + u_2 + u_3 + u_4$ 12
items.why: Periodic sequences came up in Jun2026, Jan2026, Jun2025, Oct2024, Jan2024 and Oct2023, always from a first-order recurrence; a second-order recurrence (as in May2024 Q1) that turns out to be periodic is the natural variation.

items.name: Increasing sequences, decreasing sequences and periodic…
items.question: A sequence $u_1, u_2, u_3, \ldots$ is defined by $$u_1 = 3, \qquad un+1 = \dfrac{u_n + k{u_n - 1, \quad n \geq 1$$ where $k$ is a constant and $k > 3$. Find $u_2$ in terms of $k$. Show that the sequence is periodic and state its order. Given that $$\sumr=141 u_r = 143$$ find the value of $k$.
items.ms: $u_2 = \dfrac{k + 3{2$ Substitutes their $u_2$: $u_3 = \dfrac{\frac{k + 3{2 + k{\frac{k + 3{2 - 1$ Simplifies, e.g. multiplies through by 2: $u_3 = \dfrac{3k + 3{k + 1$ $u_3 = 3 = u_1$, so the terms repeat $3, \dfrac{k + 3{2, 3, \dfrac{k + 3{2, \ldots$ and the sequence is periodic with order 2 (as $u_2 \neq 3$ when $k > 3$) 21 terms equal to 3 and 20 terms equal to $u_2$: $21 \times 3 + 20 \times \dfrac{k + 3{2$ Sets equal to 143 and solves the linear equation: $93 + 10k = 143$ $k = 5$
items.why: Showing that a recurrence is periodic and summing it came up in six sessions from Oct2023 to Jun2026, and Jun2026 and Oct2024 then found a constant from a sum; here the period has to be shown for a general k.

items.name: Geometric sequences and series
path: P2.4.4 - and work with geometric sequ
items.question: The second term of a geometric series is 48 and the fifth term is 20.25. The series has common ratio $r$. Show that $r = 0.75$ Find the sum to infinity of the series. The sum of the first $n$ terms of the series is $S_n$. Using algebra, find the smallest value of $n$ for which $S_n > 255.5$
items.ms: $ar = 48$ and $ar4 = 20.25$, divides to get $r3 = 0.421875$ (or $\dfrac{27{64$) $r = \sqrt[3]{0.421875 = 0.75$ $a = 64$ and uses $S_\infty = \dfrac{a{1 - r$ 256 $\dfrac{64(1 - 0.75n){1 - 0.75 > 255.5$ leading to $0.75n < \dfrac{1{512$ (or $0.001953\ldots$) Uses logs correctly, e.g. $n > \dfrac{\log \frac{1{512{\log 0.75 = 21.68\ldots$ $n = 22$
items.why: Geometric series came up in 21 of 22 sessions; finding r from two terms and then S∞ (Jun2025 Q2) and using logs for the least n (Jun2025 Q7(b), named in the spec guidance) are the core types.

items.name: Geometric sequences and series
path: P2.4.4 - and work with geometric sequ
items.question: The diagram shows the first six squares $S_1, S_2, S_3, \ldots$ of a pattern. Square $S_1$ has sides of length 10 cm. For $n \geq 1$, square $Sn+1$ is drawn by joining the midpoints of the sides of square $S_n$. The region between $S_1$ and $S_2$, the region between $S_3$ and $S_4$, the region between $S_5$ and $S_6$, and so on, are shaded. The pattern continues indefinitely. Show that the side lengths of the squares form a geometric sequence with common ratio $\dfrac{1{\sqrt{2$ Find the total of the perimeters of all the squares in the pattern. Give your answer in the form $a + b\sqrt{2$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Find the exact total area of the shaded regions.
items.ms: Uses Pythagoras on a corner triangle of a square of side $l$: side of the next square $= \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{l{2\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{l{2\right)2$ $= \dfrac{l{\sqrt{2$, so each side is $\dfrac{1{\sqrt{2$ times the one before: geometric with $r = \dfrac{1{\sqrt{2$ $S_\infty = \dfrac{40{1 - \frac{1{\sqrt{2$ Rationalises, e.g. $\dfrac{40\sqrt{2{\sqrt{2 - 1 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + 1{\sqrt{2 + 1$ $80 + 40\sqrt{2$ cm Areas of the squares are $100, 50, 25, \ldots$ ($r = \dfrac{1{2$), so the shaded regions are $50, 12.5, 3.125, \ldots$ Uses $S_\infty$ with $a = 50$ and $r = \dfrac{1{4$ $\dfrac{200{3$ cm$2$
items.why: Sum-to-infinity parts came up in Jan2026, Jun2025 (twice) and Jan2025; a geometric sequence that has to be found from a diagram, with an exact surd answer, has not been asked.

items.name: Geometric sequences and series
path: P2.4.4 - and work with geometric sequ
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. A geometric series has first term $a$ and common ratio $r$, where $a > 0$ and $r > 0$. The sum to infinity of the series is four times the sum of the first two terms of the series. Show that $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2$ Show that the sum to infinity of the series is $a(4 + 2\sqrt{3)$ Given that the fifth term of the series is 18, find the value of $a$. Hence find the sum to infinity of the series, giving your answer in the form $p + q\sqrt{3$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers.
items.ms: $\dfrac{a{1 - r = 4(a + ar)$ Simplifies to $1 = 4(1 - r)(1 + r)$ or $4r2 = 3$ $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2$, rejecting $r = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3{2$ because $r > 0$ $\dfrac{a{1 - \frac{\sqrt{3{2 = \dfrac{2a{2 - \sqrt{3$ and multiplies by $\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{3{2 + \sqrt{3$ $\dfrac{2a(2 + \sqrt{3){4 - 3 = a(4 + 2\sqrt{3)$ $a\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3{2\right)4 = 18$, i.e. $\dfrac{9a{16 = 18$ $a = 32$ Their $a \times (4 + 2\sqrt{3)$ $128 + 64\sqrt{3$
items.why: Conditions linking S∞ to other sums came up in Jan2025 Q4 (S3 and S∞ given) and Jun2025; a condition that leads to a surd common ratio and an exact answer is a variation not yet asked.

items.name: Geometric sequences and series
path: P2.4.4 - and work with geometric sequ
items.question: A geometric series has first term $a$ and common ratio $r$, where $r \neq 1$. Prove that the sum of the first $n$ terms of the series is $$\dfrac{a(1 - rn){1 - r$$ A ball is dropped from a height of 2.4 m above horizontal ground and bounces repeatedly. After each bounce the ball rises vertically to 70% of the height from which it last fell. The graph shows the height of the ball above the ground against time for the first few bounces. Show that the ball rises to a height of approximately 0.58 m after it hits the ground for the 4th time. Find the total vertical distance travelled by the ball from the moment it is dropped until it hits the ground for the 8th time. According to the model, find the total vertical distance travelled by the ball.
items.ms: $S_n = a + ar + ar2 + \ldots + arn-1$ $rS_n = ar + ar2 + \ldots + arn$ and subtracts the two lines $S_n - rS_n = a - arn \Rightarrow S_n(1 - r) = a(1 - rn) \Rightarrow S_n = \dfrac{a(1 - rn){1 - r$ $2.4 \times 0.74$ (or lists $1.68, 1.176, 0.8232, \ldots$) $0.57624$ m $\approx 0.58$ m The heights after bounces 1 to 7 form a geometric series with $a = 1.68$, $r = 0.7$: $S_7 = \dfrac{1.68(1 - 0.77){1 - 0.7$ $(= 5.138\ldots)$ Total $= 2.4 + 2 \times \text{their S_7$ 12.7 m (awrt 12.68) $2.4 + 2 \times \dfrac{1.68{1 - 0.7$ 13.6 m
items.why: Geometric models in context came up in Jan2026 (mining), Oct2025 (evaporating barrels) and Oct2024; the proof of the sum formula is named in the spec but has not been asked recently, and a bouncing ball needs the up-and-down doubling that students often miss.

items.name: Binomial expansion
items.question: Find the first 3 terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of $$(5 - 2x)6$$ giving each term in its simplest form. Find the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $$\left(2 - \dfrac{1{x\right)(5 - 2x)6$$
items.ms: 15625 Correct structure for the $x$ or $x2$ term, e.g. $\binom{6{155(-2x)$ or $\binom{6{254(-2x)2$ $-37500x + 37500x2$ $2 \times 15625 + \left(-\dfrac{1{x\right) \times (-37500x)$ 68750
items.why: P2.4.5 came up in 19 of 22 sessions, nearly always opening with the first terms of (a + bx)^n; a product with a 1/x factor (as in Oct2024 Q5) is the variation most likely to recur.

items.name: Binomial expansion
items.question: In the binomial expansion of $(k + x)7$, where $k$ is a non-zero constant, the coefficients of $x$, $x2$ and $x3$ are, in that order, consecutive terms of an arithmetic sequence. Find, in terms of $k$, the coefficients of $x$, $x2$ and $x3$. Find the possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Correct form for at least one coefficient, e.g. $\binom{7{2k5$ $7k6$, $21k5$, $35k4$ Uses an arithmetic-sequence condition, e.g. $2 \times 21k5 = 7k6 + 35k4$ or $21k5 - 7k6 = 35k4 - 21k5$ Divides by $7k4$ (as $k \neq 0$) to reach a 3TQ: $k2 - 6k + 5 = 0$ Solves their 3TQ, e.g. $(k - 1)(k - 5) = 0$ $k = 1$ and $k = 5$
items.why: Unknown constants found from conditions on the coefficients came up in Jun2026, Jan2026 and Oct2025; making the coefficients consecutive terms of an arithmetic sequence brings in P2.4.2 and has not yet been asked.

items.name: Binomial expansion
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Expand $(3 + x)5$, simplifying each term. Hence show that $(3 + \sqrt{2)5 + (3 - \sqrt{2)5 = 1686$ Hence, or otherwise, find the exact value of $(3 + \sqrt{2)5 - (3 - \sqrt{2)5$, giving your answer in the form $k\sqrt{2$, where $k$ is an integer.
items.ms: Uses the coefficients $1, 5, 10, 10, 5, 1$ with decreasing powers of 3 and increasing powers of $x$ At least three terms correct $243 + 405x + 270x2 + 90x3 + 15x4 + x5$ Substitutes $x = \sqrt{2$ and $x = -\sqrt{2$ and adds, so the odd powers cancel: $2\left(243 + 270 \times 2 + 15 \times 4\right)$ $= 2 \times 843 = 1686$ $2\left(405\sqrt{2 + 90(\sqrt{2)3 + (\sqrt{2)5\right)$ with $(\sqrt{2)3 = 2\sqrt{2$ or $(\sqrt{2)5 = 4\sqrt{2$ used $1178\sqrt{2$
items.why: Binomial expansions came up in 19 of 22 sessions; using a full expansion to evaluate surd expressions exactly links to P1 surds and has not been asked, so it is a likely surprise.

items.name: Binomial expansion
items.question: In the binomial expansion of $(1 + kx)n$, where $k$ is a constant and $n$ is a positive integer, the coefficient of $x$ is $-6$ and the coefficient of $x2$ is 16. Find the value of $n$ and the value of $k$. Find the coefficient of $x3$ in the expansion of $$(3 - x)(1 + kx)n$$
items.ms: $nk = -6$ $\dfrac{n(n - 1){2k2 = 16$ Eliminates $k$, e.g. $\dfrac{n(n - 1){2 \times \dfrac{36{n2 = 16$, and solves for $n$ $n = 9$ $k = -\dfrac{2{3$ Coefficient of $x3$ in $(1 + kx)n$: $\binom{9{3\left(-\dfrac{2{3\right)3 = -\dfrac{224{9$ $3 \times \text{their \left(-\dfrac{224{9\right) - 1 \times \text{their 16$ $-\dfrac{272{3$
items.why: Finding n and k from two coefficients came up in Jan2026 Q10 and Jun2025 Q7 (8 marks each), followed by a further coefficient; the product with (3 - x) adds the step from May2024 Q4.

items.name: Binomial expansion
items.question: Find the first four terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of $$\left(2 + \dfrac{3x{4\right)8$$ giving each term in its simplest form. Use your expansion, with a suitable value of $x$, to find an estimate for $2.068$. Give your answer to 2 decimal places. State, with a reason, whether your estimate in part (b) is an overestimate or an underestimate of $2.068$.
items.ms: 256 Correct structure for the $x2$ or $x3$ term, e.g. $\binom{8{226\left(\dfrac{3x{4\right)2$ Two of $768x$, $1008x2$, $756x3$ All of $256 + 768x + 1008x2 + 756x3$ $x = 0.08$ (from $2 + \dfrac{3x{4 = 2.06$) Substitutes their $x$ into their four-term expansion 324.28 The terms left out of the expansion (in $x4, x5, \ldots, x8$) are all positive when $x = 0.08$ So the estimate is an underestimate
items.why: Using an expansion to estimate a power came up in Jun2026 Q7 and Jan2025 Q2; deciding whether the estimate is too big or too small has not been asked and tests understanding of the terms left out.

items.name: Evaluation of definite integrals
items.question: The function $\mathrm{f$ is such that $$\int15 \mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx = 12 \quad \text{and \quad \int35 \mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx = -4$$ Write down the value of $$\int53 \mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx$$ Find the value of $$\int13 \left(2\mathrm{f(x) - 3x2\right)\mathrm{dx$$
items.ms: $4$ Uses $\displaystyle\int13\mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx = 12 - (-4) = 16$ and evaluates $\left[x3\right]13 = 26$, combining them as $2 \times 16 - 26$ $6$
items.why: P2.8.1 has come up in 17 of 22 sessions; Jun 2019 Q10(c) and May 2024 Q2(b) used given values of a definite integral, but splitting the interval (the integral from 1 to 5 as the sum of those from 1 to 3 and 3 to 5) has not been tested and is the likeliest new property.

items.name: Evaluation of definite integrals
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Given that $k$ is a constant and $$\int02 (kx - 1)2\,\mathrm{dx = 14$$ find the possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Expands $(kx - 1)2$ to three terms: $k2x2 - 2kx + 1$ Integrates, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least two terms $\dfrac{k2x3{3 - kx2 + x$ Substitutes the limits 2 and 0, sets the result equal to 14 and solves the 3TQ in $k$: $\dfrac{8k2{3 - 4k + 2 = 14 \Rightarrow 2k2 - 3k - 9 = 0 \Rightarrow (2k + 3)(k - 3) = 0$ $k = 3$ or $k = -\dfrac{3{2$
items.why: Three of the last four P2.8.1 questions (Jan 2026 Q4 and Q5, Jun 2026 Q2) found an unknown constant from a definite integral; a squared bracket in k that leads to a quadratic with two valid roots is the next variation.

items.name: Evaluation of definite integrals
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. The curve $C$ has equation $$y = \dfrac{(x + 3)(\sqrt{x - 2){\sqrt{x, \quad x > 0$$ Find the exact value of $$\int13 \dfrac{(x + 3)(\sqrt{x - 2){\sqrt{x\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer in the form $a + b\sqrt{3$, where $a$ and $b$ are rational numbers. Hence state the area of the region bounded by $C$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x = 1$ and $x = 3$, giving a reason for your answer.
items.ms: Multiplies out and divides by $\sqrt{x$ to obtain a sum of powers of $x$ with at least three terms correct: $x - 2x\frac{1{2 + 3 - 6x-\frac{1{2$ Integrates, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least two terms $\dfrac{x2{2 - \dfrac{4{3x\frac{3{2 + 3x - 12x\frac{1{2$ Substitutes the limits 3 and 1 and subtracts the right way round: $\left(\dfrac{27{2 - 16\sqrt{3\right) - \left(-\dfrac{59{6\right)$ $\dfrac{70{3 - 16\sqrt{3$ Area $= 16\sqrt{3 - \dfrac{70{3$ with a reason: the integral is negative because the region lies below the $x$-axis (for $1 \leqslant x \leqslant 3$, $\sqrt{x < 2$ so $y < 0$)
items.why: Oct 2019 Q8 asked for an exact integral involving surds and Jun 2019 Q10(b) for an integral equal to zero; an integrand that must be simplified first, with a negative value to be read as an area, joins these two rarely tested ideas.

items.name: Evaluation of definite integrals
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x3 + ax2 + bx - 6$$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants. Given that $(x - 2)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f(x)$, show that $2a + b = -5$ Given also that $$\int02 \mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx = -18$$ show that $4a + 3b = -21$ Hence find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$. Hence factorise $\mathrm{f(x)$ completely.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f(2) = 16 + 4a + 2b - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow 2a + b = -5$ * Integrates $\mathrm{f(x)$, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least two terms $\dfrac{x4{2 + \dfrac{ax3{3 + \dfrac{bx2{2 - 6x$ Substitutes the limits 2 and 0 and sets equal to $-18$: $8 + \dfrac{8a{3 + 2b - 12 = -18 \Rightarrow 8a + 6b = -42 \Rightarrow 4a + 3b = -21$ * Solves the equations from (a) and (b) simultaneously, e.g. substitutes $b = -5 - 2a$ into $4a + 3b = -21$ $a = 3$, $b = -11$ Divides $\mathrm{f(x) = 2x3 + 3x2 - 11x - 6$ by $(x - 2)$ (or compares coefficients) to obtain a quadratic factor $2x2 + 7x + 3$ $(x - 2)(2x + 1)(x + 3)$
items.why: P2.8.1 usually appears as a short 'find the constant' question; forming simultaneous equations from a factor (P2.2.1) and a definite integral has not been asked and is the kind of two-topic link P2 papers favour.

items.name: Definite integrals as areas
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = 8\sqrt{x - x, \quad x \geqslant 0$$ and the line $l$ with equation $y = x + 6$. The line $l$ meets $C$ at the points $A$ and $B$, as shown. The finite region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$ and $l$. Use algebra to find the $x$ coordinates of $A$ and $B$. Use algebraic integration to find the exact area of $R$.
items.ms: Sets $8\sqrt{x - x = x + 6$ and rearranges to a 3TQ in $\sqrt{x$, e.g. $x - 4\sqrt{x + 3 = 0$ Solves their 3TQ in $\sqrt{x$: $(\sqrt{x - 1)(\sqrt{x - 3) = 0$, so $\sqrt{x = 1$ or $3$ $x = 1$ and $x = 9$ Integrates $\pm\left(8\sqrt{x - x - (x + 6)\right)$, or $8\sqrt{x - x$, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $\dfrac{16{3x\frac{3{2 - x2 - 6x$ or $\dfrac{16{3x\frac{3{2 - \dfrac{x2{2$ Applies their limits from (a) and, if the area under $C$ was found, subtracts the area under $l$: $\dfrac{296{3 - \dfrac{1{2(7 + 15)(8)$ $\dfrac{32{3$
items.why: P2.8.2 has come up in 19 of 22 sessions; the spec's own example is the region between a curve and a straight line and Jun 2025 Q3 (curve and chord) shows the type recurring; here the intersections come from a quadratic in the square root of x.

items.name: Definite integrals as areas
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C1$ with equation $y = 10 - x2$ and part of the curve $C2$ with equation $$y = \dfrac{9{x2, \quad x > 0$$ The curves intersect at the points $P$ and $Q$. The finite region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C1$ and $C2$. Show that the $x$ coordinates of $P$ and $Q$ satisfy $$x4 - 10x2 + 9 = 0$$ Hence find the coordinates of $P$ and $Q$. Use algebraic integration to find the exact area of $R$.
items.ms: Sets $10 - x2 = \dfrac{9{x2$ and multiplies through by $x2$ $10x2 - x4 = 9 \Rightarrow x4 - 10x2 + 9 = 0$ * Solves as a quadratic in $x2$: $(x2 - 1)(x2 - 9) = 0$ $P(1, 9)$ and $Q(3, 1)$ Uses the difference of the curves, either way round: $\displaystyle\int\left(10 - x2 - 9x-2\right)\mathrm{dx$, or subtracts the two separate areas Integrates, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least two terms (including $x-2 \to x-1$) $10x - \dfrac{x3{3 + \dfrac{9{x$ Substitutes their limits from (b) and subtracts: $(30 - 9 + 3) - \left(10 - \dfrac{1{3 + 9\right)$ $\dfrac{16{3$
items.why: The spec requires the area of a region bounded by two curves; Oct 2024 Q8(b) is the only recent example, and a reciprocal-square curve that leads to a quartic in x squared has not been used.

items.name: Definite integrals as areas
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$y = \dfrac{18{x2, \quad x > 0$$ For each positive integer $n$, the region $Rn$ is bounded by $C$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x = 3n-1$ and $x = 3n$. The diagram shows $C$ and the regions $R1$ and $R2$. Use algebraic integration to find the area of $R1$. Show that the area of $Rn$ is $12\left(\dfrac{1{3\right)n-1$ Find the exact value of the total area of the regions $R1, R2, \ldots, R6$ Find the smallest value of $n$ for which the total area of the regions $R1, R2, \ldots, Rn$ is greater than 17.99
items.ms: Integrates $18x-2$ to $kx-1$ $-18x-1$ $\left[-\dfrac{18{x\right]13 = -6 + 18 = 12$ Uses the limits $3n$ and $3n-1$ in their $-\dfrac{18{x$: $\dfrac{18{3n-1 - \dfrac{18{3n$ Writes both terms with the same power of 3, e.g. $\dfrac{18{3n-1 - \dfrac{6{3n-1$ or $\dfrac{54 - 18{3n$ $\dfrac{12{3n-1 = 12\left(\dfrac{1{3\right)n-1$ * Uses $Sn = \dfrac{a(1 - rn){1 - r$ with $a = 12$, $r = \dfrac{1{3$ and $n = 6$ $\dfrac{1456{81$ Sets $18\left(1 - \left(\dfrac{1{3\right)n\right) > 17.99$ and uses logarithms: $\left(\dfrac{1{3\right)n < \dfrac{1{1800 \Rightarrow n > \dfrac{\log 1800{\log 3 = 6.82\ldots$ $n = 7$
items.why: Area questions normally ask for one region; a chain of regions whose areas form a geometric series links P2.8.2 with P2.4.4 and P2.5.3, has never been set and is the kind of synoptic surprise a long question can hold.

items.name: Definite integrals as areas
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = 12x - 3x2$$ and the line $l$ with equation $y = kx$, where $k$ is a constant and $0 < k < 12$. The line $l$ meets $C$ at the origin $O$ and at the point $P$. The finite region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$ and $l$. Use algebraic integration to find the area of the finite region bounded by $C$ and the $x$-axis. Show that the $x$ coordinate of $P$ is $\dfrac{12 - k{3$ Show that the area of $R$ is $\dfrac{(12 - k)3{54$ Given that $l$ divides the region bounded by $C$ and the $x$-axis into two regions of equal area, find the value of $k$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: $C$ meets the $x$-axis where $x = 0$ and $x = 4$ Integrates, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $6x2 - x3$ $\left[6x2 - x3\right]04 = 96 - 64 = 32$ $12x - 3x2 = kx \Rightarrow x(12 - k - 3x) = 0$, so at $P$, $x = \dfrac{12 - k{3$ * Uses the difference of the curves: $\displaystyle\int\left(12x - 3x2 - kx\right)\mathrm{dx$, or the area under $C$ minus the area of the triangle under $l$ Integrates, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least two terms $\dfrac{(12 - k)x2{2 - x3$, or $6x2 - x3$ with the triangle area $\dfrac{1{2X \times kX$ Substitutes $X = \dfrac{12 - k{3$ and simplifies: $\dfrac{(12 - k)3{18 - \dfrac{(12 - k)3{27 = \dfrac{(12 - k)3{54$ * Sets $\dfrac{(12 - k)3{54$ equal to half of their answer to (a): $\dfrac{(12 - k)3{54 = 16$ Solves: $(12 - k)3 = 864 \Rightarrow 12 - k = \sqrt[3]{864$ $k = 2.48$
items.why: Jan 2026 Q10(b) found a constant from equal areas and Oct 2024 Q8(b) used a region between two boundaries; a line through the origin with a general gradient, giving an area formula in k, is the natural long-question extension and has not been set.

items.name: Approximation of area under a curve using the trapezium rule
items.question: The table shows corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ for $y = \log2(3x + 2)$. The values of $y$ are given to 4 decimal places where necessary. Complete the table, giving the values of $y$ to 4 decimal places. Use the trapezium rule, with all the values of $y$ in the completed table, to find an estimate for $$\int02 \log2(3x + 2)\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer to 3 significant figures. Using your answer to part (b) and the laws of logarithms, find an estimate for $$\int02 \log2(24x + 16)\,\mathrm{dx$$
items.ms: $1.8074$ and $2.7004$ Strip width $h = 0.5$ (may be implied by $\dfrac{0.5{2$ or $0.25$) Correct structure: $\dfrac{0.5{2\left\{1 + 3 + 2(1.8074 + 2.3219 + 2.7004)\right\$ $4.41$ Writes $\log2(24x + 16) = \log28 + \log2(3x + 2) = 3 + \log2(3x + 2)$ and adds $\displaystyle\int02 3\,\mathrm{dx = 6$ to their answer to (b) $10.4$
items.why: P2.8.3 has come up in 20 of 22 sessions, and a 'use your answer to estimate a related integral' part followed in Jan 2026 Q2, Oct 2025 Q3, Jun 2025 Q5 and Oct 2024 Q1; a law of logarithms (P2.5.2) turning the related integral into a translation has not been used.

items.name: Approximation of area under a curve using the trapezium rule
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y = \sqrt{x2 + 5$. The region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by the curve, the coordinate axes and the line $x = 3$. The table shows corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ for $y = \sqrt{x2 + 5$, with the values of $y$ given to 4 decimal places where necessary. Complete the table, giving the values of $y$ to 4 decimal places. Use the trapezium rule, with all the values of $y$ in the completed table, to find an estimate for the area of $R$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures. State, with a reason, whether your answer to part (b) is an overestimate or an underestimate of the area of $R$. Using your answer to part (b), find an estimate for $$\int25 \sqrt{4x2 - 16x + 36\,\mathrm{dx$$ making your method clear.
items.ms: $2.4495$ and $3.3541$ Strip width $h = 0.5$ (may be implied) Correct structure: $\dfrac{0.5{2\left\{2.2361 + 3.7417 + 2(2.2913 + 2.4495 + 2.6926 + 3 + 3.3541)\right\$ $8.39$ Overestimate, because the curve is convex (it bends upwards), so the top of each trapezium lies above the curve Writes $\sqrt{4x2 - 16x + 36 = 2\sqrt{(x - 2)2 + 5$ and recognises the integral as $2 \times$ the area of $R$ translated 2 units in the positive $x$-direction (so the limits 2 and 5 match 0 and 3) $16.8$
items.why: Over/underestimate parts (Jun 2026 Q5(c), Jan 2024 Q4) and transformed related integrals (Jan 2026 Q2(c), Oct 2025 Q3(b)) are the two commonest follow-ups to the trapezium rule; completing the square to reveal a translation has not yet been needed.

items.name: Approximation of area under a curve using the trapezium rule
items.question: The diagram shows the cross-section of a pedestrian underpass. The floor of the underpass lies along the $x$-axis and its curved roof is part of the circle with equation $$x2 + (y + 2)2 = 20$$ The units on both axes are metres and the cross-section is symmetrical about the $y$-axis. Show that the underpass is 8 m wide at floor level. For points on the roof, $y = \sqrt{20 - x2 - 2$. The table shows some values of $y$. Complete the table, giving the values of $y$ to 4 decimal places. Use the trapezium rule, with all the values of $y$ in the completed table, to estimate the area of the cross-section of the underpass. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. State, with a reason, whether your answer to part (c) is an overestimate or an underestimate of the area of the cross-section. Explain how the trapezium rule could be used to obtain a more accurate estimate of the area of the cross-section.
items.ms: Substitutes $y = 0$ into the equation of the circle: $x2 + 4 = 20$ $x = \pm 4$, so the width is $4 - (-4) = 8$ m * $2.4721$ and $1.3166$ Strip width $h = 1$ Correct structure for $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 4$: $\dfrac{1{2\left\{2.4721 + 0 + 2(2.3589 + 2 + 1.3166)\right\$ Doubles to use the symmetry: $13.8$ m$2$ Underestimate, because the roof is an arc of a circle that curves outwards (concave), so the straight tops of the trapezia lie below it Use more strips, i.e. a smaller strip width (for example values of $y$ every 0.5 m)
items.why: Jun 2026 Q5 set the trapezium rule in a construction context (a ramp) and the circle (P2.3.1) is a P2 topic that has not yet been joined to it; an arch made from a circle also tests the shape argument for an underestimate.

items.name: Approximation of area under a curve using the trapezium rule
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$y = 3\sqrt{x + \dfrac{4{x2, \quad x > 0$$ The table shows corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ for $C$, with the values of $y$ given to 4 decimal places where necessary. Complete the table, giving the values of $y$ to 4 decimal places. Use the trapezium rule, with all the values of $y$ in the completed table, to find an estimate for $$\int14 \left(3\sqrt{x + \dfrac{4{x2\right)\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer to 4 significant figures. Use algebraic integration to find the exact value of $$\int14 \left(3\sqrt{x + \dfrac{4{x2\right)\mathrm{dx$$ Hence find the percentage error in your estimate from part (b). A student uses the trapezium rule with only the values of $y$ at $x = 1$, 2, 3 and 4. Without doing the calculation, state, with a reason, whether the percentage error in the student's estimate will be larger or smaller than your answer to part (d).
items.ms: $5.4520$ and $5.9390$ Strip width $h = 0.5$ (may be implied) Correct structure: $\dfrac{0.5{2\left\{7 + 6.25 + 2(5.4520 + 5.2426 + 5.3834 + 5.6406 + 5.9390)\right\$ $17.14$ Integrates, raising the power of $x$ by 1 in at least one term $2x\frac{3{2 - 4x-1$ $(16 - 1) - (2 - 4) = 17$ $\dfrac{17.14 - 17{17 \times 100 = 0.82\%$ Larger, because there are fewer, wider strips, so the trapezia fit the curve less closely
items.why: The spec says an estimate of the error may be required, yet no recent paper has asked for a percentage error against an exact integral; Jun 2026 Q5 and Oct 2024 Q1 already combine the trapezium rule with algebraic integration, so this is the likeliest extension.

items.question: Given that $\tan\theta = -\dfrac{\sqrt{5{2$ and that $\theta$ is an obtuse angle, find the exact value of $\cos\theta$ $\sin\theta$
items.ms: Uses $\sin\theta = \tan\theta\cos\theta$ in $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$, e.g. $\dfrac{5{4\cos^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ so $\cos^2\theta = \dfrac{4{9$; or draws a right-angled triangle with shorter sides $2$ and $\sqrt{5$ and hypotenuse $3$ $\cos\theta = -\dfrac{2{3$ (negative because $\theta$ is obtuse) $\sin\theta = \tan\theta\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{5{3$ (positive)
items.why: P2.6.1 is used in 21 of 22 sessions, mostly inside equation solving; an exact value found from the identities and the quadrant was asked directly in Jan 2026 Q8(b).

path: P2.6.1 - Knowledge and use of sin tan
items.question: Show that $$\dfrac{\cos\theta{1 - \sin\theta - \dfrac{\cos\theta{1 + \sin\theta \equiv 2\tan\theta, \qquad \sin\theta \neq \pm 1$$ Hence solve, for $0 < \theta < 2\pi$, $$\dfrac{\cos\theta{1 - \sin\theta - \dfrac{\cos\theta{1 + \sin\theta = 6\sin\theta$$ giving your answers to 3 significant figures where appropriate.
items.ms: Combines over the common denominator $(1 - \sin\theta)(1 + \sin\theta)$, with numerator $\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta) - \cos\theta(1 - \sin\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ Uses $1 - \sin^2\theta = \cos^2\theta$ for the denominator $\dfrac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta{\cos^2\theta = \dfrac{2\sin\theta{\cos\theta = 2\tan\theta$ cso Uses (a) and $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta{\cos\theta$ to reach $2\sin\theta = 6\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and factorises: $2\sin\theta(1 - 3\cos\theta) = 0$ $\theta = \pi$ (from $\sin\theta = 0$) $\theta = 1.23$ and $5.05$ (from $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1{3$)
items.why: Identity then 'hence solve' recurs (Oct 2020 Q7, Jan 2025 Q10); two fractions combined into a single trigonometric ratio, followed by an equation solved in radians, has not yet been set.

items.name: Knowledge and use of sin tan = cos and sin2 + cos2 = 1
path: P2.6.1 - Knowledge and use of sin tan
items.question: Show that $$\dfrac{\sin^4\theta - \cos^4\theta{\sin\theta\cos\theta \equiv \tan\theta - \dfrac{1{\tan\theta, \qquad \sin\theta\cos\theta \neq 0$$ Hence solve, for $0 \le \theta < 360^\circ$, $$\sin^4\theta - \cos^4\theta = 4\sin\theta\cos\theta$$ giving your answers to one decimal place.
items.ms: Factorises the numerator as a difference of two squares: $(\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta)(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)$ Uses $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ and splits the fraction: $\dfrac{\sin^2\theta{\sin\theta\cos\theta - \dfrac{\cos^2\theta{\sin\theta\cos\theta$ $= \dfrac{\sin\theta{\cos\theta - \dfrac{\cos\theta{\sin\theta = \tan\theta - \dfrac{1{\tan\theta$ cso Uses part (a) to obtain $\tan\theta - \dfrac{1{\tan\theta = 4$ and forms $\tan^2\theta - 4\tan\theta - 1 = 0$ Solves the quadratic in $\tan\theta$: $\tan\theta = 2 \pm \sqrt{5$ ($4.236$ or $-0.236$) Two correct values, e.g. $76.7^\circ$ and $256.7^\circ$ All four: $76.7^\circ$, $166.7^\circ$, $256.7^\circ$, $346.7^\circ$ and no others in the range
items.why: 'Show an identity, then hence solve' is the standard P2.6.1 question (Oct 2020 Q7, Jan 2025 Q10); a quartic numerator factorised as a difference of two squares has not been used.

items.question: A geometric series has first term $4\sin^2\theta$ and common ratio $\cos\theta$, where $-90^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$ and $\theta \neq 0$. Show that the sum to infinity of the series is $4(1 + \cos\theta)$. Given that the sum to infinity of the series is 6 times the second term of the series, show that $$6\cos^2\theta - 6\cos\theta + 1 = 0$$ Hence find the possible values of $\theta$, giving your answers to one decimal place.
items.ms: Uses $S_\infty = \dfrac{a{1 - r$ with $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$: $\dfrac{4(1 - \cos^2\theta){1 - \cos\theta$ Factorises $1 - \cos^2\theta = (1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)$ and cancels to reach $4(1 + \cos\theta)$ cso Second term $= 4\sin^2\theta\cos\theta$, and sets $4(1 + \cos\theta) = 24\sin^2\theta\cos\theta$ Uses $\sin^2\theta = (1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)$ and divides by $4(1 + \cos\theta) \neq 0$: $1 = 6\cos\theta - 6\cos^2\theta$, so $6\cos^2\theta - 6\cos\theta + 1 = 0$ cso Solves the quadratic: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{12{12 = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{3{6$ $\cos\theta = 0.7887$ and $0.2113$ (awrt $0.789$ and $0.211$) Takes $\arccos$ of a value between 0 and 1 to find a value of $\theta$ $\theta = -77.8^\circ, -37.9^\circ, 37.9^\circ, 77.8^\circ$ and no others
items.why: Jan 2026 Q8(b) put trig identities inside a geometric sequence; a sum to infinity that simplifies with sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ, and a solution interval with negative angles, have not been asked.

items.name: Knowledge and use of sin tan = cos and sin2 + cos2 = 1
path: P2.6.1 - Knowledge and use of sin tan
items.question: The circle $C$ has equation $(x - 3)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 25$ and centre $A$. The point $P$ has coordinates $(3 + 5\cos\theta,\ -1 + 5\sin\theta)$, where $\theta$ is an angle with $0 \le \theta < 360^\circ$. The diagram shows $C$, $A$ and one position of $P$. Show that $P$ lies on $C$ for all values of $\theta$. Find the values of $\theta$ for which $P$ lies on the $x$-axis, giving your answers to one decimal place. The tangent to $C$ at $P$ is parallel to the line with equation $x - 2y + 7 = 0$ Show that $\tan\theta = -2$ and hence find the values of $\theta$, giving your answers to one decimal place. Find the exact coordinates of $P$ when the tangent to $C$ at $P$ is parallel to $x - 2y + 7 = 0$ and $\theta$ is obtuse.
items.ms: Substitutes: $(3 + 5\cos\theta - 3)^2 + (-1 + 5\sin\theta + 1)^2 = 25\cos^2\theta + 25\sin^2\theta$ $= 25(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta) = 25$, using $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$, so $P$ lies on $C$ cso $-1 + 5\sin\theta = 0$, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1{5$ $\theta = 11.5^\circ$ and $168.5^\circ$ Gradient of $AP = \dfrac{5\sin\theta{5\cos\theta = \tan\theta$ The radius $AP$ is perpendicular to the tangent, whose gradient is $\dfrac{1{2$, so $\tan\theta \times \dfrac{1{2 = -1$, giving $\tan\theta = -2$ $\theta = 116.6^\circ$ and $296.6^\circ$ Uses $\tan\theta = -2$ with $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ (or a right-angled triangle with sides 1, 2, $\sqrt{5$) and the obtuse angle to get $\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1{\sqrt{5$ and $\sin\theta = \dfrac{2{\sqrt{5$ $P\left(3 - \sqrt{5,\ -1 + 2\sqrt{5\right)$
items.why: P2.6.1 identities are used in 21 of 22 sessions and circles (P2.3.1) are on almost every paper; a point on a circle written with cos θ and sin θ, needing sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and the radius-tangent property, has not been asked.

items.name: Solving trigonometric equations
items.question: A student attempts to solve the equation $$\sqrt{3\sin x = 1 - \cos x, \qquad 0 \le x < 360^\circ$$ The student's working is shown below. Line 1: $3\sin^2 x = 1 - 2\cos x + \cos^2 x$ Line 2: $3 - 3\cos^2 x = 1 - 2\cos x + \cos^2 x$ Line 3: $4\cos^2 x - 2\cos x - 2 = 0$ Line 4: $(2\cos x + 1)(\cos x - 1) = 0$ Line 5: $\cos x = -\dfrac{1{2$ or $\cos x = 1$ Line 6: $x = 120^\circ, 240^\circ, 0^\circ, 360^\circ$ State the identity that the student used to go from Line 1 to Line 2. Explain why the student's final answer is not correct, and give the correct solutions of the equation.
items.ms: $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$ (so $\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x$) $360^\circ$ is not in the interval $0 \le x < 360^\circ$ Squaring both sides in Line 1 can introduce solutions of $\sqrt{3\sin x = -(1 - \cos x)$, so each value must be checked in the original equation At $x = 240^\circ$: $\sqrt{3\sin 240^\circ = -\dfrac{3{2$ but $1 - \cos 240^\circ = \dfrac{3{2$, so $240^\circ$ is not a solution Correct solutions: $x = 0^\circ$ and $x = 120^\circ$ only
items.why: Edexcel sets 'find the error' parts across P2 (Jan 2023 Q10 completed a student's proof); extra roots created by squaring both sides of a trig equation have not been tested.

items.name: Solving trigonometric equations
items.question: Solve, for $0 \le x < \pi$, $$4\cos^2\left(2x - \dfrac{\pi{3\right) = 3$$ giving your answers as exact multiples of $\pi$. Deduce the number of solutions of $4\cos^2\left(2x - \dfrac{\pi{3\right) = 3$ in the interval $0 \le x < 10\pi$, giving a reason for your answer.
items.ms: Takes the square root: $\cos\left(2x - \dfrac{\pi{3\right) = \pm\dfrac{\sqrt{3{2$ (condone a missing $\pm$ for this mark) One correct value of $2x - \dfrac{\pi{3$ from $-\dfrac{\pi{6, \dfrac{\pi{6, \dfrac{5\pi{6, \dfrac{7\pi{6$ Correct order of operations: $x = \dfrac{1{2\left(\text{their value + \dfrac{\pi{3\right)$ Two correct values of $x$ $x = \dfrac{\pi{12, \dfrac{\pi{4, \dfrac{7\pi{12, \dfrac{3\pi{4$ and no others Recognises that $\cos^2\left(2x - \dfrac{\pi{3\right)$ repeats every $\dfrac{\pi{2$ (or every $\pi$) in $x$, so the pattern of solutions in $0 \le x < \pi$ is repeated 10 times 40 solutions
items.why: Squared compound-angle equations are in the spec (sin²(x + π/6) = 1/2) and in Jan 2026 Q8 (tan²(2θ − 30°)); exact radian answers from a ± root, and deducing the number of solutions from the period, have not been asked.

items.name: Solving trigonometric equations
items.question: The temperature, $T$ °C, inside a greenhouse on a summer day is modelled by the equation $$T = 20 - 7\cos(15t)^\circ, \qquad 0 \le t < 24$$ where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight. The diagram shows a sketch of the graph of $T$ against $t$, together with the line $T = 24$ Find the maximum temperature predicted by the model and the time of day at which it occurs. Find the times of day at which the model predicts a temperature of 23.5 °C. The roof vents of the greenhouse are open whenever the temperature is above 24 °C. Find the length of time for which the vents are open during the day, giving your answer to the nearest minute.
items.ms: Maximum temperature 27 °C When $\cos(15t)^\circ = -1$, i.e. $15t = 180$, $t = 12$: at 12:00 (noon) $20 - 7\cos(15t)^\circ = 23.5$, so $\cos(15t)^\circ = -\dfrac{1{2$ $15t = 120$ or $15t = 240$ $t = 8$ and $t = 16$, i.e. 08:00 and 16:00 $\cos(15t)^\circ = -\dfrac{4{7$, giving $15t = 124.8$ and $235.2$, so $t = 8.32$ and $15.68$ Open for 441 minutes, i.e. 7 hours 21 minutes
items.why: Times of day from a trig model were asked in Jun 2025 Q6 (tide) and Jun 2026 Q9 (temperature); finding how long a quantity stays above a level is the natural next step and has not been asked.

items.name: Solving trigonometric equations
items.question: Show that the equation $$2\log_3(\sin\theta) - \log_3(\cos\theta) = 1 - \log_3 2$$ can be written as $2\cos^2\theta + 3\cos\theta - 2 = 0$ Hence solve, for $0 < \theta < 360^\circ$, $$2\log_3(\sin\theta) - \log_3(\cos\theta) = 1 - \log_3 2$$ justifying your answer.
items.ms: Uses the power law: $2\log_3(\sin\theta) = \log_3(\sin^2\theta)$ Combines the logarithms correctly, e.g. $\log_3\left(\dfrac{2\sin^2\theta{\cos\theta\right) = 1$ or $\log_3\left(\dfrac{\sin^2\theta{\cos\theta\right) = \log_3\left(\dfrac{3{2\right)$ Removes the logarithms and uses $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$: $2(1 - \cos^2\theta) = 3\cos\theta$ $2\cos^2\theta + 3\cos\theta - 2 = 0$ cso Solves the quadratic: $(2\cos\theta - 1)(\cos\theta + 2) = 0$ $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1{2$, with $\cos\theta = -2$ rejected $\theta = 60^\circ$ Rejects $\theta = 300^\circ$ because $\sin 300^\circ < 0$, so $\log_3(\sin\theta)$ is not defined
items.why: Logarithms (P2.5) and trig equations are on every paper but have not been combined; a log equation in sin θ and cos θ is the likeliest surprise.

items.name: Solving trigonometric equations
items.question: Solve, for $0 \le x < 180^\circ$, $$10\cos(3x - 40^\circ) + 7 = 0$$ giving your answers to one decimal place. Solve, for $0 < x < 2\pi$, $$6\cos^2 x + 7\sin x = 8$$ giving exact answers where possible and other answers to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: $\cos(3x - 40^\circ) = -0.7$, so $3x - 40^\circ = 134.4^\circ$ (awrt) One correct value of $x$, e.g. $x = 58.1^\circ$ Finds a second value of $3x - 40^\circ$ in the range $-40^\circ \le 3x - 40^\circ < 500^\circ$ ($225.6^\circ$ or $494.4^\circ$), adding $40^\circ$ before dividing by 3 $x = 58.1^\circ, 88.5^\circ, 178.1^\circ$ and no others in the range Uses $\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$ $6\sin^2 x - 7\sin x + 2 = 0$ Solves the quadratic: $(2\sin x - 1)(3\sin x - 2) = 0$, so $\sin x = \dfrac{1{2$ or $\sin x = \dfrac{2{3$ $x = \dfrac{\pi{6, \dfrac{5\pi{6$ $x = 0.730, 2.41$
items.why: Two separate equations, a compound angle in degrees and a quadratic in radians, is the most common P2.6.2 question (Oct 2025 Q5 and Q7, Jan 2026 Q8); the factor 3 in 3x − 40° widens the range of angles that must be searched.

items.name: Solving trigonometric equations
items.question: A ball is kicked from a point $O$ on horizontal ground with speed 21 m s⁻¹ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal, where $0 < \theta < 90^\circ$. The ball lands at the point $A$ on the ground, as shown in the diagram. In a model of the motion, the greatest height, $H$ metres, of the ball above the ground and the distance, $R$ metres, from $O$ to $A$ are given by $$H = 22.5\sin^2\theta \qquad\qquad R = 90\sin\theta\cos\theta$$ Find the value of $\theta$ for which $H = 10$, giving your answer to one decimal place. Given that $R = 3H$, show that $\tan\theta = \dfrac{4{3$ Hence, without finding the value of $\theta$, find the exact value of $R$ when $R = 3H$. Find the two values of $\theta$ for which $R = 40$, giving your answers to one decimal place. Show each step of your working.
items.ms: $\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{10{22.5 = \dfrac{4{9$, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{2{3$ $\theta = 41.8^\circ$ (awrt) Sets $90\sin\theta\cos\theta = 3 \times 22.5\sin^2\theta = 67.5\sin^2\theta$ Divides by $\sin\theta$ ($\neq 0$ since $0 < \theta < 90^\circ$) and by $\cos\theta$, using $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta{\cos\theta$: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{90{67.5$ $\tan\theta = \dfrac{4{3$ cso Uses $\tan\theta = \dfrac{4{3$ with $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ (or a right-angled triangle with sides 3, 4, 5) to obtain $\sin\theta = \dfrac{4{5$ and $\cos\theta = \dfrac{3{5$ $R = 90 \times \dfrac{4{5 \times \dfrac{3{5 = 43.2$ $\sin\theta\cos\theta = \dfrac{4{9$; squares and uses $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$: $\sin^2\theta(1 - \sin^2\theta) = \dfrac{16{81$ $81\sin^4\theta - 81\sin^2\theta + 16 = 0$ oe Solves the quadratic in $\sin^2\theta$: $\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{81 \pm \sqrt{1377{162$ ($0.7291$ or $0.2709$), then takes the positive square root and $\arcsin$ $\theta = 31.4^\circ$ and $58.6^\circ$
items.why: Trig models in context recur (harbour tide Jun 2025 Q6, city temperatures Jun 2026 Q9); a projectile model built on sin θ and cos θ together, rather than on a single cosine, has not been set.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 3, \quad x \in \mathbb{R$$ Find $\mathrm{f'(x)$. Hence find the set of values of $x$ for which $\mathrm{f(x)$ is decreasing.
items.ms: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\mathrm{f'(x) = 6x^2 - 10x - 4$ Solves their $\mathrm{f'(x) = 0$, e.g. $2(3x + 1)(x - 2) = 0$, to find the critical values $x = -\dfrac{1{3$ and $x = 2$ $-\dfrac{1{3 < x < 2$
items.why: P2.7.1 has come up in 21 of 22 sessions, and Oct 2025 Q4(c) and Jun 2026 Q4(b) both asked for the range of values of $x$ where a curve is decreasing or increasing.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x - 11, \quad x \in \mathbb{R$$ Prove that $\mathrm{f(x)$ is an increasing function. Show that $x = 1$ is a root of the equation $\mathrm{f(x) = 0$. Hence explain why the equation $\mathrm{f(x) = 0$ has no other real roots.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f'(x) = 6x^2 + 6x + 6$ Attempts to show that $\mathrm{f'(x) > 0$ for all $x$: completes the square, $6\left[\left(x + \dfrac{1{2\right)^2 + \dfrac{3{4\right]$, or finds the discriminant of $6x^2 + 6x + 6$: $36 - 144 = -108 < 0$ $\mathrm{f'(x) = 6\left(x + \dfrac{1{2\right)^2 + \dfrac{9{2 \geq \dfrac{9{2$, so $\mathrm{f'(x) > 0$ for all $x$ and $\mathrm{f(x)$ is increasing $\mathrm{f(1) = 2 + 3 + 6 - 11 = 0$, so $x = 1$ is a root $\mathrm{f(x)$ is increasing for all $x$, so the curve $y = \mathrm{f(x)$ crosses the $x$-axis only once ($\mathrm{f(x) < 0$ for $x < 1$ and $\mathrm{f(x) > 0$ for $x > 1$); so $x = 1$ is the only real root
items.why: Increasing and decreasing functions are asked in most sessions (Jun 2026 Q4(b), Oct 2025 Q4(c)), but proving that a function is increasing for all $x$ by completing the square on $\mathrm{f}'(x)$, and using it to count roots, is not among the recent questions: a likely surprise.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$y = ax^2 + \dfrac{b{x, \quad x > 0$$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants. The point $P(2, 12)$ lies on $C$ and $P$ is a stationary point of $C$. Show that $b = 16a$. Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$. Use the second derivative to determine the nature of the stationary point $P$.
items.ms: Differentiates: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 2ax - bx-2$ ($x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term) Sets $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 0$ at $x = 2$: $4a - \dfrac{b{4 = 0$, so $b = 16a$ Substitutes $x = 2$, $y = 12$ into the equation of $C$ and uses $b = 16a$: $4a + \dfrac{16a{2 = 12$ $a = 1$ and $b = 16$ Finds $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2y{\mathrm{dx^2 = 2a + 2bx-3$ and substitutes their $a$, $b$ and $x = 2$: $2 + \dfrac{32{8$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2y{\mathrm{dx^2 = 6 > 0$, so $P$ is a minimum point
items.why: Jun 2026 Q8(b) found an unknown coefficient from a minimum point; setting up two equations in two constants from one given stationary point turns the routine P2.7.1 method round.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: The diagram shows a sketch of part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = \dfrac{x^2 + 48{2\sqrt{x, \quad x > 0$$ The point $P$ is the stationary point of $C$. Show that $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{3(x^2 - 16){4x\sqrt{x$$ Find the coordinates of $P$. Find the set of values of $x$ for which $C$ is decreasing.
items.ms: Writes $y$ as a sum of powers of $x$: $y = \dfrac{1{2x\frac{3{2 + 24x-\frac{1{2$ (at least one term correct) Differentiates their powers, $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{3{4x\frac{1{2 - 12x-\frac{3{2$ Correct derivative written over a common denominator: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{3x^2 - 48{4x\frac{3{2 = \dfrac{3(x^2 - 16){4x\sqrt{x$ Sets $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 0$, so $x^2 - 16 = 0$, giving $x = 4$, and substitutes into the equation of $C$ $P(4, 16)$ Uses their $x$ coordinate of $P$ as the critical value and selects the region where $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx < 0$: $x^2 - 16 < 0$ with $4x\sqrt{x > 0$ $0 < x < 4$
items.why: Jun 2026 Q3 and Jan 2026 Q10(a) both needed a quotient or surd rewritten as powers of $x$ before finding a stationary point, and Jun 2026 Q4(b) then asked where the curve is increasing.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$y = 3x^4 - 8x^3 + 5$$ Find the coordinates of each of the stationary points of $C$. Determine the nature of each of the stationary points of $C$, giving reasons for your answers.
items.ms: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 12x^3 - 24x^2$ Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 0$ and factorises: $12x^2(x - 2) = 0$, so $x = 0$ or $x = 2$ $(0, 5)$ and $(2, -11)$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2y{\mathrm{dx^2 = 36x^2 - 48x$ and substitutes $x = 2$: $144 - 96 = 48$ $48 > 0$, so $(2, -11)$ is a minimum point At $x = 0$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2y{\mathrm{dx^2 = 0$, so tests the gradient on each side, e.g. at $x = -0.5$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = -7.5 < 0$ and at $x = 0.5$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = -4.5 < 0$. The gradient is negative on both sides, so $(0, 5)$ is a point of inflection
items.why: Stationary points have come up in 21 of 22 sessions, nearly always on cubics or curves with fractional powers; classifying the stationary points of a quartic is not among the recent questions and is a likely surprise.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: The fuel consumption of a car, $F$ litres per 100 km, when it travels at a constant speed of $v$ km h⁻¹, is modelled by the equation $$F = \dfrac{v^2{2500 + \dfrac{270{v, \quad 20 \leq v \leq 120$$ Use calculus to find, according to the model, the minimum fuel consumption of the car and the speed at which it occurs. Give your answers to 3 significant figures. Justify that the speed found in part (a) gives the minimum fuel consumption. On one stretch of road the speed limit is 50 km h⁻¹. The driver wishes to use as little fuel as possible on this stretch. State, with a reason, the speed at which the model suggests the car should travel.
items.ms: $v^n \to vn-1$ for at least one term: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dF{\mathrm{dv = \dfrac{2v{2500 - \dfrac{270{v^2$ Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dF{\mathrm{dv = 0$ and proceeds to $v^3 = k$: $v^3 = 337\,500$ $v = 69.6$ (km h⁻¹) $F = 5.82$ (litres per 100 km) Finds $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2F{\mathrm{dv^2 = \dfrac{2{2500 + \dfrac{540{v^3$ and considers its sign at their $v$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2F{\mathrm{dv^2 = 0.0024 > 0$ at $v = 69.6$ (or $> 0$ for all $v > 0$), so this is a minimum 50 km h⁻¹, because $\dfrac{\mathrm{dF{\mathrm{dv < 0$ ($F$ is decreasing) for $20 \leq v < 69.6$, so the least value of $F$ with $v \leq 50$ is at $v = 50$
items.why: Optimisation in context is asked almost every session (Jun 2026 Q9, Jan 2026 Q7, Oct 2025 Q10); a given fuel-consumption model with a practical follow-up about a speed limit is not among the recent questions.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $y = 2\sqrt{x$, $x \geq 0$, and the point $A(5, 0)$. The point $P(x, y)$ lies on $C$. Show that $$AP^2 = x^2 - 6x + 25$$ Use calculus to find the coordinates of the point $P$ for which the distance $AP$ is least. Justify that your answer gives the least distance. The circle $S$ has centre $A$ and touches $C$ at the point $P$ found in part (b). Find an equation for $S$.
items.ms: Uses $AP^2 = (x - 5)^2 + y^2$ with $y = 2\sqrt{x$ $AP^2 = x^2 - 10x + 25 + 4x = x^2 - 6x + 25$ Differentiates $x^2 - 6x + 25$ to get $2x - 6$ and sets it equal to 0 $x = 3$ $P(3, 2\sqrt{3)$ Second derivative $= 2 > 0$, so $AP^2$ is a minimum, and so $AP$ is least (as $AP > 0$) Finds the radius: $r^2 = 3^2 - 6(3) + 25 = 16$, or $(3 - 5)^2 + (2\sqrt{3)^2 = 16$ $(x - 5)^2 + y^2 = 16$
items.why: Optimisation has come up in 21 of 22 sessions, but minimising a distance to a curve through $AP^2$, linked to the equation of a circle (P2.3.1), is not among the recent questions: a likely level-3 surprise.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: A farmer uses fencing to make a rectangular enclosure next to a straight wall. Two fences perpendicular to the wall divide the enclosure into three pens, as shown in the diagram. Each of the four fences perpendicular to the wall has length $x$ metres and the fence parallel to the wall has length $y$ metres. The wall itself is not fenced. The total area of the enclosure is 600 m². The fencing parallel to the wall costs £12 per metre and the fencing perpendicular to the wall costs £8 per metre. The total cost of the fencing is £$C$. Show that $$C = 32x + \dfrac{7200{x$$ Use calculus to find the value of $x$ for which $C$ is least, and find the least cost of the fencing. Justify that the value of $x$ found in part (b) gives the least cost.
items.ms: Uses $xy = 600$ to write $y = \dfrac{600{x$ and forms $C = 8 \times 4x + 12y$ $C = 32x + \dfrac{7200{x$ $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dC{\mathrm{dx = 32 - \dfrac{7200{x^2$ Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dC{\mathrm{dx = 0$ and proceeds to $x^2 = 225$ $x = 15$ Least cost £960 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2C{\mathrm{dx^2 = \dfrac{14\,400{x^3$ and considers its sign at their $x$ $\dfrac{14\,400{3375 = 4.27 > 0$ (or $> 0$ for all $x > 0$), so $C$ is a minimum
items.why: Fencing and perimeter problems are the commonest P2 optimisation (Jun 2026 Q9, Jan 2026 Q7, Oct 2025 Q10); a cost with two prices per metre is a fresh variant of the same show-that, calculus and justify chain.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: A company makes closed cylindrical cans of radius $r$ cm and height $h$ cm from thin metal. Each can has a volume of 400 cm³. The curved surface of a can is made from a rectangle of metal. Each circular end is cut from a square of metal of side $2r$ cm, as shown in the diagram, and the rest of the square is wasted. The total area of metal used to make one can, including the wasted metal, is $A$ cm². Show that $$A = 8r^2 + \dfrac{800{r$$ Use calculus to find the minimum value of $A$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures. Justify that the value of $A$ found in part (b) is a minimum.
items.ms: Uses $\pi r^2 h = 400$ to write $h = \dfrac{400{\pi r^2$ (or $\pi rh = \dfrac{400{r$) Forms $A = 2(2r)^2 + 2\pi rh$ Substitutes for $h$: $A = 8r^2 + \dfrac{800{r$ $r^n \to rn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dA{\mathrm{dr = 16r - \dfrac{800{r^2$ Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dA{\mathrm{dr = 0$ and proceeds to $r^3 = 50$, $r = 3.68$ $A = 326$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2A{\mathrm{dr^2 = 16 + \dfrac{1600{r^3$ and considers its sign at their $r$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2A{\mathrm{dr^2 = 48 > 0$ at $r = 3.68$ (or $> 0$ for all $r > 0$), so $A$ is a minimum
items.why: Tanks and cans are standard P2 optimisation contexts, asked in the show-that, calculus and justify pattern of Jan 2026 Q7; counting the metal wasted when the ends are cut from squares is a fresh twist (and removes $\pi$ from the function).

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: A box for chocolates is a closed right prism of length $l$ cm. The cross-section of the prism is an equilateral triangle of side $x$ cm, as shown in the diagram. The box is made from thin card and its volume is 300 cm³. The total surface area of the box is $S$ cm². Show that $$S = \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2x^2 + \dfrac{1200\sqrt{3{x$$ Use calculus to find the value of $x$ for which $S$ is a minimum. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. Justify that this value of $x$ gives a minimum value of $S$. Find the minimum surface area of the box.
items.ms: Area of each triangular end $= \dfrac{1{2x^2 \sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3{4x^2$ Uses the volume: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3{4x^2 l = 300$, so $l = \dfrac{1200{\sqrt{3x^2$ Forms $S = 2 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3{4x^2 + 3xl$ Substitutes and simplifies, using $\dfrac{3600{\sqrt{3 = 1200\sqrt{3$, to $S = \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2x^2 + \dfrac{1200\sqrt{3{x$ $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dS{\mathrm{dx = \sqrt{3x - \dfrac{1200\sqrt{3{x^2$ Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dS{\mathrm{dx = 0$ and proceeds to $x^3 = 1200$ $x = 10.6$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2S{\mathrm{dx^2 = \sqrt{3 + \dfrac{2400\sqrt{3{x^3$ and considers its sign at their $x$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{d^2S{\mathrm{dx^2 = 3\sqrt{3 = 5.20 > 0$ at $x = 10.6$ (or $> 0$ for all $x > 0$), so $S$ is a minimum $S = 293$ (cm²)
items.why: Boxes are a standard P2 optimisation context; a prism with an equilateral cross-section, whose show-that needs $\sin 60^\circ$ and surds, is a harder, fresh variant of the four-part structure of Jan 2026 Q7.

items.name: Stationary points, maxima and minima
items.question: The diagram shows a sketch of part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y = 2x^3 - 15x^2 + 24x + 20$$ The point $A$ is a maximum point of $C$ and the point $B$ is a minimum point of $C$. The line $l$ passes through $A$ and is parallel to the $x$-axis. The line $l$ meets $C$ again at the point $D$. The region $R$, shown shaded in the diagram, is bounded by $C$ and $l$. Use calculus to find the coordinates of $A$ and the coordinates of $B$. Use algebra to show that the $x$ coordinate of $D$ is $\dfrac{11{2$. Use algebraic integration to find the exact area of $R$.
items.ms: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 6x^2 - 30x + 24$ Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 0$ and solves the 3-term quadratic: $6(x - 1)(x - 4) = 0$, so $x = 1$ or $x = 4$ $A(1, 31)$ $B(4, 4)$ Sets $2x^3 - 15x^2 + 24x + 20 = 31$ (their $y$ coordinate of $A$) to give $2x^3 - 15x^2 + 24x - 11 = 0$ Uses $(x - 1)$ as a factor (since $x = 1$ at $A$), by division or inspection: $(x - 1)(2x^2 - 13x + 11) = 0$ $(x - 1)^2(2x - 11) = 0$, so at $D$, $x = \dfrac{11{2$ Integrates $31 - (2x^3 - 15x^2 + 24x + 20)$, or $y$, with $x^n \to xn+1$ for at least two terms $\displaystyle\int (-2x^3 + 15x^2 - 24x + 11)\,\mathrm{dx = -\dfrac{x^4{2 + 5x^3 - 12x^2 + 11x$ Applies the limits $\dfrac{11{2$ and $1$ and subtracts (or finds the rectangle, $31 \times \dfrac{9{2$, minus $\displaystyle\int_1\frac{11{2 y\,\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{2277{32$) Area of $R = \dfrac{2187{32$
items.why: Stationary points appear in 21 of 22 sessions and P2 often pairs a curve sketch with an area (P2.8.2); finding where the horizontal line through a maximum meets the curve again, by the factor theorem (P2.2.1), is an unusual level-3 link.

items.name: Equation of a circle
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The circle $C$ has equation $$x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y + k = 0$$ where $k$ is a constant. Find the coordinates of the centre of $C$. Given that the origin $O$ lies inside $C$, find the range of possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Attempts to complete the square for $x$ and for $y$, e.g. $(x - 4)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = \ldots$, or states a centre $(\pm 4,\ \pm 3)$ Centre $(4,\ -3)$ Uses radius$^2 = 16 + 9 - k = 25 - k$ and compares it with the square of the distance from the centre to $O$, $4^2 + 3^2 = 25$: $25 - k > 25$. Or substitutes $(0,\ 0)$ into the left-hand side and requires it to be negative: $k < 0$ $k < 0$
items.why: P2.3.1 has come up in 21 of 22 sessions and the centre from the expanded form is its commonest part (Jun 2026 Q8, Jan 2026 Q5); circles with an unknown constant k recur (Oct 2025 Q6, Jun 2026 Q7), but asking when a given point lies inside the circle has not been set.
keywords: Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.name: Equation of a circle
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The points $A(-3,\ 4)$ and $B(5,\ -2)$ are the ends of a diameter of the circle $C$. Find an equation for $C$. The point $Q(4,\ q)$, where $q > 0$, is such that angle $AQB = 90^\circ$. Find the value of $q$.
items.ms: Centre is the midpoint of $AB$: $(1,\ 1)$ Uses Pythagoras for the radius or the diameter, e.g. $r^2 = (5 - 1)^2 + (-2 - 1)^2$ or $AB = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2 = 10$ $(x - 1)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25$ Uses the angle in a semicircle, so $Q$ lies on $C$: $(4 - 1)^2 + (q - 1)^2 = 25$. Or uses gradient $AQ \times$ gradient $BQ = -1$: $\dfrac{q - 4{7 \times \dfrac{q + 2{-1 = -1$ $q = 5$ only
items.why: A circle from the ends of a diameter recurs (Oct 2025 Q6, Jun 2025 Q2, Oct 2020 Q4); the angle in a semicircle (spec property (i)) was used only in Jan 2026 Q6(d) and Jun 2022 Q3, so using it to place a point is a likely twist.

items.question: The circle $C$ has equation $$x^2 + y^2 + 2x - 6y - 15 = 0$$ and centre $A$. The point $P(3,\ 6)$ lies on $C$. The tangent to $C$ at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at the point $T$, as shown in the diagram. Find an equation of the tangent to $C$ at $P$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers. Find the area of triangle $APT$.
items.ms: Centre $A(-1,\ 3)$, e.g. from $(x + 1)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 25$ (may be implied) Gradient of $AP = \dfrac{6 - 3{3 - (-1) = \dfrac{3{4$, using their centre Uses the perpendicular gradient $-\dfrac{4{3$ with $P$: $y - 6 = -\dfrac{4{3(x - 3)$ $4x + 3y - 30 = 0$ Finds $T(7.5,\ 0)$ from their tangent and uses a complete method, e.g. $\tfrac{1{2 \times AP \times PT$ with the right angle at $P$: $\tfrac{1{2 \times 5 \times 7.5$ Area $= 18.75$
items.why: A tangent in the form ax + by + c = 0 is one of the commonest P2.3.1 parts (Jun 2023 Q3, Oct 2020 Q4, Jan 2022 Q6, Jun 2019 Q2); a triangle area built on the tangent was last asked in Jan 2021 Q9.

items.name: Equation of a circle
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.question: The circle $C$ has radius $r$. $C$ lies in the first quadrant and touches both the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis. The point $P(2,\ 9)$ lies on $C$. Write down, in terms of $r$, the coordinates of the centre of $C$. Show that $r^2 - 22r + 85 = 0$. Hence find the two possible equations for $C$. The two possible circles meet at $P$ and at a second point $Q$. Find the coordinates of $Q$.
items.ms: $(r,\ r)$ Uses $P$ on $C$: $(2 - r)^2 + (9 - r)^2 = r^2$ Expands and simplifies to $r^2 - 22r + 85 = 0$ with no errors Solves the quadratic: $(r - 5)(r - 17) = 0$, so $r = 5$ or $r = 17$ $(x - 5)^2 + (y - 5)^2 = 25$ and $(x - 17)^2 + (y - 17)^2 = 289$ Uses symmetry in the line $y = x$ (the line through both centres is the perpendicular bisector of $PQ$), or subtracts the two equations to get $x + y = 11$ and solves it with one circle $Q(9,\ 2)$
items.why: Circles touching an axis recur (Jun 2025 Q9, Jun 2021 Q6, Jan 2020 Q6); a circle touching both axes, which gives a quadratic in r and two possible circles, has not yet been asked.

items.question: The circle $C$ has equation $$x^2 + y^2 - 12x - 4y + 20 = 0$$ and centre $Z$. The diagram shows $C$ and the two tangents to $C$ that pass through the origin $O$. One tangent touches $C$ at $A$ and the other touches $C$ at $B$. Show that the line with equation $y = mx$ meets $C$ where $$(1 + m^2)x^2 - (12 + 4m)x + 20 = 0$$ Hence find the gradients of the two tangents. Find the exact length of $OA$.
items.ms: Substitutes $y = mx$ into $C$: $x^2 + m^2x^2 - 12x - 4mx + 20 = 0$ Collects terms to reach the given equation with no errors Uses $b^2 - 4ac = 0$: $(12 + 4m)^2 - 80(1 + m^2) = 0$ Simplifies to a 3-term quadratic, e.g. $2m^2 - 3m - 2 = 0$, and solves it $m = 2$ and $m = -\dfrac{1{2$ Uses the right angle between radius and tangent: $OA^2 = OZ^2 - r^2 = (6^2 + 2^2) - 20$. Or finds $A(2,\ 4)$ from the repeated root and uses $\sqrt{2^2 + 4^2$ $OA = 2\sqrt{5$
items.why: Tangency by the discriminant recurs (Oct 2024 Q10, Jun 2022 Q10); two tangents drawn from an outside point, and the length of a tangent, have not been asked directly.

items.question: The points $A(1,\ 7)$ and $B(7,\ 5)$ lie on the circle $C$. The centre of $C$ lies on the line $l$ with equation $x + 2y = 9$, as shown in the diagram. Find an equation of the perpendicular bisector of $AB$. Hence find an equation for $C$. The point $D$ lies on $C$ such that $AD$ is a diameter of $C$. Find the area of triangle $ABD$.
items.ms: Finds the midpoint $(4,\ 6)$ and the gradient of $AB$, $\dfrac{5 - 7{7 - 1 = -\dfrac{1{3$ Uses the perpendicular gradient $3$ through their midpoint: $y - 6 = 3(x - 4)$ $y = 3x - 6$ Solves $y = 3x - 6$ and $x + 2y = 9$ simultaneously Centre $(3,\ 3)$ and uses the distance to $A$ or $B$: $r^2 = (1 - 3)^2 + (7 - 3)^2$ $(x - 3)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 20$ Finds $D(5,\ -1)$ and uses angle $ABD = 90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle) with $AB = BD = \sqrt{40$: area $= \tfrac{1{2 \times \sqrt{40 \times \sqrt{40$; or any complete method Area $= 20$
items.why: The centre from the perpendicular bisector of a chord was asked in Jan 2026 Q6 and Oct 2023 Q7; adding a centre on a given line and the angle in a semicircle tests all three spec circle properties in one question.

items.question: The curve $K$ has equation $$y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 2$$ The curve has a maximum point at $A$ and a minimum point at $B$. The circle $C$ has diameter $AB$, as shown in the diagram. Using calculus, find the coordinates of $A$ and the coordinates of $B$. Find an equation for $C$. Find an equation of the tangent to $C$ at $A$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
items.ms: Differentiates: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 3x^2 - 12x + 9$ (at least two terms correct) Sets their $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 0$ and solves a 3-term quadratic $x = 1$ and $x = 3$ $A(1,\ 6)$ and $B(3,\ 2)$ Centre is the midpoint of $AB$: $(2,\ 4)$ Radius$^2 = (2 - 1)^2 + (4 - 6)^2$ or $\left(\tfrac{1{2AB\right)^2$ $(x - 2)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 5$ Gradient of the radius from $(2,\ 4)$ to $A(1,\ 6)$ is $-2$, so the tangent gradient is $\dfrac{1{2$ and $y - 6 = \dfrac{1{2(x - 1)$ $x - 2y + 11 = 0$
items.why: Stationary points (P2.7.1) are asked in almost every P2 paper and circles in 21 of 22 sessions; long P2 questions join topics (Jun 2022 Q3 joined a circle with proof), so a circle built on a curve's turning points is a strong synoptic prediction.

items.question: A coastguard radar station stands on a small island. On a map, with $x$ and $y$ axes measured in kilometres, the edge of the region covered by the radar is modelled by the circle $C$ with equation $$x^2 + y^2 - 12x - 8y + 27 = 0$$ The radar station is at the centre $R$ of $C$. A ship sails in a straight line along the path with equation $x - 2y + 7 = 0$, in the direction of increasing $x$. The ship enters the region covered by the radar at $P$ and leaves it at $Q$, as shown in the diagram. Find the coordinates of $R$ and the radius of $C$. Using algebra, find the coordinates of $P$ and the coordinates of $Q$. Find the shortest distance between the ship and the radar station during the voyage. Give your answer in kilometres to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: Attempts $(x - 6)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = \ldots$ $R(6,\ 4)$ Radius $5$ (km) Substitutes $x = 2y - 7$ (or $y = \dfrac{x + 7{2$) into $C$ $5y^2 - 60y + 160 = 0$, i.e. $y^2 - 12y + 32 = 0$ (or $x^2 - 10x + 9 = 0$) Solves their 3-term quadratic and finds the other coordinates $P(1,\ 4)$ and $Q(9,\ 8)$ Uses the perpendicular from $R$ to the chord $PQ$ bisecting it: midpoint $M(5,\ 6)$ and $RM = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2$. Or $RM^2 = RP^2 - \left(\tfrac{1{2PQ\right)^2 = 25 - 20$ $2.24$ km
items.why: Line–circle intersections and chords recur (Jan 2024 Q3, Jan 2020 Q6, Jun 2022 Q10); P2 has not yet set a circle in a modelling context, and a closest-approach distance is rarely tested.
