items.name: Equation of a circle
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P2.3.1 - Coordinate geometry of the c
items.question: The circle $C_1$ has equation $$x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 2y - 20 = 0$$ and centre $A$. The circle $C_2$ has equation $$(x - 16)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 125$$ and centre $B$. The circles meet at the points $P$ and $Q$, as shown in the diagram. Find the coordinates of $A$ and the radius of $C_1$. Show that $P$ and $Q$ lie on the line with equation $7x + y = 40$. Hence find the coordinates of $P$ and $Q$. Find the area of the quadrilateral $APBQ$.
items.ms: Attempts $(x - 2)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = \ldots$ $A(2,\ 1)$ Radius $5$ Expands $C_2$ to $x^2 + y^2 - 32x - 6y + 140 = 0$ and subtracts one circle equation from the other $28x + 4y - 160 = 0 \Rightarrow 7x + y = 40$, with a reason, e.g. a point on both circles satisfies both equations and so satisfies their difference Substitutes $y = 40 - 7x$ into $C_1$ (or $C_2$) $50x^2 - 550x + 1500 = 0$, i.e. $x^2 - 11x + 30 = 0$ $(5,\ 5)$ and $(6,\ -2)$ A complete method, e.g. $\tfrac{1{2 \times AB \times PQ$ (the diagonals are perpendicular, as $AB$ is the perpendicular bisector of the common chord $PQ$) with $AB = \sqrt{200$ and $PQ = \sqrt{50$; or triangles $APB$ and $AQB$; or the shoelace formula $50$
items.why: Two circles appear in recent papers (touching circles in Jan 2026 Q5 and Oct 2025 Q6(b)); intersecting circles and their common chord, found by subtracting the equations, have never been asked and are the natural next step.
keywords: Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 - 7x + 6$$ where $a$ is a constant. When $\mathrm{f(x)$ is divided by $(x - 2)$ the remainder is the same as the remainder when $\mathrm{f(x)$ is divided by $(x + 1)$. Use the remainder theorem to find the value of $a$. Find the remainder when $\mathrm{f(x)$ is divided by $(2x + 1)$.
items.ms: Attempts $\mathrm{f(2) = \mathrm{f(-1)$: $16 + 4a - 14 + 6 = -2 + a + 7 + 6$ $a = 1$ Attempts $\mathrm{f\left(-\tfrac{1{2\right)$ with their value of $a$ Remainder $= \dfrac{19{2$
items.why: P2.2.1 has come up in all 22 sessions; a remainder condition linking two divisors was set in Jan 2022 Q5, and remainders on dividing by (ax + b) recur (Jun 2025 Q4, Oct 2022 Q2).

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^3 - x^2 + 5x - 12$$ Use the factor theorem to show that $(2x - 3)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f(x)$. Hence show that the equation $\mathrm{f(x) = 0$ has only one real root. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.
items.ms: Attempts $\mathrm{f\left(\tfrac{3{2\right) = 2\left(\tfrac{27{8\right) - \tfrac{9{4 + \tfrac{15{2 - 12$ $= 0$, so $(2x - 3)$ is a factor Divides by $(2x - 3)$ or compares coefficients to reach $(2x - 3)(x^2 + \alpha x + \beta)$ $x^2 + x + 4$ Attempts the discriminant of their quadratic factor: $1^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 4$ $= -15 < 0$, so $x^2 + x + 4 = 0$ has no real roots and the only real root is $x = \tfrac{3{2$
items.why: Showing that f(x) = 0 has only one real root was asked in Oct 2025 (twice), Jun 2023 and Oct 2021, so it is the likeliest repeat; a factor of the form (2x − 3) tests the (ax − b) case named in the spec.

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 4x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 9$$ where $k$ is a constant. When $\mathrm{f(x)$ is divided by $(2x - 1)$ the remainder is $5$. Show that $k = -8$. Using algebra, find the quotient and the remainder when $\mathrm{f(x)$ is divided by $(x + 2)$.
items.ms: Attempts $\mathrm{f\left(\tfrac{1{2\right) = 5$: $\tfrac{1{2 + \tfrac{k{4 - \tfrac{5{2 + 9 = 5$ $k = -8$ with no errors Long division (or comparing coefficients) by $(x + 2)$ reaching $4x^2 + \alpha x + \ldots$ $4x^2 - 16x + \ldots$ Quotient $4x^2 - 16x + 27$ Remainder $-45$
items.why: A remainder condition followed by a full division for the quotient and remainder was asked in Jan 2026 Q4, Jun 2025 Q3 and Q4, and Oct 2024 Q3; the divisor (2x − 1) checks that the remainder theorem is used at x = 1/2.

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = (x + 1)(2x^2 - x + k) + 18$$ where $k$ is a constant. Write down the remainder when $\mathrm{f(x)$ is divided by $(x + 1)$. Given that $(x - 2)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f(x)$, show that $k = -12$. Hence, using algebra, factorise $\mathrm{f(x)$ completely.
items.ms: $18$ Sets $\mathrm{f(2) = 0$: $3(8 - 2 + k) + 18 = 0$ $k = -12$ with no errors Expands to a cubic: $\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^3 + x^2 - 13x + 6$ Divides their cubic by $(x - 2)$ (or compares coefficients) to obtain a quadratic factor $2x^2 + 5x - 3$ $(x - 2)(2x - 1)(x + 3)$
items.why: Reading a remainder from f(x) written as (divisor) × (quadratic) + constant recurs (Jun 2025 Q3, Oct 2021 Q4, Oct 2019 Q4); with the factor theorem and full factorisation it matches the 7–9 mark P2.2.1 questions.

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 7x + 6$$ Use the factor theorem to show that $(x - 2)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f(x)$. Hence factorise $\mathrm{f(x)$ completely. Hence solve the equation $$2(8^t) - 9(4^t) + 7(2^t) + 6 = 0$$ giving any answer that is not exact to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: Attempts $\mathrm{f(2) = 16 - 36 + 14 + 6$ $= 0$, so $(x - 2)$ is a factor Divides by $(x - 2)$ or compares coefficients to reach $2x^2 + \alpha x + \beta$ $2x^2 - 5x - 3$ $(x - 2)(2x + 1)(x - 3)$ Recognises $8^t = (2^t)^3$ and $4^t = (2^t)^2$, so the equation is $\mathrm{f(2^t) = 0$ and $2^t = 2,\ -\tfrac{1{2$ or $3$ $t = 1$ $t = \log_2 3 = 1.58$, with $2^t = -\tfrac{1{2$ rejected because $2^t > 0$
items.why: Turning a log equation into a cubic was asked in May 2024 Q9 and Jun 2021 Q7; an exponential equation that becomes a cubic in 2^t (P2.5.1, P2.5.3) has not been set.

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^4 + ax^3 - 12x^2 + bx + 6$$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants. Given that $(x - 1)$ and $(x + 2)$ are both factors of $\mathrm{f(x)$, find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$, hence factorise $\mathrm{f(x)$ completely.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f(1) = 0$: $2 + a - 12 + b + 6 = 0$, i.e. $a + b = 4$ $\mathrm{f(-2) = 0$: $32 - 8a - 48 - 2b + 6 = 0$, i.e. $4a + b = -5$ Solves their two linear equations simultaneously $a = -3$ and $b = 7$ Divides $\mathrm{f(x)$ by $(x - 1)$ and then the quotient by $(x + 2)$, or divides by $x^2 + x - 2$, or compares coefficients Quadratic factor $2x^2 - 5x - 3$ Attempts to factorise their quadratic factor $\mathrm{f(x) = (x - 1)(x + 2)(x - 3)(2x + 1)$
items.why: Two unknown coefficients from two factor or remainder conditions is a regular 7–9 mark question (Oct 2023 Q4, Jan 2023 Q5, Jan 2025 Q5); a quartic was last used in Jan 2021 Q1, so a quartic with two known factors is the likeliest stretch.

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 2x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 2$$ Use the factor theorem to show that $(x + 2)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f(x)$. Hence factorise $\mathrm{f(x)$ completely. Show that the equation $$\cos^2\theta - 3\cos\theta + 2 = 2\cos\theta\sin^2\theta$$ can be written in the form $\mathrm{f(\cos\theta) = 0$. Hence solve, for $0 \leqslant \theta < 360^\circ$, $$\cos^2\theta - 3\cos\theta + 2 = 2\cos\theta\sin^2\theta$$
items.ms: Attempts $\mathrm{f(-2) = -16 + 4 + 10 + 2$ $= 0$, so $(x + 2)$ is a factor Divides by $(x + 2)$ or compares coefficients to reach $2x^2 + \alpha x + \beta$ $2x^2 - 3x + 1$ $(x + 2)(2x - 1)(x - 1)$ Uses $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$: $\cos^2\theta - 3\cos\theta + 2 = 2\cos\theta - 2\cos^3\theta$ Rearranges to $2\cos^3\theta + \cos^2\theta - 5\cos\theta + 2 = 0$, i.e. $\mathrm{f(\cos\theta) = 0$ Uses (b) to get $\cos\theta = \tfrac{1{2$ or $\cos\theta = 1$ and finds at least one correct angle $\theta = 0^\circ,\ 60^\circ,\ 300^\circ$ only
items.why: P2.2.1 cubics are usually set on their own; a trigonometric equation that reduces to a cubic in cos θ through sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 (P2.6.1, P2.6.2) has never been asked and is a plausible synoptic long question.

items.name: Algebraic division, factor and remainder theorems
items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $y = x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x + 9$ and the line $l$ has equation $y = 2x + 3$. The diagram shows $C$ and $l$, which meet at the points $A(-1,\ 1)$, $B$ and $D$. The finite region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$ and $l$ between $A$ and $B$. Show that the $x$-coordinates of $A$, $B$ and $D$ satisfy the equation $$x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 6 = 0$$ Hence, using algebra, find the coordinates of $B$ and the coordinates of $D$. Use algebraic integration to find the exact area of $R$.
items.ms: Sets $x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x + 9 = 2x + 3$ and rearranges to the given equation Uses $(x + 1)$ as a factor (from $A$) and divides: $x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 6 = (x + 1)(x^2 + \alpha x + \beta)$ $x^2 - 5x + 6$ Solves their quadratic and substitutes into $l$ (or $C$) $B(2,\ 7)$ and $D(3,\ 9)$ Area $= \displaystyle\int-12 \left[(x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x + 9) - (2x + 3)\right] \mathrm{dx$, or the area under $C$ minus the area of the trapezium under $l$ Integrates, raising at least two powers by one $\dfrac{x^4{4 - \dfrac{4x^3{3 + \dfrac{x^2{2 + 6x$ (or $\dfrac{x^4{4 - \dfrac{4x^3{3 + \dfrac{3x^2{2 + 9x$ for the curve alone) Substitutes the limits $2$ and $-1$ (their $x$ at $B$) and subtracts $\dfrac{45{4$
items.why: Intersections of a cubic with another graph by the factor theorem were asked in Oct 2020 Q6, and a cubic with a factor condition and an integral in Jun 2022 Q7; this joins both with the area between a curve and a line (P2.8.1, P2.8.2).

items.name: y = ax and its graph
path: P2.5.1 - y  ax and its graph
items.question: The figure shows a sketch of the curve $C_1$ with equation $$y = ka^x$$ where $k$ and $a$ are positive constants. The points $A(-1,\ 20)$ and $B(2,\ 2.5)$ lie on $C_1$. Find the value of $k$ and the value of $a$. On the figure, sketch the curve $C_2$ with equation $y = 2^x + 3$. On your sketch, show the coordinates of the point where $C_2$ crosses the $y$-axis and state the equation of the asymptote to $C_2$. The curves $C_1$ and $C_2$ meet at the point $P$. Using algebra, find the coordinates of $P$.
items.ms: Substitutes both points to form two equations, $20 = ka-1$ and $2.5 = ka2$, and eliminates $k$, e.g. $a^3 = \dfrac{2.5{20 = \dfrac{1{8$ $a = \dfrac{1{2$ $k = 10$ Correct shape: an increasing curve lying entirely above the line $y = 3$, approaching it as $x \to -\infty$ and crossing $C_1$ once $C_2$ crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,\ 4)$ Asymptote $y = 3$ stated or labelled Sets $10\left(\dfrac{1{2\right)^x = 2^x + 3$, writes $\left(\dfrac{1{2\right)^x$ as $2-x$ or $\dfrac{1{2^x$ and multiplies through by $2^x$ to obtain a three-term quadratic in $2^x$ $\left(2^x\right)^2 + 3\left(2^x\right) - 10 = 0$ oe, e.g. $u^2 + 3u - 10 = 0$ where $u = 2^x$ Solves their quadratic and finds $x$ from a positive root: $(u + 5)(u - 2) = 0 \Rightarrow 2^x = 2$ $P(1,\ 5)$ only
items.why: P2.5.1 is warm (10 of 22 sessions, last Jun 2026) and sketches of y = a^x + c with intercept and asymptote recur (Jun 2021, Jun 2026); finding k and a from two points on the curve and turning (1/2)^x into 2^(-x) for a hidden quadratic is a fresh combination of the same skills.

items.name: Laws of logarithms
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Using the laws of logarithms, solve $$2\log_3(x - 1) = 2 + \log_3(x - 3)$$
items.ms: Uses a law of logarithms correctly, e.g. $2\log_3(x - 1) = \log_3(x - 1)^2$ or $\log_3(x - 1)^2 - \log_3(x - 3) = \log_3\dfrac{(x - 1)^2{x - 3$ Uses $2 = \log_3 9$ (or $3^2 = 9$) with correct laws to remove the logarithms, reaching $(x - 1)^2 = 9(x - 3)$ oe Expands and solves the resulting three-term quadratic, $x^2 - 11x + 28 = 0$ $x = 4$ and $x = 7$
items.why: P2.5.2 has come up in 21 of 22 sessions and a log equation solved with the laws of logarithms was set in Oct 2024, Jun 2025, Oct 2025 and Jun 2026; here both roots are valid, which tests the domain check rather than a reflex rejection.

items.name: Laws of logarithms
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Show that the equation $$\log_2(x + 4) + 2\log_2 x = 3 + \log_2(x + 1)$$ can be written as $$x^3 + 4x^2 - 8x - 8 = 0$$ Show that $x = 2$ is a root of $x^3 + 4x^2 - 8x - 8 = 0$ and find the other two roots, giving them in the form $p \pm \sqrt{q$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers. Hence solve $$\log_2(x + 4) + 2\log_2 x = 3 + \log_2(x + 1)$$ giving a reason for rejecting any values.
items.ms: Uses the power law: $2\log_2 x = \log_2 x^2$ Uses $3 = \log_2 8$ and the addition law to write each side as a single logarithm and removes the logarithms: $x^2(x + 4) = 8(x + 1)$ Expands and rearranges to $x^3 + 4x^2 - 8x - 8 = 0$ Substitutes $x = 2$: $8 + 16 - 16 - 8 = 0$, so $x = 2$ is a root Divides by $(x - 2)$ or compares coefficients to obtain the quadratic factor $x^2 + 6x + 4$ Solves $x^2 + 6x + 4 = 0$: $x = -3 \pm \sqrt{5$ $x = 2$ only, with a reason: $-3 \pm \sqrt{5$ are both negative, so $\log_2 x$ is not defined for them
items.why: Jan 2024 Q6 turned a log equation into a cubic; P2.5.2 has come up in 21 of 22 sessions and the long log questions regularly bring in the factor theorem and a check of which roots are valid.

items.name: Laws of logarithms
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Given that $x > 0$ and $y > 0$, solve the simultaneous equations $$\log_2 x + \log_2 y = 5$$ $$\log_2(x + y) = 2 + \log_2 3$$ Using the change of base formula, or otherwise, solve $$\log_5 t + 6\log_t 5 = 5, \qquad t > 0,\ t \neq 1$$
items.ms: Uses the addition law and removes the logarithm in the first equation: $xy = 2^5 = 32$ Uses $2 = \log_2 4$ and the addition law in the second equation: $x + y = 12$ Eliminates one variable to form a three-term quadratic and solves it, e.g. $x(12 - x) = 32 \Rightarrow x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0$ $x = 4,\ y = 8$ and $x = 8,\ y = 4$ Uses $\log_t 5 = \dfrac{1{\log_5 t$, or writes both terms in a common base, e.g. $\log_t 5 = \dfrac{\log 5{\log t$ $\left(\log_5 t\right)^2 - 5\log_5 t + 6 = 0$ oe Solves their quadratic and undoes the logarithm: $\log_5 t = 2$ or $3 \Rightarrow t = 5^2$ or $5^3$ $t = 25$ and $t = 125$
items.why: Simultaneous log equations were set in Jan 2026; the 5.3 guidance allows the change of base formula, but no recent P2 question has needed log_t 5 = 1/log_5 t, so a reciprocal-log quadratic is the likeliest surprise.

items.name: Laws of logarithms
items.question: The sound level, $L$ decibels, of a sound of intensity $I$ watts per square metre is modelled by the equation $$L = 10\log10\left(\dfrac{I{I_0\right)$$ where $I_0 = 1 \times 10-12$ A vacuum cleaner produces a sound of intensity $3.2 \times 10-5$ watts per square metre. Find, according to the model, the sound level of the vacuum cleaner, giving your answer to 3 significant figures. Show that, according to the model, doubling the intensity of a sound increases its sound level by approximately 3 decibels. A workshop has a number of identical machines. When one machine is running on its own, the sound level is 77 decibels. When several of the machines run at the same time, the total intensity is the sum of the intensities from each machine. A safety rule requires the sound level in the workshop to be no more than 85 decibels. Using the model, find the greatest number of these machines that can run at the same time.
items.ms: Substitutes: $L = 10\log10\left(\dfrac{3.2 \times 10-5{1 \times 10-12\right) = 10\log10\left(3.2 \times 107\right)$ $L = 75.1$ decibels Writes the increase as $10\log10\left(\dfrac{2I{I_0\right) - 10\log10\left(\dfrac{I{I_0\right)$ oe Uses a law of logarithms to obtain $10\log10 2$ $10\log10 2 = 3.010\ldots \approx 3$ Finds the intensity of one machine, $I_1 = 107.7 \times 10-12 = 10-4.3$ $\left(= 5.01 \times 10-5\right)$, or writes the level for $n$ machines as $10\log10\left(\dfrac{nI_1{I_0\right)$ Uses a law of logarithms to form $77 + 10\log10 n \leqslant 85$, or forms $n \times 10-4.3 \leqslant 10-3.5$ Solves to obtain $n \leqslant 100.8 = 6.31\ldots$ 6 machines
items.why: Log models in context were set in Jan 2026 (heart rate) and Jun 2022; the base-10 decibel model tests the addition and subtraction laws in context, and a greatest-whole-number answer from a log inequality has not been asked.

items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Find the exact solution of the equation $$43x - 1 = 24$$ giving your answer in the form $a + b\log_2 3$, where $a$ and $b$ are rational constants to be found. The figure shows part of the curve with equation $$y = 32x + 1 - 17 \times 3^x + 10$$ The curve crosses the $x$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$. Using algebra, find the $x$ coordinates of $A$ and $B$, giving your answers to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: Takes logs of both sides correctly or writes $43x - 1 = 26x - 2$: $6x - 2 = \log_2 24$ oe Uses $\log_2 24 = \log_2 8 + \log_2 3 = 3 + \log_2 3$ $x = \dfrac{5{6 + \dfrac{1{6\log_2 3$ Writes $32x + 1 = 3\left(3^x\right)^2$ and forms a three-term quadratic in $3^x$: $3u^2 - 17u + 10 = 0$ where $u = 3^x$ Solves the quadratic, $(3u - 2)(u - 5) = 0$, and uses logs to find $x$ from a value of $3^x$, e.g. $x = \log_3 5 = \dfrac{\log 5{\log 3$ $x = -0.369$ and $x = 1.46$
items.why: P2.5.3 has come up in 19 of 22 sessions; exact solutions in the form a + b log_2 3 were set in Jun 2019 and Jan 2026, and quadratics in a^x (Jun 2021, Jun 2025) remain the commonest way to examine it.

items.question: Two cultures of bacteria, $A$ and $B$, are grown in a laboratory. The number of bacteria in culture $A$, $t$ hours after the start of an experiment, is modelled by the equation $$N_A = 500 \times 1.6^t$$ The number of bacteria in culture $B$, $t$ hours after the start of the experiment, is modelled by the equation $$N_B = 2400 \times 1.25^t$$ The figure shows sketches of the graphs of $N_A$ and $N_B$ against $t$. Give an interpretation of the number 1.25 in the model for culture $B$. Find, according to the model, the time taken for the number of bacteria in culture $B$ to reach 6000. Give your answer in hours and minutes, to the nearest minute. Using algebra, find the set of values of $t$ for which culture $B$ contains more bacteria than culture $A$. Give the limits of your answer to 3 significant figures where appropriate. Give a reason why the model for culture $A$ may not be reliable for large values of $t$.
items.ms: The number of bacteria in culture $B$ increases by 25% every hour (is multiplied by 1.25 each hour) Sets $2400 \times 1.25^t = 6000$ and uses logs correctly: $t = \dfrac{\log 2.5{\log 1.25$ or $t = \log1.25 2.5$ $t = 4.106\ldots$ hours, i.e. 4 hours 6 minutes Forms $2400 \times 1.25^t > 500 \times 1.6^t$ (or the equation) and rearranges to $\left(\dfrac{1.6{1.25\right)^t < \dfrac{2400{500$, i.e. $1.28^t < 4.8$, or takes logs: $\log 2400 + t\log 1.25 > \log 500 + t\log 1.6$ Uses logs correctly to find the critical value: $t = \dfrac{\log 4.8{\log 1.28 = 6.3543\ldots$ $0 \leqslant t < 6.35$ The model predicts that the number of bacteria increases without limit, but in reality nutrients or space would run out, so the growth would slow down (or bacteria would die)
items.why: P2.5.3 has come up in 19 of 22 sessions, usually as 'find the time when the model reaches a value' (Jun 2022, Oct 2022, Jan 2024); comparing two exponential models and turning the result into an inequality has not been asked.

path: P2.1.1 - and use the structure of mat
items.question: Given that $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers, prove that $$\dfrac{a{b + \dfrac{b{a \ge 2$$ Show, by means of a counter-example, that the inequality in part (a) is not true for all non-zero real numbers $a$ and $b$. Hence prove that, for $0 < x < 90^\circ$, $$\tan x + \dfrac{1{\tan x \ge 2$$ Prove that, for all integers $n$, $n^3 - n$ is a multiple of 6.
items.ms: Starts from a true statement such as $(a - b)^2 \ge 0$, or considers $\dfrac{a{b + \dfrac{b{a - 2 = \dfrac{a^2 - 2ab + b^2{ab$ Obtains $a^2 + b^2 \ge 2ab$ and divides by $ab$, or writes $\dfrac{a{b + \dfrac{b{a - 2 = \dfrac{(a - b)^2{ab$ States that $ab > 0$ (so dividing keeps the inequality, or the fraction is $\ge 0$) and concludes that $\dfrac{a{b + \dfrac{b{a \ge 2$ A correct counter-example with $a$ and $b$ of opposite signs and a conclusion, e.g. $a = 1$, $b = -1$: $\dfrac{1{-1 + \dfrac{-1{1 = -2 < 2$ Writes $\tan x + \dfrac{1{\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x{\cos x + \dfrac{\cos x{\sin x$ and uses part (a) with $a = \sin x$, $b = \cos x$ (or with $a = \tan x$, $b = 1$) States that $\sin x > 0$ and $\cos x > 0$ (or $\tan x > 0$) for $0 < x < 90^\circ$, so the result of (a) applies, and concludes Factorises: $n^3 - n = n(n^2 - 1) = (n - 1)n(n + 1)$ Recognises the product of three consecutive integers Explains that at least one of three consecutive integers is even and one is a multiple of 3, so the product is a multiple of $2 \times 3 = 6$; conclusion
items.why: P2.1.1 came up in 12 of 22 sessions, as 'use algebra to prove' inequalities (Jun 2019, Jan 2021, Oct 2021) and number proofs (Jan 2026 Q6); checking that a result's conditions hold before using it (parts b and c) has not been asked.

items.name: Proof by exhaustion
items.question: Prove by exhaustion that the square of any integer that is not a multiple of 5 leaves a remainder of 1 or 4 when it is divided by 5. Hence prove that, if $n$ is an integer that is not a multiple of 5, then $n^4 - 1$ is a multiple of 5. Use part (a) to prove that no square number has 2, 3, 7 or 8 as its last digit.
items.ms: Writes every integer that is not a multiple of 5 in one of the forms $5k + 1$, $5k + 2$, $5k + 3$, $5k + 4$ (or $5k \pm 1$, $5k \pm 2$), where $k$ is an integer Squares at least one form correctly and writes it as a multiple of 5 plus a remainder, e.g. $(5k + 2)^2 = 25k^2 + 20k + 4 = 5(5k^2 + 4k) + 4$ All four cases correct: $(5k + 1)^2 = 5(5k^2 + 2k) + 1$, $(5k + 2)^2 = 5(5k^2 + 4k) + 4$, $(5k + 3)^2 = 5(5k^2 + 6k + 1) + 4$, $(5k + 4)^2 = 5(5k^2 + 8k + 3) + 1$ Conclusion: in every case the remainder is 1 or 4 Uses (a): $n^2 = 5m + 1$ or $n^2 = 5m + 4$ for some integer $m$, with $n^4 - 1 = (n^2 - 1)(n^2 + 1)$ (or squares again: $(5m + 1)^2 - 1$ and $(5m + 4)^2 - 1$) $n^2 - 1 = 5m$ or $n^2 + 1 = 5(m + 1)$, so $n^4 - 1$ is a multiple of 5 in both cases; conclusion A whole number with last digit $d$ can be written as $10q + d$, so a number ending in 2 or 7 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 5, and a number ending in 3 or 8 leaves remainder 3 The square of a multiple of 5 leaves remainder 0 and, by (a), every other square leaves remainder 1 or 4; so no square leaves remainder 2 or 3, and no square ends in 2, 3, 7 or 8
items.why: Proof by exhaustion came up in 10 of 22 sessions, recently by cases such as 3k + 1, 3k + 2 (Jun 2025 Q10) and by finite lists (Jun 2026 Q10); a 'hence' that turns remainders into last digits has not been asked.

items.name: Disproof by counter example
items.question: Show, by means of a counter-example, that the statement “if $n$ is a prime number, then $2^n - 1$ is a prime number” is not true. Show, by means of a counter-example, that the statement “if $x > y$, then $\dfrac{1{x < \dfrac{1{y$” is not true for all non-zero real numbers $x$ and $y$. Prove that, if $x > y > 0$, then $\dfrac{1{x < \dfrac{1{y$
items.ms: Evaluates $2^n - 1$ for a prime $n$ that gives a number that is not prime, e.g. $n = 11$: $211 - 1 = 2047$ Shows that $2047 = 23 \times 89$, so 2047 is not prime, and concludes that the statement is not true A correct counter-example with a conclusion, e.g. $x = 2$, $y = -1$: $\dfrac{1{2 > -1$ Considers $\dfrac{1{y - \dfrac{1{x = \dfrac{x - y{xy$ (or divides $x > y$ by the positive number $xy$) $x - y > 0$ and $xy > 0$, so $\dfrac{1{y - \dfrac{1{x > 0$, hence $\dfrac{1{x < \dfrac{1{y$; conclusion
items.why: Counter-examples came up in 10 of 22 sessions, usually on primes (Jan 2022, Jan 2024, Oct 2024 Q11); here several primes must be tested before one fails, and part (c) proves the corrected statement.

items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Find $$\int\cos x\sqrt{1+3\sin x\,\mathrm{dx$$ Use the substitution $u=\cos x$ to show that $$\int0\frac{\pi{4\dfrac{\sin3x{\cos2x\,\mathrm{dx=\dfrac{3\sqrt{2-4{2$$
items.ms: Uses $u=1+3\sin x$ with $\mathrm{du=3\cos x\,\mathrm{dx$, or works by inspection, to obtain the form $k(1+3\sin x)\frac{3{2$ $\dfrac{1{3\displaystyle\int u\frac{1{2\,\mathrm{du=\dfrac{1{3\times\dfrac{2{3u\frac{3{2$, or a correct unsimplified form in $x$ $\dfrac{2{9(1+3\sin x)\frac{3{2+c$ Uses $\mathrm{du=-\sin x\,\mathrm{dx$ and $\sin2x=1-\cos2x$ to obtain $\pm\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1-u2{u2\,\mathrm{du$ Correct integral with correct limits: $\displaystyle\int\frac{1{\sqrt{21\left(u-2-1\right)\mathrm{du$ or $-\displaystyle\int1\frac{1{\sqrt{2\left(u-2-1\right)\mathrm{du$ Integrates to the form $\dfrac{\alpha{u+\beta u$ and applies the limits 1 and $\dfrac{1{\sqrt{2$ $(-1-1)-\left(-\sqrt{2-\dfrac{1{\sqrt{2\right)=\dfrac{3\sqrt{2{2-2=\dfrac{3\sqrt{2-4{2$ with no errors
items.why: Trigonometric substitutions were set in Jun 2025 (u = tan x) and Oct 2025 (u = 3 + cos θ); integrating by inspection (the spec calls substitution the reverse of the chain rule) is not among the 12 most recent P4.6.2 questions.

items.name: Integration by substitution and by parts
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y=x2\cos x,\qquad x\geqslant 0$$ The curve meets the positive $x$-axis for the first time at the point $A$. The region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$ and the $x$-axis between $O$ and $A$. In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Find $$\int x2\cos x\,\mathrm{dx$$ Hence find the exact area of $R$.
items.ms: Integrates by parts with $u=x2$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{dv{\mathrm{dx=\cos x$ to obtain the form $\alpha x2\sin x-\displaystyle\int\beta x\sin x\,\mathrm{dx$ $x2\sin x-\displaystyle\int 2x\sin x\,\mathrm{dx$ Integrates $\displaystyle\int x\sin x\,\mathrm{dx$ by parts to the form $\gamma x\cos x+\delta\sin x$ $\displaystyle\int 2x\sin x\,\mathrm{dx=-2x\cos x+2\sin x$ $x2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x+c$ $A$ is at $x=\dfrac{\pi{2$ (from $\cos x=0$) Substitutes the limits $\dfrac{\pi{2$ and 0 into their answer to (a) and subtracts $\dfrac{\pi2{4-2$
items.why: Repeated integration by parts is named in the spec and was set in Jan 2025 (Q5, x²e^{4x}) and Jun 2026 (Q7); a trigonometric version giving an exact area is the natural next form.

items.name: Integration by substitution and by parts
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y=\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\sin x,\qquad x\geqslant 0$$ The region $R1$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$ and the $x$-axis for $0\leqslant x\leqslant\pi$. The region $R2$, also shown shaded, is bounded by $C$ and the $x$-axis for $\pi\leqslant x\leqslant 2\pi$. In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Use integration by parts to show that $$\int\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\sin x\,\mathrm{dx=-\dfrac{2{5\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\left(\sin x+2\cos x\right)+c$$ Find the exact area of $R1$. Show that $$\dfrac{\text{area of R1{\text{area of R2=\mathrm{e\frac{\pi{2$$
items.ms: Integrates by parts once to the form $\alpha\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\cos x+\beta\displaystyle\int\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\cos x\,\mathrm{dx$ (or with $u=\sin x$: $\alpha\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\sin x+\beta\displaystyle\int\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\cos x\,\mathrm{dx$) e.g. $I=-\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\cos x-\dfrac{1{2\displaystyle\int\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\cos x\,\mathrm{dx$ Integrates by parts a second time, in the same direction, to return to a multiple of $I=\displaystyle\int\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\sin x\,\mathrm{dx$ e.g. $I=-\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\cos x-\dfrac{1{2\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\sin x-\dfrac{1{4I$ Collects the $I$ terms, $\dfrac{5{4I=-\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\left(\cos x+\dfrac{1{2\sin x\right)$, and reaches the given result with $+c$ Applies the limits $\pi$ and 0 to the result of (a) and subtracts $\dfrac{4{5\left(1+\mathrm{e-\frac{\pi{2\right)$ Evaluates $\displaystyle\int\pi2\pi\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2x\sin x\,\mathrm{dx=-\dfrac{4{5\left(\mathrm{e-\frac{\pi{2+\mathrm{e-\pi\right)$ and takes the area of $R2$ as its modulus Area of $R2=\dfrac{4{5\mathrm{e-\frac{\pi{2\left(1+\mathrm{e-\frac{\pi{2\right)$, so the ratio is $\mathrm{e\frac{\pi{2$
items.why: Cyclic integration by parts (e^x sin x in the spec) was set in Jun 2025 (Q9) and Jun 2026 (Q7); a region below the x-axis, whose area needs the modulus, has not been asked with it.

items.name: Integration by substitution and by parts
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Use the substitution $u=\sin x$ to show that $$\int0\frac{\pi{2\dfrac{\sin 2x{\sin2x+4\sin x+3\,\mathrm{dx=\int01\dfrac{2u{(u+1)(u+3)\,\mathrm{du$$ Express $\dfrac{2u{(u+1)(u+3)$ in partial fractions. Hence find the exact value of $$\int0\frac{\pi{2\dfrac{\sin 2x{\sin2x+4\sin x+3\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer in the form $\ln\left(\dfrac{p{q\right)$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers.
items.ms: $\dfrac{\mathrm{du{\mathrm{dx=\cos x$ (or $\mathrm{du=\cos x\,\mathrm{dx$) Uses $\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x$ and substitutes fully to obtain $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2u{u2+4u+3\,\mathrm{du$ (allow $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{ku{u2+4u+3\,\mathrm{du$) Factorises $u2+4u+3=(u+1)(u+3)$ and changes the limits: $x=0\Rightarrow u=0$ and $x=\dfrac{\pi{2\Rightarrow u=1$, reaching the given result with no errors Uses $2u\equiv A(u+3)+B(u+1)$ and substitutes $u=-1$ and $u=-3$, or compares coefficients, to find $A$ or $B$ $\dfrac{3{u+3-\dfrac{1{u+1$ Integrates $\dfrac{A{u+1+\dfrac{B{u+3$ to $\alpha\ln(u+1)+\beta\ln(u+3)$ $3\ln(u+3)-\ln(u+1)$; ft their $A$ and $B$ Applies the limits 1 and 0 and uses the laws of logarithms correctly to combine into a single logarithm $\ln\left(\dfrac{32{27\right)$
items.why: A given substitution leading to partial fractions was set in Jan 2026 (Q4, u = e^x + 4) and partial fractions met parts in Jan 2025 (Q5); u = sin x, which first needs sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x, is the trigonometric variant.

items.name: Integration by substitution and by parts
items.question: The curve $C$ has parametric equations $$x=t2,\qquad y=t\ln t,\qquad t>0$$ The diagram shows part of $C$. The curve crosses the $x$-axis at the point $A$. The region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$, the $x$-axis and the line with equation $x=\mathrm{e2$. In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Find the exact coordinates of the point on $C$ at which the tangent to $C$ is parallel to the $x$-axis. Show that the area of $R$ is given by $$\int1\mathrm{e2t2\ln t\,\mathrm{dt$$ Hence, using integration by parts, find the exact area of $R$, giving your answer in the form $\dfrac{a\mathrm{e3+b{9$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
items.ms: Attempts $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx=\dfrac{\mathrm{dy/\mathrm{dt{\mathrm{dx/\mathrm{dt$ with the product rule for $t\ln t$: $\dfrac{\ln t+1{2t$ Sets $\ln t+1=0$ to obtain $t=\mathrm{e-1$ $\left(\mathrm{e-2,\,-\mathrm{e-1\right)$ Uses area $=\displaystyle\int y\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt\,\mathrm{dt=\displaystyle\int t\ln t\times 2t\,\mathrm{dt$ Justifies the limits: $t=1$ at $A$ (where $y=0$) and $t=\mathrm{e$ from $t2=\mathrm{e2$ with $t>0$, with no errors Integrates by parts with $u=\ln t$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{dv{\mathrm{dt=2t2$ to obtain the form $\alpha t3\ln t-\displaystyle\int\beta t2\,\mathrm{dt$ $\dfrac{2{3t3\ln t-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2{3t2\,\mathrm{dt$ $\dfrac{2{3t3\ln t-\dfrac{2{9t3$ Applies the limits $\mathrm{e$ and 1 and subtracts $\dfrac{4\mathrm{e3+2{9$
items.why: Areas under parametric curves that need a further technique were set in Oct 2025 (Q6) and Jan 2026 (Q7); a t^n ln t integrand (Jan 2026 Q2 used x³ ln(x/2)) has not yet appeared in a parametric area.

items.name: Integration by substitution and by parts
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Use the substitution $u=\sqrt{\mathrm{ex+1$ to find the exact value of $$\int0\ln 3\dfrac{\mathrm{e2x{\sqrt{\mathrm{ex+1\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer in the form $\dfrac{a+b\sqrt{2{3$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Find $$\int x\sec2x\,\mathrm{dx$$ Hence find the exact value of $$\int0\frac{\pi{4x\tan2x\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer in the form $a\pi+b\pi2+c\ln 2$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are rational constants.
items.ms: $2u\dfrac{\mathrm{du{\mathrm{dx=\mathrm{ex$, or $\mathrm{dx=\dfrac{2u{u2-1\,\mathrm{du$ Substitutes fully, using $\mathrm{ex=u2-1$, to obtain an integral in $u$ only $\displaystyle\int 2\left(u2-1\right)\mathrm{du$ Limits $\sqrt{2$ and 2 Integrates to the form $\alpha u3+\beta u$ and applies their limits $\dfrac{4+2\sqrt{2{3$ Integrates by parts with $u=x$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{dv{\mathrm{dx=\sec2x$ to obtain $x\tan x-\displaystyle\int\tan x\,\mathrm{dx$ $\displaystyle\int\tan x\,\mathrm{dx=\ln|\sec x|$ (or $-\ln|\cos x|$) $x\tan x-\ln|\sec x|+c$ Uses $\tan2x=\sec2x-1$ to write the integral as $\displaystyle\int x\sec2x\,\mathrm{dx-\displaystyle\int x\,\mathrm{dx$ $x\tan x-\ln|\sec x|-\dfrac{1{2x2$; ft their (b) Applies the limits $\dfrac{\pi{4$ and 0, using $\tan\dfrac{\pi{4=1$ and $\sec\dfrac{\pi{4=\sqrt{2$ $\dfrac{\pi{4-\dfrac{\pi2{32-\dfrac{1{2\ln 2$
items.why: Two-integral questions of 10–13 marks were set in Jan 2025 (Q5) and Jun 2026 (Q7); x tan² x, which needs an identity before parts, has not been asked and is the likeliest surprise.

items.name: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Given that $$\dfrac{5x+3{(x+1)(2x+1)\equiv\dfrac{2{x+1+\dfrac{1{2x+1$$ use algebraic integration to find the exact value of $$\int04\dfrac{5x+3{(x+1)(2x+1)\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer in the form $\ln k$, where $k$ is an integer.
items.ms: Integrates to the form $\alpha\ln(x+1)+\beta\ln(2x+1)$ $2\ln(x+1)+\dfrac{1{2\ln(2x+1)$ Substitutes $x=4$ and $x=0$, subtracts and combines logs to reach $\ln 75$
items.why: P4.6.3 has come up in 15 of 21 sessions; a pair of linear partial fractions integrated to a single log (Oct 2022 Q2, Jun 2023 Q3) is its commonest form and a typical opening question.

items.name: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x)=\dfrac{4{x2-4,\qquad x>2$$ In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Express $\mathrm{f(x)$ in partial fractions. Given that $$\int3a\mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx=\ln 3$$ where $a$ is a constant with $a>3$, use algebraic integration to find the value of $a$.
items.ms: Factorises $x2-4=(x-2)(x+2)$ and uses a correct method for one constant, e.g. cover-up or $4\equiv A(x+2)+B(x-2)$ $\dfrac{1{x-2-\dfrac{1{x+2$ Integrates their partial fractions to $\alpha\ln(x-2)+\beta\ln(x+2)$ Substitutes the limits $a$ and $3$, combines the logs and sets equal to $\ln 3$ to obtain an equation without logs, e.g. $\dfrac{5(a-2){a+2=3$ $a=8$
items.why: Finding an unknown limit from a log integral has been asked only once (Jun 2023 Q3(c)); here the student must also spot the difference of two squares before splitting.

items.name: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x)=\dfrac{4x2+x+1{(x-1)(2x+1),\qquad x>1$$ Express $\mathrm{f(x)$ in the form $$A+\dfrac{B{x-1+\dfrac{C{2x+1$$ where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are constants to be found. Hence find $$\int\mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx$$
items.ms: $A=2$ (by division or by comparing coefficients of $x2$) Correct method for $B$ or $C$, e.g. $4x2+x+1\equiv A(x-1)(2x+1)+B(2x+1)+C(x-1)$ and substitutes $x=1$ or $x=-\dfrac{1{2$ $B=2$ and $C=-1$ Integrates $\dfrac{B{x-1\to B\ln(x-1)$ or $\dfrac{C{2x+1\to k\ln(2x+1)$ Two of $2x$, $2\ln(x-1)$, $-\dfrac{1{2\ln(2x+1)$ correct (ft their constants) $2x+2\ln(x-1)-\dfrac{1{2\ln(2x+1)+c$
items.why: An improper fraction (numerator of equal degree) split and then integrated was set in both of the last two sessions (Jan 2026 Q4, Jun 2026 Q2).

items.name: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x)=\dfrac{18{9x-x3,\qquad 0<x<3$$ In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Express $\mathrm{f(x)$ in partial fractions. Hence, using algebraic integration, find the exact value of $$\int12\mathrm{f(x)\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer in the form $\ln k$, where $k$ is a rational constant.
items.ms: Factorises fully: $9x-x3=x(3-x)(3+x)$ Correct method for at least one constant, e.g. $18\equiv A(3-x)(3+x)+Bx(3+x)+Cx(3-x)$ with a suitable value of $x$ $\dfrac{2{x+\dfrac{1{3-x-\dfrac{1{3+x$ Integrates to at least two of $\alpha\ln x$, $\beta\ln(3-x)$, $\gamma\ln(3+x)$ $2\ln x-\ln(3-x)-\ln(3+x)$ (ft their constants) Substitutes $x=2$ and $x=1$, subtracts and uses log laws to combine into a single log $\ln\dfrac{32{5$
items.why: Three linear factors were last set in Jun 2025 Q4; here the cubic must be factorised first and the factor (3 − x) carries the sign trap that the mark schemes flag.

items.name: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions
items.question: $$\dfrac{5x+7{(x+1)2(x+3)\equiv\dfrac{A{x+1+\dfrac{B{(x+1)2+\dfrac{C{x+3$$ In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Find the values of the constants $A$, $B$ and $C$. Hence, using algebraic integration, find the exact value of $$\int03\dfrac{5x+7{(x+1)2(x+3)\,\mathrm{dx$$ giving your answer in the form $p+\ln q$, where $p$ and $q$ are rational constants.
items.ms: $B=1$ (cover-up or substituting $x=-1$) Correct method for $A$ or $C$, e.g. $5x+7\equiv A(x+1)(x+3)+B(x+3)+C(x+1)2$ with $x=-3$, or comparing coefficients $A=2$ and $C=-2$ Integrates $\dfrac{A{x+1\to A\ln(x+1)$ and $\dfrac{C{x+3\to C\ln(x+3)$ Integrates $\dfrac{B{(x+1)2\to-\dfrac{B{x+1$ $2\ln(x+1)-\dfrac{1{x+1-2\ln(x+3)$ (ft their $A$, $B$, $C$) Substitutes $x=3$ and $x=0$, subtracts and applies log laws (depends on both M marks) $\dfrac{3{4+\ln 4$
items.why: A repeated linear factor followed by an exact answer of the form p + ln q was set in Jan 2024 Q2 and Jun 2025 Q7, and the non-log term is where marks are lost.

items.name: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y=\dfrac{4\sqrt{x{x+1,\qquad x\geqslant 0$$ The region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$, the $x$-axis and the line with equation $x=3$. The region $R$ is rotated through $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis to form a solid of revolution, which is used to model a wooden spinning top. The units are centimetres. In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Express $\dfrac{16x{(x+1)2$ in partial fractions. Hence, using algebraic integration, show that the volume of the spinning top is $(32\ln 2-12)\pi$ cm³. A larger spinning top is modelled by rotating, through $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis, the region bounded by the curve with equation $y=\dfrac{4k\sqrt{x{x+1$, where $k$ is a positive constant, the $x$-axis and the line $x=3$. The larger top has volume 40 cm³. Find the value of $k$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: Uses the form $\dfrac{P{x+1+\dfrac{Q{(x+1)2$ with a correct method for one constant $\dfrac{16{x+1-\dfrac{16{(x+1)2$ Uses $V=\pi\displaystyle\int03y2\,\mathrm{dx$ with $y2=\dfrac{16x{(x+1)2$ Integrates their partial fractions to $\alpha\ln(x+1)+\dfrac{\beta{x+1$ $16\ln(x+1)+\dfrac{16{x+1$ Substitutes $x=3$ and $x=0$ and subtracts: $\pi\left[(16\ln 4+4)-(0+16)\right]$ $(32\ln 2-12)\pi$ with $16\ln 4=32\ln 2$ seen Uses volume $=k2\times(32\ln 2-12)\pi=40$ $k=1.12$
items.why: Volumes of revolution (P4.6.1) came up in all 21 sessions and a rational y² has had to be split before (Oct 2024 Q7, by division); a repeated-factor partial fraction for y² and a rescaled solid are new.

items.name: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions
items.question: The diagram shows part of the curve $C$ with equation $$y=\dfrac{3{x+3\sqrt{x+2,\qquad x>0$$ The region $R$, shown shaded, is bounded by $C$, the $x$-axis and the lines with equations $x=1$ and $x=9$. In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Use the substitution $u=\sqrt{x$ to show that the area of $R$ is given by $$\int13\dfrac{6u{(u+1)(u+2)\,\mathrm{du$$ Express $\dfrac{6u{(u+1)(u+2)$ in partial fractions. Hence find the exact area of $R$, giving your answer in the form $a\ln b$, where $a$ is an integer and $b$ is a rational number.
items.ms: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{du=2u$ or $\dfrac{\mathrm{du{\mathrm{dx=\dfrac{1{2\sqrt{x$ oe Substitutes fully: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{3{u2+3u+2\times 2u\,\mathrm{du$ Factorises $u2+3u+2=(u+1)(u+2)$ and reaches the given integrand with no errors Correct limits: $x=1\Rightarrow u=1$ and $x=9\Rightarrow u=3$ Correct method for one constant, e.g. $6u\equiv P(u+2)+Q(u+1)$ $\dfrac{12{u+2-\dfrac{6{u+1$ Integrates to $\alpha\ln(u+2)+\beta\ln(u+1)$ $12\ln(u+2)-6\ln(u+1)$ (ft their constants) Substitutes $u=3$ and $u=1$, subtracts and combines the logs $6\ln\dfrac{25{18$
items.why: A substitution that leads to partial fractions was set in Jun 2025 Q7 (an exponential substitution); a root substitution has not been used yet and is the natural variant.

items.name: First-order differential equations
items.question: Given that $y=0$ when $x=0$, solve the differential equation $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx=\mathrm{e2x-y$$ giving your answer in the form $y=\ln\left(\mathrm{f(x)\right)$.
items.ms: Separates the variables: $\displaystyle\int\mathrm{ey\,\mathrm{dy=\int\mathrm{e2x\,\mathrm{dx$ Integrates both sides to the form $\mathrm{ey=\alpha\mathrm{e2x+c$ Uses $x=0$, $y=0$ to find $c$: $1=\dfrac{1{2+c$, $c=\dfrac{1{2$ $y=\ln\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{e2x+1{2\right)$
items.why: P4.6.4 has come up in 17 of 21 sessions; a short separable equation with a particular solution (Jun 2025 Q3) often opens the paper, and e^(2x − y) tests the index law before separating.

items.name: First-order differential equations
items.question: Find $$\int x\mathrm{e2x\,\mathrm{dx$$ Hence find the particular solution of the differential equation $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx=\dfrac{x\mathrm{e2x{y,\qquad y>0$$ for which $y=2$ when $x=0$. Give your answer in the form $y2=\mathrm{g(x)$.
items.ms: Integration by parts the right way round: $\alpha x\mathrm{e2x-\beta\displaystyle\int\mathrm{e2x\,\mathrm{dx$ $\dfrac{1{2x\mathrm{e2x-\dfrac{1{4\mathrm{e2x+c$ Separates: $\displaystyle\int y\,\mathrm{dy=\int x\mathrm{e2x\,\mathrm{dx$ $\dfrac{1{2y2=$ their (a) $+\,c$ Substitutes $x=0$, $y=2$ to find $c$: $2=-\dfrac{1{4+c$, $c=\dfrac{9{4$ $y2=x\mathrm{e2x-\dfrac{1{2\mathrm{e2x+\dfrac{9{2$
items.why: Integration by parts (P4.6.2) came up in 18 of 21 sessions but none of the 12 recent P4.6.4 questions needed it inside a separable equation; Edexcel often joins the two with 'Hence'.

items.name: First-order differential equations
items.question: $$\cos2x\,\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx=y2\sin x,\qquad 0\leqslant x<\dfrac{\pi{2$$ Given that $y=1$ when $x=\dfrac{\pi{3$, solve the differential equation, giving your answer in the form $y=\mathrm{f(x)$. The solution in part (a) is valid only for $0\leqslant x<\alpha$. Explain why, and find the value of $\alpha$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: Separates: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1{y2\,\mathrm{dy=\int\dfrac{\sin x{\cos2x\,\mathrm{dx$ or $\displaystyle\int\sec x\tan x\,\mathrm{dx$ Integrates both sides to the forms $\dfrac{\alpha{y$ and $\beta\sec x$ (or $\dfrac{\beta{\cos x$) $-\dfrac{1{y=\sec x+c$ Substitutes $x=\dfrac{\pi{3$, $y=1$: $-1=2+c$, so $c=-3$ $y=\dfrac{1{3-\sec x$ $y$ is undefined (tends to infinity) when $3-\sec x=0$, i.e. when $\cos x=\dfrac{1{3$ $\alpha=1.23$
items.why: Trigonometric separable equations recur (Jun 2025 Q3 with cos²2x); the interval on which a solution is valid has never been asked and is a likely new angle.

items.name: First-order differential equations
items.question: A patient is given a medicine through a drip. The medicine enters the patient's bloodstream at a constant rate of 6 mg per hour. It is removed from the bloodstream at a rate proportional to the amount of medicine present. At time $t$ hours after the drip is started, the amount of medicine in the bloodstream is $x$ mg. When $x=8$, the amount of medicine in the bloodstream is increasing at a rate of 4 mg per hour. Show that $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt=\dfrac{24-x{4$$ Given that there is no medicine in the patient's bloodstream when the drip is started, solve the differential equation to find $x$ in terms of $t$. The medicine is effective when there is at least 15 mg of it in the bloodstream. Find, according to the model, how long after the drip is started the medicine becomes effective. Give your answer in hours and minutes, to the nearest minute.
items.ms: Forms $\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt=6-kx$ and substitutes $x=8$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt=4$ $k=\dfrac{1{4$, so $\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt=6-\dfrac{x{4=\dfrac{24-x{4$ Separates and integrates: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{4{24-x\,\mathrm{dx=\int 1\,\mathrm{dt$ to give $\alpha\ln(24-x)=t+c$ $-4\ln(24-x)=t+c$ Uses $t=0$, $x=0$ to find $c$ ($c=-4\ln 24$) and removes the logs correctly $x=24-24\mathrm{e-t/4$ Sets $15=24-24\mathrm{e-t/4$ and uses logs correctly: $t=4\ln\dfrac{8{3$ 3 hours 55 minutes
items.why: Inflow-outflow models of the form dx/dt = a − bx recur (Jun 2026 Q8 algae, Jun 2023 Q6 cooling); forming the equation from a rate statement (P4.5.2) is often the first part.

items.name: First-order differential equations
items.question: The number of fish in a lake varies with the seasons. The number of fish, $N$, in the lake $t$ months after the start of a year is modelled by the differential equation $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dN{\mathrm{dt=kN\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t{6\right)$$ where $k$ is a positive constant. At the start of the year there are 800 fish in the lake. Three months later there are 1000 fish in the lake. Solve the differential equation to show that $$N=800\left(\dfrac{5{4\right)\sin\left(\frac{\pi t{6\right)$$ Find the minimum number of fish in the lake predicted by the model. Find, according to the model, the length of time in each year for which there are more than 900 fish in the lake. Give your answer in months to 2 decimal places.

items.question: The diagram shows a container in the shape of an inverted right circular cone, with its axis vertical. Liquid flows out of the container through a small hole at the vertex. At time $t$ minutes, the depth of the liquid is $h$ cm and the volume of liquid in the container is $V$ cm³, where $$V=\dfrac{1{12\pi h3$$ The liquid flows out of the container at a rate that is proportional to $\sqrt{h$. Show that $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dh{\mathrm{dt=-\dfrac{\lambda{h\frac{3{2$$ where $\lambda$ is a positive constant. Initially the depth of the liquid is 16 cm. Ten minutes later the depth is 9 cm. Solve the differential equation to show that $$h\frac{5{2=1024-78.1t$$ Find, according to the model, the time taken for the container to empty completely, starting from when the depth is 16 cm. Give your answer in minutes and seconds, to the nearest second.
items.ms: $\dfrac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dt=-k\sqrt{h$ and $\dfrac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dh=\dfrac{1{4\pi h2$ Uses $\dfrac{\mathrm{dh{\mathrm{dt=\dfrac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dt\div\dfrac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dh$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{dh{\mathrm{dt=-\dfrac{4k{\pih-\frac{3{2$, so $\lambda=\dfrac{4k{\pi$ Separates: $\displaystyle\int h\frac{3{2\,\mathrm{dh=-\int\lambda\,\mathrm{dt$ Integrates to $\alpha h\frac{5{2=-\lambda t+c$ $\dfrac{2{5h\frac{5{2=-\lambda t+c$ Uses $t=0$, $h=16$ to give $c=409.6$ and $t=10$, $h=9$ to find $\lambda$ ($\lambda=31.24$) $h\frac{5{2=1024-78.1t$ Sets $h=0$: $t=\dfrac{1024{78.1$ 13 minutes 7 seconds
items.why: Connected rates leading to a separable model with two conditions (Jan 2025 Q4 water depth, Jan 2026 Q8 balloon) is the current pattern for the long differential-equation question.

items.question: A new phone app is launched. The number of people who have downloaded the app, $x$ thousand, $t$ days after the launch is modelled by the differential equation $$\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt=\dfrac{x(8-x){16$$ When $t=0$, $x=1$. Express $\dfrac{16{x(8-x)$ in partial fractions. Hence show that $$x=\dfrac{8{1+7\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2t$$ Find, according to the model, the time taken for the number of people who have downloaded the app to reach 6000. Give your answer in days to 1 decimal place. Use the differential equation to find, according to the model, the maximum rate at which the app is being downloaded. Give your answer in people per day.
items.ms: Correct method for one constant, e.g. $16\equiv P(8-x)+Qx$ $\dfrac{2{x+\dfrac{2{8-x$ Separates: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{16{x(8-x)\,\mathrm{dx=\int 1\,\mathrm{dt$ Integrates their partial fractions to $\alpha\ln x+\beta\ln(8-x)$ $2\ln x-2\ln(8-x)=t+c$ Uses $t=0$, $x=1$ to find $c$: $c=-2\ln 7$ Correct log work to $\dfrac{7x{8-x=\mathrm{e\frac{1{2t$ and rearranges to $x=\dfrac{8{1+7\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2t$ Substitutes $x=6$ and uses logs: $7\mathrm{e-\frac{1{2t=\dfrac{1{3$, so $t=2\ln 21$ $t=6.1$ days Recognises that $x(8-x)$ is greatest when $x=4$ (completing the square, symmetry or differentiation) $\dfrac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt=\dfrac{4\times 4{16=1$, so 1000 people per day
items.why: Partial fractions followed by a logistic-type separable model came up in Oct 2023, Oct 2024 and Oct 2025; reading the maximum rate from the differential equation itself has not been asked.

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$3x^2 - xy + 2y = 12$$ The point $P(2, 2)$ lies on $C$. In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$ in terms of $x$ and $y$. The normal to $C$ at $P$ meets the $y$-axis at the point $Q$. Find the $y$ coordinate of $Q$, giving your answer in the form $p + q\ln 2$, where $p$ and $q$ are rational numbers.
items.ms: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d{\mathrm{dx\left(2y\right) = 2y\ln 2\,\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$ Differentiates implicitly with the product rule on $xy$: $xy \to x\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx + y$ (and $3x^2 \to 6x$) Collects the terms in $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$ and factorises: $\left(2y\ln 2 - x\right)\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = y - 6x$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{6x - y{x - 2y\ln 2$ oe Substitutes $x = 2$, $y = 2$ into their $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$: $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{10{2 - 4\ln 2$ $\left(= \dfrac{5{1 - 2\ln 2\right)$ Normal gradient $-1 \div$ their gradient, $\dfrac{2\ln 2 - 1{5$, used with $(2, 2)$ and $x = 0$: $y - 2 = \dfrac{2\ln 2 - 1{5(0 - 2)$ $y = \dfrac{12{5 - \dfrac{4{5\ln 2$

items.question: The curve $C$ has equation $$2x^2 + xy - y^2 + 18 = 0$$ In this question you must show all stages of your working. items.ms: Differentiates implicitly with $-y^2 \to \pm\alpha y\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$ (and $2x^2 \to 4x$) $xy \to x\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx + y$ Collects the terms in $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx$ and factorises: $(x - 2y)\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = -(4x + y)$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{4x + y{2y - x$ oe Sets their $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 1$ and obtains a linear relation: $4x + y = 2y - x \Rightarrow y = 5x$ Substitutes into the equation of $C$: $2x^2 + 5x^2 - 25x^2 + 18 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 = 1$ $(1, 5)$ and $(-1, -5)$ Sets their $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 2$: $4x + y = 4y - 2x \Rightarrow y = 2x$, and substitutes into the equation of $C$ $2x^2 + 2x^2 - 4x^2 + 18 = 0$ gives $18 = 0$, which is impossible, so no tangent to $C$ has gradient 2 *

items.question: The diagram shows a sketch of the curve $C$ with equation $$\sin x\cos y = \frac{1{4, \quad 0 < x < \pi, \quad 0 \leqslant y < \frac{\pi{2$$ The point $P\left(\dfrac{\pi{6, \dfrac{\pi{3\right)$ lies on $C$. items.ms: Uses the product rule with the chain rule on $\cos y$: $\cos x\cos y \pm \sin x\sin y\,\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 0$ $\cos x\cos y - \sin x\sin y\,\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 0$ $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{\cos x\cos y{\sin x\sin y = \cot x\cot y$ * Gradient at $P$: $\cot\dfrac{\pi{6\cot\dfrac{\pi{3 = \sqrt{3\times\dfrac{1{\sqrt{3 = 1$ Correct straight-line method with their gradient and $P$: $y - \dfrac{\pi{3 = 1\left(x - \dfrac{\pi{6\right)$ $y = x + \dfrac{\pi{6$ Normal: gradient $-1 \div$ their $m$, through $P$: $y - \dfrac{\pi{3 = -\left(x - \dfrac{\pi{6\right)$, i.e. $y = \dfrac{\pi{2 - x$ Sets $y = 0$ in both lines: $A\left(-\dfrac{\pi{6, 0\right)$ and $B\left(\dfrac{\pi{2, 0\right)$ Area $= \dfrac{1{2\times AB\times\dfrac{\pi{3 = \dfrac{1{2\times\dfrac{2\pi{3\times\dfrac{\pi{3$ $\dfrac{\pi^2{9$
items.why: Implicit curves in past papers have mixed polynomial and exponential terms (Oct 2025, Jun 2025, Oct 2024); a trigonometric implicit equation, needing the product and chain rules together, has not been set, and a tangent–normal triangle is a typical follow-on.

Show that a Cartesian equation of $C$ is $$y^2 = (x - 1)^3$$ The finite region $R$, shown shaded in the diagram, is bounded by $C$ and the line with equation $x = 5$. Use calculus to find the exact area of $R$.
items.ms: Attempts $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dt \div \frac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt$ with $\frac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt = 2t$ and $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dt = 3t^2$ $\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \dfrac{3t{2$ At $t = 2$: $P(5, 8)$ and gradient $\dfrac{3\times 2{2 = 3$, with a correct straight-line method: $y - 8 = 3(x - 5)$ $y = 3x - 7$ * Substitutes $x = t^2 + 1$ and $y = t^3$ into $y = 3x - 7$: $t^3 - 3t^2 + 4 = 0$ Uses $(t - 2)$ as a factor (twice, or divides by $(t - 2)^2$): $(t - 2)^2(t + 1) = 0$ $t = -1$ $Q(2, -1)$ Uses $t^2 = x - 1$ with $y^2 = \left(t^3\right)^2 = \left(t^2\right)^3$ (or substitutes $t = y\frac{1{3$ into $x = t^2 + 1$) $y^2 = (x - 1)^3$ * Uses area $= \displaystyle\int y\,\frac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt\,\mathrm{dt = \int t^3(2t)\,\mathrm{dt$ $\displaystyle\int 2t^4\,\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{2t^5{5$ Applies the limits $t = 0$ and $t = 2$ (from $x = 1$ and $x = 5$) and doubles, as $R$ is symmetrical about the $x$-axis: $2\times\dfrac{64{5$ $\dfrac{128{5$
items.why: Long parametric questions where the tangent meets the curve again were set in Oct 2025 (Q8) and Jan 2025 (Q9); adding a Cartesian conversion and a parametric area, as the 14–15 mark P4 questions do, makes this the likeliest long shape.

items.name: Formation of simple differential equations
items.question: A spherical balloon is being inflated. At time $t$ seconds, the radius of the balloon is $r$ cm, its volume is $V$ cm³ and its surface area is $S$ cm². Air is pumped into the balloon at a constant rate of 250 cm³ s⁻¹. [The volume of a sphere is $V = \frac{4{3\pi r^3$ and its surface area is $S = 4\pi r^2$.] Find the rate at which the surface area of the balloon is increasing at the instant when the radius is 10 cm.
items.ms: $\frac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dr = 4\pi r^2$ and $\frac{\mathrm{dS{\mathrm{dr = 8\pi r$ $\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{250{4\pi r^2$; at $r = 10$, $\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{5{8\pi$ (0.199) Uses $\frac{\mathrm{dS{\mathrm{dt = \frac{\mathrm{dS{\mathrm{dr\times\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = 8\pi r\times\dfrac{250{4\pi r^2$ 50 cm² s⁻¹
items.why: Connected rates on a solid recur in P4.5.2 (Jan 2024 cone surface area, Jan 2022 icosahedron, Jan 2023 balloon radius); linking two rates through the radius, with the volume rate given, is the likeliest short form.

items.name: Formation of simple differential equations
items.question: A sweet is modelled as a sphere. At time $t$ minutes after the sweet is put into a person's mouth, its radius is $r$ mm and its volume is $V$ mm³. In the model, the sweet dissolves so that the rate of decrease of $V$ is proportional to the surface area of the sweet. [The volume of a sphere is $\frac{4{3\pi r^3$ and its surface area is $4\pi r^2$.] Show that $\dfrac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = -k$, where $k$ is a positive constant. The radius of the sweet decreases from 9 mm to 7.5 mm in the first 6 minutes. Find, according to the model, the time taken from when the sweet is put into the mouth until it has dissolved completely.
items.ms: Forms the differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dt = -\lambda\times 4\pi r^2$, $\lambda > 0$ (minus sign and a constant of proportionality) Uses the chain rule: $\frac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dt = \frac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dr\times\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = 4\pi r^2\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt$ $4\pi r^2\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = -4\pi\lambda r^2 \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = -\lambda$, a negative constant, so $\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = -k$ * Integrates: $r = 9 - kt$, and uses $r = 7.5$ when $t = 6$: $k = 0.25$ $r = 0 \Rightarrow t = 36$ minutes
items.why: P4.5.2 has come up in 11 of 21 sessions, mostly as connected rates; Oct 2022 Q10 stated the rate of change of the radius directly ('inversely proportional to $r^2$'), but deriving $\frac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}t}$ from a statement about the volume, through the chain rule, has not been asked.

items.name: Formation of simple differential equations
items.question: A ladder $AB$ of length 6.5 m has its end $A$ on horizontal ground and its end $B$ against a vertical wall, as shown in the diagram. The end $A$ slides away from the wall at a constant speed of 0.4 m s⁻¹, so that $B$ slides down the wall. At time $t$ seconds, $A$ is $x$ m from the foot of the wall, $B$ is $y$ m above the ground and the ladder makes an angle of $\theta$ radians with the ground. The ladder is modelled as a rod that stays in a vertical plane perpendicular to the wall. Find the speed at which $B$ is moving down the wall at the instant when $x = 2.5$ Find the rate at which $\theta$ is decreasing at this instant.
items.ms: $y = \sqrt{6.5^2 - 2.5^2 = 6$ when $x = 2.5$ Differentiates $x^2 + y^2 = 6.5^2$ with respect to $t$: $2x\frac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt + 2y\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dt = 0$, and substitutes $\frac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dt = -\dfrac{2.5\times 0.4{6 = -\dfrac{1{6$, so the speed is $\dfrac{1{6$ m s⁻¹ (0.167 m s⁻¹) Uses $x = 6.5\cos\theta$ (or $y = 6.5\sin\theta$ or $\tan\theta = \frac{y{x$) and differentiates with respect to $t$: $\frac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt = -6.5\sin\theta\,\frac{\mathrm{d\theta{\mathrm{dt$ Substitutes $\sin\theta = \dfrac{6{6.5$ and $\frac{\mathrm{dx{\mathrm{dt = 0.4$: $0.4 = -6\,\frac{\mathrm{d\theta{\mathrm{dt$ $\theta$ decreases at $\dfrac{1{15$ rad s⁻¹ (0.0667 rad s⁻¹)
items.why: Connected rates in past papers have used containers and solids (Jun 2026, Jan 2024, Jun 2021); rates linked through Pythagoras, and the rate of change of an angle, are within the spec and have not yet been set.

items.name: Formation of simple differential equations
items.question: A hemispherical bowl has internal radius 15 cm. The bowl is fixed with its rim horizontal, as shown in the diagram. Water flows into the empty bowl at a constant rate of 75 cm³ s⁻¹. When the depth of the water is $h$ cm, the volume of water in the bowl is $V$ cm³, where $$V = \frac{\pi{3h^2(45 - h), \quad 0 \leqslant h \leqslant 15$$ Find the time taken to fill the bowl. Give your answer in seconds to 3 significant figures. Find the rate at which the depth of the water is increasing at the instant when $h = 6$ Find the depth of the water at the instant when the depth is increasing at a rate of 0.25 cm s⁻¹.
items.ms: $V = \dfrac{\pi{3\times 15^2\times 30 = 2250\pi$ when $h = 15$ $t = \dfrac{2250\pi{75 = 30\pi = 94.2$ s $\frac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dh = 30\pi h - \pi h^2$ $\frac{\mathrm{dh{\mathrm{dt = 75 \div$ their $\frac{\mathrm{dV{\mathrm{dh$ at $h = 6$: $\dfrac{75{144\pi$ $\dfrac{25{48\pi = 0.166$ cm s⁻¹ $\dfrac{75{\pi(30h - h^2) = 0.25 \Rightarrow 30h - h^2 = \dfrac{300{\pi$ Solves $h^2 - 30h + \dfrac{300{\pi = 0$: $h = 15 \pm \sqrt{225 - \dfrac{300{\pi$ $h = 3.62$ cm, rejecting $26.4$ because $h \leqslant 15$
items.why: Filling a container whose volume is given in terms of depth is the most common P4.5.2 question (Jun 2026 Q4, Jun 2021 Q3: time to fill, then rate of change of depth); working back from a given rate to the depth has not yet been asked.

items.name: Formation of simple differential equations
items.question: Oil leaks from a damaged ship and forms a circular slick on the surface of the sea. At time $t$ hours after the slick is first observed, the radius of the slick is $r$ m and its area is $A$ m². In a model of the slick, the rate of increase of $A$ is inversely proportional to $r$. Show that $\dfrac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{\lambda{r^2$, where $\lambda$ is a positive constant. When the slick is first observed, its radius is 10 m. Seven hours later its radius is 20 m. Show that, according to the model, $$r^3 = 1000(1 + t)$$ Find, according to the model, the time taken, from when the slick is first observed, for its radius to reach 30 m. Find the rate at which the area of the slick is increasing at the instant when its radius is 25 m. Give your answer in m² per hour to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: $A = \pi r^2$, so $\frac{\mathrm{dA{\mathrm{dr = 2\pi r$ Forms $\frac{\mathrm{dA{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{k{r$ and uses the chain rule: $2\pi r\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{k{r$ $\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{k{2\pi r^2 = \dfrac{\lambda{r^2$, where $\lambda = \dfrac{k{2\pi > 0$ * Separates and integrates: $\displaystyle\int r^2\,\mathrm{dr = \int\lambda\,\mathrm{dt \Rightarrow \dfrac{r^3{3 = \lambda t + c$ Uses $t = 0$, $r = 10$ to find $c = \dfrac{1000{3$, and $t = 7$, $r = 20$ to find $\lambda = \dfrac{1000{3$ $\dfrac{r^3{3 = \dfrac{1000{3t + \dfrac{1000{3 \Rightarrow r^3 = 1000(1 + t)$ * $27000 = 1000(1 + t) \Rightarrow t = 26$ hours Uses $\frac{\mathrm{dA{\mathrm{dt = 2\pi r\times\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt$ with $\frac{\mathrm{dr{\mathrm{dt = \dfrac{1000{3r^2$ at $r = 25$: $2\pi\times 25\times\dfrac{1000{3\times 625$ 83.8 m² per hour
items.why: Oct 2021 Q9 derived a tank's differential equation from given flow rates and Jan 2023 Q7 followed a solved model with a connected rate; a rate of growth inversely proportional to the radius, with the constant found from two readings, has not yet been set.

items.name: Vectors in two and three dimensions
path: P4.7.1 - Vectors in two and three dimensions.
items.question: The diagram shows a storage unit modelled as a cuboid $OABCDEFG$, where $OA = 6$ m, $OC = 4$ m and $OD = 3$ m. Relative to the fixed origin $O$, the unit vectors $\mathbf{i$, $\mathbf{j$ and $\mathbf{k$ are in the directions $OA$, $OC$ and $OD$ respectively, and each has length 1 m. A straight cable runs from the corner $D$ to the point $M$, the midpoint of the edge $AB$. A second straight cable runs from $O$ to the corner $F$. Write down the position vector of $F$ and the position vector of $M$. Show that the length of the cable $DM$ is 7 m. Find, in degrees to one decimal place, the acute angle between the directions of the two cables.
items.ms: $\overrightarrow{OF = 6\mathbf{i + 4\mathbf{j + 3\mathbf{k$ or $\begin{pmatrix6\\4\\3\end{pmatrix$ $\overrightarrow{OM = 6\mathbf{i + 2\mathbf{j$ or $\begin{pmatrix6\\2\\0\end{pmatrix$ $\overrightarrow{DM = \overrightarrow{OM - \overrightarrow{OD = \begin{pmatrix6\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix$ (either sign) $DM = \sqrt{6^2 + 2^2 + (-3)^2 = \sqrt{49 = 7$ m * Scalar product of $\overrightarrow{OF$ and $\overrightarrow{DM$ (or multiples): $6(6) + 4(2) + 3(-3) = 35$ $\cos\theta = \dfrac{35{\sqrt{61 \times 7\left(= \dfrac{5{\sqrt{61\right)$ $\theta = 50.2^\circ$
items.why: P4.7.1 has been the main point in only 2 of 21 sessions (last Jan 2026), but every vectors question depends on reading three-dimensional position vectors; a cuboid with i, j and k along its edges and an angle between two non-intersecting directions (as in Jun 2026 Q7(c)) tests it directly.

items.name: Magnitude of a vector
items.question: Relative to a fixed origin $O$, the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(-5, 3, 2)$ and $(-1, 1, 6)$ respectively. Find a unit vector in the direction of $\overrightarrow{AB$. The line $l$ passes through $A$ and $B$. The point $P$ lies on $l$ and $|\overrightarrow{OP| = \sqrt{65$. Find the possible position vectors of $P$.
items.ms: $\overrightarrow{AB = \begin{pmatrix4\\-2\\4\end{pmatrix$ and $|\overrightarrow{AB| = \sqrt{4^2 + (-2)^2 + 4^2 = 6$ $\dfrac{1{6\begin{pmatrix4\\-2\\4\end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix\frac{2{3\\-\frac{1{3\\\frac{2{3\end{pmatrix$ General point on $l$, e.g. $\overrightarrow{OP = \begin{pmatrix-5\\3\\2\end{pmatrix + \lambda\begin{pmatrix2\\-1\\2\end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix-5 + 2\lambda\\3 - \lambda\\2 + 2\lambda\end{pmatrix$ Sets $(-5 + 2\lambda)^2 + (3 - \lambda)^2 + (2 + 2\lambda)^2 = 65$ and expands to a 3-term quadratic $9\lambda^2 - 18\lambda - 27 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 3$ or $\lambda = -1$ $-7\mathbf{i + 4\mathbf{j$ and $\mathbf{i + 8\mathbf{k$
items.why: Magnitude has come up in 13 of 21 sessions, almost always inside triangle areas (Jun 2025 Q8(c), Oct 2023 Q6(c)); the unit vector was last asked in Jun 2021 Q7(a), and a condition on |OP| that gives a quadratic in the parameter has not been asked.

items.name: Algebraic operations of vector addition and multiplication by…
items.question: Relative to a fixed origin $O$, the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ have position vectors $$\mathbf{a = \mathbf{i + 5\mathbf{j - 2\mathbf{k, \qquad \mathbf{b = 3\mathbf{i + 2\mathbf{j + 2\mathbf{k, \qquad \mathbf{c = 7\mathbf{i - 4\mathbf{j + 10\mathbf{k$$respectively. Find $\overrightarrow{AB$ and $\overrightarrow{AC$, and hence show that $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on a straight line. Write down the ratio $AB : BC$.
items.ms: Attempts $\mathbf{b - \mathbf{a$ or $\mathbf{c - \mathbf{a$ $\overrightarrow{AB = 2\mathbf{i - 3\mathbf{j + 4\mathbf{k$ and $\overrightarrow{AC = 6\mathbf{i - 9\mathbf{j + 12\mathbf{k$ $\overrightarrow{AC = 3\overrightarrow{AB$, so $AB$ and $AC$ are parallel, and they have the point $A$ in common, so $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear * $1 : 2$
items.why: Adding and subtracting vectors appears in 13 of 21 sessions (Oct 2022 Q3(a), Jan 2025 Q8(b), Oct 2025 Q9(b)); the geometric meaning of a scalar multiple (collinear points and the ratio they divide a line in) is named in the spec but has not been asked.

items.name: Position vectors
items.question: Relative to a fixed origin $O$, the point $A$ has position vector $6\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j + 4\mathbf{k$ and $$\overrightarrow{AB = -\mathbf{i - 3\mathbf{j + 4\mathbf{k$$ Find the coordinates of $B$. The point $C$ is such that $B$ is the midpoint of $AC$. Find the position vector of $C$. The point $P$ lies on the line segment $OC$ such that $OP : PC = 3 : 1$. Find the position vector of $P$.
items.ms: $(5, -5, 8)$ $\mathbf{c = 2\mathbf{b - \mathbf{a$ or $\mathbf{c = \mathbf{b + \overrightarrow{AB$ (ft their $B$) $4\mathbf{i - 8\mathbf{j + 12\mathbf{k$ $\overrightarrow{OP = \tfrac{3{4\overrightarrow{OC$ (ft their $C$) $3\mathbf{i - 6\mathbf{j + 9\mathbf{k$
items.why: Position vectors appear in 14 of 21 sessions (May 2024 Q2(a) found B from OA and AB; Jan 2026 Q9(a) a fourth vertex); the image of a point under reflection in another point and a point dividing a line segment in a given ratio have not yet been asked.

items.name: The distance between two points
path: P4.7.5 - The distance between two poi
items.question: Relative to a fixed origin $O$, the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(3, -1, 4)$ and $(-1, 5, 2)$ respectively. The line $l$ has equation $$\mathbf{r = \begin{pmatrix1\\6\\1\end{pmatrix + \lambda\begin{pmatrix1\\-1\\2\end{pmatrix$$where $\lambda$ is a scalar parameter. The point $P$ lies on $l$ and is equidistant from $A$ and $B$, as shown in the diagram. Find the exact distance $AB$, giving your answer as a simplified surd. Find the coordinates of $P$. The point $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Find the exact area of triangle $ABP$, giving your answer as a simplified surd.
items.ms: $\overrightarrow{AB = \begin{pmatrix-4\\6\\-2\end{pmatrix$ and $AB = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + 6^2 + (-2)^2$ $AB = \sqrt{56 = 2\sqrt{14$ General point on $l$: $(1 + \lambda,\ 6 - \lambda,\ 1 + 2\lambda)$ used to form $\overrightarrow{AP$ or $\overrightarrow{BP$ Sets $AP^2 = BP^2$: $(\lambda - 2)^2 + (7 - \lambda)^2 + (2\lambda - 3)^2 = (\lambda + 2)^2 + (1 - \lambda)^2 + (2\lambda - 1)^2$ $6\lambda^2 - 30\lambda + 62 = 6\lambda^2 - 2\lambda + 6 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2$ $P(3, 4, 5)$ $M(1, 2, 3)$, $PM = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (-2)^2 + (-2)^2 = 2\sqrt{3$ and uses $\tfrac{1{2 \times AB \times PM$ (since $PM \perp AB$) Area $= \tfrac{1{2 \times 2\sqrt{14 \times 2\sqrt{3 = 2\sqrt{42$
items.why: The distance between two points has been the main point in 6 of 21 sessions (Jun 2023 Q4 |PP'| as a surd); a point on a line equidistant from two given points, where the squared terms cancel to a linear equation, has never been asked.

items.name: Vector equations of lines
items.question: Relative to a fixed origin $O$, the points $A$ and $B$ have position vectors $4\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j + \mathbf{k$ and $2\mathbf{i + \mathbf{j - 5\mathbf{k$ respectively. The line $l_1$ passes through $A$ and $B$. Find a vector equation for $l_1$. The point $C(p, -5, q)$ lies on $l_1$. Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$. The line $l_2$ has equation $$\mathbf{r = (2\mathbf{i + 10\mathbf{j - 7\mathbf{k) + \mu(\mathbf{i + \alpha\mathbf{j + 2\mathbf{k)$$where $\mu$ is a scalar parameter and $\alpha$ is a constant. Given that $l_1$ and $l_2$ intersect, find the value of $\alpha$ and the coordinates of the point of intersection. Explain why there is no value of $\alpha$ for which $l_1$ and $l_2$ are parallel.
items.ms: Direction $\pm(\mathbf{b - \mathbf{a) = \pm(-2\mathbf{i + 3\mathbf{j - 6\mathbf{k)$ $\mathbf{r = (4\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j + \mathbf{k) + \lambda(-2\mathbf{i + 3\mathbf{j - 6\mathbf{k)$ oe Uses the $\mathbf{j$ component: $-2 + 3\lambda = -5 \Rightarrow \lambda = -1$ (for their line) $p = 6$ and $q = 7$ Equates the $\mathbf{i$ and $\mathbf{k$ components and solves: $4 - 2\lambda = 2 + \mu$, $1 - 6\lambda = -7 + 2\mu$ $\lambda = 2$, $\mu = -2$ Uses the $\mathbf{j$ component: $-2 + 3(2) = 10 - 2\alpha$ $\alpha = 3$ and point $(0, 4, -11)$ For parallel lines $\mathbf{i + \alpha\mathbf{j + 2\mathbf{k = t(-2\mathbf{i + 3\mathbf{j - 6\mathbf{k)$: the $\mathbf{i$ components need $t = -\tfrac{1{2$ but the $\mathbf{k$ components need $t = -\tfrac{1{3$, so this is impossible whatever $\alpha$ is
items.why: A line through two points (Jun 2026 Q7(a), Jun 2025 Q6(a)) and unknown coordinates of a point on it (Jun 2026 Q7(b), Oct 2025 Q9(a)) recur; an unknown constant in a direction vector of intersecting lines was Jan 2026 Q6(b), and showing no value of the constant makes the lines parallel is new.

items.name: Vector equations of lines
items.question: With respect to a fixed origin $O$, the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ have equations $$l_1: \mathbf{r = \begin{pmatrix1\\-1\\-3\end{pmatrix + \lambda\begin{pmatrix3\\-1\\2\end{pmatrix \qquad\qquad l_2: \mathbf{r = \begin{pmatrix8\\-1\\-1\end{pmatrix + \mu\begin{pmatrix1\\2\\-2\end{pmatrix$$where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are scalar parameters. Show that $l_1$ and $l_2$ intersect, and find the coordinates of their point of intersection, $P$. Find the acute angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$, giving your answer in degrees to one decimal place. The line $l_3$ passes through the point $Q(3, -4, 4)$ and is parallel to $l_1$. Determine whether $l_2$ and $l_3$ intersect, are parallel or are skew. Give reasons for your answer.
items.ms: Equates two components and solves simultaneously, e.g. $1 + 3\lambda = 8 + \mu$ and $-1 - \lambda = -1 + 2\mu$ One parameter correct: $\lambda = 2$ or $\mu = -1$ Both: $\lambda = 2$ and $\mu = -1$ Checks the third component: $-3 + 2(2) = 1$ and $-1 - 2(-1) = 1$, so the lines intersect $P(7, -3, 1)$ Scalar product of the direction vectors: $3(1) + (-1)(2) + 2(-2) = -3$ $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\pm 3{\sqrt{14 \times 3\left(= \dfrac{1{\sqrt{14\right)$ $\theta = 74.5^\circ$ $\begin{pmatrix3\\-1\\2\end{pmatrix$ is not a multiple of $\begin{pmatrix1\\2\\-2\end{pmatrix$, so $l_2$ and $l_3$ are not parallel $l_3: \mathbf{r = \begin{pmatrix3\\-4\\4\end{pmatrix + t\begin{pmatrix3\\-1\\2\end{pmatrix$; equates two components with $l_2$ and solves, e.g. $3 + 3t = 8 + \mu$, $-4 - t = -1 + 2\mu \Rightarrow t = 1,\ \mu = -2$ Third component: $4 + 2(1) = 6$ but $-1 - 2(-2) = 3$, so no common point; the lines are skew
items.why: Vector equations of lines appear in 18 of 21 sessions and the intersection of two lines recurs (Oct 2025 Q5, Jan 2026 Q6); Jun 2026 Q2(a) asked why two lines are not parallel, so a full parallel/intersect/skew decision, which the spec names, is the likeliest next step.

items.name: The scalar product. Its use for calculating the angle between…
path: P4.7.7 - The scalar product. Its use
items.question: With respect to a fixed origin $O$, the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ have equations $$l_1: \mathbf{r = (4\mathbf{i - \mathbf{j + 2\mathbf{k) + \lambda(\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j + 2\mathbf{k)$$ $$l_2: \mathbf{r = (-3\mathbf{i + 5\mathbf{j) + \mu(3\mathbf{i + 4\mathbf{k)$$where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are scalar parameters. Find, in degrees to one decimal place, the acute angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$. The line $l_3$ has direction vector $p\mathbf{i + q\mathbf{j + 3\mathbf{k$, where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Given that $l_3$ is perpendicular to both $l_1$ and $l_2$, find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
items.ms: $(\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j + 2\mathbf{k) \cdot (3\mathbf{i + 4\mathbf{k) = 3 + 0 + 8 = 11$ $\cos\theta = \dfrac{11{3 \times 5$ $\theta = 42.8^\circ$ Sets a scalar product of $p\mathbf{i + q\mathbf{j + 3\mathbf{k$ with a direction vector equal to 0 $p - 2q + 6 = 0$ and $3p + 12 = 0$ Solves their two equations $p = -4$, $q = 1$
items.why: The angle between two lines from the scalar product appears in 18 of 21 sessions (Oct 2024 Q8(c), Jun 2026 Q7(c)); using a·b = 0 twice to find a direction perpendicular to two lines has not been asked.

items.name: The scalar product. Its use for calculating the angle between…
path: P4.7.7 - The scalar product. Its use
items.question: Relative to a fixed origin $O$, the line $l$ has equation $$\mathbf{r = \begin{pmatrix1\\5\\-2\end{pmatrix + \lambda\begin{pmatrix2\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix$$where $\lambda$ is a scalar parameter. The point $A(1, 5, -2)$ lies on $l$ and the point $P$ has coordinates $(10, 2, 1)$. The point $N$ lies on $l$ such that $PN$ is perpendicular to $l$, as shown in the diagram. Find the acute angle between $\overrightarrow{AP$ and $l$, giving your answer in degrees to one decimal place. Hence find the exact shortest distance from $P$ to $l$, giving your answer as a simplified surd. Find the coordinates of $N$. The point $P'$ is the reflection of $P$ in the line $l$. Find the coordinates of $P'$.
items.ms: $\overrightarrow{AP = \begin{pmatrix9\\-3\\3\end{pmatrix$ and $\overrightarrow{AP \cdot \begin{pmatrix2\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix = 18 + 6 + 3 = 27$ $\cos\theta = \dfrac{27{\sqrt{99 \times 3\left(= \dfrac{3{\sqrt{11\right)$ $\theta = 25.2^\circ$ $PN = |\overrightarrow{AP|\sin\theta$ with $\sin\theta = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{9{11 = \sqrt{\tfrac{2{11$, or $PN^2 = AP^2 - AN^2$ with $AN = \sqrt{99\cos\theta = 9$ $PN = \sqrt{99 \times \sqrt{\tfrac{2{11 = 3\sqrt{2$ $AN = \sqrt{99\cos\theta = 9$ so $\lambda = \dfrac{9{3 = 3$, or solves $\left(\begin{pmatrix1\\5\\-2\end{pmatrix + \lambda\begin{pmatrix2\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix - \begin{pmatrix10\\2\\1\end{pmatrix\right) \cdot \begin{pmatrix2\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix = 0 \Rightarrow 9\lambda - 27 = 0$ $N(7, -1, 1)$ $\overrightarrow{OP' = 2\overrightarrow{ON - \overrightarrow{OP$ or $\overrightarrow{ON + \overrightarrow{PN$ (ft their $N$) $P'(4, -4, 1)$
items.why: The foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line was asked in Jun 2026 Q7(d), Jan 2026 Q6(a) and Jun 2023 Q4, and reflection in a line in Jun 2023 Q4 and Oct 2021 Q7(b); reaching the shortest distance 'hence' from the angle, as an exact surd, is the form not seen recently.

items.question: Relative to a fixed origin $O$, the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ have position vectors $$\mathbf{a = \begin{pmatrix1\\3\\-2\end{pmatrix, \qquad \mathbf{b = \begin{pmatrix5\\1\\2\end{pmatrix, \qquad \mathbf{c = \begin{pmatrix7\\5\\6\end{pmatrix$$respectively.
