items.name: Proof by contradiction
items.question: Prove by contradiction that there are infinitely many prime numbers. Ali says that, in a proof like the one in part (a), the number formed by multiplying the primes together and adding 1 is always prime. Given that $$2\times3\times5\times7\times11\times13+1=59\times509$$ explain why Ali is wrong and why this does not affect the proof.
items.ms: Assumption: there are only finitely many primes, so they can all be listed as $p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$ Considers $N=p_1p_2\cdots p_n+1$ $N$ leaves remainder 1 when divided by each of $p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$, so none of the listed primes is a factor of $N$ So $N$ is either prime or has a prime factor that is not in the list; either way there is a prime not in the list, which contradicts the assumption, so there are infinitely many primes 30031 $=59\times509$ is not prime, but its prime factors 59 and 509 are not in the list $2, 3, \dots, 13$, so there is still a prime not in the list (the proof needs only a prime factor outside the list)
items.why: P4.1.1 has come up in 18 of 21 sessions; the spec names the infinity of primes as a required proof, but it has never been asked.

items.name: Proof by contradiction
items.question: Use proof by contradiction to prove that $\sqrt{2$ is irrational. You may assume that if $n^2$ is even, then $n$ is even. Hence prove, by contradiction, that $5-3\sqrt{2$ is irrational. Show, by means of a counter-example, that the following statement is not true. The sum of two irrational numbers is always irrational.
items.ms:
Assumes $\sqrt2$ is rational: $\sqrt2=\dfrac{a{b$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers, $b
eq0$, with no common factors $a^2=2b^2$, so $a^2$ is even and therefore $a$ is even Writes $a=2c$: $4c^2=2b^2\Rightarrow b^2=2c^2$, so $b^2$ is even and therefore $b$ is even $a$ and $b$ are both even, so they have a common factor 2, which contradicts the assumption; hence $\sqrt2$ is irrational Assumes $5-3\sqrt2=\dfrac{p{q$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers, $q
eq0$, and makes $\sqrt2$ the subject: $\sqrt2=\dfrac{5q-p{3q$ $5q-p$ and $3q$ are integers with $3q
eq0$, so $\sqrt2$ would be rational, contradicting part (a); hence $5-3\sqrt2$ is irrational A correct counter-example with a conclusion, e.g. $5-3\sqrt2$ and $3\sqrt2$ are irrational but $(5-3\sqrt2)+3\sqrt2=5$, which is rational
items.why: Irrationality proofs came up in Oct 2021, Jan 2023 and Jun 2023 (cube roots of 2 and 3, √7), but √2 itself, named in the spec, has not; a counter-example part was last set in Oct 2023.

items.name: Proof by contradiction
items.question: Given that $x$ and $y$ are integers, show that $x+y$ and $x-y$ are either both even or both odd. Hence prove by contradiction that no integer of the form $4k+2$, where $k$ is an integer, can be written as the difference of the squares of two integers. Deduce that 2026 cannot be written as the difference of the squares of two integers. Write 2027 as the difference of the squares of two positive integers.
items.ms: Considers $(x+y)+(x-y)=2x$ (or $(x+y)-(x-y)=2y$), or considers the four cases of $x$ and $y$ odd or even $2x$ is even, so $x+y$ and $x-y$ cannot be one odd and one even; hence they are both even or both odd Assumes there are integers $x$, $y$ and $k$ with $x^2-y^2=4k+2$, and writes $(x+y)(x-y)=4k+2$ Uses part (a) to consider the two cases: both factors odd, and both factors even Both odd: the product is odd, but $4k+2=2(2k+1)$ is even. Both even: $(x+y)(x-y)=2m\times2n=4mn$, a multiple of 4, but $4k+2$ leaves remainder 2 when divided by 4 Both cases give a contradiction, so no integer of the form $4k+2$ is the difference of the squares of two integers $2026=4\times506+2$, so it has the form $4k+2$ (with $k=506$) and by part (b) it is not a difference of two squares $2027=1014^2-1013^2$
items.why: No-integer-solutions proofs by factorising came up in Oct 2022 and twice in Jan 2026 (both differences of squares); the parity argument for every number of the form 4k + 2 is the unfamiliar-proof version of the same idea.

items.name: Proof by contradiction
items.question: The curve $C$ has parametric equations $$x=t+\dfrac{1{t, \qquad y=t-\dfrac{1{t, \qquad t>0$$ The figure shows a sketch of $C$. Prove by contradiction that $x\geq2$ at every point on $C$. Show that a Cartesian equation of $C$ is $x^2-y^2=4$. Use proof by contradiction to prove that the line with equation $y=x+2$ does not intersect $C$. The line with equation $y=x+2$ does meet the curve with equation $x^2-y^2=4$. Explain why this does not contradict your answer to part (c).
items.ms: Assumes there is a value of $t>0$ for which $t+\dfrac1t<2$ Multiplies by $t$ (valid as $t>0$) and rearranges: $t^2-2t+1<0\Rightarrow(t-1)^2<0$ $(t-1)^2\geq0$ for all real $t$, a contradiction; so $x\geq2$ at every point on $C$ Uses $x+y=2t$ and $x-y=\dfrac2t$, or squares: $x^2=t^2+2+\dfrac{1{t^2$ and $y^2=t^2-2+\dfrac{1{t^2$ $x^2-y^2=(x+y)(x-y)=2t\times\dfrac2t=4$ * Assumes there is a point of $C$ that lies on the line $y=x+2$ Substitutes: $t-\dfrac1t=t+\dfrac1t+2\Rightarrow-\dfrac2t=2\Rightarrow t=-1$, or $x^2-(x+2)^2=4\Rightarrow-4x-4=4\Rightarrow x=-2$ $t=-1$ contradicts $t>0$ (or $x=-2$ contradicts $x\geq2$ from part (a)), so the line does not intersect $C$ Finds the common point $(-2, 0)$: it is on $y=x+2$ and $(-2)^2-0^2=4$ At this point $x=-2<2$ (it would need $t=-1$), so it is not on $C$: $C$ is only the part of $x^2-y^2=4$ with $x\geq2$, because $t>0$
items.why: Proofs that a line and a curve do not meet came up in Oct 2024, May 2024 and Jun 2026, and a k + 9/k ≥ 6 style inequality in Oct 2023 and Oct 2025; here both are tied to a parametric curve whose restricted domain is the twist.

items.name: Proof by contradiction
items.question: With respect to a fixed origin $O$, the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ have equations $$l_1: \mathbf{r=(4\mathbf{i-5\mathbf{j-2\mathbf{k)+\lambda(2\mathbf{i-\mathbf{j+2\mathbf{k)$$ $$l_2: \mathbf{r=(\mathbf{i-\mathbf{j+3\mathbf{k)+\mu(\mathbf{i+2\mathbf{j+2\mathbf{k)$$ where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are scalar parameters. Find the acute angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$, giving your answer in degrees to one decimal place. Prove by contradiction that $l_1$ and $l_2$ do not intersect. The point $P$ lies on $l_1$ and has parameter $\lambda$. Show that $$OP^2=9\lambda^2+18\lambda+45$$ Hence prove by contradiction that every point on $l_1$ is at least 6 units from $O$.
items.ms: $(2\mathbf{i-\mathbf{j+2\mathbf{k)\cdot(\mathbf{i+2\mathbf{j+2\mathbf{k)=2-2+4=4$ $\cos\theta=\dfrac{4{3\times3=\dfrac49$ $\theta=63.6^\circ$ Assumes the lines intersect, so for some $\lambda$ and $\mu$: $4+2\lambda=1+\mu$, $-5-\lambda=-1+2\mu$ and $-2+2\lambda=3+2\mu$ Solves two of the equations, e.g. the first two give $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=-1$ Substitutes into the third equation: $-2+2(-2)=-6$ but $3+2(-1)=1$ $-6\neq1$, a contradiction, so $l_1$ and $l_2$ do not intersect $\overrightarrow{OP=(4+2\lambda)\mathbf{i+(-5-\lambda)\mathbf{j+(-2+2\lambda)\mathbf{k$ and $OP^2=(4+2\lambda)^2+(5+\lambda)^2+(2\lambda-2)^2$ $=16+16\lambda+4\lambda^2+25+10\lambda+\lambda^2+4\lambda^2-8\lambda+4=9\lambda^2+18\lambda+45$ * Assumes there is a point on $l_1$ with $OP<6$, so $9\lambda^2+18\lambda+45<36$ for some $\lambda$ Rearranges and completes the square: $9\lambda^2+18\lambda+9<0\Rightarrow9(\lambda+1)^2<0$ $(\lambda+1)^2\geq0$ for all real $\lambda$, a contradiction; so every point on $l_1$ is at least 6 units from $O$
items.why: Jun 2026 Q2(b) asked for a proof by contradiction that two lines do not intersect; a distance bound proved by completing the square is an unfamiliar-proof angle not yet asked.

Hence find the exact value of the gradient of the curve with equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$ at the point where $x = 1$.

items.question: The rectangular hyperbola $H$ has equation $xy = 8$. The line $l$ has equation $y + kx = 8$, where $k$ is a non-zero constant. Show that the $x$-coordinates of any points where $l$ meets $H$ satisfy the equation $$kx^2 - 8x + 8 = 0$$ Given that $l$ is a tangent to $H$, find the value of $k$ and the coordinates of the point where $l$ touches $H$. items.ms: Substitutes $y = 8 - kx$ into $xy = 8$: $x(8 - kx) = 8$ $8x - kx^2 = 8$ leading to $kx^2 - 8x + 8 = 0$ * Uses $b^2 - 4ac = 0$: $(-8)^2 - 4 \times k \times 8 = 0$ $k = 2$ Solves $2x^2 - 8x + 8 = 0$, i.e. $2(x - 2)^2 = 0$: point $(2,\ 4)$ $k > 2$ (from $64 - 32k < 0$)

items.question: The parabola $C$ has parametric equations $x = 4t^2$, $y = 8t$. The distinct points $P\left(4p^2,\ 8p\right)$ and $Q\left(4q^2,\ 8q\right)$ lie on $C$, where $p$ and $q$ are non-zero. The diagram shows $C$ and the triangle $OPQ$, where $O$ is the origin and angle $POQ$ is a right angle. Show that $pq = -4$. Show that an equation of the chord $PQ$ is $$(p + q)y = 2x + 8pq$$ Hence show that the chord $PQ$ always passes through a fixed point on the $x$-axis, and state the coordinates of this point. items.question: A point moves in the $x$-$y$ plane so that its distance from the point $S(7,\ 0)$ is always equal to its distance from the line with equation $x = -7$. Show that the locus of the point is the parabola $C$ with equation $y^2 = 28x$. The point $P$ lies on $C$, above the $x$-axis. The point $Q$ lies on the line $x = -7$ such that $PQ$ is parallel to the $x$-axis, as shown in the diagram. Given that triangle $PQS$ is equilateral, find the exact coordinates of $P$.
items.ms: Equates the distances for a general point $(x,\ y)$: $\sqrt{(x - 7)^2 + y^2 = x + 7$ Squares and simplifies: $x^2 - 14x + 49 + y^2 = x^2 + 14x + 49$, so $y^2 = 28x$ * Uses $PS = PQ = x + 7$ (focus–directrix property) and $QS = PS$ with $Q(-7,\ y)$: $(x + 7)^2 = 14^2 + y^2$ Uses $y^2 = 28x$ to form and solve $x^2 - 14x - 147 = 0$: $x = 21$ $P\left(21,\ 14\sqrt{3\right)$

items.question: The parabola $C$ has equation $y^2 = 4ax$, where $a$ is a positive constant, and focus $S$. The point $P\left(ap^2,\ 2ap\right)$, where $p > 0$, lies on $C$. The tangent to $C$ at $P$ has equation $$py = x + ap^2$$ and meets the $x$-axis at the point $T$. The point $R$ lies on the line through $P$ parallel to the $x$-axis and the point $U$ lies on the tangent, with $R$ and $U$ both to the right of $P$, as shown in the diagram. Using the focus–directrix property, show that triangle $SPT$ is isosceles. Hence show that angle $UPR$ is equal to angle $SPT$. Given that the tangent at $P$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the $x$-axis, and that the area of triangle $SPT$ is $36\sqrt{3$, find the value of $a$.
items.ms: $T\left(-ap^2,\ 0\right)$ $S(a,\ 0)$, so $ST = a + ap^2$ $SP$ equals the distance from $P$ to the directrix $x = -a$, so $SP = ap^2 + a$ $ST = SP = a\left(1 + p^2\right)$, so triangle $SPT$ is isosceles * Angle $SPT$ = angle $STP$ (base angles of the isosceles triangle $SPT$) Angle $STP$ = angle $UPR$ (corresponding angles, as $PR$ is parallel to $TS$), so angle $UPR$ = angle $SPT$ * Gradient of tangent $\dfrac{1{p = \tan 30^\circ$, so $p = \sqrt{3$ Area $= \dfrac{1{2 \times ST \times 2ap = \dfrac{1{2 \times a(1 + p^2) \times 2ap$, which is $4\sqrt{3\,a^2$ when $p = \sqrt{3$ $a = 3$
items.why: FP1.4.3 carries 4.3% of the unit's marks and the focus is combined with a tangent in most long questions (Jan 2026 Q8(b), Jan 2023 Q8); the isosceles triangle behind the reflective property, with a found from an area (Jan 2023 Q8(c) found a from an area ratio), is a likely late-question angle.

items.name: The focus-directrix property of the Concept of focus and…
items.question: The parabola $C$ has equation $y^2 = 4x$ and focus $S$. The line $l$ has equation $y = 2x - k$, where $k$ is a positive constant. The line $l$ meets $C$ at the distinct points $A$ and $B$. Show that the $x$-coordinates of $A$ and $B$ are the roots of the equation $$4x^2 - 4(k + 1)x + k^2 = 0$$ Using the focus–directrix property, show that $AS + BS = k + 3$. Given that $AS + BS = 9$, find the exact length of $AB$. Find the exact area of triangle $ABS$.
items.ms: Substitutes $y = 2x - k$ into $y^2 = 4x$: $(2x - k)^2 = 4x$ $4x^2 - 4kx + k^2 - 4x = 0$, so $4x^2 - 4(k + 1)x + k^2 = 0$ * Directrix $x = -1$ (or focus $S(1,\ 0)$) $AS = x_A + 1$ and $BS = x_B + 1$ Uses the sum of the roots $x_A + x_B = k + 1$: $AS + BS = k + 1 + 2 = k + 3$ * $k = 6$, and uses $(x_A - x_B)^2 = (x_A + x_B)^2 - 4x_Ax_B = 7^2 - 4 \times 9 = 13$ $AB^2 = (x_A - x_B)^2 + (y_A - y_B)^2 = 5(x_A - x_B)^2$, using $y_A - y_B = 2(x_A - x_B)$ $AB = \sqrt{65$ Uses $l$ meeting the $x$-axis at $(3,\ 0)$, so a base of $2$ from $S(1,\ 0)$, with $|y_A - y_B| = 2\sqrt{13$: area $= \dfrac{1{2 \times 2 \times 2\sqrt{13$ $2\sqrt{13$

items.question: The rectangular hyperbola $H$ has equation $xy = c^2$, where $c$ is a positive constant. The point $P\left(ct,\ \dfrac{c{t\right)$, where $t > 0$, lies on $H$. The tangent to $H$ at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at the point $A$ and the $y$-axis at the point $B$, as shown in the diagram. Use calculus to show that the tangent to $H$ at $P$ has equation $$x + t^2y = 2ct$$ Show that $P$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Show that the area of triangle $OAB$, where $O$ is the origin, does not depend on $t$. Given that $c = 6$, the triangle $OAB$ is transformed onto the triangle $OA'B'$ by the transformation represented by the matrix $$\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix 3 & -1 \\ 2 & k \end{pmatrix$$ where $k$ is a constant. items.question: The parabola $C$ has equation $y^2 = 8x$. The point $X$ has coordinates $(0,\ 10)$. The point $P\left(2p^2,\ 4p\right)$, where $p > 0$, is the point on $C$ that is nearest to $X$, so the normal to $C$ at $P$ passes through $X$, as shown in the diagram. Use calculus to show that the normal to $C$ at $P$ has equation $$y + px = 2p^3 + 4p$$ Show that $p$ satisfies the equation $$p^3 + 2p - 5 = 0$$ Show that the equation $p^3 + 2p - 5 = 0$ has a root $\alpha$ in the interval $[1.3,\ 1.4]$. Taking $1.3$ as a first approximation to $\alpha$, apply the Newton–Raphson procedure once to $\mathrm{f(p)$ to find a second approximation to $\alpha$. Give your answer to 3 decimal places. Hence find, to 3 significant figures, the shortest distance from $X$ to $C$.
items.ms: $2y\dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = 8$, or $y = 2\sqrt{2\,x\frac{1{2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{dy{\mathrm{dx = \sqrt{2\,x-\frac{1{2$ Gradient of the tangent at $P$ is $\dfrac{1{p$, so the gradient of the normal is $-p$ $y - 4p = -p\left(x - 2p^2\right)$ $y + px = 2p^3 + 4p$ * Substitutes $x = 0$, $y = 10$: $10 = 2p^3 + 4p$ $p^3 + 2p - 5 = 0$ * With $\mathrm{f(p) = p^3 + 2p - 5$, evaluates $\mathrm{f(1.3) = -0.203$ and $\mathrm{f(1.4) = 0.544$ Sign change and $\mathrm{f$ is continuous, so there is a root in $[1.3,\ 1.4]$ * $\mathrm{f'(p) = 3p^2 + 2$ $1.3 - \dfrac{\mathrm{f(1.3){\mathrm{f'(1.3) = 1.3 - \dfrac{-0.203{7.07$ $1.329$ Uses $P\left(2p^2,\ 4p\right)$ with $p = 1.329$: $XP = \sqrt{\left(2p^2\right)^2 + (4p - 10)^2$ $5.87$
items.why: The normal to the parabola by calculus was asked in Jun 2026 Q9(a), and Newton–Raphson (FP1.3.1) appears in almost every paper; a normal through a given point that leads to a cubic solved numerically is a synoptic long question the real papers have not yet set.

items.question: $$z = -3 - 3\sqrt{3\,i$$ Find $|z|$. Find $\arg z$, giving your answer as an exact multiple of $\pi$, where $-\pi < \arg z \leqslant \pi$. Write down $z^*$ in the form $r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)$, where $r > 0$ and $-\pi < \theta \leqslant \pi$.
items.ms: $|z| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + (-3\sqrt{3)^2 = 6$ Uses $\arctan\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt{3{3\right) = \dfrac{\pi{3$ (or $\arctan\left(\dfrac{3{3\sqrt{3\right) = \dfrac{\pi{6$) and attempts the third-quadrant angle, e.g. $-\pi + \dfrac{\pi{3$ or $-\dfrac{\pi{2 - \dfrac{\pi{6$ $\arg z = -\dfrac{2\pi{3$ $z^* = 6\left(\cos\dfrac{2\pi{3 + i\sin\dfrac{2\pi{3\right)$
items.why: FP1.1.1 has come up in 23 of 26 sessions, usually as the modulus and exact argument of a surd complex number (Oct 2020 Q4(a), Jan 2024 Q2(a)); the modulus-argument form of the conjugate has not been asked recently.

items.name: Definition of complex numbers in the form a + ib and r cos + i…
items.question: The complex numbers $z$ and $w$ are given by $$z = r\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi{6 + i\sin\dfrac{5\pi{6\right) \qquad w = 3 - 4i$$ where $r$ is a positive real constant. Given that $|zw| = 20$ write down the value of $r$. Express $z$ in the form $a + ib$, where $a$ and $b$ are exact real numbers. Given that $z + kw$ is real, where $k$ is a real constant, find the value of $k$. Determine $\arg(z + w)$, giving your answer in radians to 2 decimal places.
items.ms: $r = 4$ Uses $a = r\cos\dfrac{5\pi{6$ and $b = r\sin\dfrac{5\pi{6$ with their $r$ $z = -2\sqrt{3 + 2i$ Sets the imaginary part of $z + kw$ equal to zero: $2 - 4k = 0$ $k = \dfrac{1{2$ $z + w = (3 - 2\sqrt{3) - 2i$ and a correct third-quadrant method, e.g. $-\pi + \arctan\left(\dfrac{2{2\sqrt{3 - 3\right)$ $\arg(z + w) = -1.80$
items.why: FP1.1.1: Jun 2025 Q5(a) used |z₁z₂| to find r in a modulus-argument form; a 'real' condition and the third-quadrant argument of a sum (a common sign trap) have not been combined with it.

items.name: Definition of complex numbers in the form a + ib and r cos + i…
items.question: $$z = 2 - 2\sqrt{3\,i \qquad w = -\sqrt{3 + i$$ Express $z$ in the form $r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)$, where $r > 0$ and $-\pi < \theta \leqslant \pi$. Give the value of $\theta$ as an exact multiple of $\pi$. Show that $z = w^2$. Hence, or otherwise, find the exact value of $|z^3 w^*|$. The diagram shows the points $W$ and $Z$, which represent $w$ and $z$ respectively on an Argand diagram. $O$ is the origin. Find the exact area of triangle $OWZ$.
items.ms: $r = |z| = 4$ Uses $\arctan\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{3{2\right) = \dfrac{\pi{3$ and places $z$ in the fourth quadrant $z = 4\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi{3\right) + i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi{3\right)\right)$ $w^2 = (-\sqrt{3 + i)^2 = 3 - 2\sqrt{3\,i + i^2$ $= 2 - 2\sqrt{3\,i = z$ Uses $|z^3 w^*| = |z|^3|w^*|$ with $|w^*| = |w| = 2$ (or $|w|^7$) $|z^3 w^*| = 4^3 \times 2 = 128$ Correct method, e.g. $\tfrac{1{2\left|(-\sqrt{3)(-2\sqrt{3) - (2)(1)\right|$, or $\tfrac{1{2\times 2 \times 4 \times \sin\dfrac{5\pi{6$ with angle $WOZ = \dfrac{5\pi{6$ Area $= 2$
items.why: Modulus-argument form is asked in most sessions (Oct 2020 Q4(a), Jan 2024 Q2(a)); |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂| (Jun 2025) and areas on Argand diagrams (Jan 2024 Q2(d)) recur, while a hidden relation such as z = w² has not been used.

items.name: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers
path: FP1.1.2 - Sum, product and quotient of
items.question: $$z = \dfrac{7 + 4i{2 - i$$ Showing all stages of your working, express $z$ in the form $a + ib$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Hence find the value of the real constant $k$ for which $z^2 + kz$ is real.
items.ms: Multiplies numerator and denominator by $2 + i$ Expands using $i^2 = -1$: $\dfrac{14 + 7i + 8i - 4{4 + 1 = \dfrac{10 + 15i{5$ $z = 2 + 3i$ $z^2 = -5 + 12i$ and sets the imaginary part of $z^2 + kz$ to zero: $12 + 3k = 0$ $k = -4$
items.why: FP1.1.2 has come up in 20 of 26 sessions, usually opening with a quotient in the form a + ib with all working shown (Jan 2021 Q6(c), May 2024 Q4(a)); a 'real' condition with a parameter is a fresh follow-up.

items.name: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers
path: FP1.1.2 - Sum, product and quotient of
items.question: $$zz^* - 4iz = 16 + 8i$$ where $z^*$ is the complex conjugate of $z$. Given that $z = x + iy$, where $x$ and $y$ are real, use algebra to determine the complex numbers $z$ that satisfy this equation. You must show all stages of your working.
items.ms: Substitutes $z = x + iy$ and $z^* = x - iy$ and expands, with $zz^* = x^2 + y^2$: $x^2 + y^2 - 4ix + 4y$ Equates real parts and imaginary parts to obtain two equations $x^2 + y^2 + 4y = 16$ and $-4x = 8$ $x = -2$ Substitutes their $x$ and solves the resulting 3-term quadratic $y^2 + 4y - 12 = 0$ $z = -2 + 2i$ and $z = -2 - 6i$
items.why: Equations in z and z* came up in Jan 2026 Q4 ((z − 2i)(z* − 2i) = 21 − 12i) and earlier sessions; the same 'equate real and imaginary parts' method in a fresh form is likely to recur.

items.name: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers
path: FP1.1.2 - Sum, product and quotient of
items.question: $$w = \dfrac{a + 8i{2 - i$$ where $a$ is a real constant. Express $w$ in the form $x + iy$, where $x$ and $y$ are real, giving $x$ and $y$ in terms of $a$. Given that $w$ is real, write down the value of $a$. Given instead that $|w| = 2\sqrt{5$, determine the possible values of $a$. For the negative value of $a$ found in part (c), find $\arg w$, giving your answer in radians to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: Multiplies numerator and denominator by $2 + i$ Expands the numerator with $i^2 = -1$: $(2a - 8) + (a + 16)i$, over $5$ $w = \dfrac{2a - 8{5 + \dfrac{a + 16{5\,i$ $a = -16$ Uses $|w| = \dfrac{|a + 8i|{|2 - i|$, i.e. $\dfrac{\sqrt{a^2 + 64{\sqrt{5 = 2\sqrt{5$, or $\left(\dfrac{2a - 8{5\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{a + 16{5\right)^2 = 20$ Simplifies to $a^2 = 36$ (or $5a^2 = 180$) $a = 6$ or $a = -6$ $w = -4 + 2i$ and a correct second-quadrant method, e.g. $\pi - \arctan\dfrac{2{4$ $\arg w = 2.68$
items.why: A quotient with a real parameter has come up in Jan 2020, Jun 2021, Jun 2023, Jan 2024 and Jan 2026; the modulus of a quotient and a second-quadrant argument are the usual follow-ups.

items.name: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers
path: FP1.1.2 - Sum, product and quotient of
items.question: In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Use algebra to find the two complex numbers $z$ such that $z^2 = -15 + 8i$, giving your answers in the form $x + iy$, where $x$ and $y$ are real. Hence, using algebra, find the four roots of the equation $$z^4 + 30z^2 + 289 = 0$$ Show the four roots on a single Argand diagram. The points representing the four roots are the vertices of a rectangle. Find the area of this rectangle.
items.ms: Expands $(x + iy)^2 = x^2 - y^2 + 2xyi$ Equates real and imaginary parts: $x^2 - y^2 = -15$ and $2xy = 8$ Eliminates $y$ (or $x$) to obtain a quartic: $x^4 + 15x^2 - 16 = 0$ Solves as a quadratic in $x^2$: $(x^2 + 16)(x^2 - 1) = 0$, so $x = \pm 1$ (rejecting $x^2 = -16$) $z = 1 + 4i$ and $z = -1 - 4i$ Solves the quadratic in $z^2$: $z^2 = \dfrac{-30 \pm \sqrt{900 - 1156{2$ $z^2 = -15 + 8i$ or $z^2 = -15 - 8i$ $z = 1 + 4i,\ -1 - 4i,\ 1 - 4i,\ -1 + 4i$ Two roots plotted correctly, e.g. $1 + 4i$ in the first quadrant and $-1 - 4i$ in the third All four roots plotted, symmetric about both axes Area $= 2 \times 8 = 16$
items.why: Square roots of a complex number by equating real and imaginary parts have not appeared in recent FP1 papers, and a quartic in z² with no real roots is a likely surprise; plotting all roots recurs (Jan 2026 Q2(b), Jun 2026 Q6(e)).

items.name: Geometrical representation of complex numbers in the Argand…
items.question: The complex number $z = 4 + i$. On an Argand diagram, $O$ is the origin and the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ represent the complex numbers $z$, $iz$ and $(1 + i)z$ respectively. Find $iz$ and $(1 + i)z$ in the form $a + ib$. Show that $OACB$ is a square. The transformation $T$ of the plane maps the point representing any complex number $x + iy$ to the point representing $(1 + i)(x + iy)$. Write down the $2 \times 2$ matrix that represents $T$. Describe fully the transformation $T$ as a combination of two geometrical transformations.
items.ms: $iz = -1 + 4i$ $(1 + i)z = 3 + 5i$ Uses $(1 + i)z = z + iz$, so $\overrightarrow{OC = \overrightarrow{OA + \overrightarrow{OB$ and $OACB$ is a parallelogram (or finds the lengths of all four sides) $OA = |z| = \sqrt{17$ and $OB = |iz| = \sqrt{17$ Gradient of $OA = \dfrac{1{4$, gradient of $OB = -4$, product $= -1$, so $OA$ is perpendicular to $OB$; hence $OACB$ is a square $\begin{pmatrix 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix$ Rotation through $\dfrac{\pi{4$ (or $45^\circ$) anticlockwise about $O$ Enlargement, scale factor $\sqrt{2$, centre $O$
items.why: FP1.1.3 comes up in 24 of 26 sessions, almost always as plotting roots; the spec's 'geometrical representation of products' (multiplying by i and by 1 + i) has not been asked and links naturally to the unit's transformation matrices.

items.name: Complex solutions of quadratic equations with real coefficients
items.question: The quadratic equation $$z^2 - 2kz + 25 = 0$$ where $k$ is a real constant, has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$, which are not real. Find the set of possible values of $k$. Find $\alpha$ and $\beta$ in terms of $k$, giving your answers in the form $a + ib$. Show that $|\alpha| = 5$ for all values of $k$ in your answer to part (a). Given that $\arg\alpha = \dfrac{2\pi{3$, find the exact value of $k$ and write $\alpha$ in the form $a + ib$.
items.ms: Uses $b^2 - 4ac < 0$: $4k^2 - 100 < 0$ $-5 < k < 5$ Quadratic formula or completing the square: $(z - k)^2 = k^2 - 25$ $z = k \pm i\sqrt{25 - k^2$ $|\alpha|^2 = k^2 + (25 - k^2) = 25$, so $|\alpha| = 5$ $\alpha = 5\left(\cos\dfrac{2\pi{3 + i\sin\dfrac{2\pi{3\right)$, or $\tan\dfrac{2\pi{3 = \dfrac{\sqrt{25 - k^2{k$ with $k < 0$ $k = -\dfrac{5{2$ and $\alpha = -\dfrac{5{2 + \dfrac{5\sqrt{3{2\,i$
items.why: FP1.1.4 appears in most sessions but almost always inside a cubic or quartic (Jun 2014 Q2 was the last stand-alone quadratic); a real quadratic with a parameter, linking non-real roots to modulus and argument, has not been set.

items.name: Finding conjugate complex roots and a real root of a cubic…
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(z) = 2z^3 + az^2 + bz + 15$$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Show that $(2 + i)^3 = 2 + 11i$. Given that $z = 2 + i$ is a root of the equation $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$, use your answer to part (a) to determine the value of $a$ and the value of $b$. Hence solve $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ completely. The roots of $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ are represented by the points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ on an Argand diagram. Find the area of triangle $PQR$.
items.ms: $(2 + i)^2 = 3 + 4i$ and multiplies by $(2 + i)$ $(3 + 4i)(2 + i) = 6 + 3i + 8i - 4 = 2 + 11i$ Substitutes: $2(2 + 11i) + a(3 + 4i) + b(2 + i) + 15 = 0$ Equates real parts and imaginary parts to zero $3a + 2b + 19 = 0$ and $4a + b + 22 = 0$ $a = -5$ and $b = -2$ $2 - i$ is a root Forms $(z - (2 + i))(z - (2 - i)) = z^2 - 4z + 5$ and divides $\mathrm{f(z)$ by it (or compares coefficients) to find the linear factor $z = -\dfrac{3{2$ Base $2$ (between $2 + i$ and $2 - i$) and height $2 + \dfrac{3{2$: $\tfrac{1{2 \times 2 \times \dfrac{7{2$ Area $= \dfrac{7{2$
items.why: FP1.1.5 came up in 12 of 26 sessions (most recently Jun 2026 Q1 and Jan 2025 Q4); finding the coefficients by substituting the complex root and equating real and imaginary parts is the rarely seen route, and triangle areas recur (Jan 2024 Q2(d)).

items.name: Finding conjugate complex roots and/or real roots of a quartic…
items.question: $$\mathrm{g(z) = z^4 - 3z^3 + 10z^2 - 6z - 20$$ Given that $\mathrm{g(2) = 0$ and $\mathrm{g(-1) = 0$ use algebra to solve $\mathrm{g(z) = 0$ completely. The points representing the roots of $\mathrm{g(z) = 0$ on an Argand diagram are the vertices of a quadrilateral. Find the area of this quadrilateral.
items.ms: Forms the quadratic factor $(z - 2)(z + 1) = z^2 - z - 2$ and divides $\mathrm{g(z)$ by it (or compares coefficients) $z^2 - 2z + 10$ Solves their 3-term quadratic, e.g. $(z - 1)^2 = -9$ $z = 1 \pm 3i$ (with $z = 2$ and $z = -1$) Perpendicular diagonals of lengths $3$ and $6$: $\tfrac{1{2 \times 3 \times 6$ (or two triangles, or the shoelace method) Area $= 9$
items.why: FP1.1.6 is worth 5.9% of the unit (16 of 26 sessions); solving a quartic from two given real roots is the spec's own second example and has not been asked recently, and areas of root polygons recur (Jan 2024 Q2(d), May 2024 Q2(d)).

items.name: Finding conjugate complex roots and/or real roots of a quartic…
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(z) = z^4 - 4z^3 + Az^2 + Bz + 117$$ where $A$ and $B$ are real constants. Given that $z = 3 - 2i$ is a root of the equation $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ write down another complex root of this equation. Hence determine a quadratic factor of $\mathrm{f(z)$ with real coefficients. Determine the value of $A$ and the value of $B$. Without using a calculator, find the other two roots of $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$, giving your answers in simplest form.
items.ms: $3 + 2i$ $(z - (3 - 2i))(z - (3 + 2i))$ expanded, or uses sum of roots $6$ and product $13$ $z^2 - 6z + 13$ Writes $\mathrm{f(z) = (z^2 - 6z + 13)(z^2 + pz + q)$ and compares $z^3$ and constant terms: $p = 2$, $q = 9$ Expands or compares the $z^2$ and $z$ coefficients $A = 10$ and $B = -28$ Solves their $z^2 + 2z + 9 = 0$, e.g. $(z + 1)^2 = -8$ $z = -1 \pm 2\sqrt{2\,i$
items.why: A given complex root of a real quartic with unknown coefficients came up in Jun 2022 Q4, Jun 2025 Q7 and Jun 2026 Q6; this is the core type with fresh numbers and a surd answer.

items.name: Finding conjugate complex roots and/or real roots of a quartic…
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(z) = z^4 + 2z^3 + 2z^2 + 10z + 25$$ In this question you must show all stages of your working. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable. Show that $z = 1 + 2i$ is a root of the equation $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$. Hence solve $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ completely. Show the four roots of $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ on a single Argand diagram. Show that the four roots have the same modulus.
items.ms: Finds $(1 + 2i)^2 = -3 + 4i$ and at least one of $(1 + 2i)^3 = -11 - 2i$, $(1 + 2i)^4 = -7 - 24i$ Substitutes all powers: $(-7 - 24i) + 2(-11 - 2i) + 2(-3 + 4i) + 10(1 + 2i) + 25$ $= 0$, so $1 + 2i$ is a root $1 - 2i$ is a root Forms $z^2 - 2z + 5$ and divides $\mathrm{f(z)$ by it (or compares coefficients) $z^2 + 4z + 5$ $z = -2 \pm i$ $1 + 2i$ and $1 - 2i$ plotted correctly, symmetric about the real axis $-2 + i$ and $-2 - i$ plotted correctly relative to the first pair $|1 \pm 2i| = \sqrt{5$ and $|-2 \pm i| = \sqrt{5$
items.why: FP1.1.6 is the heaviest complex-numbers point; Jan 2026 Q2 asked students to show a given number is a root before solving, and plotting all roots followed in Jan 2026, Jun 2025 and Jun 2026.

items.name: Finding conjugate complex roots and/or real roots of a quartic…
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(z) = z^4 - 6z^3 + (k + 10)z^2 - 6kz + 10k$$ where $k$ is a real constant. Given that $z = 3 + i$ is a root of the equation $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ write down another root of $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$. Hence find a quadratic factor of $\mathrm{f(z)$ with real coefficients. Show that $\mathrm{f(z) = (z^2 - 6z + 10)(z^2 + k)$. Given that $k = -16$ show all four roots of $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ on a single Argand diagram, determine the exact perimeter of the quadrilateral whose vertices are the points representing the four roots, giving your answer as a simplified surd. Given instead that $k > 0$, and that the points representing the four roots of $\mathrm{f(z) = 0$ on an Argand diagram are the vertices of a quadrilateral of area $12$, determine the value of $k$.
items.ms: $3 - i$ $(z - (3 + i))(z - (3 - i))$ expanded, or sum of roots $6$ and product $10$ $z^2 - 6z + 10$ Divides $\mathrm{f(z)$ by $z^2 - 6z + 10$, or expands $(z^2 - 6z + 10)(z^2 + k)$ fully $z^4 - 6z^3 + (k + 10)z^2 - 6kz + 10k$ with a conclusion $z = \pm 4$ plotted on the real axis, symmetric about $O$ $3 + i$ and $3 - i$ plotted, symmetric about the real axis and between $O$ and $4$ in real part Distances from $3 \pm i$ to $-4$ and to $4$: $\sqrt{7^2 + 1^2 = 5\sqrt{2$ and $\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2 = \sqrt{2$ Perimeter $= 2(5\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2) = 12\sqrt{2$ Roots of $z^2 + k = 0$ are $\pm i\sqrt{k$ Recognises a trapezium with parallel sides $2\sqrt{k$ and $2$ a distance $3$ apart Sets up the area: $\tfrac{1{2(2\sqrt{k + 2) \times 3 = 12$ Solves for $\sqrt{k$: $3\sqrt{k + 3 = 12$, so $\sqrt{k = 3$ $k = 9$
items.why: FP1.1.6 carries the most marks of any complex-numbers point (Jun 2026 Q6, Jan 2026 Q2, Jun 2025 Q7); Jan 2026 put a parameter into the quartic, and finding a parameter from the area of the root quadrilateral is the natural next step.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$\mathrm{f(n) = 6n+1 + 72n-1$$ is divisible by 43.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f(1) = 6^2 + 7^1 = 43$, which is divisible by 43 Assumes $\mathrm{f(k)$ is divisible by 43 and attempts $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ in terms of $6k+1$ and $72k-1$, e.g. $\mathrm{f(k+1) = 6\left(6k+1\right) + 49\left(72k-1\right)$, or attempts $\mathrm{f(k+1) - \mathrm{f(k)$ $\mathrm{f(k+1) = 6\mathrm{f(k) + 43\left(72k-1\right)$ (or $49\mathrm{f(k) - 43\left(6k+1\right)$, or $\mathrm{f(k+1) - \mathrm{f(k) = 5\mathrm{f(k) + 43\left(72k-1\right)$), so $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ is divisible by 43 Conclusion: if $\mathrm{f(k)$ is divisible by 43 then $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ is divisible by 43; as $\mathrm{f(1)$ is divisible by 43, $\mathrm{f(n)$ is divisible by 43 for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$
items.why: FP1.8.1 has come up in all 26 sessions and a two-power divisibility proof is set almost every year (Jun 2026 by 5, May 2024 by 57); this one uses a new pair of powers and divisor.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$\sumr=1n r\left(3r-1\right) = \frac{1{4\left[(2n-1)3n + 1\right]$$
items.ms: $n = 1$: LHS $= 1 \times 3^0 = 1$ and RHS $= \frac{1{4(1 \times 3 + 1) = 1$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes true for $n = k$ and adds the $(k+1)$th term: $\displaystyle\sumr=1k+1 r\left(3r-1\right) = \frac{1{4\left[(2k-1)3k + 1\right] + (k+1)3k$ Collects the terms in $3^k$: $\frac{1{4\left[(2k - 1 + 4k + 4)3k + 1\right] = \frac{1{4\left[(6k+3)3k + 1\right]$ $= \frac{1{4\left[(2k+1)3k+1 + 1\right] = \frac{1{4\left[\left(2(k+1) - 1\right)3k+1 + 1\right]$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$
items.why: Summation proofs came up in Jun 2026, Jan 2026 and Jan 2023 with polynomial or log terms; a sum that mixes $r$ with powers of 3 has not been set in any of the 12 most recent induction parts, so it is a likely new angle.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(n) = 62n + 3n+2 + 3n$$ Prove by induction that, for all positive integers $n$, $\mathrm{f(n)$ is divisible by 11.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f(1) = 36 + 27 + 3 = 66 = 6 \times 11$, so divisible by 11 Assumes $\mathrm{f(k)$ is divisible by 11 and attempts $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ or $\mathrm{f(k+1) - \lambda\mathrm{f(k)$ Correct expression, e.g. $\mathrm{f(k+1) = 36\left(62k\right) + 3\left(3k+2\right) + 3\left(3k\right)$ Uses the assumption to write $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ as a multiple of $\mathrm{f(k)$ plus other terms, e.g. $\mathrm{f(k+1) - 3\mathrm{f(k) = 33\left(62k\right)$ or $\mathrm{f(k+1) - 36\mathrm{f(k) = -33\left(3k+2 + 3k\right)$ $\mathrm{f(k+1) = 3\mathrm{f(k) + 33\left(62k\right)$ (or $36\mathrm{f(k) - 330\left(3k\right)$), with both terms divisible by 11 Conclusion: if $\mathrm{f(k)$ is divisible by 11 then $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ is divisible by 11; as $\mathrm{f(1)$ is divisible by 11, $\mathrm{f(n)$ is divisible by 11 for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$
items.why: Divisibility proofs came up in Jun 2026, May 2024, Jan 2024, Jun 2023 and Jun 2022, always with two terms; a three-term expression, where the multiple of $\mathrm{f}(k)$ chosen decides how easy the algebra is, has not been asked.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: $$\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix$$ Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$\mathbf{M^n = \frac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 3^n + (-1)^n & 3^n - (-1)^n \\ 3^n - (-1)^n & 3^n + (-1)^n \end{pmatrix$$ Use the result in part (a) to show that $\det\left(\mathbf{M^n\right) = (-3)^n$
items.ms: $n = 1$: $\frac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 3 - 1 & 3 + 1 \\ 3 + 1 & 3 - 1 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix = \mathbf{M$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes true for $n = k$ and multiplies $\mathbf{M^k$ by $\mathbf{M$ (either order): $\frac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 3^k + (-1)^k & 3^k - (-1)^k \\ 3^k - (-1)^k & 3^k + (-1)^k \end{pmatrix\begin{pmatrix 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix$ Correct product, e.g. $\frac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 3^k + (-1)^k + 2\left(3^k - (-1)^k\right) & 2\left(3^k + (-1)^k\right) + 3^k - (-1)^k \\ 3^k - (-1)^k + 2\left(3^k + (-1)^k\right) & 2\left(3^k - (-1)^k\right) + 3^k + (-1)^k \end{pmatrix = \frac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 3\left(3^k\right) - (-1)^k & 3\left(3^k\right) + (-1)^k \\ 3\left(3^k\right) + (-1)^k & 3\left(3^k\right) - (-1)^k \end{pmatrix$ Uses $-(-1)^k = (-1)k+1$ to reach $\frac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 3k+1 + (-1)k+1 & 3k+1 - (-1)k+1 \\ 3k+1 - (-1)k+1 & 3k+1 + (-1)k+1 \end{pmatrix$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$ $\det\left(\mathbf{M^n\right) = \frac{1{4\left[\left(3^n + (-1)^n\right)^2 - \left(3^n - (-1)^n\right)^2\right]$ $= \frac{1{4\left[4\left(3^n\right)(-1)^n\right] = (-3)^n$ cso
items.why: Matrix-power proofs came up in Jan 2025, May 2024 and Jan 2024; the powers of this matrix mix $3^n$ and $(-1)^n$, a sign-alternating form none of the recent matrix proofs needed.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$\sumr=1n (2r-1)^3 = n^2\left(2n^2 - 1\right)$$ Using the result in part (a) and the standard result for $\displaystyle\sumr=1n r^3$, show that $$\sumr=1n\left[(2r)^3 - (2r-1)^3\right] = n^2(4n+3)$$
items.ms: $n = 1$: LHS $= 1^3 = 1$ and RHS $= 1^2(2 - 1) = 1$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes true for $n = k$ and adds the $(k+1)$th term: $\displaystyle\sumr=1k+1 (2r-1)^3 = k^2\left(2k^2 - 1\right) + (2k+1)^3$ Expands to a quartic and attempts to factorise (or expands $(k+1)^2\left(2(k+1)^2 - 1\right)$ to compare): $2k^4 + 8k^3 + 11k^2 + 6k + 1$ $= (k+1)^2\left(2k^2 + 4k + 1\right) = (k+1)^2\left(2(k+1)^2 - 1\right)$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$ Uses $\displaystyle\sumr=1n(2r)^3 = 8\sumr=1n r^3 = 8 \times \frac{1{4n^2(n+1)^2 = 2n^2(n+1)^2$ Subtracts the result of part (a): $2n^2(n+1)^2 - n^2\left(2n^2 - 1\right)$ $= n^2\left(2n^2 + 4n + 2 - 2n^2 + 1\right) = n^2(4n+3)$ cso
items.why: Jun 2026 followed a summation proof with a 'hence' part; here the proved result is combined with the standard sum of cubes from the Series section, as FP1 long questions often link topics.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: A sequence $u_1, u_2, u_3, \dots$ is defined by $$u_1 = 1, \qquad un+1 = \frac{u_n{1 + 2u_n, \quad n \geqslant 1$$ Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$u_n = \frac{1{2n-1$$ Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$\begin{pmatrix 4 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix^n = \begin{pmatrix 3n+1 & -3n \\ 3n & 1-3n \end{pmatrix$$
items.ms: $n = 1$: $\dfrac{1{2(1) - 1 = 1 = u_1$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes $u_k = \dfrac{1{2k-1$ and substitutes into the recurrence: $uk+1 = \dfrac{\frac{1{2k-1{1 + \frac{2{2k-1$ $= \dfrac{1{2k-1 \times \dfrac{2k-1{2k+1 = \dfrac{1{2k+1 = \dfrac{1{2(k+1) - 1$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$ $n = 1$: $\begin{pmatrix 3+1 & -3 \\ 3 & 1-3 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 4 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes true for $n = k$ and multiplies by $\begin{pmatrix 4 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix$ (either order) Correct unsimplified product, e.g. $\begin{pmatrix 4(3k+1) - 9k & -3(3k+1) + 6k \\ 12k + 3(1-3k) & -9k - 2(1-3k) \end{pmatrix$ $= \begin{pmatrix 3k+4 & -3k-3 \\ 3k+3 & -3k-2 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 3(k+1)+1 & -3(k+1) \\ 3(k+1) & 1-3(k+1) \end{pmatrix$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$
items.why: Two separate proofs in one question is the usual FP1 format (Jan 2025, Jan 2024, Jun 2022); matrix powers recur, and a recurrence defined by a fraction rather than a linear rule has not been asked in the recent papers.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: A sequence of numbers $u_1, u_2, u_3, \dots$ is defined by $$u_1 = 3, \quad u_2 = 12, \quad un+2 = 6un+1 - 9u_n, \quad n \geqslant 1$$ Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$u_n = (n+2)3n-1$$ Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$\sumr=1n \frac{r{(r+1)! = 1 - \frac{1{(n+1)!$$
items.ms: $n = 1$: $(1+2)3^0 = 3 = u_1$ and $n = 2$: $(2+2)3^1 = 12 = u_2$ Assumes true for $n = k$ and $n = k + 1$: $u_k = (k+2)3k-1$ and $uk+1 = (k+3)3k$ Substitutes into the recurrence: $uk+2 = 6(k+3)3k - 9(k+2)3k-1$ Writes both terms with the same power of 3, e.g. $= 2(k+3)3k+1 - (k+2)3k+1$ $= (k+4)3k+1 = \left((k+2) + 2\right)3(k+2)-1$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$ and $n = k + 1$, then it is true for $n = k + 2$; as it is true for $n = 1$ and $n = 2$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$ $n = 1$: LHS $= \dfrac{1{2! = \dfrac{1{2$ and RHS $= 1 - \dfrac{1{2! = \dfrac{1{2$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes true for $n = k$ and adds the $(k+1)$th term: $1 - \dfrac{1{(k+1)! + \dfrac{k+1{(k+2)!$ Uses $(k+2)! = (k+2)(k+1)!$: $1 - \dfrac{(k+2) - (k+1){(k+2)! = 1 - \dfrac{1{(k+2)! = 1 - \dfrac{1{\left((k+1)+1\right)!$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$
items.why: Jan 2026 set a second-order recurrence with two base cases; this one has a repeated-root form $(n+2)3^{n-1}$, and the factorial sum follows the factorial and log style of Jan 2023, a summation type rarely set.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: $$\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix 4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix$$ Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $$\mathbf{M^n = \begin{pmatrix 2\left(3^n\right) - 2^n & 2n+1 - 2\left(3^n\right) \\ 3^n - 2^n & 2n+1 - 3^n \end{pmatrix$$ The diagram shows the parallelogram $R$ with vertices $O(0, 0)$, $A(4, 0)$, $B(5, 3)$ and $C(1, 3)$. The parallelogram $R$ is transformed onto the parallelogram $R_n$ by the transformation represented by $\mathbf{M^n$, where $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$. Find the smallest value of $n$ for which the area of $R_n$ is greater than $10^6$ square units. Show that the formula for $\mathbf{M^n$ in part (a) also gives $\mathbf{M-1$ when $n = -1$
items.ms: $n = 1$: $\begin{pmatrix 6 - 2 & 4 - 6 \\ 3 - 2 & 4 - 3 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix = \mathbf{M$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes true for $n = k$ and multiplies $\mathbf{M^k$ by $\mathbf{M$ (either order) Correct unsimplified product, e.g. $\begin{pmatrix 8\left(3^k\right) - 4\left(2^k\right) + 2k+1 - 2\left(3^k\right) & -4\left(3^k\right) + 2k+1 + 2k+1 - 2\left(3^k\right) \\ 4\left(3^k\right) - 4\left(2^k\right) + 2k+1 - 3^k & -2\left(3^k\right) + 2k+1 + 2k+1 - 3^k \end{pmatrix$ $= \begin{pmatrix 6\left(3^k\right) - 2\left(2^k\right) & 4\left(2^k\right) - 6\left(3^k\right) \\ 3\left(3^k\right) - 2\left(2^k\right) & 4\left(2^k\right) - 3\left(3^k\right) \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 2\left(3k+1\right) - 2k+1 & 2k+2 - 2\left(3k+1\right) \\ 3k+1 - 2k+1 & 2k+2 - 3k+1 \end{pmatrix$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$ Area of $R = 4 \times 3 = 12$ $\det\mathbf{M = 4 + 2 = 6$, so the area scale factor of $\mathbf{M^n$ is $6^n$ Sets up $12 \times 6^n > 10^6$ and solves, e.g. $n > \dfrac{\log\left(\frac{10^6{12\right){\log 6 = 6.32\ldots$, or finds $12 \times 6^6 = 559\,872$ and $12 \times 6^7 = 3\,359\,232$ $n = 7$ Finds $\mathbf{M-1 = \dfrac{1{6\begin{pmatrix 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 \end{pmatrix$ and substitutes $n = -1$ into the formula: $\begin{pmatrix \frac{2{3 - \frac{1{2 & 1 - \frac{2{3 \\ \frac{1{3 - \frac{1{2 & 1 - \frac{1{3 \end{pmatrix$ Both equal $\begin{pmatrix \frac{1{6 & \frac{1{3 \\ -\frac{1{6 & \frac{2{3 \end{pmatrix$, so the formula gives $\mathbf{M-1$ when $n = -1$
items.why: Matrix-power proofs came up in Jan 2025, May 2024 (followed by an area) and Jan 2024; this matrix is not triangular and its powers mix $2^n$ and $3^n$, and the inverse check takes the result beyond the positive integers.

items.name: Proof by induction
items.question: A sequence $u_1, u_2, u_3, \dots$ is defined by $$u_1 = 4, \qquad un+1 = 3u_n - 4n + 2, \quad n \geqslant 1$$ The constants $p$ and $q$ are such that $p\left(3n-1\right) + qn$ is equal to $u_n$ when $n = 1$ and when $n = 2$. Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$. Prove by induction that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$, $u_n = p\left(3n-1\right) + qn$, where $p$ and $q$ are your values from part (a)(i). $$\mathrm{f(n) = n^3 + 3n^2 + 8n$$ A student is trying to prove by induction that $\mathrm{f(n)$ is divisible by 6 for all positive integers $n$. The student correctly shows that $\mathrm{f(1) = 12$, then shows that $\mathrm{f(k+1) - \mathrm{f(k)$ is a multiple of 3 and concludes that, if $\mathrm{f(k)$ is divisible by 6, then $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ is divisible by 6. Explain the error in the student's reasoning. Prove by induction that, for all positive integers $n$, $\mathrm{f(n)$ is divisible by 6.
items.ms: Finds $u_2 = 3(4) - 4 + 2 = 10$ and forms two equations, $p + q = 4$ and $3p + 2q = 10$ $p = 2$, $q = 2$ $n = 1$: $2\left(3^0\right) + 2(1) = 4 = u_1$, so true for $n = 1$ Assumes $u_k = 2\left(3k-1\right) + 2k$ and substitutes into the recurrence: $uk+1 = 3\left[2\left(3k-1\right) + 2k\right] - 4k + 2$ $= 2\left(3k\right) + 6k - 4k + 2 = 2\left(3k\right) + 2k + 2$ $= 2\left(3(k+1)-1\right) + 2(k+1)$ Conclusion: if the result is true for $n = k$, then it is true for $n = k + 1$; as it is true for $n = 1$, it is true for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$ A multiple of 3 need not be a multiple of 6 (e.g. 9), so $\mathrm{f(k+1) = \mathrm{f(k) + 3m$ is only divisible by 6 if $3m$ is; the student must show that $\mathrm{f(k+1) - \mathrm{f(k)$ is a multiple of 6 (i.e. $m$ is even) $\mathrm{f(1) = 1 + 3 + 8 = 12 = 2 \times 6$, so divisible by 6 Assumes $\mathrm{f(k)$ is divisible by 6 and attempts $\mathrm{f(k+1) - \mathrm{f(k)$ (or expands $\mathrm{f(k+1)$) $\mathrm{f(k+1) - \mathrm{f(k) = 3k^2 + 9k + 12 = 3\left(k^2 + 3k + 4\right)$ Shows $k^2 + 3k + 4$ is even, e.g. $k^2 + 3k = k(k+3)$ and one of $k$, $k + 3$ is even (or $k^2 + 3k = k(k+1) + 2k$), so $\mathrm{f(k+1) = \mathrm{f(k) + 6m$ for an integer $m$ Conclusion: if $\mathrm{f(k)$ is divisible by 6 then $\mathrm{f(k+1)$ is divisible by 6; as $\mathrm{f(1)$ is divisible by 6, $\mathrm{f(n)$ is divisible by 6 for all $n \in \mathbb{Z^+$
items.why: General-term proofs came up in Jan 2026, Jan 2025 and Jun 2022 and divisibility in nearly every session; finding the constants first and a polynomial whose step needs a parity argument (with a flawed proof to criticise) have not been asked.

items.name: Sum of roots and product of roots of a quadratic equation
path: FP1.2.1 - Sum of roots and product of
items.question: The quadratic equation $$2x^2 + px + 9 = 0$$ where $p$ is a negative constant, has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Write down, in terms of $p$ where necessary, the value of $\alpha + \beta$ and the value of $\alpha\beta$. Given that $\alpha = 2\beta$, determine the value of $p$.
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{p{2$ and $\alpha\beta = \dfrac{9{2$ Substitutes $\alpha = 2\beta$ into the product of the roots: $2\beta^2 = \dfrac{9{2$ $\beta = \pm\dfrac{3{2$ Uses the sum of the roots, $3\beta = -\dfrac{p{2$, and rejects $\beta = -\dfrac{3{2$ (which gives $p = 9 > 0$): $p = -9$
items.why: FP1.2.1 has come up in 21 of 26 sessions, almost always as a 1-mark 'write down α + β and αβ'; using the sum and product to find an unknown coefficient (Jun 2025 Q6(b), Jan 2022 Q6) is how it earns more marks, and roots in a given ratio have not appeared in the papers listed.

items.name: Manipulation of expressions involving the sum of roots and…
items.question: The quadratic equation $$3x^2 + 2x - 4 = 0$$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$, where $\alpha > \beta$. Without solving the equation, write down the value of $\alpha + \beta$ and the value of $\alpha\beta$, show that $(\alpha - \beta)^2 = \dfrac{52{9$, hence determine the exact value of $\alpha^2 - \beta^2$.
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{2{3$ and $\alpha\beta = -\dfrac{4{3$ Uses $(\alpha - \beta)^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 4\alpha\beta$, or $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 - 2\alpha\beta$ with $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta$, and their values $\left(-\dfrac{2{3\right)^2 - 4\left(-\dfrac{4{3\right) = \dfrac{4{9 + \dfrac{16{3 = \dfrac{52{9$ * $\alpha - \beta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{13{3$, taking the positive square root because $\alpha > \beta$ Uses $\alpha^2 - \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)(\alpha - \beta)$ with their values $\alpha^2 - \beta^2 = -\dfrac{4\sqrt{13{9$
items.why: FP1.2.2 has come up in 25 of 26 sessions, nearly always as α² + β² or α³ + β³; the difference of the roots, (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ with its sign fixed by α > β, has not appeared in the recent papers and is the natural next variation.

items.name: Manipulation of expressions involving the sum of roots and…
items.question: The quadratic equation $$x^2 - x + 4 = 0$$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Write down the value of $\alpha + \beta$ and the value of $\alpha\beta$. Use the fact that $\alpha$ is a root of the equation to show that $$\alpha^3 = -3\alpha - 4$$ Hence determine the value of $\alpha^3 + \beta^3$. Determine the value of $\alpha^6 + \beta^6$.
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = 1$ and $\alpha\beta = 4$ Uses $\alpha^2 = \alpha - 4$ and multiplies by $\alpha$: $\alpha^3 = \alpha^2 - 4\alpha$ $\alpha^3 = (\alpha - 4) - 4\alpha = -3\alpha - 4$ * Uses $\beta^3 = -3\beta - 4$ as well and adds: $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = -3(\alpha + \beta) - 8$ $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = -11$ Uses $\alpha^6 + \beta^6 = (\alpha^3 + \beta^3)^2 - 2(\alpha\beta)^3$ with their values, or squares (b): $\alpha^6 = 9\alpha^2 + 24\alpha + 16 = 33\alpha - 20$ and adds the result for $\beta$ $\alpha^6 + \beta^6 = 121 - 128 = -7$
items.why: α³ + β³ came up again in Jan 2026 and Jun 2026; reducing powers with the equation itself (α² = α − 4) is a method the papers have not yet required, and it extends naturally to sixth powers.

items.name: Manipulation of expressions involving the sum of roots and…
items.question: The quadratic equation $$2x^2 + kx + (k - 1) = 0$$ where $k$ is a real constant, has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Write down, in terms of $k$, the value of $\alpha + \beta$ and the value of $\alpha\beta$. Show that $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = \dfrac{(k - 2)^2{4$. Given that $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = \dfrac{9{4$ and that $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are real, determine the value of $k$, giving a reason for your answer. Using your value of $k$, determine the exact value of $\alpha^3 + \beta^3$.
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{k{2$ and $\alpha\beta = \dfrac{k - 1{2$ Uses $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta$ with their expressions: $\dfrac{k^2{4 - (k - 1)$ $= \dfrac{k^2 - 4k + 4{4 = \dfrac{(k - 2)^2{4$ * Sets $\dfrac{(k - 2)^2{4 = \dfrac{9{4$ and solves: $k - 2 = \pm 3$ $k = 5$ or $k = -1$ Uses the discriminant $k^2 - 8(k - 1)$: $k = 5$ gives $-7 < 0$, so the roots are not real; $k = -1$ gives $17 > 0$. Hence $k = -1$ Uses $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha + \beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha + \beta)$ with $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{1{2$ and $\alpha\beta = -1$ (their $k$) $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = \dfrac{1{8 + \dfrac{3{2 = \dfrac{13{8$
items.why: Expressions in a parameter recur (Jan 2023 in k, Jan 2022 in A, Jun 2025 Q6(b) 'α + β = 9αβ'); a condition that gives two values of k, one rejected because the roots must be real, is an untested twist.

items.name: Quadratics with new roots
items.question: The quadratic equation $$3x^2 - 4x + 6 = 0$$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Without solving the equation, write down the value of $\alpha + \beta$ and the value of $\alpha\beta$, determine a quadratic equation, with integer coefficients, that has roots $(2\alpha - \beta)$ and $(2\beta - \alpha)$.
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{4{3$ and $\alpha\beta = 2$ Sum of new roots $= \alpha + \beta = \dfrac{4{3$ Expands the product: $(2\alpha - \beta)(2\beta - \alpha) = 5\alpha\beta - 2(\alpha^2 + \beta^2)$, and uses $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta$ Product $= 10 - 2\left(-\dfrac{20{9\right) = \dfrac{130{9$ Applies $x^2 - (\text{sum)x + (\text{product) = 0$ with their sum and product $9x^2 - 12x + 130 = 0$
items.why: FP1.2.3 has come up in 24 of 26 sessions as a 3–6 mark 'quadratic with integer coefficients' part; linear combinations of the roots such as 2α − β are the core type with fresh numbers.

items.name: Quadratics with new roots
items.question: The quadratic equation $$3x^2 + 5x + 4 = 0$$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Without solving the equation, write down the value of $\alpha + \beta$ and the value of $\alpha\beta$, determine the value of $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$, determine a quadratic equation in the form $px^2 + qx + r = 0$, where $p$, $q$ and $r$ are integers, that has roots $$\dfrac{\alpha + 1{\beta \quad \text{and \quad \dfrac{\beta + 1{\alpha$$
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{5{3$ and $\alpha\beta = \dfrac{4{3$ Uses $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta$ with their values $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = \dfrac{25{9 - \dfrac{8{3 = \dfrac{1{9$ Sum over a common denominator: $\dfrac{\alpha^2 + \alpha + \beta^2 + \beta{\alpha\beta = \dfrac{(\alpha^2 + \beta^2) + (\alpha + \beta){\alpha\beta$ Sum $= \dfrac{\frac{1{9 - \frac{5{3{\frac{4{3 = -\dfrac{7{6$ Product: $\dfrac{(\alpha + 1)(\beta + 1){\alpha\beta = \dfrac{\alpha\beta + (\alpha + \beta) + 1{\alpha\beta$ Product $= \dfrac{1{2$ Applies $x^2 - (\text{sum)x + (\text{product) = 0$ with their sum and product $6x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0$
items.why: Fractional new roots dominate recent papers (Jan 2025 α + 1/α, Jan 2024 α − 1/β², Jun 2023 α/(α² + 1), Jan 2023 α/β²); (α + 1)/β tests both the sum and the product over a common denominator with fresh numbers.

items.name: Quadratics with new roots
items.question: The quadratic equation $$2x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0$$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Write down the value of $\alpha + \beta$ and the value of $\alpha\beta$. Without solving the equation, determine a quadratic equation, with integer coefficients, that has roots $\dfrac{\alpha{\beta$ and $\dfrac{\beta{\alpha$. Solve the equation found in part (b), giving each root in the form $a + b\mathrm{i$, where $a$ and $b$ are real, and show that each root has modulus 1. Find the argument of each root found in part (c), giving your answers in radians to 2 decimal places.
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = 1$ and $\alpha\beta = \dfrac{5{2$ Uses $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = -4$ Sum of new roots $= \dfrac{\alpha^2 + \beta^2{\alpha\beta$ and product $= \dfrac{\alpha{\beta \times \dfrac{\beta{\alpha = 1$ Sum $= -\dfrac{8{5$ $5x^2 + 8x + 5 = 0$ Solves their 3TQ, e.g. $x = \dfrac{-8 \pm \sqrt{64 - 100{10$ or by completing the square $x = -\dfrac{4{5 \pm \dfrac{3{5\mathrm{i$ $\left|-\dfrac{4{5 \pm \dfrac{3{5\mathrm{i\right| = \sqrt{\dfrac{16{25 + \dfrac{9{25 = 1$ Uses $\arctan\dfrac{3{4$ (or $\arctan\dfrac{4{3$) and places the roots in the second and third quadrants: $\pm\left(\pi - \arctan\dfrac{3{4\right)$ $\arg = 2.50$ and $-2.50$
items.why: Most quadratics in this topic have non-real roots, yet the papers listed never link the new roots to modulus and argument (FP1.1); α/β and β/α of conjugate roots lie on the unit circle, a natural synoptic question.

items.name: Quadratics with new roots
items.question: The quadratic equation $$x^2 + px + q = 0$$ where $p$ and $q$ are real constants, has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Show that a quadratic equation whose roots are $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$ is $$x^2 - (p^2 - 2q)x + q^2 = 0$$ In the rest of this question, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $$x^2 + 3x - 1 = 0$$ Using the result of part (a) twice, determine a quadratic equation, with integer coefficients, whose roots are $\alpha^4$ and $\beta^4$. Hence determine the value of $\alpha^8 + \beta^8$. Determine a quadratic equation, with integer coefficients, whose roots are $\alpha^3$ and $\beta^3$.
items.ms: $\alpha + \beta = -p$ and $\alpha\beta = q$ $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = p^2 - 2q$ and $\alpha^2\beta^2 = (\alpha\beta)^2 = q^2$ Applies $x^2 - (\text{sum)x + (\text{product) = 0$ to reach $x^2 - (p^2 - 2q)x + q^2 = 0$ * Applies (a) with $p = 3$, $q = -1$: $x^2 - (9 + 2)x + 1 = 0$ $x^2 - 11x + 1 = 0$ has roots $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$ Applies (a) again with $p = -11$, $q = 1$: $x^2 - (121 - 2)x + 1 = 0$ $x^2 - 119x + 1 = 0$ Applies the sum from (a) to $x^2 - 119x + 1 = 0$: $\alpha^8 + \beta^8 = 119^2 - 2(1)$ $\alpha^8 + \beta^8 = 14159$ Uses $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha + \beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha + \beta)$ with $\alpha + \beta = -3$ and $\alpha\beta = -1$ $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = -27 - 9 = -36$ and $\alpha^3\beta^3 = (\alpha\beta)^3 = -1$ $x^2 + 36x - 1 = 0$
items.why: Jan 2026 Q6 asked for a quadratic in terms of letters (q and r) and Jan 2026 Q5 used fourth powers; a general α², β² result applied twice is the likeliest extension, with α³ and β³ (Jun 2026 Q7) as the core type.
