items.name: Solving equations numerically
path: FP1.3.1 - Equations of the form f(x)
items.question: $$\mathrm{f(x) = 8\sqrt{x + \dfrac{11{x - 18, \qquad x > 0$$ The diagram shows a sketch of part of the curve with equation $y = \mathrm{f(x)$. The curve crosses the $x$-axis at the points where $x = \alpha$ and $x = \beta$, where $\alpha < \beta$. A student calculates $\mathrm{f(1)$ and $\mathrm{f(4)$ and concludes that the equation $\mathrm{f(x) = 0$ has no root in the interval $[1,\ 4]$. Find $\mathrm{f(1)$ and $\mathrm{f(4)$ and, with reference to the diagram, explain why the student's conclusion is wrong. Show that $\alpha$ lies in the interval $[1.1,\ 1.2]$. Use linear interpolation once on the interval $[1.1,\ 1.2]$ to find an approximation to $\alpha$, giving your answer to 3 decimal places. Taking $x_0 = 3.5$ as a first approximation to $\beta$, apply the Newton-Raphson process once to $\mathrm{f(x)$ to find a second approximation to $\beta$. Give your answer to 3 decimal places. Given that $\alpha = 1.183$ to 3 decimal places, explain, with reference to the shape of the curve, why your answer to part (c) is greater than $\alpha$.
items.ms: $\mathrm{f(1) = 1$ and $\mathrm{f(4) = 0.75$ (both positive) No change of sign does not mean no root: the curve crosses the $x$-axis twice between $x = 1$ and $x = 4$ (at $\alpha$ and $\beta$), so $\mathrm{f$ changes sign twice and the signs at the ends are the same Attempts $\mathrm{f(1.1)$ and $\mathrm{f(1.2)$, with at least one correct to 1 s.f. (rounded or truncated) $\mathrm{f(1.1) = 0.390$ and $\mathrm{f(1.2) = -0.0698$; change of sign and $\mathrm{f$ continuous on $[1.1,\ 1.2]$, so $1.1 < \alpha < 1.2$ A correct linear interpolation statement with their values, e.g. $\dfrac{\alpha - 1.1{0.390 = \dfrac{1.2 - \alpha{0.0698$ $\alpha = 1.1 + 0.1 \times \dfrac{0.390{0.390 + 0.0698$ $(= 1.18484\ldots)$ $\alpha = 1.185$ Differentiates: $x^n \to xn-1$ for at least one term $\mathrm{f'(x) = 4x-\frac{1{2 - 11x-2$ Correct use of the Newton-Raphson formula: $3.5 - \dfrac{0.109{1.240$ $x_1 = 3.412$ Between $x = 1.1$ and $x = 1.2$ the curve is convex (it bends upwards), so the chord joining $(1.1,\ \mathrm{f(1.1))$ and $(1.2,\ \mathrm{f(1.2))$ lies above the curve; the chord therefore crosses the $x$-axis to the right of $\alpha$
items.why: Long FP1 questions combine a sign change, interpolation and Newton–Raphson on one f(x) (Jan 2025 Q2, Jun 2026 Q4); why the same sign at both ends does not rule out roots, and why interpolation over- or underestimates, have not been asked in the papers listed.

items.name: Linear transformations of column vectors in two dimensions and…
items.question: The transformation $T$ of the plane is represented by the matrix $\mathbf{M$, where $$\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix 3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix$$ The point $P(2p - 1,\ p + 3)$, where $p$ is a constant, is mapped by $T$ onto the point $P'(q,\ -5)$. Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$. Show that $T$ maps every point on the line with equation $y = -x$ onto itself. The line $l$ has equation $y = x + 1$. Find a Cartesian equation of the image of $l$ under $T$.
items.ms: Multiplies $\begin{pmatrix 3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix\begin{pmatrix 2p - 1 \\ p + 3 \end{pmatrix$ to give $\begin{pmatrix 8p + 3 \\ 1 - 2p \end{pmatrix$ Sets $1 - 2p = -5$ (or $8p + 3 = q$) and solves for $p$ $p = 3$ and $q = 27$ Applies $\mathbf{M$ to a general point of the line, e.g. $\begin{pmatrix 3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix\begin{pmatrix t \\ -t \end{pmatrix$ $= \begin{pmatrix 3t - 2t \\ -t \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix t \\ -t \end{pmatrix$, so every point $(t, -t)$ is mapped onto itself Applies $\mathbf{M$ to a general point of $l$: $\begin{pmatrix 3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix\begin{pmatrix t \\ t + 1 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 5t + 2 \\ -t \end{pmatrix$ Eliminates the parameter, e.g. $x = 5t + 2$ with $t = -y$ $x + 5y = 2$ oe
items.why: FP1.6.1 has come up in 7 of 26 sessions, almost always as 'find p from a mapped point' (Jan2020, Jan2021); points mapped onto themselves were last asked in Jun2014 and the image of a whole line has never been asked, so these are the likeliest new angles.

items.name: 2 × 2 matrices as transformations
items.question: $$\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix$$ Describe fully the single geometrical transformation represented by the matrix $\mathbf{A$. The matrix $\mathbf{B$ represents a rotation through 135° anticlockwise about $(0, 0)$. Write down the matrix $\mathbf{B$, giving each element in exact form. The matrix $\mathbf{C$ represents an enlargement with centre $(0, 0)$ and scale factor $\dfrac{2{3$. The triangle $T$ has area 4.5 square units and is transformed onto the triangle $T'$ by $\mathbf{C$. Write down the matrix $\mathbf{C$ and find the area of $T'$.
items.ms: Reflection in the line $y = -x$ $\mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix -\dfrac{\sqrt{2{2 & -\dfrac{\sqrt{2{2 \\ \dfrac{\sqrt{2{2 & -\dfrac{\sqrt{2{2 \end{pmatrix$ $\mathbf{C = \begin{pmatrix \dfrac{2{3 & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac{2{3 \end{pmatrix$ Area of $T' = \dfrac{4{9 \times 4.5 = 2$ square units
items.why: FP1.6.2 has come up in all 26 sessions; 'describe fully' a reflection and 'write down' an exact rotation matrix recur (Jun2025, Jan2024), while an enlargement with a fractional scale factor that shrinks the area has not been asked.

items.name: 2 × 2 matrices as transformations
items.question: $$\mathbf{R = \dfrac{1{5\begin{pmatrix 4 & 3 \\ -3 & 4 \end{pmatrix$$ Describe fully the single geometrical transformation represented by the matrix $\mathbf{R$, giving the angle in degrees to one decimal place. Write down the matrix $\mathbf{R-1$, giving a geometrical reason for your answer. The matrix $\mathbf{S$ represents a reflection in the $x$-axis. Show that $\mathbf{S\mathbf{R\mathbf{S = \mathbf{R-1$.
items.ms: Rotation about $(0, 0)$ Uses $\cos\theta = \dfrac{4{5$ and $\sin\theta = -\dfrac{3{5$ (or $\tan\theta = -\dfrac{3{4$) to find the angle 36.9° clockwise (or 323.1° anticlockwise) The inverse transformation undoes $\mathbf{R$: it is a rotation through 36.9° anticlockwise about $(0, 0)$ $\mathbf{R-1 = \dfrac{1{5\begin{pmatrix 4 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix$ Uses $\mathbf{S = \begin{pmatrix 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix$ and finds one product correctly, e.g. $\mathbf{S\mathbf{R = \dfrac{1{5\begin{pmatrix 4 & 3 \\ 3 & -4 \end{pmatrix$ or $\mathbf{R\mathbf{S = \dfrac{1{5\begin{pmatrix 4 & -3 \\ -3 & -4 \end{pmatrix$ $\mathbf{S\mathbf{R\mathbf{S = \dfrac{1{5\begin{pmatrix 4 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix = \mathbf{R-1$ cso
items.why: Every session has a 'describe fully' part, but only rotations through exact angles (90°, 120°, 210°) have been asked; a rotation through a non-standard clockwise angle, and its inverse written down from the geometry, have not.

items.name: 2 × 2 matrices as transformations
items.question: The transformation $U$ of the plane is represented by the matrix $$\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix k & 3 \\ 4 & k + 4 \end{pmatrix$$ where $k$ is a real constant. Find the values of $k$ for which $U$ has no inverse transformation. In this part $k = 2$. Show that $U$ maps every point of the plane onto a point of a single straight line, and find an equation of this line. The triangle $D$ has area 4 square units. $U$ transforms $D$ onto the triangle $D'$, which has area 132 square units. Find the possible values of $k$.
items.ms: $\det\mathbf{M = k(k + 4) - 12$ set equal to 0 and solves $k2 + 4k - 12 = 0$ $k = 2$ or $k = -6$ $\begin{pmatrix 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 6 \end{pmatrix\begin{pmatrix x \\ y \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 2x + 3y \\ 4x + 6y \end{pmatrix$ Notes $4x + 6y = 2(2x + 3y)$, so the image $(X, Y)$ of every point satisfies $Y = 2X$ $y = 2x$ Area scale factor $= \dfrac{132{4 = 33$, so $|k2 + 4k - 12| = 33$ Solves $k2 + 4k - 12 = 33$, i.e. $k2 + 4k - 45 = 0$ $k = 5$ or $k = -9$ Considers $k2 + 4k - 12 = -33$, i.e. $k2 + 4k + 21 = 0$, and shows it has no real roots, e.g. discriminant $16 - 84 < 0$
items.why: Area-scale-factor parts appear in most recent sessions (Jan2026, Jun2026); the negative-determinant case and the collapse of the whole plane onto a line by a singular matrix have never been asked.

items.name: 2 × 2 matrices as transformations
items.question: $$\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix k - 1 & k - 3 \\ 3 - k & k - 1 \end{pmatrix$$ where $k$ is a real constant. Find the value of $k$ for which $\mathbf{M$ represents an enlargement, and describe this enlargement fully. Show that $\det\mathbf{M = 2(k - 2)2 + 2$ Hence show that there is no value of $k$ for which $\mathbf{M$ represents a rotation about $(0, 0)$. In this part $k = 0$. Describe fully the transformation represented by $\mathbf{M$ as a combination of an enlargement and a rotation, giving the angle in degrees to one decimal place.
items.ms: An enlargement matrix has zero off-diagonal elements: $k - 3 = 0$ $k = 3$, giving $\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix$ Enlargement, centre $(0, 0)$, scale factor 2 $\det\mathbf{M = (k - 1)(k - 1) - (k - 3)(3 - k)$ $= (k - 1)2 + (k - 3)2 = 2k2 - 8k + 10$ $= 2(k2 - 4k + 5) = 2(k - 2)2 + 2$ A rotation matrix $\begin{pmatrix \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{pmatrix$ has determinant $\cos2\theta + \sin2\theta = 1$ (a rotation does not change area) $(k - 2)2 \geqslant 0$, so $\det\mathbf{M \geqslant 2$ and can never equal 1: no value of $k$ gives a rotation $\det\mathbf{M = 10$, so $\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix -1 & -3 \\ 3 & -1 \end{pmatrix = \sqrt{10\begin{pmatrix -\dfrac{1{\sqrt{10 & -\dfrac{3{\sqrt{10 \\ \dfrac{3{\sqrt{10 & -\dfrac{1{\sqrt{10 \end{pmatrix$, with $\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1{\sqrt{10$ and $\sin\theta = \dfrac{3{\sqrt{10$ Enlargement, centre $(0, 0)$, scale factor $\sqrt{10$ Rotation through 108.4° anticlockwise about $(0, 0)$
items.why: Matrices with a parameter come up regularly (Jan2025 'find k', Jun2026 'describe C when p = 3'); asking which value of k gives an enlargement, proving that no value gives a rotation, and splitting a matrix into an enlargement and a rotation through an obtuse angle have not been asked.

items.name: Combinations of transformations
items.question: The diagram shows the triangle $T$ with vertices $P(1, 2)$, $Q(3, 2)$ and $R(1, 3)$, and the triangle $T'$ with vertices $P'(-2, 3)$, $Q'(-2, 9)$ and $R'(-3, 3)$. The linear transformation represented by the $2 \times 2$ matrix $\mathbf{M$ maps $P$, $Q$ and $R$ onto $P'$, $Q'$ and $R'$ respectively. Find the matrix $\mathbf{M$. The transformation represented by $\mathbf{M$ is equivalent to a stretch followed by a rotation. Describe fully the stretch and the rotation. Find $\mathbf{M2$ and describe fully the single geometrical transformation represented by $\mathbf{M2$.
items.ms: Forms $\mathbf{M\begin{pmatrix 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix -2 & -2 \\ 3 & 9 \end{pmatrix$ or equivalent simultaneous equations using two of the vertices Finds $\begin{pmatrix 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 \end{pmatrix-1 = -\dfrac{1{4\begin{pmatrix 2 & -3 \\ -2 & 1 \end{pmatrix$ and post-multiplies, or solves the equations One correct row of $\mathbf{M$ $\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix 0 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 \end{pmatrix$ Stretch parallel to the $x$-axis scale factor 3 Rotation about $(0, 0)$ through 90° anticlockwise $\mathbf{M2 = \begin{pmatrix -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 \end{pmatrix$ Enlargement, centre $(0, 0)$, scale factor $-3$
items.why: Combined transformations have come up in 23 of 26 sessions, always as a product to be found; working back from a diagram to the matrix and splitting it into a stretch and a rotation has not been asked, and a negative scale factor (allowed by the spec) never has.

items.name: Combinations of transformations
items.question: $$\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix -\dfrac{1{2 & -\dfrac{\sqrt{3{2 \\ \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2 & -\dfrac{1{2 \end{pmatrix$$ The diagram shows the equilateral triangle $T$ with vertices $P(0, 4)$, $Q(-2\sqrt{3, -2)$ and $R(2\sqrt{3, -2)$. Describe fully the single geometrical transformation represented by the matrix $\mathbf{A$. Show that the transformation represented by $\mathbf{A$ maps $T$ onto itself, stating the image of each vertex. Find the matrix $\mathbf{A100$. The matrix $\mathbf{B$ represents a stretch parallel to the $y$-axis with scale factor 2. Write down the matrix $\mathbf{B$. The transformation represented by $\mathbf{A$ followed by the transformation represented by $\mathbf{B$ is represented by the matrix $\mathbf{C$. Find $\mathbf{C$. The triangle $T$ is transformed onto the triangle $T'$ by $\mathbf{C$. Find the exact area of $T'$.
items.ms: Rotation about $(0, 0)$ through 120° anticlockwise Multiplies $\mathbf{A$ by at least one vertex, e.g. $\mathbf{A\begin{pmatrix 0 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix -2\sqrt{3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix$ Two images correct, e.g. $P \mapsto Q$ and $Q \mapsto R$, since $\mathbf{A\begin{pmatrix -2\sqrt{3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix = \begin{pmatrix 2\sqrt{3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix$ $R \mapsto P$, and concludes that the vertices are permuted so $T$ is mapped onto itself Uses $\mathbf{A3 = \mathbf{I$ (three rotations of 120° make 360°), so $\mathbf{A100 = (\mathbf{A3)33\mathbf{A = \mathbf{A$ $\mathbf{A100 = \begin{pmatrix -\dfrac{1{2 & -\dfrac{\sqrt{3{2 \\ \dfrac{\sqrt{3{2 & -\dfrac{1{2 \end{pmatrix$ $\mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix$ $\mathbf{C = \mathbf{BA$ (correct order) with an attempt at the product $\mathbf{C = \begin{pmatrix -\dfrac{1{2 & -\dfrac{\sqrt{3{2 \\ \sqrt{3 & -1 \end{pmatrix$ Area of $T = \dfrac{1{2 \times 4\sqrt{3 \times 6 = 12\sqrt{3$, multiplied by their $\det\mathbf{C$ $\det\mathbf{C = 2$, so the area of $T'$ is $24\sqrt{3$ square units
items.why: Powers and combinations of rotations recur (Jun2019 A⁶, Jun2022 smallest n with Aⁿ = I, Jan2024 'A followed by B'); reducing a high power with A³ = I, and a shape that a rotation maps onto itself, are the likely new angles.

items.name: The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or…
items.question: The transformation $U$ is represented by the matrix $$\mathbf{U = \begin{pmatrix 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix$$ The transformation $V$ is a rotation through 90° anticlockwise about $(0, 0)$ and is represented by the matrix $\mathbf{V$. The transformation $U$ followed by the transformation $V$ maps the triangle $T$ onto the triangle $T'$. The diagram shows $T'$, which has vertices $A'(-2, 2)$, $B'(-4, 2)$ and $C'(-3, 5)$, the images of the vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ of $T$. Write down the matrix $\mathbf{V$. Find the matrix which represents the transformation that maps $T'$ back onto $T$. Hence find the coordinates of $A$, $B$ and $C$.
items.ms: $\mathbf{V = \begin{pmatrix 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix$ Recognises that the matrix is $(\mathbf{VU)-1$ or $\mathbf{U-1\mathbf{V-1$ Attempts the inverse of a product of $\mathbf{U$ and $\mathbf{V$, e.g. finds $\mathbf{VU = \begin{pmatrix -2 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 \end{pmatrix$ and attempts its inverse, or finds $\mathbf{U-1 = \dfrac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 \end{pmatrix$ and $\mathbf{V-1 = \begin{pmatrix 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix$ and multiplies them $\dfrac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 1 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 \end{pmatrix$ Applies their matrix from (b) to at least one vertex of $T'$, e.g. $\dfrac{1{2\begin{pmatrix 1 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 \end{pmatrix\begin{pmatrix -2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix$ $A(0, 2)$, $B(-1, 6)$, $C(1, 1)$
items.why: FP1.6.4 has come up in only 6 of 26 sessions but in both Jun2025 and Jun2026 (working back from an image point); inverting a combination with (VU)⁻¹ = U⁻¹V⁻¹ to recover a whole shape is the natural next step.

items.name: Summing finite series
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s
items.question: Use the standard results for $\sumr=1n r$ and $\sumr=1n r2$ to show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$\sumr=1n(3r - 1)(r + 2) = n(n2 + an + b)$$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers to be found. Hence find the value of $$\sumr=1130(3r - 1)(r + 2)$$
items.ms: Expands to $3r2 + 5r - 2$ and substitutes at least one standard result correctly $\dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)(2n + 1) + \dfrac{5{2n(n + 1) - 2n$ (all three terms, with $\sumr=1n 2 = 2n$) $= \dfrac{1{2n(2n2 + 8n + 2) = n(n2 + 4n + 1)$, so $a = 4$, $b = 1$ Uses $\mathrm{f(30) - \mathrm{f(10)$ with $\mathrm{f(n) = n(n2 + 4n + 1)$: $30 \times 1021 - 10 \times 141$ 29220
items.why: FP1.7.1 has come up in all 26 sessions, almost always as 'use the standard results to show' followed by a 'hence' evaluation between two limits (Jun2026 Q3, Jan2026 Q1).

items.name: Summing finite series
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s
items.question: $$S_n = 1 \times 4 + 3 \times 7 + 5 \times 10 + \dots + (2n - 1)(3n + 1)$$ Use the standard results for $\sumr=1n r$ and $\sumr=1n r2$ to show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$S_n = \dfrac{n{2(4n2 + 5n - 1)$$ Hence find the value of $$1 \times 4 + 3 \times 7 + 5 \times 10 + \dots + 39 \times 61$$
items.ms: Writes $S_n = \sumr=1n(2r - 1)(3r + 1) = \sumr=1n(6r2 - r - 1)$ Substitutes the standard results: $n(n + 1)(2n + 1) - \dfrac{1{2n(n + 1) - n$ Takes out a factor of $\dfrac{n{2$ (or $n$) and collects terms: $\dfrac{n{2\left(2(2n2 + 3n + 1) - (n + 1) - 2\right)$ $= \dfrac{n{2(4n2 + 5n - 1)$ Identifies $n = 20$ (from $2n - 1 = 39$ and $3n + 1 = 61$) and substitutes into $S_n$ 16990
items.why: Series of products written out term by term were asked in Jun2022 and Jan2025; forming the general term and the number of terms from a written series is a step examiners report candidates often get wrong.

items.name: Summing finite series
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s
items.question: Use the standard results to show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$\sumr=1n r2(4r - 3) = \dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)(2n2 - 1)$$ Hence, or otherwise, show that $$\sumr=1n(r + 1)2(4r + 1) = \dfrac{n{2(2n3 + an2 + bn + c)$$ where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers to be found.
items.ms: Uses $4\sumr=1n r3 - 3\sumr=1n r2$ with at least one correct standard result $n2(n + 1)2 - \dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)(2n + 1)$ Takes out a factor of $\dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)$: $\dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)\left(2n(n + 1) - (2n + 1)\right)$ $= \dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)(2n2 - 1)$ Recognises $(r + 1)2(4(r + 1) - 3)$, so the sum is $\sumr=2n+1 r2(4r - 3) = \mathrm{f(n + 1) - \mathrm{f(1)$, where $\mathrm{f(n)$ is the result in (a) $\dfrac{1{2(n + 1)(n + 2)\left(2(n + 1)2 - 1\right) - 1$ and expands $= \dfrac{n{2(2n3 + 10n2 + 17n + 11)$, so $a = 10$, $b = 17$, $c = 11$
items.why: Show-that sums using the standard result for r³ were asked in Jan2024 and Jan2025; reusing the result with the index shifted (r replaced by r + 1) has not been asked and rewards understanding over routine expansion.

items.name: Summing finite series
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s
items.question: In this question $k$ is a constant. Show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$\sumr=1n(2r + k)2 = \dfrac{n{3\left(4n2 + 6(k + 1)n + 3k2 + 6k + 2\right)$$ Given that $$\sumr=112(2r + k)2 = 3644$$ find the two possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Expands $(2r + k)2 = 4r2 + 4kr + k2$ and uses at least one standard result $\dfrac{2{3n(n + 1)(2n + 1) + 2kn(n + 1) + nk2$ (with $\sumr=1n k2 = nk2$) Takes out a factor of $\dfrac{n{3$ and expands: $\dfrac{n{3\left(2(2n2 + 3n + 1) + 6k(n + 1) + 3k2\right)$ $= \dfrac{n{3\left(4n2 + 6(k + 1)n + 3k2 + 6k + 2\right)$ Substitutes $n = 12$ into the result in (a) and sets it equal to 3644: $4(650 + 78k + 3k2) = 3644$ $k2 + 26k - 87 = 0$ oe, e.g. $12k2 + 312k - 1044 = 0$ Solves their 3TQ $k = 3$ or $k = -29$
items.why: Solving for an unknown after a summation recurs (Jan2022 Q9(c), May2024 Q7 found n); an unknown constant inside the general term, with two valid answers, has not been asked.

items.name: Summing finite series
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s
items.question: A shop builds a display of boxes in horizontal layers. The top layer is layer 1. Layer $r$ is a rectangle of boxes, $r$ boxes by $(2r + 1)$ boxes. The diagram shows layers 1, 2 and 3, viewed from above. A display with $n$ layers contains $B_n$ boxes in total. Use the standard results to show that $$B_n = \dfrac{1{6n(n + 1)(4n + 5)$$ Find the total number of boxes in layers 6 to 10 inclusive. Show that the equation $n(n + 1)(4n + 5) = 12\,000$ has a root between 13 and 14. Hence find the greatest number of complete layers that the shop can build from 2000 boxes, and the number of boxes left over.
items.ms: $B_n = \sumr=1n r(2r + 1) = \sumr=1n(2r2 + r)$ Uses the standard results: $\dfrac{1{3n(n + 1)(2n + 1) + \dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)$ Takes out a factor of $\dfrac{1{6n(n + 1)$: $\dfrac{1{6n(n + 1)\left(2(2n + 1) + 3\right)$ $= \dfrac{1{6n(n + 1)(4n + 5)$ $B10 - B5 = 825 - 125$ 700 Evaluates $\mathrm{g(13)$ and $\mathrm{g(14)$ where $\mathrm{g(n) = n(n + 1)(4n + 5) - 12\,000$ $\mathrm{g(13) = -1626 < 0$ and $\mathrm{g(14) = 810 > 0$: sign change, so a root lies between 13 and 14 13 complete layers, with $2000 - 1729 = 271$ boxes left over
items.why: Every session tests the standard results, but never in a context; a counting model with a 'greatest number of complete layers' answer is a likely surprise, and it links to the sign-change idea of FP1.3.1.

items.name: Summing finite series
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s
items.question: Use the standard results to show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$\sumr=1n r(n - r) = \dfrac{1{6n(n - 1)(n + 1)$$ Hence find the value of $$1 \times 39 + 2 \times 38 + 3 \times 37 + \dots + 39 \times 1$$ Show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$\sumr=1n r(n - r)2 = \dfrac{1{12n2(n2 - 1)$$
items.ms: Writes the sum as $n\sumr=1n r - \sumr=1n r2$, treating $n$ as a constant $\dfrac{1{2n2(n + 1) - \dfrac{1{6n(n + 1)(2n + 1)$ $= \dfrac{1{6n(n + 1)(3n - 2n - 1) = \dfrac{1{6n(n - 1)(n + 1)$ Recognises the terms as $r(40 - r)$, i.e. $n = 40$ Notes the sum runs to $r = 39$ but the $r = 40$ term is $40 \times 0 = 0$, so the sum equals $\sumr=140 r(40 - r)$; substitutes $n = 40$ 10660 Expands $r(n - r)2 = n2r - 2nr2 + r3$ Uses the standard results with $n$ as a constant: $\dfrac{1{2n3(n + 1) - \dfrac{1{3n2(n + 1)(2n + 1) + \dfrac{1{4n2(n + 1)2$ Takes out a factor of $\dfrac{1{12n2(n + 1)$: $\dfrac{1{12n2(n + 1)\left(6n - 4(2n + 1) + 3(n + 1)\right)$ $= \dfrac{1{12n2(n + 1)(n - 1) = \dfrac{1{12n2(n2 - 1)$
items.why: FP1.7.1 has come up in all 26 sessions, but the general term has always been a fixed polynomial in r; a sum whose terms also contain n (to be treated as a constant) has not been asked and is a natural way to stretch candidates.

items.name: Summing finite series
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s
items.question: Use the standard results for $\sumr=1n r$, $\sumr=1n r2$ and $\sumr=1n r3$ to show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$\sumr=1n(r3 + 3r2 - r) = \dfrac{1{4n2(n + 1)(n + 5)$$ Hence find the value of $n$ for which $$\sumr=1n(r3 + 3r2 - r) = 13\sumr=1n r2$$ Show that, for all positive integers $n$, $$\sumr=n+12n(r3 + 3r2 - r) = \dfrac{3{4n2(5n2 + 14n + 5)$$
items.ms: Substitutes at least two of the standard results correctly $\dfrac{1{4n2(n + 1)2 + \dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)(2n + 1) - \dfrac{1{2n(n + 1)$ Takes out a factor of $\dfrac{1{4n(n + 1)$: $\dfrac{1{4n(n + 1)\left(n(n + 1) + 2(2n + 1) - 2\right)$ $= \dfrac{1{4n(n + 1)(n2 + 5n) = \dfrac{1{4n2(n + 1)(n + 5)$ $\dfrac{1{4n2(n + 1)(n + 5) = \dfrac{13{6n(n + 1)(2n + 1)$ Cancels $n(n + 1)$ to reach a 3TQ: $3n2 - 37n - 26 = 0$ Solves their 3TQ, e.g. $(3n + 2)(n - 13) = 0$ $n = 13$ only (rejects $n = -\dfrac{2{3$) Uses $\mathrm{f(2n) - \mathrm{f(n)$, where $\mathrm{f(n) = \dfrac{1{4n2(n + 1)(n + 5)$ $\dfrac{1{4(2n)2(2n + 1)(2n + 5) - \dfrac{1{4n2(n + 1)(n + 5)$ Takes out a factor of $\dfrac{1{4n2$ and expands: $\dfrac{1{4n2\left(4(4n2 + 12n + 5) - (n2 + 6n + 5)\right)$ $= \dfrac{1{4n2(15n2 + 42n + 15) = \dfrac{3{4n2(5n2 + 14n + 5)$
items.why: The long series question (May2024 Q7, Jun2025 Q8, Jan2024 Q8) regularly combines a show-that using Σr³, a 'hence solve for n' and a sum from n + 1 to 2n; this is that core 12-mark pattern with a fresh general term.

items.name: Addition and subtraction of matrices
path: FP1.5.1 - Addition and subtraction of matrices.
items.question: The $2 \times 2$ matrices $\mathbf{A$ and $\mathbf{B$ are such that $$\mathbf{A + \mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix 3 & -1 \\ 3 & 6 \end{pmatrix \qquad \text{and \qquad \mathbf{A - \mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix -1 & -5 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix$$ Find the matrix $\mathbf{A$ and the matrix $\mathbf{B$. Given that the matrix $\mathbf{A + k\mathbf{B$, where $k$ is a constant, is singular, determine the possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Adds (or subtracts) the two matrix equations to obtain $2\mathbf{A$ or $2\mathbf{B$, e.g. $2\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix 2 & -6 \\ 4 & 8 \end{pmatrix$ $\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix$ $\mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix$ Forms $\mathbf{A + k\mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix 1 + 2k & -3 + 2k \\ 2 + k & 4 + 2k \end{pmatrix$ and attempts its determinant, $(1 + 2k)(4 + 2k) - (2k - 3)(k + 2)$ Sets the determinant equal to zero and solves their 3TQ: $2k2 + 9k + 10 = 0$, $(2k + 5)(k + 2) = 0$ $k = -2$ and $k = -\dfrac{5{2$
items.why: Matrix addition and subtraction appear in only 4 of 26 sessions, most recently Jun2026 Q1 (C = 3A + 2B, then k for C singular); recovering A and B from A + B and A − B has never been asked.

items.name: Multiplication of a matrix by a scalar
path: FP1.5.2 - Multiplication of a matrix by a scalar.
items.question: $$\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix$$ Show that, for any $2 \times 2$ matrix $\mathbf{M$ and any real constant $k$, $$\det(k\mathbf{M) = k2\det\mathbf{M$$ The matrix $\mathbf{B = k\mathbf{A$, where $k$ is a constant, has $\det\mathbf{B = 126$. Hence, or otherwise, determine the possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Writes $\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix$ and $k\mathbf{M = \begin{pmatrix ka & kb \\ kc & kd \end{pmatrix$, then $\det(k\mathbf{M) = (ka)(kd) - (kb)(kc)$ $= k2ad - k2bc = k2(ad - bc) = k2\det\mathbf{M$ $\det\mathbf{A = 4 \times 3 - (-1) \times 2 = 14$ Uses the result in (a), or finds $\det\begin{pmatrix 4k & -k \\ 2k & 3k \end{pmatrix = 12k2 + 2k2$, to form $14k2 = 126$ $k = 3$ and $k = -3$
items.why: Scalar multiples of a matrix appear in only 2 of 26 sessions (Jun2026 Q1 3A + 2B); the result det(kM) = k² det M has never been asked and is the likeliest new angle on this point.

items.name: Products of matrices
items.question: $$\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \end{pmatrix$$ Find $\mathbf{A2$. Find the integers $p$ and $q$ such that $\mathbf{A2 = p\mathbf{A + q\mathbf{I$, where $\mathbf{I$ is the $2 \times 2$ identity matrix. Hence show that $\mathbf{A3 = 15\mathbf{A - 4\mathbf{I$. Hence, or otherwise, find the constants $\alpha$ and $\beta$ such that $\mathbf{A-1 = \alpha\mathbf{A + \beta\mathbf{I$.
items.ms: Correct row-by-column method, shown by at least two correct entries $\mathbf{A2 = \begin{pmatrix 19 & 8 \\ -12 & -5 \end{pmatrix$ Compares corresponding entries of their $\mathbf{A2$ and $p\mathbf{A + q\mathbf{I$ to form equations, e.g. $2p = 8$ and $5p + q = 19$ $p = 4$, $q = -1$ $\mathbf{A3 = \mathbf{A\,\mathbf{A2 = \mathbf{A(4\mathbf{A - \mathbf{I) = 4\mathbf{A2 - \mathbf{A$ $= 4(4\mathbf{A - \mathbf{I) - \mathbf{A = 15\mathbf{A - 4\mathbf{I$ Multiplies $\mathbf{A2 = 4\mathbf{A - \mathbf{I$ by $\mathbf{A-1$ to give $\mathbf{A = 4\mathbf{I - \mathbf{A-1$, or finds $\mathbf{A-1 = \begin{pmatrix -1 & -2 \\ 3 & 5 \end{pmatrix$ and compares entries $\mathbf{A-1 = -\mathbf{A + 4\mathbf{I$, so $\alpha = -1$, $\beta = 4$
items.why: Matrix products come up in 17 of 26 sessions and powers of a matrix recur (Jan2019 P³ = 8I, Jun2026 A⁵); writing A² as pA + qI and deducing A³ and A⁻¹ from it has not yet been asked.

items.name: Evaluation of 2 2 determinants
items.question: $$\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix 0 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \end{pmatrix \qquad \mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix k - 2 & 1 \\ -1 & k - 2 \\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix$$ where $k$ is a real constant. Find $\mathbf{A\mathbf{B$ in terms of $k$. Show that $\mathbf{A\mathbf{B$ is non-singular for all real values of $k$. The diagram shows the triangle $R$ with vertices $(1, 1)$, $(5, 1)$ and $(2, 4)$. The transformation represented by the matrix $\mathbf{A\mathbf{B$ maps $R$ onto the triangle $R'$. Find, in terms of $k$, an expression for the area of $R'$. Hence find the least possible area of $R'$ and the value of $k$ for which it occurs.
items.ms: Correct method for the product of a $2 \times 3$ and a $3 \times 2$ matrix, shown by at least two correct entries $\mathbf{A\mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix -2 & 2k \\ -k & 2k - 5 \end{pmatrix$ Attempts $\det(\mathbf{A\mathbf{B)$ for their $\mathbf{A\mathbf{B$: $-2(2k - 5) - (2k)(-k)$ $\det(\mathbf{A\mathbf{B) = 2k2 - 4k + 10$ Completes the square, $2(k - 1)2 + 8$, or finds the discriminant $(-4)2 - 4 \times 2 \times 10 = -64$ $2(k - 1)2 + 8 \geqslant 8 > 0$ (or discriminant $< 0$ so no real roots), so $\det(\mathbf{A\mathbf{B) \neq 0$ for all real $k$ and $\mathbf{A\mathbf{B$ is non-singular Area of $R = \dfrac{1{2 \times 4 \times 3 = 6$ Uses the determinant as the area scale factor: area of $R' = 6\det(\mathbf{A\mathbf{B) = 6(2k2 - 4k + 10)$ $= 12k2 - 24k + 60$ Finds the minimum of their quadratic, e.g. $6\left(2(k - 1)2 + 8\right) = 12(k - 1)2 + 48$ using (b), or $24k - 24 = 0$ by differentiation Least area $48$ square units, when $k = 1$
items.why: Determinants are asked in 20 of 26 sessions; 2×3 by 3×2 products (Jun2017, Jan2023), non-singular for all values by completing the square (Jan2025 Q1) and area scale factors (Jun2018, Jun2023) all recur and are combined here.

items.name: Inverse of 2 2 matrices
items.question: $$\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix k + 1 & 3 \\ 3 & k - 1 \end{pmatrix$$ where $k$ is a real constant. Determine the exact values of $k$ for which $\mathbf{A$ is singular. Given that $\mathbf{A$ is non-singular, find $\mathbf{A-1$ in terms of $k$. Given that $\mathbf{P$ and $\mathbf{Q$ are non-singular $2 \times 2$ matrices, prove that $(\mathbf{PQ)-1 = \mathbf{Q-1\mathbf{P-1$. Given that $k = 3$ and that $\mathbf{B$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix such that $$(\mathbf{A\mathbf{B)-1 = \begin{pmatrix 5 & -7 \\ 7 & -10 \end{pmatrix$$ use the result in part (c) to determine the matrix $\mathbf{B$.
items.ms: Attempts $\det\mathbf{A = (k + 1)(k - 1) - 9$ Sets their $\det\mathbf{A = 0$ and solves: $k2 = 10$ $k = \pm\sqrt{10$ Uses $\dfrac{1{\det\begin{pmatrix d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix$ with their determinant: swaps the leading diagonal and negates the other two entries $\mathbf{A-1 = \dfrac{1{k2 - 10\begin{pmatrix k - 1 & -3 \\ -3 & k + 1 \end{pmatrix$ Considers $(\mathbf{PQ)(\mathbf{Q-1\mathbf{P-1)$ and uses associativity to obtain $\mathbf{P(\mathbf{Q\mathbf{Q-1)\mathbf{P-1$ $= \mathbf{P\mathbf{I\mathbf{P-1 = \mathbf{P\mathbf{P-1 = \mathbf{I$, so $\mathbf{Q-1\mathbf{P-1$ is the inverse of $\mathbf{PQ$ Uses $\mathbf{B-1\mathbf{A-1 = (\mathbf{A\mathbf{B)-1$ and post-multiplies by $\mathbf{A$: $\mathbf{B-1 = (\mathbf{A\mathbf{B)-1\mathbf{A$ with $\mathbf{A = \begin{pmatrix 4 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 \end{pmatrix$ $\mathbf{B-1 = \begin{pmatrix -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \end{pmatrix$ Finds the inverse of their $\mathbf{B-1$ $\mathbf{B = \begin{pmatrix 1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{pmatrix$
items.why: Inverses are asked in 19 of 26 sessions: an inverse in terms of k is near-certain (Jun2026, Jan2026, Jan2025, Jan2021), (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹ was last used in Jun2022, and proving it has never been asked.

M1.4.1 - The concept of a force. Newt
items.question: [In this question $\mathbf{i$ and $\mathbf{j$ are perpendicular unit vectors in a horizontal plane.] A particle $P$ of mass 2.5 kg moves on a smooth horizontal plane under the action of a single constant force $\mathbf{F$ newtons. At time $t = 0$ the velocity of $P$ is $(3\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j)$ m s⁻¹. At time $t = 4$ seconds the velocity of $P$ is $(11\mathbf{i + 4\mathbf{j)$ m s⁻¹. Find the acceleration of $P$, giving your answer in the form $(p\mathbf{i + q\mathbf{j)$ m s⁻². Find the magnitude of $\mathbf{F$.
items.ms: Use of $\mathbf{a = \dfrac{\mathbf{v - \mathbf{u{t$: $\dfrac{(11\mathbf{i + 4\mathbf{j) - (3\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j){4$ $\mathbf{a = (2\mathbf{i + 1.5\mathbf{j)$ m s⁻² Use of $\mathbf{F = m\mathbf{a$ and Pythagoras: $|\mathbf{F| = 2.5\sqrt{2^2 + 1.5^2$ or $\sqrt{5^2 + 3.75^2$ $|\mathbf{F| = 6.25$ N
items.why: M1.4.1 has come up in 29 of 34 sessions, most often as a short vector F = ma question (Jun 2026 Q4, Jan 2026 Q3, Oct 2025 Q3, Jan 2025 Q1); here the force is found from a change of velocity, the reverse of the usual direction.

items.name: The concept of a force. Newton's laws of motion
path: Topic 4 Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane
M1.4.1 - The concept of a force. Newt
items.question: A ship of mass 80 tonnes is towed into a harbour by two tugs, $A$ and $B$, using two horizontal cables. The ship moves in a straight line. The cable from tug $A$ has tension 25 kN and makes an angle of 20° with the direction of motion of the ship. The cable from tug $B$ has tension $T$ kN and makes an angle of 30° with the direction of motion, on the other side of the line of motion, as shown in the diagram. The resistance to the motion of the ship is modelled as a constant force of magnitude 30 kN acting in the opposite direction to the motion. The ship is modelled as a particle. Find the value of $T$. Find the acceleration of the ship.
items.ms: Resolves perpendicular to the direction of motion (no resultant sideways force) $25\sin 20^\circ = T\sin 30^\circ$ $T = 17.1$ Equation of motion parallel to the motion with both cable components and the resistance $25000\cos 20^\circ + 17100\cos 30^\circ - 30000 = 80000a$ with at most one error Fully correct equation $a = 0.104$ m s⁻² (or 0.10 m s⁻²)

items.ms: Equation of motion with weight and resistance both opposing the motion: $0.5g + 1.1 = 0.5a$ $a = \dfrac{4.9 + 1.1{0.5 = 12$ m s⁻² * Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$, $u = 12$, $a = -12$ Greatest height $= 6$ m Equation of motion for the ball moving downwards: $0.5g - 1.1 = 0.5a$, giving $a = 7.6$ m s⁻² Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$, their 7.6 and their 6: $v^2 = 2 \times 7.6 \times 6$ $v = 9.5$ or $9.55$ m s⁻¹ Time up $= \dfrac{12{12 = 1$ s and a complete method for the time down, e.g. $\dfrac{9.55{7.6$ or $6 = \frac{1{2(7.6)t^2$ Total time $= 2.26$ s (or 2.3 s)

items.question: A lift of mass 500 kg is raised by a vertical cable attached to the top of the lift. A crate of mass 80 kg rests on the floor of the lift. The lift starts from rest and moves vertically upwards. It accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 4 m s⁻¹ in 2.5 s, then moves at a constant speed of 4 m s⁻¹ and then decelerates uniformly to rest. The cable is modelled as light and inextensible, the crate is modelled as a particle and air resistance is ignored. Find the tension in the cable while the lift is accelerating. Find the magnitude of the force exerted on the floor of the lift by the crate while the lift is accelerating. While the lift is decelerating, the tension in the cable is 5220 N. Find the deceleration of the lift. Given that the lift rises a total distance of 39 m, find the length of time for which the lift moves at constant speed.
items.ms: Acceleration $= \dfrac{4{2.5 = 1.6$ m s⁻² Equation of motion for the lift and crate together: $T - 580g = 580 \times 1.6$ $T = 6610$ N (or 6600 N) Equation of motion for the crate: $R - 80g = 80 \times 1.6$ $R = 912$ N, so the crate exerts a force of 912 N on the floor Equation of motion for the lift and crate with $T = 5220$: $580g - 5220 = 580d$ Correct equation Deceleration $= 0.8$ m s⁻² Distances while speeding up and slowing down: $\frac{1{2(4)(2.5) = 5$ m and $\frac{1{2(4)\left(\frac{4{0.8\right) = 10$ m (their deceleration) Equation for the constant-speed stage, e.g. $5 + 4t + 10 = 39$ $t = 6$ s

items.question: [In this question $\mathbf{i$ and $\mathbf{j$ are perpendicular unit vectors in a horizontal plane.] A particle $P$ of mass 2 kg moves on a smooth horizontal plane under the action of three constant horizontal forces, $\mathbf{F_1 = (4\mathbf{i - 2\mathbf{j)$ N, $\mathbf{F_2 = (-7\mathbf{i + 5\mathbf{j)$ N and $\mathbf{F_3$ N. No other horizontal forces act on $P$. The particle moves with constant velocity $(5\mathbf{i + 2\mathbf{j)$ m s⁻¹. Find $\mathbf{F_3$. At time $t = 0$ the force $\mathbf{F_3$ is removed. The forces $\mathbf{F_1$ and $\mathbf{F_2$ continue to act. Find the acceleration of $P$ for $t > 0$. Find the value of $t$ when $P$ is moving in the direction of the vector $(\mathbf{i + \mathbf{j)$, and find the speed of $P$ at this instant. At time $t = T$ seconds the force $\mathbf{F_3$ is applied again. The particle then moves with constant velocity $(-\mathbf{i + 8\mathbf{j)$ m s⁻¹. Find the value of $T$. Find the distance travelled by $P$ in the 5 seconds after $\mathbf{F_3$ is applied again.
items.ms: Constant velocity so the resultant force is zero: $\mathbf{F_1 + \mathbf{F_2 + \mathbf{F_3 = \mathbf{0$ $\mathbf{F_3 = (3\mathbf{i - 3\mathbf{j)$ N Use of $\mathbf{F = m\mathbf{a$ with the resultant $\mathbf{F_1 + \mathbf{F_2 = (-3\mathbf{i + 3\mathbf{j)$ (or $-\mathbf{F_3$) $\mathbf{a = (-1.5\mathbf{i + 1.5\mathbf{j)$ m s⁻² Use of $\mathbf{v = \mathbf{u + \mathbf{at$: $\mathbf{v = (5 - 1.5t)\mathbf{i + (2 + 1.5t)\mathbf{j$ Sets the $\mathbf{i$ and $\mathbf{j$ components equal: $5 - 1.5t = 2 + 1.5t$ $t = 1$ Speed $= \sqrt{3.5^2 + 3.5^2 = 4.95$ m s⁻¹ (or $\frac{7\sqrt{2{2$) $(-\mathbf{i + 8\mathbf{j) = (5\mathbf{i + 2\mathbf{j) + T(-1.5\mathbf{i + 1.5\mathbf{j)$ Equates one component, e.g. $-1 = 5 - 1.5T$ $T = 4$ Speed $= \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 8^2 = \sqrt{65$ and distance $= 5\sqrt{65$ Distance $= 40.3$ m

items.question: Two particles $A$ and $B$ have masses 2 kg and 3 kg respectively. The particles are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string which passes over a small smooth pulley. The pulley is fixed above a horizontal floor. Particle $A$ is held at rest on the floor and $B$ hangs at a height of 1.5 m above the floor, with the string taut and the hanging parts of the string vertical, as shown in the diagram. The system is released from rest. Particle $B$ hits the floor and does not rebound. In the subsequent motion, $A$ does not reach the pulley. Find the tension in the string while both particles are moving. Find the greatest height above the floor reached by $A$. State how you used the fact that the string is inextensible in your answer to part (a).
items.ms: Equation of motion for $A$: $T - 2g = 2a$ Equation of motion for $B$ (or for the whole system): $3g - T = 3a$ (or $3g - 2g = 5a$) $a = 1.96$ m s⁻² $\left(\frac{g{5\right)$ $T = 23.5$ N (or 24 N) Speed when $B$ hits the floor: $v^2 = 2 \times 1.96 \times 1.5$ ($= 5.88$) $A$ then moves freely under gravity: $0 = 5.88 - 2gs$, giving $s = 0.3$ m Greatest height $= 1.5 + 0.3 = 1.8$ m The particles have accelerations of the same magnitude (the same $a$ is used for $A$ and for $B$)

items.question: A particle $P$ of mass 1.2 kg lies on a smooth horizontal table. One end of a light inextensible string is attached to $P$. The string passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the edge of the table and a particle $Q$ of mass $m$ kg is attached to the other end of the string. Particle $P$ is held at rest on the table at a distance of 1.75 m from the pulley, with the string taut and perpendicular to the edge of the table. Particle $Q$ hangs vertically at a height of 1 m above the floor, as shown in the diagram. The system is released from rest. Particle $Q$ hits the floor with speed 2.8 m s⁻¹ and does not rebound. Find the acceleration of $Q$ before it hits the floor. Find the tension in the string before $Q$ hits the floor. Find the value of $m$. Find the time from the instant the system is released until $P$ reaches the pulley.
items.ms: Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$: $2.8^2 = 2a \times 1$ $a = 3.92$ m s⁻² Equation of motion for $P$: $T = 1.2a$ with their $a$ $T = 4.70$ N (or 4.7 N) Equation of motion for $Q$: $mg - T = ma$ (or whole system $mg = (m + 1.2)a$) Correct equation with their $T$ and $a$: $9.8m - 4.704 = 3.92m$ $m = 0.8$ Time for $Q$ to reach the floor: $2.8 = 3.92t_1$, $t_1 = 0.714$ s $\left(\frac{5{7\right)$ $P$ then moves at constant speed 2.8 m s⁻¹ for the remaining 0.75 m: $t_2 = \dfrac{0.75{2.8$ ($= 0.268$ s) Total time $= 0.98$ s (or 0.982 s)

items.question: A particle $P$ of mass 2 kg lies on a rough plane which is inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{3{4$. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is $\dfrac{1{4$. One end of a light inextensible string is attached to $P$. The string passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the top of the plane and a particle $Q$ of mass 3 kg is attached to the other end of the string. The part of the string between $P$ and the pulley lies along a line of greatest slope of the plane. Particle $Q$ hangs freely at a height of 1.6 m above horizontal ground, as shown in the diagram. The system is released from rest with the string taut and $P$ moves up the plane. Particle $Q$ hits the ground and does not rebound. In the subsequent motion $P$ does not reach the pulley. Find the tension in the string while $Q$ is moving. Find the further distance that $P$ moves up the plane after $Q$ hits the ground, before $P$ first comes to instantaneous rest. Determine whether $P$ remains at rest after it first comes to instantaneous rest, giving a reason for your answer.
items.ms: Normal reaction on $P$: $R = 2g\cos\alpha$ ($= 1.6g$) and friction $F = \frac{1{4R$ ($= 0.4g$) Equation of motion for $P$ parallel to the plane: $T - 2g\sin\alpha - F = 2a$ Correct equation: $T - 1.2g - 0.4g = 2a$ Equation of motion for $Q$: $3g - T = 3a$ (or for the whole system) Correct equation $T = 21.2$ N (or 21 N) Speed of $P$ when $Q$ hits the ground: $v^2 = 2 \times 2.744 \times 1.6$ ($= 8.78$, $v = 2.96$ m s⁻¹) Equation of motion for $P$ with no tension: $-2g\sin\alpha - F = 2a$ Deceleration $= 0.8g = 7.84$ m s⁻² $0 = 8.78 - 2(7.84)s$, $s = 0.56$ m Compares the component of the weight down the plane, $2g\sin\alpha = 11.76$ N, with the maximum friction, $\frac{1{4 \times 2g\cos\alpha = 3.92$ N $11.76 > 3.92$, so $P$ does not remain at rest: it slides back down the plane

items.question: A truck of mass 2400 kg tows a car of mass 1200 kg along a straight horizontal road using a tow-rope, as shown in the diagram. The tow-rope is modelled as a light inextensible string and is horizontal. The resistances to the motion of the truck and of the car are modelled as constant forces of magnitude 600 N and 360 N respectively. The car's engine is not working and its brakes are not used. The engine of the truck produces a constant driving force. The truck starts from rest with the tow-rope taut and accelerates uniformly, reaching a speed of 12 m s⁻¹ after 20 s. Find the tension in the tow-rope while the truck is accelerating. Find the driving force produced by the engine of the truck. When the speed is 12 m s⁻¹, the truck's engine is switched off and its brakes are applied, giving a constant braking force of 3000 N on the truck. The resistances to motion are unchanged. By assuming that the tow-rope remains taut, show that the tow-rope must become slack. At the instant the brakes are applied, the front of the car is 4.8 m behind the back of the truck. The car then moves under its resistance alone. Find the time from the instant the brakes are applied until the car hits the truck.
items.ms: Acceleration $= \dfrac{12{20 = 0.6$ m s⁻² Equation of motion for the car: $T - 360 = 1200 \times 0.6$ Correct equation $T = 1080$ N Equation of motion for the truck, $D - 600 - T = 2400 \times 0.6$, or for the whole system, $D - 960 = 3600 \times 0.6$ Correct equation with their $T$ (or whole system) $D = 3120$ N Equation of motion for the whole system with the rope taut: $3000 + 600 + 360 = 3600d$ $d = 1.1$ m s⁻² Equation of motion for the car with a force $F$ in the rope: $360 + F = 1200 \times 1.1$, $F = 960$ N The rope would have to push the car backwards with a force of 960 N (a thrust); a rope can only pull, so it becomes slack Distances for both vehicles: truck $12t - \frac{1{2(1.5)t^2$, car $12t - \frac{1{2(0.3)t^2$ Car's distance $-$ truck's distance $= 4.8$: $0.6t^2 = 4.8$ $t = 2.83$ s (or $2\sqrt{2$ s)

items.question: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses 0.5 kg and 0.4 kg respectively, are moving in opposite directions along the same straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. Particle $A$ has speed 6 m s⁻¹ and particle $B$ has speed 2 m s⁻¹. The particles collide directly. The magnitude of the impulse exerted on $A$ by $B$ in the collision is 3.2 N s. Find the speed of $A$ immediately after the collision. State whether the direction of motion of $A$ has been reversed by the collision. Give a reason for your answer. Find the speed of $B$ immediately after the collision.
items.ms: Impulse equals change in momentum for $A$: $-3.2 = 0.5(v_A - 6)$ or $3.2 = 0.5(6 - v_A)$ Correct equation with consistent signs Speed of $A$ is 0.4 m s⁻¹ Yes, it is reversed: the velocity of $A$ is $-0.4$ m s⁻¹ in its original direction (or: the impulse 3.2 N s is greater than the momentum of $A$ before the collision, 3 N s) Impulse–momentum for $B$, $3.2 = 0.4(v_B - (-2))$, or conservation of momentum $0.5(6) - 0.4(2) = 0.5(-0.4) + 0.4v_B$ Speed of $B$ is 6 m s⁻¹
items.why: M1.4.3 has come up in 33 of 34 sessions, and 'impulse given, find both speeds and whether a direction is reversed' opened Jan 2016, Jun 2017, Oct 2025 and Jan 2026; here it is set in numbers rather than in terms of m and u.

items.question: A bullet of mass 20 g is fired horizontally with speed 400 m s⁻¹ into a block of wood of mass 1.98 kg. The block is at rest on rough horizontal ground. The bullet becomes embedded in the block, and immediately afterwards the block and the bullet move together along the ground in the original direction of motion of the bullet. The bullet and the block are modelled as particles. Find the speed of the block immediately after the bullet becomes embedded in it. Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted on the block by the bullet. The block, with the bullet embedded, slides 2.5 m along the ground before coming to rest. Find the coefficient of friction between the block and the ground.
items.ms: Conservation of momentum: $0.02 \times 400 = (0.02 + 1.98)v$ $v = 4$ m s⁻¹ $1.98(4 - 0)$ or $0.02(400 - 4)$ 7.92 N s $0 = 4^2 - 2a(2.5)$, giving deceleration $a = 3.2$ m s⁻² $R = 2g$ and Newton's second law with $F = \mu R$: $\mu(2g) = 2(3.2)$ $\mu = 0.327$ $\left(\tfrac{16{49\right)$

items.question: Two small spheres $A$ and $B$, of masses 0.16 kg and 0.24 kg respectively, lie at rest on a smooth horizontal table. Sphere $A$ is struck with a cue, directly towards $B$. The force exerted on $A$ by the cue is modelled as a constant force of magnitude 240 N acting for 0.004 s. Sphere $A$ then moves towards $B$ and collides directly with it. Immediately after the collision, $B$ moves with speed 3.6 m s⁻¹. The spheres are modelled as particles. Find the speed of $A$ immediately after it has been struck. Find the speed of $A$ immediately after the collision and state its direction of motion. The spheres are in contact for 0.002 s. Assuming that the force between the spheres is constant while they are in contact, find the magnitude of this force.
items.ms: Impulse of the cue $= Ft = 240 \times 0.004 = 0.96$ N s Impulse = change in momentum: $0.96 = 0.16v - 0$ $v = 6$ m s⁻¹ Conservation of momentum, correct number of terms: $0.16 \times 6 = 0.16v_A + 0.24 \times 3.6$ Correct equation, ft their speed from (a) $v_A = 0.6$ m s⁻¹, moving in the same direction as before the collision Impulse on $B$: $0.24 \times 3.6 = 0.864$ N s (or on $A$: $0.16(6 - 0.6)$) Uses $I = Ft$: $F = \dfrac{0.864{0.002$ $F = 432$ N

items.question: Three particles $A$, $B$ and $C$ have masses $2m$, $3m$ and $km$ respectively, where $k$ is a constant. The particles lie at rest in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface, with $B$ between $A$ and $C$, as shown in the diagram. Particle $A$ is projected towards $B$ with speed $5u$ and collides directly with $B$. Immediately after this collision, $A$ is moving in the same direction as before with speed $\tfrac12u$. Find, in terms of $u$, the speed of $B$ immediately after its collision with $A$. Find, in terms of $m$ and $u$, the magnitude of the impulse exerted on $A$ by $B$ in this collision. Particle $B$ then collides directly with $C$. Immediately after this collision $C$ moves with speed $2u$ and the direction of motion of $B$ is unchanged. Find, in terms of $k$ and $u$, the speed of $B$ immediately after its collision with $C$. Given that there is a further collision between $A$ and $B$, find the range of possible values of $k$.
items.ms: Conservation of momentum, correct number of terms: $2m(5u) = 2m\left(\tfrac12u\right) + 3mv_B$ Correct equation $v_B = 3u$ Change in momentum of $A$: $2m\left(5u - \tfrac12u\right)$, or of $B$: $3m(3u - 0)$ $9mu$ Conservation of momentum, correct number of terms: $3m(3u) = 3mv + km(2u)$ Correct equation, ft their $3u$ $v = \dfrac{(9 - 2k)u{3$ A further collision needs $B$ to move more slowly than $A$: $\dfrac{(9 - 2k)u{3 < \dfrac{u{2$ $k > \dfrac{15{4$ Direction of $B$ unchanged, so $\dfrac{(9 - 2k)u{3 > 0$, giving $k < \dfrac92$; hence $\dfrac{15{4 < k < \dfrac92$

items.question: A pile driver is used to drive a vertical post into the ground. The hammer of the pile driver has mass 1200 kg and the post has mass 300 kg. The hammer is released from rest at a height of 4.9 m above the top of the post, as shown in the diagram, and falls freely. The hammer strikes the post and does not rebound. Immediately after the impact, the hammer and the post move downwards together with the same speed. The hammer and the post are modelled as particles. Show that the speed of the hammer immediately before it strikes the post is 9.8 m s⁻¹. Find the speed of the hammer and the post immediately after the impact. Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted on the post by the hammer in the impact. After the impact, the hammer and the post move downwards together until they come to rest. The resistance to the motion from the ground is modelled as a constant force of magnitude 1.2 × 10⁵ N. Find the distance that the post moves into the ground. Sketch a velocity–time graph for the motion of the hammer from the instant it is released until it comes to rest. Show on your sketch the values of $v$ and $t$ at the impact and when the hammer comes to rest.
items.ms: $v^2 = 0^2 + 2(9.8)(4.9)$ $v^2 = 96.04$, so $v = 9.8$ m s⁻¹ * Conservation of momentum, correct number of terms: $1200 \times 9.8 = (1200 + 300)w$ Correct equation $w = 7.84$ m s⁻¹ $300(7.84 - 0)$ or $1200(9.8 - 7.84)$ 2352 N s Equation of motion for the hammer and post together, with weight and resistance: $1.2 \times 10^5 - 1500g = 1500a$ Deceleration $a = 70.2$ m s⁻² Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with their deceleration: $0 = 7.84^2 - 2(70.2)s$ $s = 0.438$ m (43.8 cm) Straight line from the origin to $v = 9.8$ at $t = 1$ s Vertical drop from 9.8 to 7.84 at $t = 1$ (the impact is instantaneous) Straight line from 7.84 down to $v = 0$, steeper than the first line, ending at $t = 1.11$ s; values 9.8, 7.84, 1 and 1.11 shown

items.question: A particle $P$ of mass 0.5 kg is projected with speed 6 m s⁻¹ from a point $O$ up a line of greatest slope of a fixed rough plane, as shown in the diagram. The plane is inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is 0.3. Particle $P$ comes to instantaneous rest at the point $A$ on the plane. Find the deceleration of $P$ as it moves up the plane. Find the distance $OA$. Particle $P$ then slides back down the plane. Find the speed of $P$ as it passes $O$.
items.ms: Resolves perpendicular to the plane: $R = 0.5g\cos30°$ (4.24 N) Equation of motion up the plane with the weight component and friction $0.3R$ both opposing the motion: $-0.5g\sin30° - 0.3R = 0.5a$ Deceleration $= 7.45$ m s⁻² $0 = 6^2 - 2(7.45\ldots)s$ $OA = 2.42$ m Equation of motion down the plane with friction now acting up the plane: $0.5g\sin30° - 0.3R = 0.5a$ $a = 2.35$ m s⁻² $v^2 = 2(2.35\ldots)(2.42\ldots)$, $v = 3.37$ m s⁻¹
items.why: Projection up a rough plane followed by the speed on the way back recurs (Jun 2018 Q4, Jun 2021 Q6, Jun 2025 Q6(a)); the key idea is that friction changes direction while R stays the same.
keywords: Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Friction
path: Topic 4 Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane
items.question: After a road accident, an investigator examines the skid marks left by a car. The car was moving down a straight road inclined at 5° to the horizontal when the driver braked hard. The wheels locked and the car skidded in a straight line down a line of greatest slope of the road, leaving skid marks of length 24 m before it came to rest. The coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road surface is 0.7. In a model of the skid, the car is treated as a particle sliding on a rough inclined plane and air resistance is ignored. Find the deceleration of the car while it was skidding. Find the speed of the car at the instant its wheels locked. The speed limit on the road is 50 km h⁻¹. Determine whether the car was travelling above the speed limit when its wheels locked. Explain why the investigator did not need to know the mass of the car. State, with a reason, how including air resistance in the model would change the speed found in part (b).
items.ms: $R = mg\cos5°$ Equation of motion down the road, with friction $0.7R$ up the slope and the weight component down the slope: $mg\sin5° - 0.7R = ma$ $a = g(\sin5° - 0.7\cos5°)$ Deceleration $= 5.98$ m s⁻² $0 = u^2 - 2(5.98\ldots)(24)$ $u = 16.9$ m s⁻¹ Converts consistently: $16.9$ m s⁻¹ $= 61$ km h⁻¹, or 50 km h⁻¹ $= 13.9$ m s⁻¹ Yes: 61 km h⁻¹ > 50 km h⁻¹ (or 16.9 > 13.9), so the car was above the speed limit The weight, the normal reaction, the friction and $ma$ are all proportional to $m$, so $m$ cancels and the deceleration does not depend on the mass The speed would be greater: air resistance also opposes the motion, so the deceleration would be greater and a greater initial speed is needed to stop in 24 m
items.why: Sliding down a rough slope (Jan 2017 Q6, Jan 2018 Q4, Oct 2018 Q8, Oct 2024 Q6) is usually 'from rest'; a skid in which friction exceeds the weight component, worked back from the stopping distance to a speed in km h⁻¹, is a fresh real-world angle with a modelling comment.
keywords: Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Friction
path: Topic 4 Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane
items.question: A loaded sledge of total mass 25 kg is pulled from rest across horizontal snow by a rope inclined at 20° above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is constant. After 4 s the rope breaks and the sledge then slides until it comes to rest. The sledge is modelled as a particle and the rope as light. The coefficient of friction between the sledge and the snow is $\mu$. The speed–time graph shows the motion of the sledge from the instant it starts to move until it comes to rest. Use the graph to find the total distance moved by the sledge. Find the value of $\mu$. Find the tension in the rope. In a second trial, the sledge starts from rest on the same snow and is pushed from behind by a force whose magnitude is equal to the tension found in part (c). This force acts at 20° below the horizontal. Find the acceleration of the sledge.
items.ms: Area under the graph: $\tfrac12 \times 5.5 \times 3$ 8.25 m Deceleration after the rope breaks, from the gradient: $\dfrac{3{1.5 = 2$ m s⁻² $R = 25g$ and $\mu(25g) = 25 \times 2$ $\mu = 0.204$ $\left(\tfrac{10{49\right)$ Acceleration while the sledge is pulled $= \dfrac{3{4 = 0.75$ m s⁻², from the graph Resolves vertically: $R = 25g - T\sin20°$ Equation of motion horizontally with $F = \mu R$: $T\cos20° - \mu(25g - T\sin20°) = 25(0.75)$ Correct equation in $T$ only $T = 68.1$ N Resolves vertically: $R' = 25g + T\sin20°$ (268.3 N) Equation of motion: $T\cos20° - \mu R' = 25a$ $a = 0.37$ m s⁻²
items.why: μ from motion data recurs (Jan 2014 Q6, Oct 2021 Q2, Oct 2025 Q5, the last with a force on a horizontal surface); reading the deceleration from a speed–time graph and switching from a pull to a push, which increases R, are fresh angles.
keywords: Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Friction
path: Topic 4 Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane
items.question: A particle $P$ of mass 3 kg lies on a rough horizontal table. One end of a light inextensible string is attached to $P$. The string passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the edge of the table, and a particle $Q$ of mass 2 kg hangs freely at the other end of the string, as shown in the diagram. The part of the string between $P$ and the pulley is horizontal and perpendicular to the edge of the table. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the table is 0.3. Particle $P$ is projected along the table, directly away from the pulley, with speed 4 m s⁻¹ and with the string taut. In the motion that follows, $P$ does not reach the pulley and $Q$ does not reach the pulley or the floor. Find the deceleration of $P$ while it is moving away from the pulley. Find the tension in the string while $P$ is moving away from the pulley. Find the distance that $P$ moves before it comes to instantaneous rest. Explain why $P$ does not remain at rest when it comes to instantaneous rest. Find the acceleration of $P$ as it moves back towards the pulley. Find the speed of $P$ as it passes the point from which it was projected.
items.ms: $R = 3g$ and $F = 0.3R = 0.9g$ Equation of motion for $P$, with the tension and friction both opposing the motion of $P$ $T + 0.9g = 3a$ ($a$ the deceleration) Equation of motion for $Q$, which is rising and slowing down $2g - T = 2a$ $a = 0.58g = 5.68$ m s⁻² Substitutes their $a$ into either equation of motion $T = 8.23$ N (8.232) $0 = 4^2 - 2(5.68\ldots)s$ $s = 1.41$ m If the system were at rest the tension would be $2g$ (19.6 N), which is greater than the maximum friction $0.9g$ (8.82 N), so $P$ moves back towards the pulley Equations of motion with the friction on $P$ now acting away from the pulley: $T - 0.9g = 3a'$ and $2g - T = 2a'$ Both equations correct (or the correct whole-system equation) $a' = 0.22g = 2.16$ m s⁻² $v^2 = 0 + 2a's$ with their $a'$ and their distance from (c) $v^2 = 2(2.16\ldots)(1.41\ldots) = 6.07$ $v = 2.46$ m s⁻¹
items.why: A rough table with a pulley and a hanging particle is the commonest long M1.4.4 question (Jan 2015 Q8, Jan 2020 Q7, Jan 2026 Q8, Jun 2026 Q8), always released from rest; projecting P away from the pulley, so that the friction and the tension change when P turns back, has not been asked.
keywords: Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.question: A small ball is projected vertically upwards with speed 17.5 m s⁻¹ from a point $A$. The ball is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity. Find the greatest height above $A$ reached by the ball. Find the length of time for which the ball is more than 10 m above $A$.
items.ms: Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$, $u = 17.5$ and $a = \pm 9.8$, e.g. $0 = 17.5^2 - 2 \times 9.8 \times s$ 15.6 m or 16 m Use of $s = ut + \frac{1{2at^2$ with $s = 10$, $u = 17.5$, $a = -9.8$ to give a 3-term quadratic, e.g. $4.9t^2 - 17.5t + 10 = 0$ Solves to find both roots, $t = \dfrac{5{7$ and $t = \dfrac{20{7$ (0.714 and 2.86), and subtracts 2.1 s or 2.14 s
items.why: Vertical motion under gravity comes up in almost every session (Jun 2026 Q4, Jan 2026 Q3, Jun 2025 Q3); the time spent above a given height was asked in Jan 2024 Q6(c) and again in Jun 2026 Q4(b).
keywords: Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line

items.question: A train moves along a straight horizontal track with constant acceleration. It passes three signals $P$, $Q$ and $R$, in that order. The distance $PQ$ is 96 m and the distance $QR$ is 165 m. The train takes 8 s to travel from $P$ to $Q$ and 10 s to travel from $Q$ to $R$. The train is modelled as a particle. Find the acceleration of the train. Find the speed of the train as it passes $R$.
items.ms: Use of $s = ut + \frac{1{2at^2$ for $PQ$, where $u$ is the speed at $P$: $96 = 8u + 32a$ A second equation, e.g. for $PR$: $261 = 18u + 162a$, or for $QR$: $165 = 10(u + 8a) + 50a$ Solves the two equations simultaneously to find $a$ $a = 0.5$ m s⁻² Use of $v = u + at$ with their $u$ $(= 10)$, their $a$ and $t = 18$, or another complete method 19 m s⁻¹
items.why: Constant acceleration past three marker points (Jan 2014 Q5, Jun 2016 Q1, Jan 2023 Q5) is a recurring opening question; it rests on forming and solving two suvat equations.

items.question: A car is travelling along a straight horizontal road at a constant speed of 24 m s⁻¹. The driver sees a fallen tree lying across the road 66 m ahead. The driver takes 0.75 s to react, during which time the car continues at 24 m s⁻¹. The brakes are then applied and the car decelerates uniformly, coming to rest just as it reaches the tree. The car is modelled as a particle. Find the deceleration of the car. On another day the road is wet. The driver's reaction time is again 0.75 s, but now the greatest possible deceleration of the car is 5 m s⁻². The car is travelling at a constant speed of $V$ m s⁻¹ when the driver sees an obstacle 66 m ahead. Find the greatest value of $V$ for which the car can stop without hitting the obstacle.
items.ms: Distance travelled while the driver reacts $= 24 \times 0.75 = 18$ m Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$, $u = 24$ and $s = 66 -$ their 18 6 m s⁻² Distance travelled while the driver reacts $= 0.75V$ Braking distance from $0 = V^2 - 2 \times 5 \times s$, i.e. $s = \dfrac{V^2{10$ $0.75V + \dfrac{V^2{10 = 66$ oe, e.g. $V^2 + 7.5V - 660 = 0$ $V = 22.2$ (awrt)
items.why: Braking after a reaction delay was asked once (Oct 2021 Q3(c)); working backwards to the greatest safe speed, which needs a quadratic, has not been asked.

items.question: A robot vacuum cleaner moves along a straight corridor. At time $t$ seconds its displacement from a fixed point $O$ in the corridor is $s$ metres. The displacement-time graph shows the motion of the robot for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 26$. The graph consists of four straight line segments. Find the velocity of the robot for $12 < t < 22$. Find the average speed of the robot for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 26$. Sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion of the robot for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 26$.
items.ms: Gradient of the third segment, $\dfrac{-2 - 6{22 - 12$ $-0.8$ m s⁻¹, or 0.8 m s⁻¹ in the negative direction (back towards $O$) Total distance $= 6 + 8 + 2 = 16$ m, divided by 26 0.615 m s⁻¹ (awrt 0.62) or $\dfrac{8{13$ m s⁻¹ Four horizontal segments, with $v = 0$ for $8 < t < 12$ The segment for $12 < t < 22$ below the $t$-axis and the segments for $0 < t < 8$ and $22 < t < 26$ above it Velocities 0.75 and 0.5 and their $-0.8$ shown, with the times 8, 12, 22 and 26
items.why: A displacement-time graph was set for the first time in Jun 2026 (Q3) with a velocity-time sketch; the average speed for a journey that doubles back past $O$ is the natural next question.

items.question: A ball $P$ is projected vertically upwards with speed 24.5 m s⁻¹ from a point $A$ on horizontal ground. One second later, a second ball $Q$ is released from rest at a point $B$, which is 49 m vertically above $A$, as shown in the diagram. The balls move in the same vertical line and are modelled as particles moving freely under gravity. The time $t$ seconds is measured from the instant when $P$ is projected. Find the greatest height above the ground reached by $P$. Find the value of $t$ when $P$ and $Q$ collide. Find the speed of $P$ immediately before the collision, and state whether $P$ is moving upwards or downwards at this instant.
items.ms: Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$, $u = 24.5$, $a = -9.8$ 30.6 m or 31 m Height of $P$ above $A$: $24.5t - 4.9t^2$ Height of $Q$ above $A$: $49 - 4.9(t - 1)^2$ Equates their expressions and solves for $t$ $t = 3$ Use of $v = u + at$ with $u = 24.5$, $a = -9.8$ and their $t$: $v = 24.5 - 9.8 \times 3$ 4.9 m s⁻¹, downwards
items.why: Two vertically moving particles that collide were set in Jan 2020 Q3, Oct 2024 Q7 and Oct 2025 Q4; here $P$ is already falling when $Q$ catches it, a twist not yet asked.

items.question: A go-kart moves along a straight horizontal track. It starts from rest at time $t = 0$. The acceleration-time graph shows the acceleration, $a$ m s⁻², of the go-kart for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant T$. At time $t = T$ the go-kart comes to rest. Find the value of $T$. Sketch a speed-time graph for the motion of the go-kart for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant T$. Find the time taken for the go-kart to travel the first 100 m.
items.ms: Speed at $t = 5$: $2.4 \times 5 = 12$ m s⁻¹ (area under the graph, or $v = u + at$) $0 = 12 - 1.5(T - 20)$ $T = 28$ Three straight segments: rising from the origin, horizontal, then falling to the $t$-axis 12, 5, 20 and their $T$ shown Distance in the first 5 s $= \frac{1{2 \times 5 \times 12 = 30$ m Time for the remaining $100 - 30 = 70$ m at 12 m s⁻¹ $= \dfrac{70{12$ s 10.8 s (awrt) or $\dfrac{65{6$ s
items.why: Acceleration-time graphs were given in Oct 2020 Q8 and Oct 2023 Q2 and sketched in Jan 2026 and Jun 2026; reading a journey off one and finding when a set distance is reached is a fresh angle.

items.question: A particle $P$ of mass 0.4 kg moves along a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. At time $t = 0$, $P$ passes through the point $O$ on the line with speed 12 m s⁻¹. Throughout the motion, $P$ is acted on by a constant horizontal force of magnitude 1.6 N whose direction is opposite to the direction of motion of $P$ at $t = 0$. At time $t$ seconds the displacement of $P$ from $O$ is $s$ metres, measured in the direction of motion of $P$ at $t = 0$. Show that the acceleration of $P$ has magnitude 4 m s⁻². Find the value of $s$ when $P$ is instantaneously at rest. Find the total distance travelled by $P$ in the interval $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 5$. Find the value of $t$ when $P$ returns to $O$, and the speed of $P$ at this instant.
items.ms: Use of $F = ma$: $1.6 = 0.4a$ $a = 4$ m s⁻² cso Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$, $u = 12$, $a = -4$ $s = 18$ Time at which $P$ is at rest: $0 = 12 - 4t$, $t = 3$ Distance moved back towards $O$ for $3 \leqslant t \leqslant 5$: $\frac{1{2 \times 4 \times 2^2 = 8$ m, or $s = 12 \times 5 - 2 \times 5^2 = 10$ at $t = 5$ and uses $18 + (18 - 10)$ 26 m Solves $12t - 2t^2 = 0$, or uses symmetry: $2 \times 3$ $t = 6$ and speed 12 m s⁻¹
items.why: Almost every M1.3.1 change of direction has been vertical; a particle on a horizontal line that turns back (distance against displacement, return to the start) is rarely set, and it links to $F = ma$ (M1.4.1).

items.question: A cyclist rides along a straight horizontal road from junction $A$ to junction $B$. She starts from rest at $A$ and accelerates uniformly at 0.5 m s⁻² until her speed is $V$ m s⁻¹. She then rides at constant speed $V$ m s⁻¹ before decelerating uniformly at 1.5 m s⁻², coming to rest at $B$. The journey from $A$ to $B$ takes 80 s and the distance from $A$ to $B$ is 612 m. The cyclist is modelled as a particle. Sketch a speed-time graph for the motion of the cyclist from $A$ to $B$. Show that the cyclist rides at constant speed for $\left(80 - \dfrac{8V{3\right)$ seconds. Hence show that $V^2 - 60V + 459 = 0$. Find the value of $V$, giving a reason for rejecting the other solution of the equation.
items.ms: Trapezium shape starting at the origin and finishing on the $t$-axis $V$ and 80 marked Uses $v = u + at$ (or the gradient) for one of the variable-speed stages Accelerating for $2V$ s and decelerating for $\dfrac{2V{3$ s $80 - 2V - \dfrac{2V{3 = 80 - \dfrac{8V{3$ cso Total area under the graph $= 612$, using all three stages or a trapezium, e.g. $\frac{1{2(2V)V + V\left(80 - \dfrac{8V{3\right) + \frac{1{2\left(\dfrac{2V{3\right)V = 612$ Correct unsimplified equation, e.g. $\frac{1{2\left(80 + 80 - \dfrac{8V{3\right)V = 612$ Simplifies to $V^2 - 60V + 459 = 0$ cso Solves the quadratic, e.g. $(V - 9)(V - 51) = 0$ $V = 9$, with a reason: $V = 51$ would make the time at constant speed $80 - 136 < 0$ (or the accelerating time, 102 s, longer than the whole journey)
items.why: A three-stage speed-time journey leading to a quadratic in $V$ appears in most sessions (Oct 2016 Q7, Oct 2017 Q6, Jan 2019 Q6, Jan 2025 Q2); justifying the rejected root (Oct 2017 Q6(d)) is often lost.

items.question: A ball is projected vertically upwards with speed 8.4 m s⁻¹ from a point $A$ which is 4.5 m above horizontal ground. The ball moves freely under gravity until it hits the ground. It then rebounds vertically upwards with two-thirds of the speed it had immediately before it hit the ground. The ball is modelled as a particle and the time for which it is in contact with the ground is ignored. Find the speed of the ball immediately before it first hits the ground. Find the time between the projection of the ball and the instant when it first hits the ground. Find the greatest height above the ground reached by the ball after it rebounds. Taking upwards as positive, sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion of the ball from the instant it is projected until it reaches its greatest height after the rebound. Show on your sketch the velocity of the ball when it is projected, immediately before and immediately after it hits the ground, the time at which it hits the ground and the time at which it reaches its greatest height after the rebound.
items.ms: Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ from $A$ with $u = \pm 8.4$, $a = \pm 9.8$ and $s = \pm 4.5$ Correct equation, e.g. $v^2 = 8.4^2 + 2 \times 9.8 \times 4.5$ 12.6 m s⁻¹ Use of $v = u + at$: $-12.6 = 8.4 - 9.8t$, or another complete method 2.14 s (awrt) or $\dfrac{15{7$ s Rebound speed $\frac{2{3 \times 12.6 = 8.4$ m s⁻¹ and use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$ 3.6 m Straight line from $(0, 8.4)$ with negative gradient, crossing the $t$-axis and ending at $v = -12.6$ Then a vertical jump to $v = 8.4$ at the same time, followed by a straight line parallel to the first, ending on the $t$-axis Values 8.4, $-12.6$, $\dfrac{15{7$ (or 2.14) and 3 shown
items.why: Projection from above the ground with a rebound was set in Jun 2017 Q4, Jun 2019 Q6 and Jun 2026 Q4, and velocity-time sketches for vertical motion appear in about one session in four (Oct 2020, Jan 2024, Jun 2025).

items.question: A hot-air balloon is rising vertically with constant speed 4.9 m s⁻¹. When the balloon is 29.4 m above horizontal ground, a small sandbag of mass 2 kg is released from the balloon. After its release, the sandbag is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity until it hits the ground. Write down the velocity of the sandbag immediately after it is released. Find the time taken for the sandbag to reach the ground. Find the height of the balloon above the ground at the instant when the sandbag hits the ground. Find the speed of the sandbag immediately before it hits the ground. The sandbag sinks 0.35 m vertically into soft ground before coming to rest. The ground exerts a constant resistive force on the sandbag. Find the magnitude of this force.
items.ms: 4.9 m s⁻¹ vertically upwards Use of $s = ut + \frac{1{2at^2$ with $s = -29.4$, $u = 4.9$, $a = -9.8$ (consistent signs) Correct quadratic, e.g. $4.9t^2 - 4.9t - 29.4 = 0$ or $t^2 - t - 6 = 0$ 3 s $29.4 + 4.9 \times$ their 3 44.1 m Use of $v = 4.9 - 9.8 \times$ their 3, or $v^2 = 4.9^2 + 2 \times 9.8 \times 29.4$ 24.5 m s⁻¹ Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u =$ their 24.5, $v = 0$, $s = 0.35$ to find the deceleration, 857.5 m s⁻² Equation of motion with the resistance, the weight and $ma$: $R - 2g = 2 \times 857.5$ 1730 N or 1700 N
items.why: A body released from something already moving (the sandbag starts with the balloon's upward velocity) has not been set; a particle hitting the ground and sinking in (M1.4.2) is the usual bridge from kinematics to dynamics in long questions.

items.question: A drone carrying a parcel moves vertically. At time $t = 0$ the drone rises from rest from a point $O$ on horizontal ground. The velocity-time graph shows the velocity, $v$ m s⁻¹, of the drone for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 56$, with upwards taken as positive. The drone hovers for $21 \leqslant t \leqslant 30$ and then descends, coming to rest at $t = 56$ at a point 24 m vertically above $O$. The drone is modelled as a particle. Find the greatest height above $O$ reached by the drone. Find the value of $V$. Find the two values of $t$ at which the drone is 50 m above $O$. The parcel has mass 1.2 kg and hangs below the drone on a light inextensible vertical string. Find the tension in the string for $0 < t < 5$.

items.question: Two stations $X$ and $Y$ are 4.2 km apart on a straight horizontal railway with two parallel tracks. At time $t = 0$, train $A$ leaves $X$ from rest and travels towards $Y$. It accelerates uniformly for 50 s until its speed is 20 m s⁻¹ and then travels at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹. At time $t = 30$, train $B$ leaves $Y$ from rest and travels on the other track towards $X$. It accelerates uniformly for 50 s until its speed is 25 m s⁻¹ and then travels at a constant speed of 25 m s⁻¹. The trains are modelled as particles. The time $t$ is measured in seconds. Taking the direction from $X$ to $Y$ as positive, sketch, on the same axes, velocity-time graphs for the motion of the two trains for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 150$. Show that the trains pass each other when $t = 135$. Find the distance from $X$ of the point where the trains pass each other. After passing $B$, train $A$ continues at 20 m s⁻¹ and then decelerates uniformly at 0.5 m s⁻², coming to rest at $Y$. Find the total time taken by train $A$ to travel from $X$ to $Y$.

items.question: A model rocket is launched vertically upwards from rest at a point $O$ on horizontal ground. While its motor is burning, the rocket moves upwards with constant acceleration 14 m s⁻². The motor burns for 2.5 s and then stops. The rocket then moves freely under gravity until it hits the ground. The rocket is modelled as a particle of constant mass and air resistance is ignored. Find the height of the rocket above $O$ when the motor stops. Find the greatest height above $O$ reached by the rocket. Find the total time from the launch of the rocket until it hits the ground. Sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion of the rocket from its launch until it hits the ground. The mass of the rocket is 0.6 kg. Find the magnitude of the upward thrust produced by the motor. Suggest one refinement to the model that would make it more realistic.
items.ms: Use of $s = ut + \frac{1{2at^2$ with $u = 0$, $a = 14$, $t = 2.5$ 43.75 m (accept 43.8 m or 44 m) Speed when the motor stops $= 14 \times 2.5 = 35$ m s⁻¹ Use of $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 35$, $v = 0$, $a = -9.8$ to find the further rise, 62.5 m 106 m or 110 m Complete method for the free-flight time, e.g. $s = ut + \frac{1{2at^2$ with $s = -43.75$, $u = 35$, $a = -9.8$ Correct equation, e.g. $4.9t^2 - 35t - 43.75 = 0$ Solves for the positive root ($t = 8.23$) and adds 2.5 10.7 s or 11 s Straight line from the origin rising to a maximum at $t = 2.5$, then a less steep straight line falling, crossing the $t$-axis and ending below it 35 and 2.5 shown, with the graph ending at their total time and a velocity of about $-45.6$ Equation of motion: $F - 0.6g = 0.6 \times 14$ 14.3 N or 14 N e.g. include air resistance; or allow for the mass of the rocket decreasing as the fuel burns; or allow for the thrust not being constant
items.why: Two-stage vertical motion in which the first stage is not free fall (parachutists in Jan 2021 Q7 and May 2024 Q5) recurs; a powered upward stage followed by free flight, with the velocity changing sign, has not been asked.

items.question: A car and a van move in the same direction along parallel lanes of a straight horizontal road. At time $t = 0$ they pass the point $P$ side by side. The car passes $P$ with speed 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1.5 m s⁻² for 12 s. It then moves at constant speed. The van passes $P$ with speed 24 m s⁻¹ and decelerates uniformly for 12 s until its speed is 12 m s⁻¹. It then moves at a constant speed of 12 m s⁻¹. Later, the car overtakes the van. The car and the van are modelled as particles. The time $t$ is measured in seconds. Sketch, on the same axes, speed-time graphs for the motion of the car and the van for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 20$. Find the value of $t$ at which the car and the van have the same speed. Explain why, before the car overtakes the van, the distance between them is greatest at this time, and find this greatest distance. Find the value of $t$ when the car overtakes the van. Find the distance from $P$ of the point where the car overtakes the van. Sketch an acceleration-time graph for the motion of the van for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 20$.

Show that $d^2 = 68t^2 - 204t + 425$ The light from $L$ can be seen from $S$ only when $S$ is within 17 km of $L$.
